children.title: Weather radar and terrain on the ND and VD
A380X weather radar on the ND and weather on the VD

blocks.text: The A380X ND always showed WXR INOP (both WXR systems were hard-coded as failed) and had no radar picture. It now has the native radar of the A32NX, with the A380 rules, and the VD shows the weather on its vertical cut.
A380X ND with weather cells ahead, and the same cells on the VD below. Development picture: the WX+T label and the hatched off-path areas seen here were removed later; the A380X ND now reads WX.

items: EFIS control panel: select the WX overlay.

MFD SURV CONTROLS: WXR AUTO or OFF, TURB AUTO or OFF, MODE WX or MAP, WX ON VD. These buttons are wired on `core/surveillance`; with this branch alone the radar runs at their default settings (WXR AUTO, TURB AUTO, MODE WX, WX ON VD AUTO).
The radar is shown when the WXR & TAWS system selected on the SURV panel is not failed. A system is failed only while its AESU is reset or its power is lost (AC ESS for system 1, AC 4 for system 2).

The ND range table is -1 (ZOOM, the airport map) and 10 to 640 NM; the radar is hidden at ZOOM and at 640 NM: "The ND can only display the weather, if the selected range is below, or equal to, 320 nm" (A380 FCOM DSC-31-20-50).

blocks.text: Moderate rain (yellow) over a wide area, with its VD cut. Development picture: the WX+T label and the hatched off-path areas seen here were removed later; the A380X ND now reads WX.
TURB on: heavy rain drawn magenta (turbulence proxy). Development picture: the WX+T label and the hatched off-path areas seen here were removed later; the A380X ND now reads WX.

items: WX ON VD (SURV CONTROLS) shows the weather on the VD, along the same cut as the terrain (see Radar, terrain and VD after the A380 and A320 manuals).
Cells are drawn green and yellow with a red core; no magenta: the real VD does not display turbulence (FCOM DSC-31-20-40-10).
Heights are placed on the ADR baro-corrected altitude, like the VD's aircraft symbol.
The VD weather is stylised. Why: The vertical MapView of MSFS is a single thin beam (tilting it crashes the gauge); the VD picture is built from the ND radar views.
PRED W/S and GAIN are not drawn. Why: The MSFS radar has no predictive windshear or gain.
No TURB-only mode. Why: The A380 has none: TURB off gives WX, on gives WX+T.

blocks.text: The picture covers the real antenna sweep of the A380's Honeywell RDR-4000: 160 degrees (80 degrees each side of the nose; Honeywell IntuVue white paper). The real display fills up to 90 degrees from the radar's memory, which the MSFS radar does not have, so nothing is painted beside and behind the aircraft there.

items: On the EFIS control panel select the WX overlay, the ARC or a ROSE mode and a range of 10 to 320 NM.
With `core/surveillance`: set the WXR block of MFD SURV > CONTROLS (WXR, TURB, MODE, WX ON VD). Without it the radar runs at the default settings.
Read the weather on the ND and its vertical cut on the VD below.

children.title: Weather radar mode and messages on the ND

blocks.text: Nothing on the ND told the crew which radar mode was selected. The mode now appears in green on the right of the ARC and ROSE pages while the radar is selected, as on the real ND. The A32NX shows the Honeywell list of the A320 FCOM (DSC-34-SURV-30-30); the A380X shows the A380's own WXR messages (A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-30-20 "WXR MESSAGES"): WX for the WX display function whatever the TURB button, MAP, WXR OFF.

head: ND message
A32NX (MODE knob)
A380X (SURV CONTROLS)
rows: WX display function, whatever the TURB button
no WX overlay on the EFIS panel, or the WXR & TAWS system failed

blocks.text: A32NX ARC: WX+T above the TERR box.
A32NX ROSE NAV: WX.

items: Shown on the ARC and ROSE pages (NAV, ILS, VOR), not in PLAN, and not while the terrain replaces the weather (TERR ON ND).
Shown on the ground too, where the radar also scans.
The native radar gauge decides and publishes the label (`A32NX_WXR_ND_{L,R}_MODE`), so the ND follows exactly what the gauge draws.
No label in PLAN. Why: The radar is not shown in PLAN.
Nothing to set: the message follows the radar selection (A32NX MODE knob; A380X WX overlay and SURV CONTROLS).
Check the message on the right of the ND, above the TERR box, after each radar change.

children.title: Terrain on the ND (TERR ON ND) and A380X VD terrain

blocks.text: TERR ON ND needed SimBridge. The native gauge now draws it from MSFS's own terrain, with the EGPWS colours, on every map page but PLAN, also on the ground.
A380X at Aspen, 10 NM: terrain far above the aircraft in red, close in yellow, below in green; the VD terrain profile in brown.
The same place at 160 NM.

head: Terrain relative to the aircraft
Colour
rows: 500 ft below (250 ft gear down) to 1000 ft above
Down to 1000 ft below (500 ft gear down)

blocks.text: The dots are a random stipple, as on the real display. The map turns with the ND's heading; ARC shows the forward half, the ROSE modes the whole disk.
The A380X VD terrain profile (brown), water in cyan from sea level down.

items: Needs the TERR SYS button of the SURV page not OFF (otherwise NO TERR DATA AVAILABLE).
The cut follows the flight plan or the track (see Radar, terrain and VD after the A380 and A320 manuals).

blocks.text: The TERR box with the highest and lowest elevations of the range needs real elevations, which a gauge cannot read from MSFS: its figures come from SimBridge when it runs. Without SimBridge the box stays empty and the terrain is drawn as usual.

items: At most 8 map views per module. Why: MSFS crashes a 9th; the A380X switches its views between weather and terrain.
Peaks box only with SimBridge. Why: No elevation readback from MSFS. What to do: Run SimBridge.
Terrain far above the range top is shown red. Why: MSFS does not clamp to the first colour entry.

blocks.text: When the SimBridge figures say that the highest terrain of the range is more than 2000 ft below the aircraft, the terrain is drawn in green by its elevation within the range: solid for the top 5 %, dense dots down to 65 %, light dots down to 35 %, nothing lower. Without SimBridge the standard colours above apply.

items: When descending faster than 1000 ft/min, the colours use the altitude expected in 30 s (A320 FCOM DSC-31-45).

The old `terronnd` gauge (SimBridge's own terrain picture) is no longer loaded: SimBridge is only used for the peaks box figures. The A32NX systems host now posts the aircraft status to SimBridge itself.
A32NX: press the TERR ON ND pushbutton of the side wanted (ND in ARC or ROSE).
A380X: select the TERR overlay on the EFIS control panel; keep the TERR SYS of the SURV page not OFF for the VD profile.
Optional: run SimBridge for the peaks box figures and the peaks mode.

children.title: Radar, terrain and VD after the A380 and A320 manuals

items: In the managed lateral modes the VD shows the terrain and weather along the flight plan (a 200 NM window from just behind the aircraft, with the turns); in the selected modes along the track (FCOM: VIEW ALONG ACFT TRK). More than 5 NM off the plan: the track.
The terrain is the highest across a width of 2 × RNP (1 NM terminal, 2 NM en route above 18 000 ft).
The grey area starts at the next track change of more than 3° (the VD no longer matches the ND beyond it).

children.title: The VD scale and the terrain height

items: With a trajectory, the highest of the aircraft and the path sits at three quarters of the window: in cruise the ground stays on the plot, as on the real aircraft at FL400.
The gap under the aircraft symbol is the true height, whatever the altimeter setting (FCOM / FCTM).
Water in the ND teal; no magenta on the VD; no VD weather when TERR is not available.

blocks.text: A380X VD with the terrain profile and water (in-sim).

items: The radar scans and draws on the ground too (A320 FCOM DSC-34-SURV-30-30: "on the ground, the radar is scanning when the flight crew sets one radar to ON and selects a display mode").
MAP mode is a ground map from the terrain.
The picture builds up over 30 s after the radar starts, sweeping left to right (A380 FCOM).
The ARC picture keeps the ND bottom corners free and stops just above the TCAS / WXR message box, as on the real display.

blocks.text: Just after WX is selected: the picture is building up.
A few seconds later.

items: No A380 AUTO off-path display. Why: MSFS runs one radar per aircraft; a third view changed what the beam views delivered, so it was removed.
Nothing to set: the VD cut follows the lateral mode (managed: the flight plan; selected: the track).
After switching the radar on, allow 30 s for the picture to build up.

children.title: Fewer stutters: idle map views paused, 20 Hz / 10 Hz redraw

blocks.text: The radar and terrain gauge uses up to eight MSFS map views per aircraft, and the sim renders every visible view each frame, drawn or not. On the A380X this cost frame rate and caused stutters.

items: A view nothing has shown for 120 frames is now paused (made invisible). It is woken up with a 60-frame warm-up before it is drawn again. With WX and TERR off, in PLAN or with the ND unpowered, no view renders at all.

The ND picture is redrawn at 20 Hz and the VD terrain at 10 Hz instead of every frame, and at once when what the display shows changes (page, range, WX / TERR selection). The first radar sweep is still drawn every frame. At 20 Hz a 3 degree/s turn moves the picture by less than one pixel per step.

head: A380X in cruise, WX on, ARC 40 NM (PresentMon, 2 x 120 s)
Before
Views paused
+ 20/10 Hz

blocks.text: The A32NX never had the problem (its result is neutral). The picture itself is the same.

items: A paused view needs about 1 s to come back. Why: The 60-frame warm-up lets the sim render the view again before it is drawn (no white flash). What to do: Normal: switching WX / TERR already took about a second on the A380X.
Nothing to set.

children.title: Terrain and radar views get their settings again after a pause

blocks.text: On the A380X F/O VD showed a terrain profile (flat blocks) that the CPT VD did not, with the same inputs. The gauge pauses the map views nothing shows (previous feature) and wakes them up when needed. It is not known whether the sim keeps a view's settings while it is paused, and a setting the sim ignored was never sent again, since the gauge only sent changes. As a safeguard:

items: A view that wakes up gets its whole setup again (terrain, radar, VD view, each by its role).
The view radius (the range) is sent on a change, after a wake-up, when the sim time goes back, and again every second while the view is in use, not only on a change.
CPT and F/O ND with the same mode and range, terrain shown: The two VD terrain profiles are identical.
A view woken up after a pause (WX / TERR switched, page or range changed): The right terrain zoom and picture, as on the other side.
The cause is a likely one, not a proven one. Why: The F/O stale terrain view zoom was cured by the resend (user test); whether the sim drops settings of a paused view is still not known.
Nothing to set.

children.title: A380X: the OANS map takes the mouse through the radar gauges

blocks.text: The radar and terrain gauges sit over the ND and caught every mouse event on the map area: the OANS airport map could not be dragged and its runway and exit labels could not be clicked (BTV selection). The gauges only draw, so they no longer take the mouse.

items: Select the ND ZOOM range to show the OANS airport map (stock FBW OANS, needs its airport data).
Drag the map with the mouse or the KCCU cursor, click runway and exit labels as usual.

children.title: Surveillance: SURV controls, ECAM SURV lines and TCAS
A380X SURV controls, STATUS & SWITCHING and the pedestal SURV panel

blocks.text: The weather radar block of the MFD SURV CONTROLS page, the STATUS & SWITCHING system selection and the pedestal SURV panel buttons were stubs. They now work and drive the same systems.

The A380 has no separate radar, TCAS or TAWS control panels: they are on the MFD SURV pages and the pedestal SURV panel (FCOM DSC-34-20-60-50). In FBW the weather radar block of the page was a stub (every button greyed), STATUS & SWITCHING did not reflect failures, and no button of the pedestal panel worked. Now they do, and the page and the panel stay in step.
SURV CONTROLS: XPDR (code, IDENT, AUTO / ON / STBY, ALT RPTG), TCAS (TA/RA, TA ONLY, STBY; NORM, ABV, BLW), WXR, TAWS, and DEFAULT SETTINGS.

head: WXR button
Effect
rows: Weather radar on or off (the ND radar picture of `core/nd-weather-terrain`).
Predictive windshear (written for the systems; MSFS has no predictive windshear).
Turbulence detection (magenta on the ND with the native radar of `core/nd-weather-terrain`).
Radar gain (written; MSFS has no gain).
AUTO, or a manual elevation or tilt.

blocks.text: The WXR buttons are inhibited only when the selected WXR system has really failed.
STATUS & SWITCHING: SYS 1 / SYS 2 of the WXR and TAWS (top) and of the XPDR and TCAS (bottom); the selected system is lit, each item shows its real state.

items: WXR DISPLAY, TURB, PRED W/S, TERR SYS, GPWS items show the real failure of each system.
XPDR / TCAS SYS 1 / SYS 2 select the transponder system (the one the TCAS uses) and light from it.

blocks.text: The SURV CONTROLS page in the sim (in-sim screenshot).

The panel buttons never worked: their light template runs the button code only when the panel is powered, and the pedestal never told it so. They are powered from DC 1 now and linked to the MFD pages:

head: Panel button
Does
Same as
rows: Glide slope mode of the GPWS on / off

blocks.text: Each button lights from the same value the page uses, so pressing one on the pedestal changes the page, and the reverse.

items: PRED W/S and GAIN MAN do nothing visible. Why: The MSFS radar has no predictive windshear and no gain; the values are written for when it does.
One MSFS radar for both systems. Why: SYS 1 / SYS 2 select the failure state and the lights; the picture comes from the same sim radar.

blocks.text: Code clean-up on this branch with no visible effect: the ECAM procedure tables read the selected XPDR & TCAS system through one helper.

items: Open the SURV pages: MFD system menu SURV (or the KCCU SURV key), then CONTROLS or STATUS & SWITCHING.
On CONTROLS set the WXR (WXR, PRED W/S, TURB, GAIN, MODE, WX ON VD, ELEVN/TILT), the TCAS (TA/RA, TA ONLY, STBY; NORM, ABV, BLW) and the TAWS options.
On STATUS & SWITCHING, or with the pedestal buttons, select WXR / TAWS SYS 1 or SYS 2 and XPDR / TCAS SYS 1 or SYS 2.
Use the pedestal TCAS ABV / BLW / TA ONLY and G/S MODE buttons as shortcuts: the MFD page follows.

children.title: A380X VD: separate NO TERR / NO WX DATA messages

blocks.text: TERR SYS OFF removed both the terrain and the weather from the VD message logic, so the VD always said "NO TERR AND WX DATA AVAILABLE". Each source now has its own message.
The VD message was always "NO TERR AND WX DATA AVAILABLE" when TERR SYS was off. Now:

head: Situation
VD message
rows: WXR failed or OFF, or WX ON VD OFF
NO TERR AND WX DATA AVAILABLE

blocks.text: WXR off: NO WX DATA AVAILABLE.
TERR SYS off and WXR off: NO TERR AND WX DATA AVAILABLE.

items: Nothing to set: the VD message follows the TERR SYS, WXR and WX ON VD buttons of MFD > SURV > CONTROLS.

children.title: A380X ECAM procedures: WXR & TAWS and XPDR & TCAS lines sensed

blocks.text: The dual ADR and IR fault procedures ask the crew to move the WXR & TAWS and the XPDR & TCAS to the system that still has valid data. Those lines were hard-coded as done, so the ECAM ticked them even when the wrong system stayed selected. They now follow the selection made on the MFD SURV STATUS & SWITCHING page, and the TCAS 1 / 2 FAULT procedures show their XPDR & TCAS line, which was hidden.
MFD SURV STATUS & SWITCHING: the SYS 1 / SYS 2 buttons of WXR & TAWS (top) and XPDR & TCAS (bottom).
IR 1+2 FAULT with both systems on SYS 2: the two lines wait, in cyan.
After selecting SYS 1 on the SURV page: the lines are done (white) and the cursor moves on.

head: Procedure
WXR & TAWS
XPDR & TCAS
rows: ADR 1+2 FAULT, ADR 2+3 FAULT, IR 1+2 FAULT, IR 2+3 FAULT

blocks.text: TCAS 1 FAULT: the XPDR & TCAS line is now shown.

items: The right system is already selected when the fault appears: The line is shown already done.
The crew selects the other system: The line ticks within a second; the cursor moves to the next line.
The crew goes back to the failed side: The line becomes due again (it follows the live selection).

TCAS 1 FAULT and TCAS 2 FAULT come together. Why: FBW has one TCAS computer: both procedures read the same TCAS fault (an FBW note in the code). What to do: Select the system the procedure you follow asks for.
When an ADR / IR dual fault or a TCAS fault procedure asks for WXR & TAWS ... SYS n or XPDR & TCAS ... SYS n, select that system on MFD > SURV > STATUS & SWITCHING (or with the pedestal SYS buttons).
The line ticks by itself; the E/WD cursor moves to the next line.

children.title: A380X ECAM LINE-UP checklist: CABIN CREW line

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM BEFORE TAKEOFF checklist has a CABIN CREW item; the ECAM LINE-UP checklist did not.
ECAM LINE-UP: the CABIN CREW ... ADVISED line (crew check).
The ECAM LINE-UP checklist gets the CABIN CREW line that the flyPad checklist already had (A380 FCOM BEFORE TAKEOFF checklist: CABIN CREW ... ADVISE). It is ticked by the crew.

items: No SURV lines in the normal checklists. Why: The A380 FCOM normal checklists (PRO-NOR-C-L) have none (SURV, WX & TERR and TCAS are SOP flow items); an earlier version of this change added some and was reverted.
At line-up, call the ECAM LINE-UP checklist (C/L key on the ECAM control panel).
Advise the cabin crew, then tick the CABIN CREW ... ADVISED line.

children.title: TCAS: intruders shown and announced as TAs while RAs are inhibited

blocks.text: With every RA inhibited (TA ONLY selected, or low: below 900 ft radio altitude in descent, until 1100 ft in climb, see the next feature), the TCAS kept classifying an intruder that met the RA criteria as an RA. The ND drew it as a red RA square, and since it was not a TA, there was no "TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC" and no TA state. A real TCAS in TA ONLY shows it as an amber TA with the TA aural. The classification is now capped at TA while all RAs are inhibited.
The ND traffic symbols: other, proximate, TA, RA, with the relative altitude in hundreds of feet and the vertical trend arrow.
A32NX: TA ONLY, centred at the bottom of the ND (A320 FCOM DSC-34-SURV-60-20 figure).
A380X: TA ONLY in the message box.

items: TA ONLY selected, intruder meeting the RA criteria: Amber TA circle and "TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC" (before: red RA square, no aural).
Below 900 ft radio altitude in descent, until 1100 ft in climb (all RAs inhibited): Same: TAs only, TA ONLY on the ND.
Partial inhibits (no CLIMB / DESCEND / INCREASE DESCENT RA): Unchanged: RAs are still issued.
An RA already running when the inhibit starts: It runs to its own end.
Same change on both aircraft. Why: The A32NX TcasComputer and the A380X LegacyTcasComputer share the classification code.
Select TA ONLY: A32NX ATC/TCAS panel TCAS mode selector to TA; A380X MFD > SURV > CONTROLS TCAS TA ONLY (or the pedestal TA ONLY button).
Traffic that would give an RA is shown as an amber TA with the "TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC" aural.

children.title: TCAS: low-altitude RA and TA aural inhibitions with the real hysteresis

blocks.text: The TCAS inhibits all RAs close to the ground, and lower down the TA aural too. Both used a flat threshold (1000 ft and 500 ft radio altitude). The A380 FCTM (Supplementary Information, TCAS) gives a hysteresis, the FCOM "below 1000 ft ±100 ft". Both TCAS computers now use it:

head: Inhibition
Starts (descending through)
Ends (climbing through)
rows: All RAs (TA ONLY on the ND)

items: Without a valid radio altitude, neither low-altitude inhibition applies.
The four altitudes are named constants of the TCAS code (no other effect).
Nothing to set: the inhibitions follow the radio altitude.

children.title: TCAS traffic display, ND TCAS messages, TRAF pb, WXR/TAWS SYS pbs

blocks.text: Deviations from the FCOM TCAS and SURV descriptions found by the FCOM gap audit (A320 FCOM DSC-34-SURV-40 TCAS, A380 FCOM SURV TCAS and SURV panel descriptions):

items: A32NX TRAFFIC selector THRT: while a TA or an RA is present, the proximate and the other intruders within ±2700 ft are shown too, not only the threat (A320 FCOM: "THRT: Proximate and other intruders are displayed only if a TA or an RA is present").
ND TCAS messages (both aircraft): TCAS: CHANGE MODE in PLAN mode and TCAS: REDUCE RANGE above the 40 NM range while there is a TA or an RA; the message is amber for a TA and red for an RA.
A380X only: TCAS: INCREASE RANGE in ROSE VOR or ROSE LS with the ZOOM range in flight; no such message in ZOOM on the ground.

A380X WXR/TAWS SYS 1 and SYS 2 pushbuttons (pedestal SURV panel and MFD SURV STATUS & SWITCHING): pressing the pushbutton that is already lit keeps that system selected. Before, it selected no system.

A380X TRAF pb: the TCAS now reads the FCU TRAF light (the variable it read before was written by nothing). A TA or an RA selects TRAF on each side once, so the traffic shows; the crew can then deselect it.
TA or RA present, ND in PLAN mode: ND message TCAS: CHANGE MODE (amber for a TA, red for an RA).
TA or RA present, ND range above 40 NM: ND message TCAS: REDUCE RANGE (amber / red).
A380X, TA or RA present, ROSE VOR or ROSE LS in ZOOM, in flight: ND message TCAS: INCREASE RANGE. On the ground in ZOOM: no message.
A380X, TRAF off on the FCU, a TA or an RA starts: TRAF comes on by itself on both sides (once); a press turns it off again.
A32NX, TRAFFIC selector THRT, a TA or an RA: The threat plus the proximate and other intruders within ±2700 ft show on the ND; with no TA/RA, no traffic.
No TCAS TEST. Why: Not done yet.
No-bearing intruder lines are not shown. Why: Not done yet.
Nothing to set: the messages and the TRAF selection follow the TCAS.
A32NX: use the THRT position of the TRAFFIC selector (ATC/TCAS panel) to see traffic only around a TA or an RA.
A380X: select the WXR/TAWS system with its SYS pushbutton; pressing the lit one again changes nothing.
The ND message position: centred, above the MODE/RANGE CHANGE line.
A380X: a TA turns TRAF on, and a second press turns it off.
The TCAS message colours (amber TA, red RA) and the THRT traffic display on the A32NX.
These changes are not sim-tested: report any message that does not match the FCOM.

children.title: ECAM procedures, EMER CANC and FIRE TEST

blocks.text: Many ABN PROC procedures were marked WIP: they had no lines and no FWS entry, so selecting one showed nothing. They now carry the FCOM text (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10 and -20). Some sensed alerts also got their FCOM lines, with the lines the FWS can check ticking by themselves.

items: Press ABN PROC on the ECP. The EWD lists the red emergency procedures, then the categories (ENG, F/CTL, L/G, NAV, FUEL, MISCELLANEOUS).
Move the cursor with the ECP UP / DOWN keys and press CHECK: the category opens, then the procedure.
The procedure shows in grey with ACTIVATE: a preview. CHECK on ACTIVATE runs it: the lines turn cyan and the cursor walks through them.

blocks.text: ABN PROC > MISCELLANEOUS.
ABN PROC > L/G: the landing gear procedures.
DITCHING before ACTIVATE (grey preview).
DITCHING activated: ATC and CABIN & CKPT checked by the crew; the cursor on JETTISON ARM.

head: Menu
Procedures
rows: CKPT WINDOW CRACKED, CKPT WINDOW ELEC ARCING, OIS FAULT
FUEL LEAK (the FUEL LEAK DETECTED procedure, with LAND ANSA), MAN BALANCING PROCEDURE
LDG WITH ABNORM NOSE L/G, WITH 2 ABNORM L/Gs ON SAME SIDE, WITH 1 ABNORM WING OR BODY L/G, WITH 2 ABNORM BODY L/Gs, WITH 2 ABNORM WING L/Gs (they call the WHEEL page)
HI VIBRATIONS (was missing from the list)

blocks.text: LDG WITH ABNORM NOSE L/G (preview).
IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE (preview).
These appear by themselves when the failure is detected.
ENG 1 FAIL in flight: AUTO RELIGHT IN PROGRESS, THR LEVER 1 IDLE (ticked, the lever is at idle), then the relight / damaged branches.
ENG 1 FAIL on the ground: the ground lines only.

items: ENG x FAIL just after lift-off: The first line is L/G ... UP, until the gear lever is up.
ENG x FAIL in flight: AUTO RELIGHT IN PROGRESS; THR LEVER x IDLE, ENG x MASTER OFF, FIRE P/B, APU BLEED, AGENT: these tick from the cockpit controls.
ENG x FAIL on the ground: Only the ground part of the procedure.

All four engines fail in flight: ALL ENGINES FAILURE (red, LAND ASAP): the FCOM ALL ENG FLAME OUT procedure, fuel remaining / no fuel, relight, then forced landing or ditching; it scrolls with the cursor.
COND HOT AIR 1 (2) FAULT (hot air valve fault): CARGO TEMP MONITOR; HOT AIR 1 (2) ON shows only while the HOT AIR pushbutton is OFF.
COND TEMP CTL FAULT: Now with its FCOM lines.

blocks.text: ALL ENGINES FAILURE, first page.
COND HOT AIR 1 FAULT.

items: Upper case .IF ... lines are ECAM conditions: the crew confirms them (CONFIRM ...), then the lines below become active.
Headers such as AT TOP OF DESCENT : are centred sub-headings.
Sensed lines tick by themselves once the action is done; the others are ticked by the crew with the ECP CHECK key.
A line fits the 41 characters of the EWD; nesting is capped at three levels.
About 85 sensed alerts show their title only. Why: The FCOM gives no lines for them ("Crew awareness").
Limitations, INOP SYS, INFO and deferred procedures of the new procedures. Why: They are on the STATUS page: see the feature A380X STATUS of the ABN PROC procedures below.
FLUCTUATING VERTICAL SPEED stays WIP; HOT AIR 1(2) OFF / VLV OPEN, T.O V1/VR/V2 DISAGREE, OVERSPEED LOAD ANALYSIS REQUIRED have no lines. Why: They are not in the 2011 FCOM used as the source.
ALL ENGINES FAILURE is long. Why: It is the full FCOM procedure; the EWD scrolls with the cursor.
For a failure the ECAM does not detect: press ABN PROC on the ECP.
Choose the category, then the procedure, with the ECP UP / DOWN keys and CHECK.
Read the grey preview; put the cursor on ACTIVATE and press CHECK to run it.
Tick each line with CHECK once it is done; the sensed lines tick by themselves.
Sensed alerts (ENG FAIL, COND...) show by themselves: read and do their lines the same way.

children.title: A380X STATUS of the ABN PROC procedures

blocks.text: The not-sensed procedures of the feature above had no STATUS: after them, the STATUS page stayed NORMAL. The FCOM gives each one its limitations, inoperative systems, information and deferred procedure (A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28, -32 and -80). The FWS now writes them from the lines the crew ticks: the STATUS follows the branch of the procedure that was flown.

head: Procedure
Line ticked
STATUS
rows: LDG LIMITED TO MAX LDG WEIGHT
LIMITATIONS (approach and landing): MAX LDG WEIGHT, LDG DIST AFFECTED; MAX LDG WEIGHT on the PFD. INOP SYS (approach and landing): BTV, always.
No limitation. Deferred procedure AT TOP OF DESCENT: CKPT WINDOW CRACKED.

MAX FL : 230/MEA (STATUS and PFD); INFO: the cabin altitude table (ACFT FL / CABIN ALT TRGT: 100 = LDG ELEVN, 150 = 3000, 200 = 6000, 230 = 8000); deferred procedure at top of descent: CABIN ALT MODE AUTO.
INOP SYS: L (R) WINDSHIELD HEATG, SLIDG WINDOW HEATG, FIXED WINDOW HEATG; with both AICU pulled, WING A-ICE too.
The same window heating INOP SYS.
LAND ANSA (STATUS and PFD), and FUEL PARTLY UNUSABLE unless LEAK STOPS is ticked.
INFO: MIN FUEL USABLE : OTHER FEED TKs, (ALL OTHER FUEL MAYBE LOST).
DELAY T.O while on the ground.
INFO: FUEL CONSUMPT INCRSD : FMS PRED DISREGARD.

items: A deferred procedure that depends on a crew choice carries that choice as its first line (for example INTERNAL LAYER CRACKED OR NO DIAGNOSIS). Why: The FWS creates the deferred procedures when the abnormal procedure is first shown, before the crew has ticked anything. What to do: Read the condition line before doing the deferred line.
Run the ABN PROC procedure and tick the lines that match your case (for example INTERNAL LAYER CRACKED).
Press STS on the ECP (or wait for the STATUS page at the end of the procedures).
Read the LIMITATIONS, INOP SYS and INFO; the deferred procedure comes up at top of descent.

blocks.text: EMER CANC stops an alert that is wrong or no longer useful: a spurious warning whose aural alert would sound for the rest of the approach, or a caution the crew has dealt with and does not want to see again. Until now the pushbutton did nothing on the FBW A380.
It acts on the alert at the top of the EWD (A380 FCOM DSC-31-40-20):

head: Top alert
EMER CANC
rows: Its aural alert and the MASTER WARN light stop. The procedure stays on the EWD. If the warning goes away and comes back, the aural alert and MASTER WARN come back.
The caution, its procedure and the MASTER CAUT light go away for the rest of the flight, even if the failure comes back. It is listed in white under CANCELLED CAUTION on the STATUS page (MORE).
All the aural alerts stop (the one sounding and those waiting), and the procedures you called from ABN PROC are removed.
The memo EMERGENCY CANCEL ON shows for 3 seconds.

items: Press and hold RCL for more than 3 seconds.
The cancelled cautions that are still active come back on the EWD with their procedures.

blocks.text: The cancelled cautions are also forgotten when the warning system loses power, or 50 minutes after the engines are shut down, as the other ECAM memories.

items: A cancelled caution never sounds again in the flight, even if the failure comes back: check the STATUS page.
A silenced warning comes back only if it goes away and triggers again.
EMERGENCY CANCEL ON lasts 3 seconds: the FCOM gives no time; 3 s as the RCL "NORMAL" message.
Lift the guard and press EMER CANC on the ECP: it acts on the alert at the top of the EWD.
A warning: its aural and MASTER WARN stop, the procedure stays. A caution: it goes away for the rest of the flight.
Check the cancelled cautions on the STATUS page (MORE, CANCELLED CAUTION).
To get them back, press and hold RCL more than 3 seconds.

children.title: A380X ECP MORE key and light on the STATUS page

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-31-40-10 (STATUS MORE PAGE): the crew displays the STATUS MORE page "if MORE appears at the bottom of the STATUS page, by pressing MORE pb on the ECP"; pressing the pb again clears it (DSC-31-40-20). In FBW the ECP MORE key did nothing: the SD paused and resumed its STATUS page in an order that lost the value telling the FWS that MORE was available, and the MORE pb light read a variable nobody wrote. The STATUS MORE page holds the INOP SYS REDUND items and the CANCELLED CAUTION list (see EMER CANC above).

items: STATUS page with REDUND LOSS items or a cancelled caution: MORE in a box at the bottom of the page.
MORE key pressed: The STATUS MORE page (INOP SYS REDUND, CANCELLED CAUTION); the light of the MORE key comes on.
MORE key pressed again: Back to the STATUS page; the light goes off.
Another SD page selected, or the STATUS page has nothing MORE any more: The MORE page and the light go away.
STATUS page without MORE, or another SD page: The MORE key does nothing (only STATUS has a MORE page in FBW).
Only the STATUS page has a MORE page. Why: The other SD MORE pages are not built in FBW.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update for the light. Why: The MORE key light is in the cockpit behaviour file (ecam-cp.xml). What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Press STS on the ECP.
If MORE shows at the bottom of the STATUS page, press MORE to see the STATUS MORE page.
Press MORE again (or another page key) to leave it.

children.title: FIRE TEST extended after the button release

blocks.text: On the aircraft, the FIRE TEST lasts as long as the button is held. In the simulator, holding the button with the mouse while looking at the ECAM, the master warning and every FIRE and AGENT light is awkward. This option keeps the test running for 7 seconds after you release the button. It is marked unrealistic and is on by default.
Settings > Realism on the A380X: "Extend Fire Test Warnings After Button Release".

head: Aircraft
Test
Kept 7 s after the release
rows: APU, ENG 1 and ENG 2 FIRE TEST pushbuttons
master warning and CRC, ECAM, FIRE pushbutton lights, AGENT / SQUIB DISCH lights, together
the fire detection test itself: FIRE lights, squib lights and the FWS warnings, together

blocks.text: Option off: the test stops the instant you release the button, as on the aircraft.

items: The test starts half a second after you press (A380X), as before.
Pressing again during the 7 seconds starts a new 7 seconds after the next release.
The A380X systems host and fire protection system changed: a full MSFS restart after an update.
flyPad > Settings > Realism: set "Extend Fire Test Warnings After Button Release" ON (the default) or OFF.
Press and release the FIRE TEST pushbutton: with the option ON, check the warnings and lights during the 7 seconds that follow.

children.title: A380X RWY AHEAD without an airport map

blocks.text: While taxiing, the A380 OANS warns the crew before the aircraft enters a runway: RWY AHEAD with the runway name, on the PFD and the ND. In FBW this advisory came from the Navigraph airport map (AMDB): without a Navigraph subscription, or at an airport without a map, it never came. Now, while no airport map is loaded, the OANS uses the runways of the sim's own airport database with the same rule.
The prediction volume: from the nose to 7 seconds ahead at the current ground speed, 60 m wide. When it reaches a runway, RWY AHEAD appears for that runway.

items: On the ground, from 1 to 40 kt.
The advisory stays at most 30 s, and goes when the aircraft is on the runway.
With an airport map loaded, nothing changes: the map is used as before.

blocks.text: The ND advisory: the runway name in a yellow box at the top (here 09-27, when the aircraft taxis south towards runway 09/27). The PFD shows RWY AHEAD too.

items: Taxiing towards a runway, no Navigraph map: RWY AHEAD with the runway name, up to 30 s.
Taxiing towards a runway, with the Navigraph map: RWY AHEAD from the map (as before).
Stopped, or above 40 kt: No advisory.
On the runway: The advisory goes.
Runway rectangles only. Why: The sim database gives each runway as a rectangle (threshold, length, width); displaced thresholds and runway shapes of the airport map are not known.
Shares its runway search with the A32NX RAAS. Why: One runway module (sim airport database) serves both; both are on this branch.
Nothing to set: taxi as usual. Before entering a runway, RWY AHEAD shows on the PFD and the ND with the runway name.
With the Navigraph airport map loaded the advisory comes from the map; without it, from the sim runways.

blocks.text: The OANS draws the airport around the aircraft on the ND. The FCOM (DSC-34-10-70-20, MOVING AIRPORT MAP) says no manual selection is needed: the OANS shows a default airport. FBW loaded the nearest airport on ground, but in flight only the destination (within 50 NM, at any height), and a manual selection stopped the automatic choice for 10 minutes. Now the FCOM rules apply.

head: ND mode
Default airport
rows: The airport where the aircraft is.
The origin, destination or alternate of the FMS while the aircraft is inside its virtual cylinder: 20 NM radius, 5000 ft above the airport. The OANS keeps it while the aircraft stays in the cylinder.
The origin if it is closer than 50 NM, otherwise the destination; the destination when origin and destination are less than 300 NM apart.
Only in PLAN: another airport can be displayed. It stays until the ND leaves PLAN, or the aircraft lands or takes off. In ARC / ROSE-NAV the OANS says SET PLAN MODE.

blocks.text: Each ND has its own OANS and its own airport (see A380X one OANS airport per side below): the rules apply to each ND by itself.
In flight, 12 NM from the destination XTST at 3000 ft: the destination loads by itself (name top right; the arrow points to the airport, still outside the zoom range).
30 NM away at 9000 ft: outside the cylinder, no airport is loaded.
On ground at XTST: the current airport, with the aircraft at its gate.

items: On ground: The airport where you are, whatever the flight plan.
Climbing out of the origin: The origin until you leave its 20 NM / 5000 ft cylinder, then nothing (or the alternate / destination when inside theirs).
Approach to the destination: The destination from 20 NM and 5000 ft above it.
Diversion to the alternate: The alternate from 20 NM and 5000 ft above it.
ARPT SEL in PLAN: Your airport until you leave PLAN, land or take off.
No present position: No automatic airport.
Needs the Navigraph airport database. Why: The OANS map is the Navigraph AMDB. What to do: Link Navigraph in the flyPad.
The Captain and F/O NDs can show different airports. Why: Each side has its own OANS (FCOM DSC-34-10-70-10); see the airport per side below.
The destination arrow (5 NM range, map out of range) is FBW's. Why: Not part of this change.
Set the ND to ARC or ROSE-NAV and turn the range knob to ZOOM: the OANS shows the default airport by itself.
To look at another airport: ND in PLAN, open the OANS ARPT SEL panel, choose the airport. It stays until the ND leaves PLAN, or the aircraft lands or takes off.

children.title: A380X one OANS airport per side

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-70-10: there is a Captain's OANS (ADIRS 1, MMR 1, FMS 1) and a First Officer's OANS (side 2), each shown on its own ND. FBW loaded one airport for both NDs, so an airport chosen on one side replaced the airport of the other. Now each side displays its own airport.

items: Both NDs at ZOOM on the ground: Each OANS shows the current airport (each finds it by itself).
F/O ND in PLAN, another airport chosen with ARPT SEL: The F/O ND shows that airport; the Captain ND keeps its own airport.
PLAN default airport: Follows the mode of that ND only (before, it also looked at the other ND).
RWY AHEAD: Still one advisory for the aircraft, computed by the Captain side OANS: from its airport map when the aircraft is within that airport, else from the sim runways.
An airport unloaded on one side: The BTV runway and exit selection is cleared only if it was made on that side.
The runway crossing and flag events are not split by side. Why: An item of the other side's airport is not found on this side's map.
RWY AHEAD comes from the Captain side only. Why: It is one advisory for the aircraft (one PFD / ND message word).
Use each ND's OANS as usual: ZOOM range for the default airport, PLAN + ARPT SEL for another one.
Each pilot can look at a different airport without changing the other's map.

children.title: Runways around the aircraft: airports with a runway only

blocks.text: The RAAS callouts and the A380X RWY AHEAD without an airport map take their runways from one search of the sim airports around the aircraft (the closest 20 airports within 8 NM). That search took every airport class, so near a city the heliports filled the list: in a sim test at RJTT (25 NM / 24 airports for the VD) only RJTT itself had runways, though three other airports are within 25 NM, and RJTT dropped out of the list a few miles after take-off.

The search now keeps only the airports with a land runway (hard, soft or private) whose longest runway is at least 100 m long: no heliports, no water-only seaplane bases. The same search feeds the A380X VD airports on `core/a380x-vd-runways`.

items: Airports with only runways shorter than 100 m are left out. Why: Design choice: it removes the private heliports the class filter keeps; no runway that matters to RAAS, RWY AHEAD or the VD is that short.
Nothing to set: the RAAS callouts and RWY AHEAD use the new list by themselves.

blocks.text: The A380 has two ISIS (integrated standby instrument systems): the upper one is the Standby Flight Display (SFD: attitude, speed, altitude), the lower one the Standby Navigation Display (SND): heading, position and a small navigation of its own, independent of the FMS (A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-20). On the FBW A380 the lower screen was black; it is now the SND.
The SND: ground speed, heading source IR3, heading rose with the yellow heading index and the green track diamond, aircraft symbol, position from ADIRU 3.

head: Item
Meaning
rows: the heading comes from ADIRU 3 (IR1 when ADIRU 3 has none); TRU in cyan in true reference
240° shown, a mark every 5°, numbers every 30°; white markers at 45° and 90°
the aircraft position (degrees and minutes) and its source

blocks.text: True reference (TRU), no position (PPOS), no ground speed.
No heading from either ADIRU: HDG replaces the rose.

head: Button
Action
rows: SFD/SND reconfiguration: see the feature below
opens the menu under the white line; press again to leave it
turn: next item or value; push: select, or go to the next field
DIR TO (see below); press again to leave it

blocks.text: The SND has its own list of waypoints, entered by coordinates (it has no database). Press MENU: the menu shows INSERT WPT, INSERT FIX, EDIT WPT / FIX and CLEAR WPT / FIX in cyan; turn the knob to choose, push to select.

items: MENU, then push on INSERT WPT: the coordinates show, starting from the last waypoint (or your position).
Turn the knob to change the underlined field, push to go to the next one: N/S, degrees, minutes, tenths, then E/W, degrees, minutes, tenths.
Push on the last field: the waypoint is added at the end of the list.

blocks.text: The menu: INSERT WPT.
Entering the coordinates: the degrees of latitude being set.
EDIT and CLEAR WPT / FIX: turn to choose the waypoint ("2/3 N5015/E00232", then the FIX last), push to edit or to delete it.

items: Press LS/DIR TO. With a list, turn to choose the waypoint and push. Without a list, enter the coordinates of the point as above.
The navigation starts from your position: FROM, TO (white) and NEXT under the line, the bearing and distance to the TO waypoint top right, and the course on the rose.
Passing abeam the TO waypoint, the SND goes on to the next one.

blocks.text: Two waypoints, navigation not active: the true bearing and distance between them.
After DIR TO: FROM / TO / NEXT, TO WPT 342° 126 NM, the course arrow.
About 5 NM right of the track: the deviation bar one large mark left of the aircraft (large marks every 5 NM, small every 2.5 NM).

One point you want to watch (a beacon, an airport): MENU, INSERT FIX, enter its coordinates. The SND shows its distance top left, a magenta pointer towards it on the rose, and its coordinates in magenta at the bottom of the list. A new FIX replaces the old one; EDIT / CLEAR WPT / FIX offer it after the waypoints.
A FIX alone: 291 NM, bearing 060°.
The FIX together with a DIR TO: FROM / TO / NEXT / FIX.

head: Limitation
Why
rows: FBW has no ISIS display failure; the MODE pb reconfigures by hand (see SFD/SND reconfiguration below)
The list is lost when the flight is reloaded
the ISIS keeps it while it runs
the FBW ADIRS has no separate GPS / IRS positions yet
Coordinate entry, 10 waypoints at most, sequencing abeam
the FCOM figures of these procedures stop at the first frame: this is our reading

items: Read heading, track, ground speed and position on the lower ISIS.
Waypoints: MENU, INSERT WPT, set the coordinates with the SET/SEL knob (turn to change, push for the next field).
LS/DIR TO, choose a waypoint and push: the SND guides you there (TO WPT bearing and distance, course, deviation bar).
One point to watch: MENU, INSERT FIX. EDIT / CLEAR WPT / FIX to change the list.
+ / - for the brightness.

blocks.text: The two ISIS of the A380 are the same unit, SFD or SND (A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-20-10). The SFD (upper ISIS) already ran its power-up tests: a yellow INIT box and a countdown for 90 seconds. The SND came on at once. It now behaves as the SFD. The A380 FCOM gives no time: the 90 s and the 10 s below are the ones of the FBW SFD.

items: Cold and dark spawn, first power-up: INIT and the seconds left in a yellow box for 90 s; HDG and PPOS flags meanwhile; then the normal SND.
Spawn with the aircraft powered (runway, cruise...): The SND is on at once, no test.
Power loss: The display stays on for 10 s; power back within 10 s: no new test. Longer: off, and the tests run again at the next power-up.
Power supply: As the SFD: DC ESS bus, or DC HOT 1 above 50 kt.
Nothing to do: after a cold and dark start, wait for the end of INIT (90 s) before using the SND.

children.title: SFD/SND reconfiguration with the MODE pb

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-20-20-10: the MODE pb "enables to switch from SFD to SND display or to switch off the corresponding standby display". Before, MODE only switched the SND off and on. Now each press goes to the next configuration, and one SFD is always displayed. Both ISIS screens carry both displays; the knob and the pushbuttons of an ISIS act on the display it shows.

items: The SND waypoint list, DIR TO and FIX are the same whichever ISIS shows the SND.
On the SFD, the MENU pb opens the BUGS page (the A380 FCOM puts the bugs in the SFD menu); the A320 ATT RST on that pb is gone (not in the A380 FCOM).
No automatic reconfiguration. Why: The FCOM reconfigures automatically on an SFD display failure; FBW has no ISIS display failure. What to do: Use the MODE pb.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The cockpit behaviour files and panel.cfg change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Press MODE on either ISIS to go to the next configuration (swapped, SND off, normal).
Use the knob and the pushbuttons of the ISIS that shows the display you want to work on.

children.title: Normal ISIS configuration at each power-up

blocks.text: The configuration chosen with the MODE pb survived a power cycle: an ISIS could come back swapped or off. The ISIS now start in the normal configuration (upper ISIS SFD, lower ISIS SND) at each power-up. The FCOM (DSC-34-10-20-20-10) says nothing about it: this is a design choice.

items: ISIS off, then powered (they run INIT): Normal configuration, whatever MODE showed before.
Power loss shorter than the 10 s standby: The configuration is kept (not a power-up).
Spawn with the aircraft powered: The configuration is not changed by the spawn.
Nothing to do: after a power-up the ISIS are back to normal; use MODE again if you need another configuration.

children.title: Lights: strobe and beacon timing, interior lighting presets
Strobe double flash and beacon phase

blocks.text: The FCOM gives no flash rates (A320 DSC-33-20-20, A380 DSC-33-30-20); the A380 FCOM only says that the strobes and the beacons alternate. The timing of the real lights comes from the Collins LED light data: a wing strobe double flash of 50 ms on, 60 ms off, 50 ms on, about 60 times a minute, the beacons flashing between the strobes. The FBW effects had a 50 ms gap (A32NX) and a 150 ms gap (A380X) in the double flash, and the A380X beacons flashed too close to the strobes.

head: Light
Before
Now
rows: double flash 50-60-50 ms, 60 per minute (unchanged rate)
double flash 50-60-50 ms, 45 per minute (unchanged rate)
at +0.5 s in a 1.33 s cycle
at +0.67 s: exactly halfway between two strobe flashes
unchanged (beacon already halfway, at +0.5 s in a 1 s cycle)

items: The A380X keeps its 45 flashes per minute. Why: There is no A380 source for the rate; 45 per minute is inside the Collins LED range (45 +/- 2).
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The effect files (.fx) are loaded at sim start. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to set: switch the STROBE and BEACON lights ON on the overhead EXT LT panel as usual.

children.title: Interior lighting presets save and load again

blocks.text: The flyPad interior lighting presets did nothing or the wrong thing on both aircraft, because of three bugs in the C++ extra-backend:

items: No preset was ever saved. The shared ini library refused the existing work folder (it read the mkdir result the wrong way), so every save failed silently and no presets file was written. It now accepts an existing folder. The FADEC fuel configuration save uses the same library and benefits too.

An unsaved row faded every light to off. Loading a row that was never saved left the target values unset, so every light, the PFD, ND, ECAM and MCDU brightness included, faded to 0. Such a row now loads the default preset, all lights at 50 %, as the flyPad page says. The A32NX default also had its DCDU and MCDU values in the wrong scale (0.5 instead of 50).
A load before the first save failed. With no presets file yet (fresh install), a load now gives the default 50 % preset instead of leaving the lights untouched.

A32NX: the dome light came on without its switch. The captain flyPad auto-loads a preset at every power-up, and the preset code set the dome light to 0, 50 or 100 %, while the overhead DOME switch only has OFF (0), DIM (20) and BRT (100): the lamps lit, the switch stayed at OFF, and a preset saved at DIM came back at 50 %. A preset now moves the dome light to the nearest switch position, so the switch follows, and the default preset keeps the dome light off.
Save Preset on a row (aircraft powered): The current lighting levels are stored; the row loads them later, also after a sim restart.
Load Preset on a saved row: The cockpit lights and display brightness fade to the saved levels.
Load Preset on a row never saved: Every light and display brightness fades to 50 %, the A32NX dome light stays off; nothing goes dark.

Automatic loading (Day / Dawn/Dusk / Night set to a row): The selected row loads as above: its saved levels, or the 50 % default if it was never saved. On the A32NX the dome light only comes on when the saved preset had it on.
A32NX DOME switch after a preset load: The switch sits at OFF, DIM or BRT, matching the lamps.
Presets saved before the fix do not exist. Why: No save ever reached the file before. What to do: Save the rows again once.
The aircraft must be powered to save or load. Why: Stock flyPad rule. What to do: Power the aircraft first.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The extra-backend WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Power the aircraft and set the cockpit lights and display brightness as you like.
Open flyPad > Presets, optionally rename a row, and press the Save icon button on it.
Later, press Load on that slot to get the same lighting back.

children.title: Fire warnings and the ENG FIRE pushbutton
A380X: the ENG FIRE pushbutton closes the LP fuel valve

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-28-10 ENGINE LP VALVES: "The ENG MASTER sw control the LP valves. The LP valves automatically close, when their associated ENG FIRE pb is pushed." Pushing an ENG FIRE pushbutton closed no valve, so the engine kept running. The four engines now have the same logic as the A32NX, with a 3 s valve travel.

The A380 FCOM gives no shutdown delay. The fuel left after the valve is the 1 gallon tank the FBW fuel model already has between each LP valve and its engine: the engine stops about 17 s after the pushbutton at a sea-level idle (about 24 s at 14 100 ft).

items: ENG FIRE pushbutton pushed: The engine LP valve closes; the engine shuts down after about 17 s at idle; no start or relight while it is starved.
SD FUEL page: LP valve per FCOM DSC-28-20: green inline = open, amber inline = abnormally open, amber crossline = closed.
ENG MASTER switches: Unchanged: they still open and close their engine valves as before.

A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and FADEC WASM modules, flight_model.cfg and systems.cfg change (new feed valves 60 to 63). What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
In an engine fire, follow the ECAM: ENG MASTER OFF, ENG FIRE pushbutton PUSH.
Check the LP valve of that engine on the SD FUEL page.

children.title: A380X MFD FMS and SURV pages
MFD FMS pages to the reference

blocks.text: Every FMS page of the MFD is laid out on its figure of the A380 FCOM (DSC-22-FMS-20-30, PDF pages 1009 to 1409), the fields accept the FCOM entry formats, and the pages and functions the FCOM describes and FBW did not have are added.

items: Layout: each page is placed on its figure of the A380 FCOM (DSC-22-FMS-20-30, the 2011 KAL FCOM): field positions, 40 px entry fields, 22.5 px labels, 38 px tab bar, the title bar. Where FBW followed a newer FMS standard than this FCOM, the FCOM figure was followed (the WIND page is the exception: it is FlyByWire's own page, see the WIND page feature).
Entry formats: every field accepts the FCOM entry formats (DSC-22-FMS-20-100) and answers with the FCOM messages (FORMAT ERROR, ENTRY OUT OF RANGE, NOT IN DATABASE...).

New pages: ALTERNATE, CLOSEST AIRPORTS, OFFSET, EQUI-TIME POINT, LL XING / TIME MKR, WIND, the POSITION pages, DATA / WAYPOINT, NAVAID, ROUTE, PRINTER, company requests (wind, flight plan, report, takeoff data), TRANSFER TO MAILBOX, REJECTED ATC INFO.
New functions: FUEL PLANNING with CONFIRM BLOCK, LRC and MAX TURB speeds, VERT REV RTA, FMS P/N, pilot-stored elements, automatic airway connection, printing.

blocks.text: The menus at the top of the FMS pages give access to everything: ACTIVE (the active flight plan and its pages), POSITION, SEC INDEX (the secondary flight plans) and DATA.
INIT

INIT: every button is live. CPNY F-PLN REQUEST (flight plan from the airline, i.e. SimBrief), RTE SEL / ALTN RTE SEL (route selection from the stored and company routes), CPNY WIND REQUEST, CPNY T.O. REQUEST, WIND, and the shortcuts IRS, DEPARTURE, NAVAIDS, FUEL&LOAD, T.O. PERF and RTE SUMMARY.

items: Amber boxes are mandatory entries; blue dashes are optional ones.
CPNY RTE: type a stored or company route of the city pair: it is inserted; otherwise NOT IN DATABASE.
RTE SUMMARY stores the active route as a pilot-stored route (DATA / ROUTE).

blocks.text: FUEL&LOAD and FUEL PLANNING
FUEL&LOAD. FUEL PLANNING (next to BLOCK) is available when the flight plan and the weights allow the predictions.

FUEL PLANNING computes the minimum block fuel from the FMS predictions (trip, reserves, alternate, final, taxi) and offers CONFIRM BLOCK, which inserts it (FCOM P 179; see the FUEL PLANNING feature below). The EXTRA line shows what is left above the minimum.
PERF
PERF T.O with the company takeoff data button (the flyPad takeoff calculator that answers it is on `core/efb-performance`).
PERF CRZ: MANAGED, PRESEL, and the LRC and MAX TURB speeds.

items: LRC (long range cruise): the Mach giving 99 % of the maximum specific range (FCOM PER-IFT).
MAX TURB: the recommended speed for flying in turbulence.

blocks.text: F-PLN and its revisions
F-PLN without a flight plan: P.POS, DISCONTINUITY, END OF F-PLN, NO ALTN F-PLN.
Click a waypoint name to open the lateral revision menu, a speed/altitude to open the vertical revision. The new pages below open from these menus or from F-PLN INFO.
ALTERNATE: the selected alternate, the database alternates with their company route, track, distance and EXTRA fuel, and two OTHER ALTN fields.
CLOSEST AIRPORTS: the 4 closest airports from P.POS with distance, bearing, UTC, EFOB and effective wind, and up to three OTHER ARPTs.
OFFSET: start and end waypoints, distance LEFT / RIGHT, intercept angle (30° by default), CANCEL OFFSET.
EQUI-TIME POINT: two reference airports, their cruise wind, and the ETP with its bearing, distance and time.
LL XING / TIME MKR: a waypoint at every LAT or LONG crossing (start, increment, number, INSERT AS WPT); a time marker with remaining time and an aural alert.
VERT REV, RTA tab: time at a waypoint (AT, AT OR BEFORE, AT OR AFTER), ETA and the speed to meet it; the time error thresholds of the FCOM apply.
AIRWAYS: up to 31 segments; typing the next airway after a waypoint connects the two airways automatically at their intersection.
Company requests (flight plan, report)
COMPANY F-PLN REQUEST: flight number, company route, free text.
COMPANY F-PLN REPORT: free text, SEND REPORT TO CPNY.
The company functions use SimBrief (flight plan) and the flyPad (takeoff data). A request without a company able to answer ends after a timeout with the FCOM message.
MONITOR: FMS1/2, RADIO, MIXIRS, GPIRS, IRS and GPS positions, accuracy, EPU and RNP, FREEZE POSITION, BRG / DIST TO.
IRS: alignment, the three IRS with their data, FREEZE ALL IRS.
NAVAIDS: tuned for display (VOR, ADF, LS) and selected for FMS NAV, DESELECT GLIDE.
GPS: both receivers: position, mode, satellites, accuracy, track, UTC, altitude, ground speed.
TIME: UTC, date, flight and block time, OUT / OFF / ON / IN, and PERM DATA SETUP (what the permanent data shows).
REPORT: last, to and next waypoints with time and altitude, the last sequenced waypoint data, the next cruise profile change, destination.
The TIME page is not in the 2011 FCOM; it follows a later FMS standard at the user's request.
SEC INDEX: SEC 1 / 2 / 3, IMPORT, CPNY F-PLN REQUEST into a SEC, the pages of the SEC, DELETE, XFER TO MAILBOX and PRINT.
TRANSFER TO MAILBOX: sends the SEC flight plan to the ATC mailbox with a free text.
REJECTED ATC INFO (FCOM P 321-323) lists the elements of an ATC flight plan inserted in SEC 3 that the FMS rejected, 4 per page. MSFS cannot send an ATC flight plan, so the list stays empty.
STATUS: aircraft and engine, IDLE / PERF factors (FMS P/N tab), navigation database SWAP, and the count of the pilot-stored elements with DELETE ALL.
PRINTER: print the F-PLN INIT, T.O and wind data, the active and SEC flight plan reports, and the AUTO PRINT options.
WAYPOINT: database waypoints by ident; pilot-stored waypoints (lat/long, place/bearing/distance, place-bearing/place-bearing), NEW WPT.
NAVAID: database navaids (class, position, frequency, ILS course and slope...); pilot-stored navaids, NEW NAVAID.
ROUTE: database (company) routes of a city pair, pilot-stored routes with their summary, NEW RTE, DELETE.
AIRPORT: database airports, and the PILOT STORED RWYs tab.
The printouts appear in the flyPad printouts list (see the print feature below).

items: An entry in a wrong format: FORMAT ERROR in the message area; the field keeps its value.
A value out of the FCOM range: ENTRY OUT OF RANGE.
A waypoint or navaid not found: NOT IN DATABASE (or the NEW WPT / NEW NAVAID page when the FCOM says so).
A company request with no company answer: The FCOM timeout message after a few minutes.
A page not available in the flight phase: Its button is greyed.
The layout follows the 2011 A380 FCOM. Why: It is the reference available; later FMS standards differ in places. What to do: Report a difference with its FCOM page.
Some values are FBW model stand-ins. Why: For example GPS satellites and accuracy, like on the A32NX MCDU GPS page; MSFS does not simulate them.
Company functions answer only through SimBrief and the flyPad. Why: There is no airline datalink in MSFS.
Pilot-stored navaids cannot be tuned. Why: The radio tuning uses the MSFS navaids only.
Open the FMS pages with the MFD menus: ACTIVE (F-PLN, PERF, FUEL&LOAD, WIND, INIT), POSITION, SEC INDEX, DATA.
Fill the amber boxes (mandatory) and the blue dashes you need (optional), in the FCOM formats.
Open the flight plan revisions by clicking a waypoint (lateral) or a speed / altitude (vertical) on F-PLN.
Read a wrong entry's message in the message area (FORMAT ERROR gives the expected format), clear it with CLR INFO.

children.title: WIND page: FBW wind page, draft winds, and the fork additions

blocks.text: The WIND page enters, shows and inserts the climb, cruise and descent winds and the alternate trip wind that the FMS uses for its predictions, and loads the winds of the previous flight or of the company. This branch used to carry its own WIND page. FlyByWire has since added a WIND page of its own to the A380X (FlyByWire master 76db0aef1, "wind page", #10929: the page, a new wind model in the flight plan, draft winds, and a company wind request through the ATSU). That page now replaces this branch's own WIND page and its company wind request; the wind model of the flight plan is shared with the A32NX FMS. What this branch adds on top is listed below.

The page is FlyByWire's layout, not the FCOM figure: the other FMS pages of this manual are laid out on the FCOM figures. The FCOM rules (DSC-22-FMS-20-30 WIND pages) are what the additions below follow.

items: Four tabs: HISTORY, CLB, CRZ, DES. A secondary flight plan has no HISTORY tab (history winds are only for the active plan). On the active plan the page opens on the tab of the flight phase: CLB in preflight, takeoff and climb, CRZ in cruise, DES afterwards.

CLB and DES: up to 5 rows of altitude (feet below the transition altitude, flight level above) and wind direction (true) and speed (kt). CRZ: choose the waypoint in the CRZ WIND AT list (or with the two arrow buttons); up to 4 levels per waypoint; an entry copied down the route from an earlier waypoint cannot have its level changed or its direction or speed cleared (NOT ALLOWED). DES also has the ALTN TRIP WIND row, with the ALTN CRZ FL.

Draft winds: adding, changing or deleting a wind creates draft winds: a DRAFT label on the CLB, CRZ and DES tabs and the buttons INSERT WIND* and CANCEL WIND* (amber on the active plan). Draft winds are not used for predictions until inserted (A380 FCOM). Inserting shows DRAFT WIND INSERTED.

HISTORY: the winds of the previous flight, with INSERT HISTORY WIND*, which inserts them directly as the climb winds (no draft) and shows the CLB tab. It is not offered while draft winds or a temporary flight plan exist (FCOM).

Phase rules: the climb winds can be changed only in preflight, the descent winds before the descent phase, and nothing while a temporary flight plan exists; the page then shows the entries as inactive. The cruise winds go inactive after the cruise phase.
Bottom: RETURN (shown only when the page was opened from another page, as the FCOM says), the CPNY WIND REQUEST button, and the draft buttons.
F-PLN: clicking the wind of a waypoint in the F-PLN wind column (or the wind item of the waypoint revision menu) opens the WIND page on the CRZ tab with that waypoint selected.

children.title: What this branch adds on top of the FBW page

head: Addition
Before (FBW page as merged)
Now
rows: The shared flight plan used the A320 rule (FL100 / FL220 / FL310) for the alternate cruise level.
FL220 when the alternate flight plan distance is under 200 NM, FL310 from 200 NM; it cannot be changed. The A32NX keeps its 100 / 220 / 310. The ALTN fuel computation uses the same level.
SAT at the cruise flight level (FCOM)
The SAT row of the CRZ tab was a pair of disabled dummies.

The row shows the cruise flight level of the loaded plan (not editable) and a SAT entry for it (the pilot temperature entry of the plan). It is disabled without a cruise level, while a temporary plan exists, and after the cruise phase of the active plan (INIT then shows the CRZ TEMP as dashes).
Only GND, or an altitude below the airport elevation, gave the ground wind.
GND, or any altitude below 400 ft, is the ground wind (shown as GND).

The CRZ FL of the previous flight and FL 250, FL 150 and FL 050, in this order; the row in the CRZ slot carries the CRZ label and a previous cruise at a fixed level (e.g. FL 250) is listed once with the measured cruise wind. The inserted check compares only the levels that INSERT inserts, so INSERT HISTORY WIND is not offered again after an insertion (a level without wind is listed with dashes and not inserted). The A32NX keeps its list.
History winds kept across the update
The history winds moved to a new storage key, so the winds of the last flight would have been lost.
Winds stored under the old keys are converted and moved once, with directions in 0 to 360 degrees and the measured cruise level in 100 ft steps; the old key is removed.
CPNY WIND REQUEST sent the request directly and was disabled while its own request was pending.

The button opens the COMPANY WIND DATA REQUEST page (free text field, SEND WIND REQUEST*, RETURN), also while the request is pending (then SEND WIND REQUEST reads REQUEST PENDING...). Only a company flight plan uplink in progress disables it. The free text stays on the page: SimBrief, the ground station, has no use for it. The INIT page button works the same.
COMPANY WIND RECIEVED, RECEIVED COMPANY WIND NOT VALID, DRAFT WINDS INSERTED.
COMPANY WIND DATA RECEIVED WAITING FOR INSERTION IN ACTIVE / SEC 1 (2, 3), RECEIVED COMPANY WIND DATA NOT VALID, DRAFT WIND INSERTED.
Reply time, one request per plan, 4 minutes
The answer came at once; REQUEST PENDING... could stay up for ever after a reload of the systems.

Described in the flyPad manual (`core/efb-performance`, company datalink reply time): the flyPad reply time applies to the winds again, NO COMPANY REPLY appears after 4 minutes, and SEND F-PLN REQUEST is blocked while a wind request is pending.
INSERT did nothing when the CLB, CRZ, DES and ALTN drafts all existed.
Every company wind INSERT raised CHECK ALTN WIND: the uplinked alternate wind level (feet) was compared with the default level (a flight level), so FL 310 never matched FL 310.
The levels are compared as flight levels (A380 FCOM, A320 FCOM), for both aircraft.

children.title: Other fixes of the same update

head: Fix
Before
Now
rows: Typed waypoints in VERT REV SPD/ALT CSTR AT and STEP ALTs
A waypoint typed with the keyboard reached the page as "no waypoint": SPD/ALT selected nothing, STEP deleted the step.
The typed waypoint is selected in the list; a text that is not in the list shows NOT IN LIST (as the RTA list does).
The typed ident stayed displayed after NOT IN DATABASE, and CLR only blanked the field.
An unknown ident is refused with the alternate unchanged; NONE or CLR deletes the alternate.
The FMC step was capped at 1 s of sim time: at 8x or 16x sim rate a normal step is 1.6 s or 3.2 s, so guidance and VNAV ran slow.
The cap is 5 s, a jump protection only (pause, sim time jump); the first step stays 0.
Pages on the new base class
Thirteen pages of this branch sat on the older page base class.
They use FBW's new page base class and still refresh (checked in the sim for ALTERNATE, CLOSEST AIRPORTS, DATA / ROUTE and POSITION / REPORT).

items: The SAT is entered for the cruise flight level only. Why: The FCOM propagates the temperature to the down path cruise waypoints like the wind and allows other altitudes; only the cruise level entry is modelled. What to do: Enter the cruise level SAT.
The WIND page is not on the FCOM figure. Why: It is FlyByWire's page, kept as it is to follow its development upstream.

A company wind request has no real operations centre behind it. Why: The answer comes from SimBrief (the OFP of the flyPad account); the free text of the request page is not sent. What to do: Set the SimBrief account in the flyPad.
MFD > FMS > ACTIVE > WIND (or click a wind in the F-PLN wind column).
On CLB, CRZ and DES: type the altitude (or GND) and the wind (direction / speed) on a row; the DRAFT label appears. For cruise winds, choose the waypoint first.
Press INSERT WIND* to use the winds in the predictions, or CANCEL WIND* to drop them.
In preflight, HISTORY > INSERT HISTORY WIND* loads the winds of the previous flight as the climb winds.
CPNY WIND REQUEST asks the company for the winds (SimBrief account set in the flyPad); when the button reads RECEIVED CPNY WIND, click it and choose INSERT* or CLEAR*.

blocks.text: Flight reload only, no restart: no WASM changed.

children.title: FUEL PLANNING: minimum BLOCK computed and confirmed

blocks.text: The FUEL PLANNING button of FUEL&LOAD (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30 P 179) could not be activated and did nothing. It now computes the minimum block fuel and offers CONFIRM BLOCK to enter it.

items: Available before engine start, with a flight plan and a cruise flight level, the ZFW and ZFWCG entered and no BLOCK entered by the crew.

BLOCK = TAXI + TRIP + RTE RSV + MIN FUEL AT DEST. The TRIP comes from the flight plan predictions, which need a fuel on board: they run with a trial BLOCK, replaced by the result until two computations in a row agree within 50 kg (no result after 8 iterations). A prediction is used only when it was computed with the current trial fuel (before, the first prediction still at the VNAV starting estimate of 4000 lb made the BLOCK grow by about 18 t per iteration: CYUL-CYVR 197.9 t instead of about 63 t).
While it runs (about 20 to 30 s, several prediction cycles) the button reads COMPUTING..., greyed. Not in the FCOM: the real FMS computes the BLOCK at once.
The minimum BLOCK shows in yellow next to the BLOCK field and the button becomes CONFIRM BLOCK, which enters it. A BLOCK entry or an engine start ends the fuel planning.
FUEL PLANNING did not react at first: the hidden CONFIRM BLOCK at the same place took the click. Hidden FCOM page elements no longer take clicks (checked on 16 FMS and SURV pages).
A few seconds of COMPUTING... Why: The FBW predictions need a fuel on board, so the BLOCK is found by iteration. What to do: Wait for the yellow value.
The TRIP comes from the FBW VNAV model. Why: It can differ from a SimBrief OFP (the user measured the model lower than SimBrief). What to do: Compare with your OFP.
Before engine start, with the flight plan, cruise FL, ZFW and ZFWCG entered, open ACTIVE > FUEL&LOAD.
Press FUEL PLANNING and wait for the yellow minimum BLOCK.
Press CONFIRM BLOCK to enter it (or type your own BLOCK).

children.title: DEST EFOB before takeoff without the TAXI fuel, ALTN EFOB units

items: Before takeoff the predictions start from the BLOCK, which still holds the TAXI fuel. The DEST EFOB is now BLOCK - TAXI - TRIP, as the FCOM FUEL&LOAD formulas (EXTRA, LW) and the A32NX FMS do. This also corrects the ALTN EFOB, the DEST EFOB BELOW MIN check, the PERF page DEST EFOB and the ALTERNATE page EXTRA.
FUEL&LOAD: the ALTN EFOB in tonnes was set as kilograms (136.3 t displayed 0.1 t).
Nothing to set: read DEST EFOB and ALTN EFOB on FUEL&LOAD as usual.

blocks.text: The block fuel includes the fuel to divert to the alternate. FBW used a fixed 6.5 t, whatever the alternate. The A380 FCOM (DSC-22-FMS-20-30, FUEL&LOAD page) defines the ALTN fuel as the fuel (and time) for the trip from the primary destination to the landing at the alternate, computed with CI 0, at FL220 when the alternate route is shorter than 200 NM and FL310 otherwise. This is what the FMS computes now.
FUEL&LOAD: the ALTN line gets its fuel and its time; the arrival at the alternate (destination + ALTN time) is under ALTN in the UTC column.
ALTERNATE page: the fuel to each alternate (EXTRA column) uses the same computation.

items: The distance is the alternate flight plan distance, without its missed approach; without an alternate route, the direct distance.
The weight is the weight at the destination (ZFW + MIN FUEL AT DEST), with the ALTN wind of the WIND page.
No ZFW: no default ALTN fuel. The value is recomputed only when its inputs change.

blocks.text: Results of the predictor for an alternate close to sea level, fuel on board 12.5 t at the destination (fuel in tonnes / time in minutes / cruise level):

items: At 200 NM the level jumps from FL220 to FL310 (the FCOM rule): the time drops a little, the fuel rises a little.
Short alternates (60-100 NM) fly lower than FL220: the cruise level is lowered until the climb and the descent fit in the distance.
The old fixed value, 6.5 t, is about right only for an alternate 200 NM away.
Climb at climb thrust, cruise, idle descent, with the aircraft's VNAV prediction models (the same as the FMS predictions).
CI 0 speeds of the A380 FMS: 290 kt climb and cruise, 288 kt descent, M0.84, 250 kt below FL100.
No ZFW entered: ALTN fuel shown as dashes (no default).
Alternate route entered: ALTN fuel and time from its distance; the arrival time at the alternate in UTC.
No alternate route, alternate airport set: Computed on the direct distance.
ALTN wind entered: More fuel with a headwind, less with a tailwind.

blocks.text: The FL220 / FL310 rule is the A380 FCOM default alternate cruise level (DSC-22-FMS-20-30). After the FBW WIND page merge the shared flight plan applied the A320 rule (FL100 / FL220 / FL310) to the A380X too: the rule is now a value of the aircraft FMS configuration (A380X FL220 below 200 NM and FL310 from 200 NM; the A32NX keeps its 100 / 220 / 310). The same level is shown as ALTN CRZ FL on the WIND page.

items: One mean wind for the alternate trip. Why: The FCOM computation uses the ALTN wind of the WIND page.
No holding or approach fuel in ALTN. Why: The FCOM definition ends at the landing at the alternate; FINAL covers the reserve.
Enter the ZFW and an alternate (INIT ALTN, or an alternate route), and the ALTN wind on the WIND page if known.
Read the ALTN fuel and time on FUEL&LOAD; the arrival time at the alternate is under ALTN in the UTC column.

children.title: EXTRA time and the FINAL holding fuel flow

blocks.text: The EXTRA time next to the EXTRA fuel (FCOM: the fuel, and time, that remains after landing at the destination, minus the MIN FUEL AT DEST) was never computed and always showed --:--. It is now the time the EXTRA fuel lasts at the holding fuel flow of the FINAL fuel default, 0.2 t/min (30 min = 6 t): 7.4 t of EXTRA shows 00:37, 12.0 t shows 01:00.
FUEL&LOAD with 7.4 t of EXTRA fuel: EXTRA time 00:37. The harness has no flight plan, so the EXTRA fuel is set by hand for this picture; the other values stay as dashes.

items: The FCOM leaves the FINAL default to the airline fuel policy (AMI file) and gives no rule to turn the EXTRA fuel into a time: the same holding flow keeps FINAL and EXTRA consistent on the page.
No EXTRA fuel (no flight plan predictions, or a SEC flight plan): --:--, as the fuel.

blocks.text: The 0.2 t/min holding flow is now one named constant used by both the FINAL fuel default (30 min = 6 t) and the EXTRA time.
On `core/fuel` (stacked on this branch) the FINAL default and the EXTRA time use the A380 holding fuel flow at the ZFW instead of the fixed 0.2 t/min.

items: EXTRA fuel shown: EXTRA time = EXTRA fuel at 0.2 t/min (6 t = 30 min).
EXTRA time at a fixed holding flow. Why: The FCOM gives no fuel-to-time rule for EXTRA; the flow is the FINAL default one, not a computed holding at the actual weight.
Read the EXTRA time next to the EXTRA fuel on FUEL&LOAD.

children.title: Fuel figures of the company flight plan
Fuel figures of the company flight plan

blocks.text: Before engine start, performance data come with the company flight plan (FCOM COMPANY F-PLN REQUEST). When the flight plan received from SimBrief is inserted (INIT CPNY F-PLN REQUEST, then INSERT), FUEL&LOAD takes from the OFP, as if typed by the crew: TAXI, RTE RSV (the OFP contingency, the % is cleared), ALTN (only with an alternate) and FINAL (the OFP final reserve).

items: The BLOCK is not taken: press FUEL PLANNING, which computes it from these figures and the FMS TRIP.
After engine start the flight plan comes in without its fuel figures.
The FINAL time is computed from the FINAL fuel at 0.2 t/min (4.8 t shows 00:24).
Any value can be overwritten as usual.
Company flight plan inserted before engine start: TAXI, RTE RSV, ALTN and FINAL from the OFP; BLOCK empty until FUEL PLANNING or an entry.
Set your SimBrief account in the flyPad and generate the OFP.
Before engine start: INIT > CPNY F-PLN REQUEST, then INSERT the received flight plan.
Check TAXI, RTE RSV, ALTN and FINAL on FUEL&LOAD, then press FUEL PLANNING for the BLOCK.

children.title: FMS print functions and the flyPad printouts

blocks.text: The DATA / PRINTER page and the SEC INDEX PRINT button work (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-70, DSC-22-FMS-20-30 P 74-77). The FMS prints the active flight plan initialization, takeoff and wind data, and the pre-flight, in-flight, post-flight and secondary flight plan reports, laid out as the FCOM printout examples, with dashes for data the FMS does not have.

DATA / PRINTER: ACTIVE DATA and CPNY DATA (F-PLN INIT, T.O DATA, WIND DATA), AUTO PRINT ON RECEPTION, the ACTIVE F-PLN REPORT (PRE-FLIGHT, IN-FLIGHT, POST-FLIGHT) with AUTO PRINT, and the SEC F-PLN REPORT.

head: Print
Available (FCOM)
Automatic print (AUTO PRINT ticked)
rows: In PREFLIGHT, with the flight plan data entered

items: On this branch the printed pages go to the flyPad: Dispatch > Printouts (A380X only), which keeps the last 30 pages. A page appears there without any notification. With `core/printer` they also come out of the pedestal printer.
The pages travel on the event bus, synced between the instruments (a view listener trigger did not cross instruments, so the first version never reached the flyPad).
The AUTO PRINT checkboxes are clickable (they did not react before).
MFD > DATA > PRINTER: press the PRINT* button of the data or report you want.
Tick the AUTO PRINT boxes for the automatic reports.
Read the pages on the flyPad: Dispatch > Printouts.

blocks.text: On the A380 the crew can store its own waypoints, navaids, routes and runways in the FMS (DATA pages). The FCOM says they are all deleted when all FMCs are shut down (DSC-22-FMS), and that is what happens by default: a new flight starts with an empty list.

In the simulator you may want to keep them from one session to the next (your own departure procedures, a favourite route). The setting below does that. It is marked Unrealistic because the real aircraft does not keep them.
flyPad > Settings > Realism: the last line. Off by default.

items: Off (default, as the FCOM): the stored elements are deleted at the end of the session.
On: they are saved in the simulator storage and restored at the next session, before the FMS loads them.
A reload of the flight (same session) never restores them twice.
Turning the setting off drops the kept copy: the next session starts empty.
The A380 OIT flyPad has the same option.

blocks.text: The DATA menu pages have a PILOT STORED tab each. The DATA / STATUS page counts them and DELETE ALL clears everything.
DATA / STATUS: PILOT STORED ELEMENTS: 2 waypoints, 2 navaids, 1 route, 2 runways.
PILOT STORED WPTs: GOUGOU, defined by place/bearing - place/bearing (AGN 123° / GAI 250°), 1/2.
PILOT STORED NAVAIDS: an ILS with its class, position, elevation, runway, frequency, category, course and figure of merit.
PILOT STORED RTEs: NEWROUTE LFBO to WSSS with its summary (runway, SID, airways and waypoints).
PILOT STORED RWYs (DATA / AIRPORT): runway 15R of LFFF with its position, elevation, length, course and LS ident.
Limits of the database (FCOM)

head: Element
Limit
When full
rows: The first one created is deleted.
The first one created is deleted.
The oldest one not used in a flight plan is replaced; if all are used: 50 WPTS MAX : ALL IN USE (see the next feature).

blocks.text: Storing an element with the name of an existing one replaces it (no duplicates).

items: Setting off, new session: DATA / STATUS shows 00 everywhere.
Setting on, new session: The elements of the last session are back.
Setting on, flight reloaded: The elements are there once (no duplicates).
Setting turned off: The kept copy is deleted; the current elements stay until the end of the session.
Stored route of another city pair: Not offered in INIT / RTE SEL (routes are per city pair).
Pilot-stored navaids cannot be tuned. Why: The radio tuning uses the MSFS navaids only.
Keeping the elements is not realistic. Why: The real FMS deletes them at shutdown. What to do: Leave the setting off for realism.
flyPad > Settings > Realism: turn on Keep MFD Pilot Stored Waypoints, Navaids, Routes and Runways Between Sessions (off by default, as the FCOM).
Store your elements on the MFD DATA pages (WAYPOINT, NAVAID, ROUTE, AIRPORT > PILOT STORED RWYs).
At the next session they are back; DATA / STATUS counts them, DELETE ALL clears them.

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30 (P 117) and DSC-22-FMS-10-40-10: the FMS stores 50 pilot-defined waypoints. FBW shared the A32NX list of 99 and its LIST OF 99 IN USE message.
