items: When the 50 are stored, a new one replaces the oldest waypoint not used in a flight plan (active, temporary or secondary).
When all 50 are used in flight plans, the new entry is rejected with 50 WPTS MAX : ALL IN USE (FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-110).
The A32NX keeps its 99 waypoints (same flight plan code, its own limit).
Store waypoints as usual (DATA > WAYPOINT > NEW WPT, or the places you create in the flight plan).
Watch the count on DATA / STATUS; the oldest unused one is replaced from the 51st on.

children.title: DIRECT TO options: ABEAM, CRS IN, CRS OUT

blocks.text: The DIRECT TO page of the A380 (FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30, DIRECT TO) has four options. FBW showed them but only the first one worked. All four work now:

head: Option
What the FMS builds
rows: A direct leg from the aircraft to the target waypoint (as before).
The direct leg, plus an abeam point for each waypoint it bypasses: the point of the direct leg abeam that waypoint, named AB + the first 5 letters of the waypoint (BERGI gives ABBERGI).
An inbound course to the target: the aircraft continues on its current track to the intercept point INTCPT on that course, then flies the course to the target.
An outbound course from the target: the aircraft continues on its current track to the intercept point INTCPT on the outbound course, then follows it (without overflying the target).

blocks.text: The three new options. Yellow: the aircraft and its path to the first point; green: the course flown after it; blue: the points the FMS creates.

items: Choose the target in DIRECT TO (a flight plan waypoint from the list, or type any fix).
Choose the option. For CRS IN / CRS OUT a course field appears next to the option.

For a flight plan waypoint the course is already filled: CRS IN = the course from the previous waypoint to the target, CRS OUT = the course from the target to the next waypoint (FCOM P 131). Type another one if ATC asks (NNN magnetic, NNNT true).
Check the temporary flight plan (TMPY, yellow) and press INSERT DIR TO.

blocks.text: The DIRECT TO page: target, UTC and distance, and the four OPTIONS.
CRS IN selected: the course field (amber boxes until a course is known).
With DIRECT WITH ABEAM, the temporary F-PLN shows (ABEAM PTS) in place of the abeam points until the direct is inserted (FCOM P 162).

items: DIRECT WITH ABEAM, waypoints bypassed: One ABxxxxx point per bypassed waypoint, on the direct leg.
DIRECT WITH ABEAM, a waypoint whose abeam is not between the aircraft and the target: No abeam point for it.
CRS IN / OUT with a course that can be intercepted ahead: INTCPT on the course, then the course.
CRS IN more than 160° from the current track, parallel, or behind: No intercept point: a course to the target.
CRS OUT parallel to the track: No intercept point: a course from the target.
CRS IN / OUT without a course: No DIR TO until a course is entered.
Abeam point names can repeat letters of the waypoint. Why: The FCOM rule is AB + 5 characters; two waypoints starting with the same 5 letters give the same name.
No intercept point when the geometry does not allow one. Why: Following the FCOM limits (160°, parallel, behind). What to do: Use DIRECT, or another course.

blocks.text: The intercept limits are named constants of the flight plan code (no other effect).

items: F-PLN > DIR TO: choose the target waypoint.
Choose DIRECT, DIRECT WITH ABEAM, CRS IN or CRS OUT; for CRS IN / OUT check or type the course (NNN or NNNT).
Check the yellow TMPY flight plan and press INSERT DIR TO.

children.title: KCCU keyboard entries: ENT validates, ESC cancels

blocks.text: On the A380 the crew types on the KCCU keyboard. Before this change a value typed on the 3D KCCU keys was often lost: the field was validated only when the display lost the focus, and clicking a 3D key ends the focus before the key reaches the field. Now the field follows the FCOM (DSC-31-30-20, KCCU):

items: ENT validates the entry directly.
ESC "cancels the current field edition. The field returns to the last valid value".

Once a field is selected with the cursor, the edition continues whatever happens to the display focus and whatever the KBD switch: only ENT, ESC or the selection of another field end it (the previous field is then validated). One field is in edition per side.
A click on a field selects it even when it already had the focus.
KBD switch OFF: the KCCU keyboard keys are not active (see the KCCU switches feature below); the PC keyboard still types in the selected field.
Set the KBD switch of your KCCU ON.
Click the field with the cursor (trackball or mouse).
Type the value on the KCCU keys (or the PC keyboard).
Press ENT. The value is checked with the FCOM entry format of the field.

blocks.text: TROPO selected, 39000 typed on the KCCU keys.
After ENT: TROPO 39000 FT entered (big cyan: a pilot entry).
ENT on a wrong value leaves the field unchanged and shows the FCOM message in the message area; the message gives the expected format. CLR INFO (KCCU key) clears it.
"ABC" in TROPO: FORMAT ERROR, FORMAT: FOR ALT XXXXX FOR FL XXX.
99999 in TROPO: ENTRY OUT OF RANGE.
41000 typed in TROPO, not validated...
... ESC: the field returns to its last valid value, 39000.

items: Value typed, ENT: The value is entered (or an FCOM error message).
Value typed, ESC: The field returns to its last valid value.
Value typed, another field clicked: The first value is validated, the new field is in edition.
Value typed, click on a 3D KCCU key or elsewhere in the cockpit: The field stays in edition, the value is not lost.
KBD switch OFF: The KCCU keyboard keys do nothing; the PC keyboard still types in the selected field, which stays in edition until ENT, ESC or another field.
One field in edition per side. Why: As on the aircraft: each KCCU drives its own side.
Click the field with the cursor (trackball or mouse).
Type on the KCCU keys (KBD switch ON) or the PC keyboard.
Press ENT to enter, or ESC to go back to the last valid value.

children.title: KCCU KBD and CCD switches: reference rules, ON by default

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-31-30-20: the keyboard and the cursor control device of each KCCU have their own ON/OFF switch ("The KCCU keyboard is not active" when OFF), independent of each other.

items: The keyboard keys work only with the KBD switch ON; the cursor control device keys (ESC2, KBD, REWIND, FORWARD) only with the CCD switch ON. Both the MFD and the ND follow this.

An entry field clicked with the mouse keeps the keyboard input until ENT or ESC whatever the KBD switch, so typing cannot land in another field; a field that disappears ends its edition. The 20 s unfocus timer and the end of edition on a display blur are removed.

Both switches are ON in every flight start (hangar, apron, taxi, runway, climb, cruise, approach, final) and the cold and dark preset no longer turns them off. The FCOM sets them ON during the preliminary cockpit preparation (PRO-NOR-SOP): ON by default is a convenience.
Leave the KBD and CCD switches ON (default). Set KBD OFF to stop the KCCU keyboard, CCD OFF to stop the cursor device keys.

children.title: SURV pages laid out and wired per the reference

blocks.text: The SURV CONTROLS and STATUS & SWITCHING pages are laid out on their figures (A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-60-50 P 4 and P 6): area frames, 120 x 78 SURV buttons, the WXR and GPWS link lines, the SURV DEFAULT SETTINGS group, and SYS boxes that no longer run off the right of the screen. The options follow the FCOM rules of the XPDR, TCAS, WXR and TAWS sections (DSC-34-20-40, -50, -30-20, -10).

head: Item
Rule
rows: Option list AUTO / ON / STBY; ON keeps the transponder replying as in flight on the ground.
ALT RPTG OFF or XPDR STBY
The TCAS option lists are not available.
Needs a confirmation. AUTO resets PRED W/S, TURB, ELEVN/TILT, GAIN, MODE and WX ON VD; OFF sets PRED W/S, TURB and WX ON VD to OFF, inhibits them and hides GAIN and MODE.
Option list (not available in MAP) with an ELEVN field (FL with the STD reference, FT with QNH: FL 0 to 600, 0 to 60 000 ft) and a TILT field (±NN.N, M for minus, -15.0 to +15.0 degrees).
Entry field with GAIN MAN: 0 to 100 %.
The FCOM indication texts: WX DISPLAY, and XPDR / TCAS STBY when the system is not in use.

items: The ELEVN, TILT and GAIN values do not change the radar picture. Why: They are stored in new documented LVars (A380X_WXR_ELEVN_TILT_MODE, A380X_WXR_ELEVN, A380X_WXR_TILT, A380X_WXR_GAIN); the MSFS radar has no gain and the native radar does not use them. What to do: The ND messages for them are on `core/a380x-wxr-controls`.
MFD > SURV > CONTROLS: choose the options in their lists; confirm the WXR and DEFAULT SETTINGS buttons.
For a manual radar setting, choose ELEVN or TILT and type the value, or GAIN MAN and the gain.

children.title: SURV memos, and TCAS STBY with ALT RPTG OFF

blocks.text: The ECAM follows the SURV CONTROLS page as in the A380 FCOM (DSC-34-20-60-140, flight phase inhibitions from its figures).

head: Memo
When
rows: TERR SYS OFF on SURV CONTROLS.
The TAWS of the selected system is operative, but the TERR function cannot rely on the aircraft position, which the TAWS takes from ADIRU 1 (DSC-34-20-20-10).
WXR button OFF. It also sets PRED W/S and TURB to OFF: only WXR OFF shows then.
PRED W/S OFF by the crew: green in flight phases 2 and 8, amber in the takeoff and landing phases (the colours of the A320 PRED W/S OFF memo).
On the ground, one engine running, WX selected on an EFIS CP and the WXR not OFF or failed: the WX pb turns the WXR on (DSC-34-20-30-20 P 1).
ALT RPTG OFF puts the TCAS in standby (DSC-34-20-50-20 P 7): also TCAS STBY on the ND and, in cruise, the SURV TCAS STBY caution (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-34-20 P 18).

items: Nothing to set: the memos follow the SURV CONTROLS settings. Restore the normal settings (WXR AUTO, TERR SYS ON, ALT RPTG ON) to clear them.

children.title: FMS function fixes: SEC pages, received company winds, FIX INFO, STORE WPT, RTE SEL

head: Fix
Before
Now
rows: SEC page kept when another flight plan is created

A page opened for an empty SEC (e.g. its COMPANY F-PLN REQUEST) jumped to the ACTIVE copy as soon as any flight plan was created; RETURN had to be clicked twice and the page was bound to the active flight plan.
The page moves to ACTIVE only when its loaded SEC flight plan is deleted.
One asterisk on SEND F-PLN REQUEST
One, on the right, as the FCOM figure (DSC-22-FMS-20-30 P 28).
Received company winds kept until INSERT
WIND INSERT did nothing after a flight plan revision: a flight plan copy (revision, temporary plan inserted) lost the received winds.
The received winds stay pending across copies until the crew inserts or clears them (A32NX and A380X). The request and the answer path are now FlyByWire's (see the WIND page feature).
An unknown ident opened NEW WAYPOINT.
Looked up only (database and pilot-stored elements): an unknown ident gives NOT IN DATABASE; FIX INFO never creates or stores a waypoint (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS FIX INFO).
Stayed inactive (the waypoint was worked out before the last value was stored).
Active as soon as the entries define the waypoint.
Did not always open ROUTE SELECTION.
Always opens the ROUTE SELECTION page; only the route entries are limited (FCOM P 199-200).

items: Nothing new to learn: use the pages as described in the FCOM; the fixes remove the wrong behaviours above.

children.title: MFD display fixes: sizes, labels, menus and clickable controls

items: FCOM sizes in the sim: the cockpit renderer counts padding and frame in a box size, so the buttons were 28 px narrower and 18 px lower than the FCOM figures and labels ran out. Buttons now have the full FCOM size as a minimum and grow around their label; labels keep the lines of the FCOM figure, 26 px apart (a one-line button is 44 px high); entry fields and selection lists are 44 px high, without a background painted over their frame. The AIRWAYS list and the RECEIVED COMPANY T.O DATA INSERT / CLEAR buttons moved to make room.
Button labels that change (REQUEST PENDING..., RECEIVED CPNY WIND, FREEZE / UNFREEZE...) showed a raw "‹br />": they now use line breaks.
Selection menus that would leave the screen at the bottom (NEW RTE on DATA / ROUTE lost SEC 3) open upwards.
F-PLN EFOB / T.WIND: the wind digits no longer run over the slash.

Clicks: a hidden FCOM page element no longer takes the clicks of the visible one; the DATA / PRINTER AUTO PRINT checkboxes, the POSITION / NAVAIDS ADF BFO toggle and the LL XING / TIME MKR AURAL checkboxes react (an onClick on a plain element never fired).
DATA / NAVAID search: written without an await used as an operand, which the sim's JavaScript engine can reject and blank the whole MFD. Same behaviour.
Code clean-up with no visible effect: shared FREE TEXT controls of the company pages, one tonnes helper on FUEL&LOAD, a test set-up fix for Node 22 and later, typing fixes.
Nothing to set: the pages look and react as the FCOM figures.

children.title: PLACE/DIST waypoints, HOLD at PPOS, DIR TO radials, OPT FL, EOSID, PRED TO

blocks.text: Flight planning functions that the FCOM describes and the FMS did not have (or had wrong), found by the FCOM gap audit. The flight plan code is shared, so both aircraft get the common parts:

items: PLACE/DIST waypoints (both): a waypoint at a distance along the flight plan path after a flight plan waypoint, or before it with a negative distance (for example `LMG/-15`). It is created as a pilot waypoint PDnn on the path, without a discontinuity. A32NX: on the MCDU F-PLN page and as LAT REV NEXT WPT (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20 F-PLN and LAT REV pages). A380X: in INSERT NEXT WPT of the revised waypoint; a place that is not the revised waypoint gives PLACE / WPT DISAGREE, a distance beyond the neighbouring waypoint ENTRY OUT OF RANGE (A380 FCOM, F-PLN revisions, INSERT NEXT WPT).

HOLD at the present position (both): the HOLD revision of the FROM waypoint (PPOS) creates a T-P and a computed hold at the present position, on the aircraft track. Before, the A32NX put the hold at the waypoint behind the aircraft, and on the A380X the item was greyed out.
A32NX DIR TO page: ABEAM PTS, RADIAL IN (the default inbound radial of a flight plan waypoint is proposed) and RADIAL OUT build the DIR TO temporary flight plan instead of NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

A32NX PROG OPT FL: the best specific range level for the gross weight, from the FCOM long range cruise ISA tables (PER-CRZ-CRT-30), never above REC MAX; dashes with an engine out. Before, it was REC MAX rounded down.
A380X PERF CLB and DES tabs: the time and distance to the PRED TO altitude instead of dashes.

A380X EOSID: the DEPARTURE page shows the engine-out SID of the runway; an engine failure in the takeoff phase below the thrust reduction altitude creates the EOSID temporary flight plan (A380 FCOM, engine failure at takeoff, EOSID).

Code fix with no visible effect today: the remote flight plan client erases the EOSID (it activated it) and sends the manual hold default in the right argument. No production code uses that client yet (specs only).
A32NX: type `LMG/-15` on the F-PLN page at a waypoint (or as LAT REV NEXT WPT): A waypoint PD01 (then PD02...) on the path 15 NM before LMG, no discontinuity.
A380X: INSERT NEXT WPT of waypoint X, entry `X/10`: A PDnn waypoint 10 NM after X on the path.
A380X: INSERT NEXT WPT of X, entry `Y/10` (another place): PLACE / WPT DISAGREE.
A380X: distance beyond the next (or previous) waypoint: ENTRY OUT OF RANGE.
HOLD revision of the FROM waypoint, in flight: T-P and a hold at the present position on the aircraft track (TMPY first).
A380X engine failure in the takeoff phase below the thrust reduction altitude, EOSID on the DEPARTURE page: The EOSID temporary flight plan is created; the crew inserts it or not.
A32NX with an engine out: PROG OPT FL shows dashes.
A380X OPT FL and EO MAX FL are not computed. Why: No source data for the A380 (no table found).
The A32NX OPT FL table is for the PW engines. Why: The closest data of the FCOM long range cruise tables.
PLACE/DIST is not accepted on DIR TO or for the STEP ALTs. Why: Left for later. What to do: Create the PDnn waypoint on the F-PLN first.
No A32NX DCDU LOAD of route clearances; the A32NX DIR TO page has the older layout (not the 2012 one). Why: Left for later.

PLACE/DIST: A32NX, type `PLACE/DIST` (for example `LMG/-15`) in the scratchpad and press the left key of the waypoint on the F-PLN page, or use LAT REV > NEXT WPT; A380X, F-PLN > waypoint revision > INSERT NEXT WPT, type `‹that waypoint>/DIST`.
HOLD at PPOS: LAT REV (A32NX) or the revision menu (A380X) of the FROM waypoint > HOLD; check the hold and insert the temporary flight plan.
A32NX DIR TO: choose the waypoint, then ABEAM PTS, RADIAL IN or RADIAL OUT (type the radial if needed), then INSERT.
A380X EOSID: check the EOSID on the DEPARTURE page before takeoff; after an engine failure below the thrust reduction altitude, review the temporary flight plan and insert it.
A380X PRED TO: PERF > CLB or DES tab, type the altitude in PRED TO; read the time and distance.
HOLD at PPOS on both aircraft (where the hold is drawn and flown).
PLACE/DIST entries (positive and negative distances, the PDnn names, the A380X error messages).
The A32NX DIR TO radial and abeam temporary flight plans.
The A380X EOSID after an engine failure below the thrust reduction altitude.
The A380X PERF CLB/DES predictions to the PRED TO altitude.
None of this is sim-tested yet.

children.title: ATC COM pages and the SD mailbox

blocks.text: The A380 talks to ATC by datalink: the crew logs on to a center, sends requests and reports, receives clearances and answers them, and gets the airport ATIS as text. The FCOM describes the MFD ATC COM pages (DSC-46-10-20-30) and the SD MAILBOX (DSC-46-10-10-70). They are all built on their FCOM figures and connected to the FBW ATSU, the same datalink system as the A32NX DCDU.
The network is chosen in the flyPad: Settings > ATSU / AOC (Hoppie, BeyondATC or SayIntentions). The datalink needs VHF3 in DATA mode on the RMP.

head: Page (header)
Use
rows: Logon (NOTIFICATION), CONNECTION STATUS with ADS, MAX UPLINK DELAY.
Build a request from frames (climb, direct, offset, weather deviation, speed, clearances...) and send it to the mailbox.
Position report, other reports, modify a prepared answer.
The record of the closed dialogues.
Request and read the ATIS of three airports.
MAYDAY / PANPAN and the emergency reports.

items: CONNECT > NOTIFICATION: type the ATC CENTER (4 letters) and press NOTIFY. The page shows NOTIFYING, then the center in NOTIFIED TO CENTERS (with the time), or NOTIFICATION FAILED.
When ATC accepts, CONNECTION STATUS shows the ACTIVE ATC (and the NEXT ATC after a transfer). DISCONNECT ends the connection.

blocks.text: CONNECT / NOTIFICATION.
CONNECTION STATUS: active and next ATC, ADS ARMED / OFF, ADS EMERGENCY.
MAX UPLINK DELAY: NONE, or a delay set on the demand of the active ATC.

items: Open the menus on the right (VERTICAL, LATERAL, SPEED, CLEARANCE, WHEN CAN WE EXPECT, OTHER) and pick the frames you need; up to 5 frames, each with its fields.
Fill the fields (FCOM entry formats; amber boxes are mandatory). ADD TEXT adds free text. The bin deletes a frame.
Press XFR TO MAILBOX: the request goes to the SD mailbox, where you SEND it.

blocks.text: A request of 5 frames: DIR TO TADEX, CLB TO FL360, OFFSET (amber: to fill), free text, DUE TO WEATHER.
CLEARANCE > DEPARTURE: the departure clearance request (DCL): departure airport, destination, gate, aircraft type, ATIS code.

AUTO & MANUAL POSITION: the position report filled by the FMS (overhead, present position, to, next, times, levels, speeds, wind, SAT, ETA, endurance); AUTO POSITION REPORT ON sends it at each reporting point.
OTHER REPORTS: back on route, passing position, leaving / reaching altitude, level, reaching block, free text.
MODIFY: a prepared answer (here PRESENT ALTITUDE 12500 FT) that the crew can change before sending.
Every message to and from ATC goes through the mailbox at the bottom of the SD. It shows the active ATC, the ADS status, the message and the answer buttons the message expects.
Mailbox without a message: ACTIVE ATC LFBO, ADS OFF.
An uplink: CLIMB TO REACH FL340 BY BERGI, OPEN, with WILCO / STANDBY / UNABLE. MSG 1/3: three messages are waiting.
A request ready to go: SEND or CANCEL.
UNABLE and NEGATIVE can add a reason (DUE TO WEATHER, A/C PERFORMANCE, TURBULENCE) and free text; MODIFY opens the answer on the MFD. The message colours follow the FCOM status legend.
MSG RECORD: the closed dialogues with their time and the answer given; ZOOM shows one in full; ERASE ALL, PRINT ALL.
ATIS: three request areas (departure, arrival, alternate, following the FMS airports), each with its ATIS text, AUTO UPDATE, and SEND REQUEST / SEND AGAIN.
ATIS RECEIVED: the full text of an ATIS, RETURN TO LIST.

EMERGENCY (orange title): MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY frame, PANPAN, CANCEL EMER and the emergency reports (climbing / descending to, diverting, offsetting, voice contact, endurance and souls). MAYDAY also switches the ADS to EMERGENCY.

items: NOTIFY with no network set: NOTIFICATION FAILED.
Request with an empty mandatory field: XFR TO MAILBOX stays greyed.
Uplink received: Mailbox message with its answer buttons.
Answer sent: The dialogue closes and goes to MSG RECORD.
ATIS requested: The text appears in its area; a newer version replaces it (AUTO UPDATE).
MAYDAY sent: ADS EMERGENCY ON.
Needs an online datalink network. Why: ATC messages come from Hoppie, BeyondATC or SayIntentions through the flyPad ATSU settings. What to do: Set the network in the flyPad.
No real ADS contracts. Why: The ATSU networks do not handle ADS-C; ADS ARMED / EMERGENCY is shown locally.
On this branch alone, every ATC COM PRINT says PRINTER NOT AVAIL. Why: Printing (ATIS, MSG RECORD, mailbox) is on `core/printer`, which builds on this branch.

Answering the uplinks of a live controller is not recorded as tested. Why: Tested in the sim: logon, MAYDAY and PAN PAN PAN downlinks, the ATIS, a route clearance uplink (LOAD-SEC3). The answer buttons were checked with harness messages. What to do: Report any wrong answer element.

blocks.text: The A380X README (list of what is not implemented, ATC / datalink line) now says that the MFD ATC COM pages and the SD mailbox work through the FBW ATSU and its ACARS providers, and that the datalink functions outside those pages are not implemented.

items: Set the network in the flyPad (Settings > ATSU / AOC), VHF3 in DATA mode on the RMP, and your network callsign as FLT NBR on the MFD FMS INIT page.
MFD system menu > ATC COM > CONNECT > NOTIFICATION: type the ATC CENTER and press NOTIFY.
To ask ATC: REQUEST, pick the frames, fill them, XFR TO MAILBOX, then SEND in the SD mailbox.
To answer ATC: use the buttons of the message in the SD mailbox (WILCO / UNABLE, AFFIRM / NEGATIVE, ROGER...).
For the ATIS: ATIS page, airport of the request area, SEND REQUEST; tick AUTO UPDATE to get the new versions.
In an emergency: EMER, MAYDAY or PANPAN frame, XFR TO MAILBOX, SEND.

children.title: Datalink connection with the flight number, and SEND FAILED

blocks.text: The INIT page FLT NBR field wrote the flight plan only: the field did not refresh and the entry never connected the datalink networks (FBW TELEX and the ACARS provider), so ATC logons and downlinks failed. And a message sent from the mailbox with no ATC center was dropped without a word. Now the FMS connects the networks whenever the flight number of the active flight plan changes, and the mailbox says SEND FAILED (A380 FCOM DSC-46-10-20-60).

The ATC COM pages send and receive through the aircraft datalink, which connects with the flight number of the active flight plan (FMS INIT, FLT NBR). It must be your callsign on the network (Hoppie, BeyondATC or SayIntentions: the one set in the flyPad, Settings > ATSU / AOC).

items: The flight number connects the datalink however it gets there: typed on the INIT page, from the company flight plan (SimBrief), from an activated secondary flight plan, or already there when you reload the flight.

If the connection is refused, or the datalink does not answer, the FMS message area shows FMS DATALINK NOT AVAIL (white). It goes away by itself once connected; typing the flight number again tries again.
A message sent from the mailbox with no ATC center connected (no logon done, or the center logged you off) shows SEND FAILED instead of nothing.

blocks.text: SEND FAILED under a message the mailbox could not send (no active ATC center).

With BeyondATC: log on to the center shown in its Frequencies tab (e.g. RJJJ), above FL145. BeyondATC does not handle MAYDAY or PAN PAN by datalink: it answers NO MESSAGE HANDLING AVAILABLE FOR THIS REQUEST. Declare an emergency by voice with it.

items: Enter the flight number on the MFD FMS INIT page (FLT NBR), or get it with the company flight plan. It must be your callsign on the network.
If FMS DATALINK NOT AVAIL shows, check the ACARS provider, then type the flight number again to retry.
Log on (ATC COM > CONNECT) before sending: without an active ATC the mailbox says SEND FAILED.

blocks.text: The ATC and company datalink of the aircraft (CPDLC logon, requests, messages, ATIS and METAR) goes through an ACARS provider you choose on the flyPad: Hoppie, BeyondATC or SayIntentions. The aircraft must find it, then connect your flight number to it.
ACARS Provider: BeyondATC, "Waiting for Connection" until BeyondATC answers (then "Connected", green).

items: Start the provider when you like. The aircraft looks for it every 5 s for 5 minutes, then once a minute, without end. Your provider, ATIS and METAR settings are never changed.
Flight number. Entered before the provider answers, it is connected as soon as it answers.

Provider closed. Within about a minute the status goes back to "Waiting for Connection"; start it again and the aircraft connects your flight number again by itself. With BeyondATC, log on to the ATC center again (it forgets the logon when it closes).
TELEX on. If FBW's TELEX service refuses your flight number, the ACARS provider is connected anyway (on the A380X, the FMS shows FMS DATALINK NOT AVAIL for the TELEX failure).
No extra traffic with Hoppie: once your flight number is connected, the regular polls (every 45 to 75 s) check the provider.
Before this change, a provider started more than 5 minutes after the aircraft set the flyPad to NONE: select your provider again once if it shows NONE.
flyPad > Settings > ATSU / AOC: choose the ACARS provider (Hoppie, BeyondATC or SayIntentions).
Start the provider program whenever you like, before or after loading the aircraft.
Enter the flight number (MFD INIT on the A380X, MCDU INIT A on the A32NX): it is connected as soon as the provider answers.

children.title: SD mailbox fixes: FILE FULL after CANCEL, uplink @ markers

blocks.text: Two mailbox problems found in the sim with BeyondATC:

items: FILE FULL for good. The mailbox keeps at most five open messages per direction and holds the next ones back with FILE FULL. A cancelled downlink (CANCEL of a prepared message) left the ATC function but kept its place in the mailbox file, so after five cancels the file stayed full: every new downlink, a PAN PAN PAN included, waited behind FILE FULL. A cancel now frees the place, the held messages move in, and FILE FULL goes when the file has room again (A380 FCOM DSC-46: "File no more full").

Triangles around values. Hoppie and BeyondATC mark the variable fields of a free text uplink with @ (CLRD TO @CYVR@ RWY @06R@), and the A380 display font draws @ as a triangle. The mailbox now shows the marked fields as main parameters, in blue (FCOM DSC-46-10-10-70), without the markers, as the A32NX DCDU does; an unclosed marker runs to the end of the text, and a word glued to a field ("@4611@.") stays glued. MSG RECORD drops the markers too.
Five downlinks prepared and cancelled, then a new one: The new downlink is shown with SEND / CANCEL; no FILE FULL.
More than five open downlinks: FILE FULL for the extra ones, until a place is freed (sent, closed or cancelled).
BeyondATC departure clearance "CLRD TO @CYVR@ RWY @06R@ ...": CLRD TO CYVR RWY 06R ..., the values in blue, no triangles.
Nothing to set: CANCEL a prepared downlink as usual, read the uplinks as usual.

children.title: LOAD-SEC3: ATC route clearances and crossing constraints into SEC 3

blocks.text: A route clearance or a crossing constraint received by CPDLC can be loaded into the FMS instead of being typed: the FCOM puts it in SEC 3, as a copy of the active flight plan with the clearance in it, for the crew to check and activate (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-40, DSC-46-10-40). The mailbox has the LOAD-SEC3 key in the 4th button position, on the uplinks that can be loaded only; it stays after WILCO, with CLOSE.

head: Uplink (CPDLC element)
What is loaded into SEC 3
rows: Route clearance: CLEARED TO ... VIA ... (UM79), CLEARED ... (UM80), AT ... CLEARED ... (UM83)
SID (not once airborne), airways, waypoints, lat/long points, STAR and a new destination. The rest of the en route part is replaced; a UM79 route ends at its clearance limit.
Crossing constraints (UM46 to 53, 55, 56, 58 to 61): CROSS ... AT / AT OR ABOVE / AT OR BELOW / BETWEEN ..., AT ... speed, AT ... time

An altitude constraint, a speed constraint (90 kt to VMO 340 kt, in knots) or an RTA on that waypoint of the flight plan. The RTA is kept per secondary flight plan and follows it on a swap or an activation; the VERT REV RTA panel now works on a SEC plan.

items: LOAD-SEC3 pressed: Mailbox information area: LOADING, then LOAD OK, LOAD PARTIAL or LOAD FAILED.
Everything loaded: FMS message ATC F-PLN INSERTED IN SEC 3. SEC 3 holds the active flight plan with the clearance.

Some elements rejected: ATC F-PLN INSERTED IN SEC 3 / REJECTED INFO SEE SEC / INDEX. SEC INDEX, SEC 3: REJECTED ATC INFO button, listing each element (description, value, AT fix) and why: NOT IN DATABASE, AWY/WPT MISMATCH, DATA NOT ALLOWED IN PHASE, NOT IN F-PLN, FORMAT ERROR, ENTRY OUT OF RANGE.
Nothing usable: RECEIVED ATC MSG NOT VALID.
No FMS answer within 30 s, or a second LOAD-SEC3 while loading: LOAD NOT AVAIL.
A speed as a Mach number (e.g. M.82): Rejected: FORMAT ERROR (the FCOM speed format is in knots).

blocks.text: The constraint upload awaits in a plain statement, not as an operand: the sim's JavaScript engine can reject an await used as an operand and then blanks the whole MFD. No visible change.

items: A duplicate waypoint ident is taken as the one nearest to the previous point. Why: Design choice: no NON UNIQUE rejection. What to do: Check the route in SEC 3 before activating it.

A constraint on an en route waypoint with no climb or descent leg type is set as a descent constraint in cruise, else from the second half of the en route part. Why: The FMS needs CLB or DES for a constraint; this is a guess. What to do: Check the constraint in SEC 3.
Needs an uplink of one of these CPDLC elements. Why: Live controllers rarely send them; BeyondATC route clearances were not seen. What to do: Send yourself the uplink (How to test).
Receive the clearance in the SD mailbox and press LOAD-SEC3.
Wait for LOAD OK (or LOAD PARTIAL), then read the FMS message.
MFD FMS: SEC INDEX, SEC 3: check the flight plan (and REJECTED ATC INFO if shown).
Answer the uplink (WILCO / UNABLE) and, if you accept the clearance, activate SEC 3 (or swap it).

children.title: OIT COMPANY COM inbox with the real AOC messages

blocks.text: The OIT COMPANY COM inbox showed two hard-coded test messages. It now lists the company (AOC) messages received by the datalink, newest first, with an unread mark, the sender and the UTC time (A380 FCOM DSC-46-40-20, COMPANY COM application). Displaying a message marks it read; the COMPANY MSG memo goes once every message is read (FCOM: COMPANY MSG, "The flight crew received a company message")..

items: A company message (for example a Hoppie free text) arrives: A new line at the top of the inbox with the unread mark; the E/WD shows COMPANY MSG.
The crew opens the message: The text shows; the line loses its unread mark.
Every message read: The COMPANY MSG memo goes.
The other OIS FLT OPS applications are not done. Why: They are separate work.
Connect the datalink (flight number on MFD FMS INIT, AOC provider in flyPad > Settings > ATSU / AOC).
When COMPANY MSG shows, open the OIT COMPANY COM inbox and click the message to read it.
A Hoppie free text reaching the inbox, and COMPANY MSG cleared after reading it.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: MFD System Message Area: CHECK FMS MESSAGE, NEW ATIS RECEIVED, ATIS SYS MSG

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM MFD header has a System Message Area that tells the crew about a message of another application while it is not shown (A380 FCOM MFD description, System Message Area). It now shows:

items: CHECK FMS MESSAGE: an amber FMS message is pending while another application (ATC COM, SURV, FCU BKUP) is shown; removed when the crew opens an FMS page.
NEW ATIS RECEIVED: a new ATIS report of the ATC COM datalink arrived while another application is shown; removed when the crew opens an ATC COM page.
ATIS SYS MSG: an ATIS system message of the ATC centre (USE VOICE, SEND AGAIN, NO AUTO UPDATE, END OF UPDATE) while another application is shown; removed when the crew opens an ATC COM page.

blocks.text: Design choices: the area shows one message, the most recent one (the FCOM gives no priority); a message comes only from a new event, so going back to another application does not bring back a message already seen in its application.

items: The KCCU MAILBOX key and the ATC MSG flashing are on `core/a380x-mailbox-du-reconf`. Why: They belong with the SD mailbox.
When a message shows in the MFD header, open the application it names (FMS, or ATC COM for the ATIS) to read it.
The layout of the message area in the header (fit, colour, position).
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X fuel jettison and FINAL fuel
Fuel jettison with the JTSN GW, ECAM memo and procedures

blocks.text: FBW had the overhead JETTISON ARM and ACTIVE pushbuttons, but they did nothing. The fuel management (FQMS) now jettisons the fuel of the transfer tanks down to the gross weight entered on the MFD, and the ECAM shows the memo and the procedures of the FCOM.

items: MFD FMS ACTIVE/FUEL&LOAD page. JTSN GW is shown when the active flight plan has its mandatory data.
Enter the gross weight at which the jettison must stop, in tonnes (or 1000 lb with the LBS unit).
Allowed range: from ZFW + 11 000 lb (5.0 t) to the maximum gross weight (FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-100). Outside it: ENTRY OUT OF RANGE with the range.

blocks.text: JTSN GW 400.0 t entered (ZFW 300.0 t).
290 t is below ZFW + 5.0 t: the range is shown in the message area.
Without a JTSN GW the FQMS has no target weight: the jettison then runs until the transfer tanks are empty (or a pushbutton is set OFF).
The ABN PROC procedure takes the crew through the steps. ECP ABN PROC, then FUEL, then JETTISON:
ABN PROC menu: FUEL selected.
FUEL sub-menu: JETTISON.
The procedure before ACTIVATE: all lines in grey.
Activated: the FMS lines checked by the crew, JETTISON ARM and ACTIVE ticked by the FWS as the pushbuttons are set (sensed lines).

items: FMS FUEL & LOAD PAGE ... SELECT, JETTISON GW ... ENTER: crew check lines.
IF TRIM TK NOT EMPTY & NO TRIM & APU LINE FAULT: TRIM TK FEED AUTO (condition line, confirmed by the crew).
JETTISON ARM ON, JETTISON ACTIVE ON: sensed, they tick themselves.
JETTISON & CG ... MONITOR: watch the SD FUEL page and the CG.
WHEN JETTISON COMPLETED (AUTO RCL) / IF RQRD TO MANUALLY STOP JETTISON: ACTIVE OFF then ARM OFF, sensed.

blocks.text: The EWD memo while the fuel is jettisoned.

items: Memo JETTISON IN PROGRESS (green).

Fuel leaves the transfer tanks (outer, mid, inner and trim) at the FCOM rate of 330 693 lb/h (about 2.5 t per minute), in proportion to their content, so they empty together. The feed tanks are never jettisoned.
The trim tank is held when the CG reaches the forward T.O/LDG limit, and resumes when the CG is 0.5 % aft of it.
The other automatic transfers pause during the jettison.

The SD FUEL page shows the two jettison valves open, with the jettison lines and JETTISON legends in white (normal, FCOM DSC-28-20), and the quantities decreasing. Before the fix on this branch they were amber during every jettison (the page did not know a jettison was running).

blocks.text: FUEL JETTISON COMPLETED: set ACTIVE then ARM OFF; the lines tick as the pushbuttons are released.

items: Gross weight reaches the JTSN GW: The jettison stops, FUEL JETTISON COMPLETED shows, the ACTIVE ON light goes off.
All transfer tanks empty (or no JTSN GW entered): Same: stops and COMPLETED.
ACTIVE or ARM set OFF by the crew: Stops at once (manual stop). No COMPLETED alert.
Both pushbuttons OFF after COMPLETED: The alert and the COMPLETED state clear; a new jettison can be started.
ACTIVE ON without ARM: Nothing: ARM is needed.
AC 1 bus not powered: No jettison (FQMS channel unpowered).

JETTISON FAULT, VLV NOT CLOSED and INOP SYS JETTISON come only from the flyPad valve failures. Why: No other cause of a jettison valve fault is simulated; the four valve failures are described in the next feature.

The fuel does not really flow out through the outlets. Why: The MSFS fuel system has no overboard dump: the FQMS sets the tank quantities directly and opens valves 57 / 58 for the SD picture. A fuel mist plume is drawn at the outlets (last feature).
After an update, the first flight needs a full MSFS restart. Why: The change touches the behaviour XML of the overhead, which MSFS loads at start. What to do: Restart MSFS once after installing.
MFD FMS ACTIVE/FUEL&LOAD: enter JTSN GW (the gross weight at which the jettison stops).
ECP ABN PROC > FUEL > JETTISON, ACTIVATE, and follow the lines.
Overhead FUEL panel: JETTISON ARM ON, then ACTIVE ON. Monitor the SD FUEL page and the CG.
At FUEL JETTISON COMPLETED (or to stop earlier): ACTIVE OFF, then ARM OFF.

children.title: Jettison valve failures: FUEL JETTISON FAULT, VLV NOT CLOSED, INOP SYS JETTISON

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM has two jettison alerts, FUEL JETTISON FAULT and FUEL JETTISON VLV NOT CLOSED (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28 P 61-63), and INOP SYS JETTISON on the STATUS page. FBW had no jettison valve failure to trigger them. There are now four failures, one per valve and position. A first version never showed the FAULT caution and the INOP SYS: the FWS read the FQMS flags as numbers (1) and combined them with a function that only counts `true`; they are now read as real booleans.

head: flyPad > Failures > ATA 28 (Fuel)
Effect
rows: Jettison valve L stuck closed / Jettison valve R stuck closed
That valve does not open: the fuel goes through the other one at half the rate. The FQMS records the valve fault when the jettison is selected (ARM and ACTIVE ON), until the failure is removed.
The jettison is not available: no fuel leaves.
Jettison valve L stuck open / Jettison valve R stuck open

That valve stays open: the OPEN light of the JETTISON ACTIVE pushbutton stays on and the SD shows the valve open, also with no jettison running. No fuel is lost by it (the jettison itself still needs ARM and ACTIVE).

items: One valve stuck closed, jettison selected: Amber caution FUEL JETTISON FAULT; on the ground with the line JETTISON L (R) VLV FAULT. Jettison at half rate. STATUS: INOP SYS JETTISON (the FWS lists it whenever FUEL JETTISON FAULT is active).

Both valves stuck closed, jettison selected: FUEL JETTISON FAULT with JETTISON NOT AVAIL, then JETTISON ACTIVE ... OFF and JETTISON ARM ... OFF (they tick as the pushbuttons are set OFF). STATUS: INOP SYS JETTISON. No fuel jettisoned.
A valve stuck open, no jettison running: Amber caution FUEL JETTISON VLV NOT CLOSED with JETTISON ACTIVE ... OFF and JETTISON ARM ... OFF; OPEN light on.
Takeoff and landing: The alerts are inhibited in the takeoff and landing flight phases (FCOM inhibitions).
flyPad > Failures > ATA 28: activate one of the four jettison valve failures.
Run a jettison (or not, for a valve stuck open) and follow the ECAM.
Deactivate the failure in the flyPad to repair the valve.

children.title: Fuel jettison plume at the outlets

blocks.text: The jettisoned fuel left no trace outside. A fuel mist plume now trails from each wing's jettison outlet while fuel flows out of that side. The FCOM says there is "one discharge point on the trailing edge of each wing" (DSC-28-40); the outlet is the tube at the aft end of the second-outermost flap track fairing (MFTF 5, forum source), where the companion model adds the effect points.

items: Jettison in progress, both valves open: A mist plume behind each wing outlet; it gets longer with the true airspeed (its particles stay where they were released).
One valve stuck closed: The plume on the other side only.
Valve stuck open, no jettison running: No plume (no fuel flows).
Below 40 kt true airspeed: The low-speed version of the mist (the stock MSFS water-ballast effect switches at 40 kt).

Needs the aircraft-large-files companion. Why: The effect hangs on the FX_JETTISON_LH / RH nodes added at the outlets in the A380_WINGS models (fa6c5d1); without them no plume shows. What to do: Install it; a full MSFS restart is needed after the update.
The look is the stock water-ballast mist. Why: Closest stock MSFS effect: design choice.
No fuel puddle on the ground. Why: Jettisoned fuel evaporates; nothing is drawn on the ground. On the ground, fuel drops fall from the outlets (next feature).
Run a fuel jettison (first feature) and look at the wings from the outside view.

children.title: Fuel jettison on the ground: fuel drip at the outlets

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM allows a jettison on the ground: "It is possible to jettison in any aircraft configuration, and at any speed" (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28 FUEL JETTISON), and the FQMS does not stop it on the ground. The fuel then falls on the ground. With the aircraft on the ground, fuel drops now fall from each jettison outlet whose valve is open, together with the plume of the previous feature.

items: On the ground, jettison running, both valves open: Fuel drops fall from both outlets, with the mist plume.
On the ground, one valve open: Drops and plume at that outlet only.
Below 40 kt true airspeed: The slow drip; from 40 kt the fast drip (the stock MSFS fuel leak effects, switched at 40 kt as Asobo does).
In flight: No drip: the plume alone, unchanged.
Valve stuck open, no jettison running: No drip (no fuel flows).
flyPad Situation Visual Effects switch OFF (the switch comes with the fire effects of `core/failures-a32nx`): Drip and plume still show: the jettison effect is not a situation effect.

Needs the aircraft-large-files companion. Why: The drip hangs on the same FX_JETTISON_LH / RH outlet nodes as the plume (fa6c5d1). What to do: Install it; a full MSFS restart is needed after the update.
The look is the stock MSFS fuel leak drip. Why: Closest stock MSFS effect: design choice. No puddle or wet patch is drawn on the ground.
On the ground, enter a JTSN GW on the MFD FMS ACTIVE/FUEL&LOAD page and set JETTISON ARM and ACTIVE ON on the overhead FUEL panel.
Look at the wing trailing edges from the outside view; set ACTIVE OFF to stop.

children.title: FINAL fuel and time from the A380 holding fuel flow

blocks.text: The FINAL fuel default of the FUEL&LOAD page was a fixed 6.0 t per 30 min (0.2 t per minute, the same flow for the EXTRA time), whatever the weight. The A380 FCOM defines the holding fuel as 30 min at 1 500 ft above the alternate, at holding speed (green dot + 25 kt, CONF CLEAN), ISA, with the landing weight at the alternate (PER-IFT-FPL-MRF HOLDING FUEL). The FINAL fuel now comes from that holding.

items: The fuel flow comes from the one A380 holding computation in the FCOM (PER-IFT-HLD-HMI, IN-FLT PERF example: 940.0 klb, 30 min, 13 100 lb), brought back from ISA+10 to ISA, and taken proportional to the weight.

FINAL fuel: a holding of the FINAL time (30 min by default) that ends at the ZFW, rounded up to the 0.1 t of the entry field, like the ALTN fuel. Check: RJTT-RKSI at ZFW 342.6 t gives 4.70 t, shown 4.8 (the airline OFP gives 4.8 t).
FINAL time from a FINAL fuel entry: the time that fuel lasts in the same holding.
EXTRA time: the time the EXTRA fuel lasts in the same holding, ending with the ZFW plus the MIN FUEL AT DEST on board.
Without a ZFW: the FCOM conservative quantity, 10 600 lb per 30 min.
This replaces the fixed 0.2 t per minute flow (30 min = 6 t) of `core/a380x-mfd-fms`.
RJTT/RKSI, ALTN RKSS, ZFW 342.6 t, no FINAL entry: FINAL 4.8, time 00:30.
ZFW 300.0 t: FINAL 4.2, time 00:30.
FINAL fuel 6.0 entered (ZFW 342.6 t): FINAL time 00:38.
FINAL fuel cleared (CLR): Back to FINAL 4.8, 00:30.
5.0 t of EXTRA fuel at ZFW 342.6 t: EXTRA time about 00:30 or 00:31 (about 6.3 min per tonne; before: 5 min per tonne).
The FINAL time stays 00:30 with a calculated fuel. Why: Design choice: the time shown is the one the fuel was computed from, not the slightly longer time of the rounded-up fuel.

The holding altitude and the temperature are not used. Why: The A380 FCOM has no holding table; the A320neo table varies by less than 5 % from FL15 to FL140, and the FCOM figure is brought back to ISA (design choice).
The fuel flow is taken proportional to the weight. Why: Maximum endurance: thrust follows the weight; the A320neo holding table confirms the near linear law (design choice).
MFD FMS INIT: FROM/TO and ALTN. FUEL&LOAD: enter the ZFW and ZFWCG.
Read the FINAL fuel and time. Overwrite the FINAL fuel or the FINAL time if the company policy asks for another value; CLR returns to the calculated value.
Read the EXTRA time next to the EXTRA fuel once the BLOCK is entered.

children.title: TRIP and cruise fuel predictions match the engines

blocks.text: The A380X FMS predicted less fuel than the engines burn: 4 to 7 % less in cruise and about 3 % less on the TRIP (e.g. 19.8 t instead of 20.5 t on a 700 NM, FL340 RJTT-RKSI-like leg), so the DEST EFOB fell during the cruise. The cause was in the VNAV engine model: to find the N1 that gives a thrust, it inverted the engine thrust table (table 1506 of engines.cfg) column by column, which is not the inverse of the table the sim engine reads (bilinear in N1 and Mach). At M.85, exactly between the M.8 and M.9 columns, it took up to 2 % N1 too little. It now interpolates the table at the Mach first and inverts that single curve.

items: The cruise fuel flow now matches the FADEC fuel flow at M.85 (A380TripFuelPrediction.spec.ts: the sim burn and the FCOM IN-FLT PERF examples).
The same RJTT-RKSI-like leg (ZFW 342.6 t, 30 t at take-off, FL340, ISA, no wind) now gives a TRIP of 20.5 t.

A32NX: `EngineModel.ts` is the shared FMGC code, so the A32NX VNAV predictions (climb, cruise, descent) use the corrected inverse too. They change only between the Mach columns of the A32NX thrust table.

The TRIP is still below a SimBrief plan (23.5 t for the real RJTT-RKSI route). Why: The sim A380X itself burns less than the FCOM IN-FLT PERF examples (climb about 24 % less fuel, cruise about 5 % less); the FMS now matches the sim engines, not the FCOM tables.
Nothing to set: enter the flight plan, the CRZ FL and the FUEL&LOAD data as usual and read the TRIP and the EFOB predictions.

children.title: Automatic refuel targets the CG of the ZFW and ZFCG last entered

blocks.text: The automatic refuel fills the trim tank so that the CG after refuelling meets the target. It always used the payload ZFW and ZFCG of the sim. The fuel system now uses the ZFW and ZFCG you entered last, on the OIS REFUEL application or on the MFD FUEL&LOAD page, whichever you changed more recently. With no entry on the REFUEL application the payload values keep applying.

items: A REFUEL application entry needs both the ZFW and the ZFCG. Why: The CG target is meaningless with only one of them, so a single value is ignored.
Enter the ZFW and ZFCG on the OIS REFUEL application or on the MFD FUEL&LOAD page, then start the automatic refuel. The last entry made sets the CG target.

children.title: GPS receivers, GPS deselection and ECAM STATUS

blocks.text: There was no GPS receiver in either aircraft: the pages showed the sim GPS position for both receivers with random satellite counts and figures of merit, and GPS PRIMARY came from a random estimate. Now each Multi-Mode Receiver (MMR 1 and MMR 2) has a GPS receiver. A320 FCOM DSC-34: "Worldwide, 24 satellites broadcast accurate navigation data"; the two independent receivers process them and send their data to the ADIRUs.

items: Satellites: the sim has none, so they are computed from the nominal 24-slot GPS constellation (six orbital planes, four satellites each) at the sim UTC date and time. A satellite counts when it is more than 5° above the horizon. Their geometry gives the dilution of precision, and from it the figure of merit (accuracy) and the integrity limit (HIL) of the position. Fewer than 5 satellites: no integrity limit.

Modes (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20 GPS MONITOR, A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-40-10): TEST (self test at power up, 1.5 to 2.5 s), INIT (2.5 to 4.5 s), ACQ (satellite acquisition), NAV (4 or more satellites, data to the ADIRUs), FAULT (failed receiver).
Acquisition time: 15 to 30 s after a short power cut (unpowered 15 min or less: warm start), 80 to 130 s from a cold start, 5 to 15 s to re-acquire after a loss of the signals.

Degraded modes (the FCOMs only name them; the behaviour follows ARINC 743A, a design choice): ALTAID with 3 satellites (the ADR barometric altitude is the fourth measurement, no integrity limit); AIDED with fewer satellites, the receiver coasts on the IR velocities for up to 2 min, its accuracy gets worse with time and it gives no integrity limit. After that: back to ACQ.
Antenna masking: the antenna is on top of the fuselage. In a turn or a steep climb, satellites low on the far side of the aircraft are masked.

DIFF (A380X only): the A380 receivers use satellite based augmentation. In NAV inside a WAAS (North America), EGNOS (Europe), MSAS (Japan) or GAGAN (India) service area, the mode shows DIFF and the position is several times more accurate. The service areas are coarse latitude/longitude boxes (design choice).

Power: A32NX: the FCOM gives none. GPS 1 is on AC ESS and GPS 2 on AC 2, as the other side 1 / side 2 navigation receivers (design choice). A380X: as the FCOM supply table, GPS 1 (MMR 1) is on AC EMER and GPS 2 (MMR 2) on AC 3. The bus named AC ESS in the A380X code is the AC EMER busbar.
Failures: flyPad > Failures > ATA 34 Navigation > GPS 1 and GPS 2 put the receiver in FAULT.

The satellite positions are the nominal constellation, not the real satellites of the day. Why: No almanac file is used: the 24 nominal slots give a realistic count and geometry anywhere in the world. What to do: None needed.
ALTAID and AIDED are rarely seen in flight. Why: With 24 satellites, 4 or more are almost always in view; masking in a steep turn seldom leaves fewer. What to do: Covered by the Rust unit tests.
A full MSFS restart is needed after installing. Why: The receivers are in the systems WASM module. What to do: Restart the sim.
Nothing to set: power the aircraft and the receivers start (TEST, INIT, ACQ, then NAV).
Watch them on the A32NX MCDU DATA > GPS MONITOR page or the A380X MFD FMS > POSITION > GPS page (see "GPS pages" below).

blocks.text: Each IR of the ADIRUs now mixes its inertial position with the position of one GPS receiver: the GPIRS position. The selection follows A320 FCOM DSC-22_20: IR 1 uses GPS 1, IR 2 uses GPS 2, IR 3 uses GPS 1 (GPS 2 with the ATT HDG selector on F/O 3). If one receiver is rejected, all the IRs use the other one. The same rule is used on the A380X (design choice: the A380 FCOM does not give it).

The FMS (the same code in the A32NX FMGC and the A380X FMC) uses the onside GPIRS, else GPIRS 3, else the offside one (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-30-10). Its estimated position uncertainty (EPU) is the GPIRS figure of merit. Accuracy is HIGH when the EPU is within the required navigation performance (RNP), and GPS PRIMARY needs accuracy HIGH and the integrity limit within the RNP. Before, a random estimate gave GPS PRIMARY.

items: IRs aligned, receivers in NAV: GPS PRIMARY (A32NX PROG page, A380X POSITION / MONITOR), accuracy HIGH.
Receivers still in ACQ, or IRs not in NAV: No GPIRS position: no GPS PRIMARY; the FMS uses radio or IRS positions.
GPS 1 failed: IR 1 and IR 3 switch to GPS 2: GPS PRIMARY stays.
Both GPS failed: GPS PRIMARY is lost: the FMS shows GPS PRIMARY LOST.
Align the IRs as usual. GPS PRIMARY comes once the IRs are in NAV and the receivers are in NAV.
Check GPS PRIMARY on the A32NX MCDU PROG page or the A380X MFD POSITION / MONITOR page before an RNAV procedure.

children.title: GPS pages: MCDU GPS MONITOR and MFD POSITION/GPS

blocks.text: Both pages showed the sim GPS solution for both receivers with random satellite counts and figures of merit. They now show the data of each receiver.
A32NX MCDU GPS MONITOR

Per receiver (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20-50-10-28): GPS1(2) POSITION, TTRK (true track, in degrees: the old page showed the magnetic track in radians), GS, UTC, MERIT (figure of merit, FT), MODE/SAT (mode and number of satellites), GPS ALT. The data is dashed while the receiver is not in NAV (or ALTAID / AIDED), and for a receiver that no ADIRU has selected ("the data of the GPS that is not selected is dashed").
A380X MFD POSITION/GPS

Per receiver (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30): position, MODE (TEST, INIT, ACQ, NAV, ALTAID, AIDED, DIFF, FAULT), NBR OF SAT (while acquiring and navigating), ACCURACY (HFOM, in FT as on the FCOM figure), TRK, UTC, ALT and GND SPD. Dashes while the receiver does not compute a position.
MFD POSITION/GPS: the page layout (picture from the browser harness, taken before the receivers existed: the values are the old stand-in values).

items: A32NX: MCDU DATA key > GPS MONITOR.
A380X: MFD FMS > POSITION menu > GPS.

blocks.text: There was no GPS alert. A failed receiver (mode FAULT) now raises the FCOM alert:

items: A32NX: NAV GPS 1 FAULT / NAV GPS 2 FAULT (FCOM PRO-ABN-NAV: "GPS 1(2) is failed"), amber caution, no procedure line. Flight phase inhibition as the radio altimeter faults (design choice). STATUS: INOP SYS GPS 1(2); with both: INOP SYS GPS 1+2 and the information FLS LIMITED TO F-APP + RAW (see "A32NX ECAM STATUS page").

A380X: NAV GPS 1 FAULT, NAV GPS 2 FAULT or NAV GPS 1+2 FAULT, crew awareness (the A380 FCOM gives no procedure), inhibited as the ADR faults (design choice). STATUS (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-34-10): INOP SYS GPS 1, GPS 2 or GPS 1+2; with both also BTV and ROW/ROP in APPR & LDG.
Read the alert on the E/WD and clear it with CLR.
Check the inoperative systems on the SD STATUS page (STS key).

blocks.text: The crew can tell the FMS not to use the GPS (for example when told GPS is unreliable in an area). The A32NX DESELECT key was inoperative and the A380X had no GPS option. Now:

items: A32NX SELECTED NAVAIDS page, key [6L] (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20-50-10-28): GPS SELECTED / DESELECTED in blue small font, the action ({DESELECT or {SELECT) in white.
A380X POSITION / NAVAIDS page: GPS SELECTED / DESELECTED radio buttons (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30).
With the GPS deselected the GPIRS position is no longer used: the FMS goes to IRS/DME/DME, IRS/VOR/DME or IRS only, and GPS PRIMARY is lost.
The deselection is reset at the end of the flight (DONE phase).

GPS IS DESELECTED (A32NX, white MCDU message) / GPS DESELECTED (A380X, white MFD message) when the GPS is deselected and the aircraft is less than 80 NM from the top of descent, or in the approach phase. The message is removed when the GPS is selected again.

Position uncertainty without GPS (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20-20-20 table): IRS/DME/DME 0.27 to 0.37 NM, IRS/VOR/DME 0.30 to 0.42 NM (growing with the distance to the navaids, up to 100 NM: design choice), IRS only growing from its starting value at 6 NM/h for 40 min, 0 for 50 min, 4 NM/h for 40 min, 0 for 45 min, then 2 NM/h; 5 NM after an IRS alignment.
The 0.2 NM reset of the uncertainty at takeoff is not done. Why: Not part of this change. What to do: None.
A32NX: MCDU DATA > POSITION MONITOR > NAVAIDS> [6R] > press [6L] {DESELECT. Press [6L] {SELECT to use the GPS again.
A380X: MFD FMS > POSITION > NAVAIDS, GPS: select DESELECTED (or SELECTED).

children.title: FM position: IRS position plus a GPS or radio bias, POSITION MONITOR pages

blocks.text: The FMS position was the sim position. The FCOM FM position is now modelled (shared FMS code; A320 FCOM DSC-22_20-20 navigation, A380 FCOM FMS position computation):

items: FM position = MIX IRS position + a bias. The bias follows the GPIRS position (on the ground and in flight) or the radio position (in flight only). In IRS only navigation the last bias is kept.
Each FMS uses the GPIRS of its own side first, then ADIRU 3, then the other side.
Without GPS PRIMARY, the position is updated at takeoff to the runway start plus the TO SHIFT.
A manual position update (A32NX PROG UPDATE AT) moves the FM position; the EPU (estimated position uncertainty) follows the updates.
The FMS writes `L:A32NX_FM_GPS_POS_DISAGREE`: the NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE alerts read it (their FWC and FWS parts are on `core/failures-a32nx` and `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`).

A32NX MCDU: POSITION MONITOR (and FROZEN) shows the real FMGC 1 and 2, GPIRS or radio, MIX IRS and IRS positions with the navigation mode and the deviations; PROG UPDATE AT works; the IRS page shows the GPIRS position and accuracy of its ADIRU.
A380X MFD POSITION / MONITOR: the onside and offside FMS positions, the navigation mode, RADIO, MIXIRS, GPIRS, GPS 1 and GPS 2 from the receiver data.
GPS PRIMARY (normal): The FM position follows the GPIRS position; it carries the small GPS receiver error, so it differs a little from the sim position.
GPS deselected or failed, in flight, radio navaids in range: The bias follows the radio position (IRS/DME/DME or IRS/VOR/DME).
IRS only: The last bias is kept; the position drifts only as the IRS position does (see the limits).
Takeoff without GPS PRIMARY: The FM position jumps to the runway start plus the TO SHIFT at the takeoff thrust.
No IRS drift and no radio position reasonableness check. Why: The sim ADIRS writes the sim position: there is no drift to correct.
No A380X POSITION UPDATE panel, no FM/IR POS DISAGREE. Why: Left for later.
No offsets, SEC / ALTN predictions, FLS beam or A32NX TRIP/EFOB table on these pages. Why: Left for later.
A32NX: MCDU DATA > POSITION MONITOR to compare the FMGC, GPIRS / radio, MIX IRS and IRS positions; FREEZE to hold them.
A32NX: for a manual update, PROG > UPDATE AT, enter the position (or a navaid ident) and confirm.
A380X: MFD FMS > POSITION > MONITOR.
The FMS position now carries the GPS receiver error: watch LNAV and the ND for jumps, also when the GPS powers up.
The takeoff update with the GPS deselected.
The POSITION MONITOR pages of both aircraft.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: FMS messages lists, and CHECK APPR SELECTION

blocks.text: Messages of the A320 MCDU message list (FCOM DSC-22_20-90) and of the A380 MFD FMS message list that the FMS never raised:

head: Message
Aircraft
When (FCOM)
rows: The RNP entered is larger than the default RNP of the flight area, and the database has no RNP for the active leg.
PROCEDURE RNP IS xx.xx (A380X: PROC RNP IS)
The RNP entered is larger than the database RNP of the active leg.

The crew enters a cruise level above the computed maximum level.
In the holding, the extra fuel is zero or less.
The active or next leg is a procedure turn that exceeds the excursion distance of the database.
The NDB of the NDB approach is deselected.
The clock reaches the ETT; shown until the takeoff or a new ETT.
A DIR TO with CRS IN or CRS OUT is inserted.

A non ILS approach in the F-PLN and an ILS tuned manually on the RAD NAV page, in cruise less than 100 NM from the T/D, in descent or in approach. Amber; it also sets the variable the PFD FMA line 3 shows.

blocks.text: The messages are type II: sent once when the condition starts and removed when it ends. A message with a value (AREA RNP IS 2.00) is replaced when the value changes.

items: Other messages of the FCOM lists are still missing. Why: They need data or functions the FMS does not have yet.
CHECK APPR SELECTION on the PFD FMA needs `core/failures-a32nx`. Why: The PFD FMA part of the change is on that branch; here only the MCDU message and the variable. What to do: Merge both.
The A380X MFD System Message Area (CHECK FMS MESSAGE) is on `core/a380x-atccom-datalink`. Why: It also shows the ATIS of the ATC COM datalink of that branch.
Read the message in the MCDU scratchpad (A32NX; CLR removes it) or in the MFD FMS message list (A380X).
Act as the FCOM says for each message (check the RNP, the database cycle, the IRS position, the approach selection...).
CHECK DATA BASE CYCLE stays silent with a current database (the main risk of a wrong date check).
Any of the new messages showing when the FCOM condition is not met.
Not sim-tested yet.

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-31-20-30-90: with the KCCU cursor on the lateral ND in ARC, PLAN or ROSE-NAV mode, the flight crew revises the flight plan directly on the ND, without going to the MFD. The FBW ND was not interactive.

items: Interactive areas: a blue box around every waypoint, NAVAID or airport under the cursor. A click gives the list of the elements there (P.POS for the aircraft mock-up), then the revision list of the chosen one.

Revision list: the ident (green in the active flight plan, yellow in the temporary one), then: for a flight plan waypoint FROM P.POS DIR TO *, INSERT NEXT WPT, DELETE *; for a database element FROM P.POS DIR TO *; for an airport also DATA; for the aircraft mock-up DIR TO.

DIRECT TO page at the bottom of the ND: the DIRECT TO target field (with a list of the flight plan waypoints, or a KCCU entry), UTC and DIST, the options DIRECT, DIRECT WITH ABEAM, CRS IN, CRS OUT, and the CRS field next to CRS IN / CRS OUT (default course from the flight plan, typed NNN, with M or T for magnetic or true). CANCEL closes the page when there is no temporary flight plan.
INSERT DIR TO * / ERASE DIR TO * buttons either side of the aircraft while the cursor is in the ND; INSERT TMPY * / ERASE TMPY * for the other revisions.

INSERT NEXT WPT page: FROM and the revised waypoint (green, or yellow with IN TMPY), its latitude / longitude, and the NEXT WPT field. A click on a blank area of the ND creates a latitude/longitude waypoint.
DUPLICATE page (DIST(NM), LAT/LONG, RETURN, scroll arrows) when a typed ident is not unique, nearest first.
DATA on an airport opens the DATA / AIRPORT page on the MFD of the same side.

DIR TO UTC: the FMS has no predictions of the temporary flight plan, so the UTC at the target is estimated from the distance and the ground speed, on the ND and on the MFD DIRECT TO page. Below 30 kt ground speed it shows --:--.

No revision on a DIR TO temporary flight plan; no DIRECT TO while the ND shows another temporary flight plan. Why: FCOM DSC-31-20-30-90 P 1 and P 9. What to do: Insert or erase the temporary flight plan first.
The vertical display is not interactive. Why: Only the lateral ND is interactive in the FCOM. What to do: None.
Pilot-defined entries (lat/long, typed places) stay as stored waypoints after ERASE. Why: They are stored waypoints, as on the FBW MFD. What to do: Delete them on the MFD DATA pages if needed.
The UTC is an estimate (distance / ground speed). Why: The FMS computes no predictions for a temporary flight plan. What to do: Read the UTC on the F-PLN page once the DIR TO is inserted.
Only the interactions listed above work. Why: The other ND interactions of the FCOM are not implemented yet (the A380X README says so). What to do: Use the MFD pages for the other revisions.
Set the ND to ARC, PLAN or ROSE-NAV (map, not the OANS) and move the KCCU cursor onto the ND.
Click a waypoint, NAVAID or airport (or the aircraft symbol); pick it in the list if several are there.
Choose the revision: FROM P.POS DIR TO *, INSERT NEXT WPT, DELETE * or DATA.
Complete the page at the bottom of the ND (target, option, course, next waypoint) by clicks or KCCU entries.
Click INSERT (DIR TO * or TMPY *) to activate, or ERASE to discard.

children.title: PLACE/DIST entries in the ND waypoint fields

blocks.text: The FMS now accepts PLACE/DIST waypoints (a PDnn waypoint at a distance along the flight plan from a flight plan waypoint, for example `‹WPT>/10`): see the PLACE/DIST waypoints feature in the `core/a380x-mfd-fms` manual. The waypoint fields of the interactive ND go through the same shared entry code, which now needs the FMS function that creates the PLACE/DIST waypoint; the ND pages pass it on. Without this, a PLACE/DIST entry typed on the ND would not create the waypoint.

items: Only the place of the revised waypoint is accepted (A380 FCOM, INSERT NEXT WPT). Why: Same rule as on the MFD: another place gives PLACE / WPT DISAGREE, a distance beyond the neighbouring waypoint ENTRY OUT OF RANGE.
Click a flight plan waypoint on the ND > INSERT NEXT WPT.
Click the NEXT WPT field and type `‹that waypoint>/DIST` with the KCCU, then ENT.
Check the yellow temporary flight plan and click INSERT TMPY *.
PLACE/DIST entries from the ND fields give the same waypoint as from the MFD.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380 takeoff calculator and company T.O data

blocks.text: Before each takeoff the crew needs the takeoff weight limit of the runway, the FLEX temperature (reduced thrust), the speeds V1, VR, V2 and the flaps. On the real A380 they come from the OIS takeoff application or from the airline (company takeoff data, sent to the FMS by datalink). The flyPad calculator does the computation; SEND TO FMS plays the airline: the MFD receives the data as company T.O data, and the crew checks and inserts it, as in FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-30.
The takeoff screen. Amber labels: inputs still missing (Calculate stays dim).

head: Part
Contents
rows: ICAO code; imports from the FMS (departure, runway, TOW, CG, THR RED / ACCEL), the OFP (SimBrief) or the METAR (wind, OAT, QNH).
Runway from the list (or Manual), heading, TORA, elevation, slope, and the entry angle (90° or 180° turn onto the runway, or 0° when rolling straight on: it sets the line-up distance lost).
Runway condition, wind, OAT, QNH, anti-ice, packs.
TOW in t (or klb), one decimal, T.O CG in % MAC, flaps (CONF 1+F, 2, 3 or OPT = the best one), thrust (TOGA, FLEX or DERATED: see "A380 takeoff calculator: DERATED takeoff" below).
THR RED, ACCEL, EO ACCEL altitudes (they default to the elevation + 1500 ft), and the noise abatement procedure (NOISE END altitude, speed, N1).
The results in the layout of the OIS takeoff application (FCOM PER-TOF-TOR-SRS).
The runway with the V1, VR and 35 ft points, the required distance and the margin, for TOGA, any FLEX temperature of the allowed range, or a DERATED level the TOW permits.

items: Fill the airport and runway (or Fill data from FMS / OFP), the conditions (METAR), the TOW and the T.O CG.
Keep Thrust FLEX and press Calculate.
Read the FLEX temperature and the speeds in RESULTS; check the takeoff run and its margin.
Send to FMS, then insert the data on the MFD (see "On the MFD: company T.O data" below).

blocks.text: 450 t, 3500 m, 20 °C, CONF 1+F: FLEX 55 °C (the maximum, amber: estimate), V1 131 / VR 144 / V2 149 kt, MTOW(perf) 602 t. The takeoff run needs 3413 m of the 3447 m available after line-up: 35 m margin.
Reading the results

head: Line
Meaning
rows: Your takeoff weight, and the maximum the runway and conditions allow at TOGA.
The takeoff speeds. V2 is at least 1.13 VS1G and 1.10 VMCA, VR at least 1.05 VMCA, V1 at least VMCG (FCOM PER-TOF-TOR-SRS).
Runway left beyond the required distance.
The configuration, the CG entered, the takeoff shift (distance lost at line-up or an intersection).
The altitudes of the DEPARTURE section.

blocks.text: Green values come from Airbus data (the takeoff weight charts of the A380 Aircraft Characteristics); amber with a star are estimates of the FBW model (see Limitations).
The TAKEOFF RUN panel lets you look at the run for TOGA, or for any FLEX temperature between the OAT and the maximum (FCOM PER-TOF-THR-FLX). Use - / + or the slider; the speeds and the run follow.
TOGA: the run needs 1681 m, margin 1767 m.
FLEX range 30 °C to 55 °C max: the selected temperature is the one sent to the FMS.
Send to FMS sends the thrust selected for the takeoff run only (TOGA, FLEX at its temperature or DERATED at its level), with its own speeds.
Flaps: CONF 1+F, 2, 3, or OPT (the calculator picks the best).
Noise procedure: NOISE END altitude, speed and N1 become available; they are sent with the data.
When the takeoff is not possible, a message says why and there is no result:
CG outside the takeoff envelope (here 30 % at 450 t: the forward limit moves aft with the weight).
510 t on 2100 m at 40 °C: the maximum takeoff weight is 438.8 t.
A wet or contaminated runway: the A380 data covers dry runways only.

head: Message
Meaning
rows: TOW above the runway limit: reduce the weight or use another runway.
The CG is outside the A380 takeoff CG envelope for this weight.
The A380 data has no wet or contaminated takeoff.
Runway shorter than the A380 performance data (1700 m)
Above Maximum Tailwind / OAT / Pressure Altitude
No FLEX temperature is possible at this weight: take off at TOGA.

children.title: On the MFD: company T.O data

blocks.text: The MFD PERF T.O page gets two buttons: CPNY T.O REQUEST (ask the airline) and, once data has arrived, RECEIVED CPNY T.O.
PERF T.O before any data: the CPNY T.O REQUEST button (bottom right).
COMPANY T.O DATA REQUEST: up to 2 runways, TOGA / FLEX / DERATED, free text; SEND T.O REQUEST.

items: After SEND T.O REQUEST the page shows REQUEST PENDING...; without an answer after 4 minutes, NO COMPANY REPLY. The flyPad Send to FMS is that answer.
When data arrives: the message COMPANY T.O DATA RECEIVED WAITING FOR INSERTION and the button RECEIVED CPNY T.O on PERF.

blocks.text: Data received: the message and the RECEIVED CPNY T.O button.
RECEIVED COMPANY T.O DATA: runway 05 in amber (not the flight plan runway), TOW in amber with UPLINK/ACTIVE TOW DISAGREE: INSERT is not available.
The RECEIVED COMPANY T.O DATA page

items: Up to 4 runways (arrows, RWY 1/4) × 2 thrust ratings (the TOGA / FLEX list at the top).
Runway in amber: not the departure runway of the active flight plan.
TOW in amber with UPLINK/ACTIVE TOW DISAGREE: the uplink TOW is more than 2 t below or 7 t above the FMS TOW (FUEL&LOAD).
TEMP shows dashes for a FLEX or DERATED takeoff (a derate reads `DRT D12` in the thrust list); T.O LIMIT is the TORA; the noise fields are filled when the procedure was sent.

INSERT (only when runway and TOW agree) fills PERF T.O: speeds, flaps, thrust, shift, THR RED, ACCEL, EO ACCEL and noise. It does not fill THS FOR: the crew enters the CG there. CLEAR deletes the data.

blocks.text: An uplink with the noise procedure: NOISE END 3000 ft, SPD 180 kt, THR 85 %.
The flyPad warns you right after Send to FMS if INSERT will not work: another departure runway in the FMS, no TOW in the FMS, or a TOW outside -2 t / +7 t of the FMS one.

items: Inputs missing: Amber labels; Calculate stays dim.
Calculate with valid inputs: RESULTS and the takeoff run; FLEX at its maximum by default.
TOW too high, CG out of envelope, wet runway...: A message with the reason; no result.
Send to FMS with a runway from the list: "Takeoff data sent to the FMS: RECEIVED CPNY T.O on the PERF page"; the MFD shows the data a moment later.
Send to FMS with a manual runway: Nothing is sent: the FMS needs the runway ident.
RECEIVED page, other runway than the flight plan: Runway in amber; INSERT not available.
INSERT: PERF T.O filled; THS FOR still to enter.

Dry runways only (the DERATED takeoff too: see its own limitations below). Why: The only public A380 takeoff data is the takeoff weight charts of the Airbus A380 Aircraft Characteristics (dry, ISA and ISA+15, runway 1700-5100 m, altitude 0-8000 ft). What to do: On a wet runway, use the dry result with extra margin, as a training estimate only.

Speeds, FLEX, wind, slope and temperature effects are estimates (amber *). Why: The charts give weights only. The rest is a model fitted on them and checked on the FCOM examples (FLEX 38 at 560 t / 614 t).
The run distances (V1, VR, 35 ft points) are all-engine estimates. Why: No A380 distance data is public.
Send to FMS needs a runway from the list. Why: The FMS checks the uplink against its departure runway. What to do: Choose the runway in the list.
Not certified data. Why: For simulation and training.
On the MFD, enter the flight plan with its departure runway and fill FUEL&LOAD (ZFW, ZFWCG, block).
flyPad > Performance > Takeoff: Fill data from FMS, then METAR (or type the data).
Check TOW, T.O CG, flaps and thrust; press Calculate.
In TAKEOFF RUN, choose TOGA, the FLEX temperature or the DERATED level you will use; press Send to FMS.
On the MFD PERF T.O page: RECEIVED CPNY T.O, check the page, INSERT; enter the T.O CG in THS FOR.

blocks.text: A derate is a lower takeoff rating that is certified on its own (A380 FCOM PER-TOF-THR-DRT): the flight manual gives it its own takeoff limits and performance. The A380 has six levels, D04, D08, D12, D16, D20, D24: each one takes about 4 % more off the maximum takeoff thrust (D04 = about 4 % less, D24 = about 24 % less). The MFD PERF T.O page and the engines already had the derate; the flyPad calculator offered only TOGA and FLEX.

A derate is not FLEX. FLEX uses an assumed temperature and the crew can still push the levers to TOGA. A derated thrust depends on the real outside temperature, and the crew may not set TOGA during a derated takeoff below the speeds of the engine failure after V1 technique (the only exception is the windshear recovery). So the FCOM expects FLEX to give the better margin in most cases, and keeps the derate for limiting runways. The lower thrust also lowers the minimum control speeds VMCG and VMCA.

480 t, 3000 m, sea level, 20 °C, CONF 1+F. TAKEOFF RUN > DERATED: D12 is chosen, the deepest level this TOW permits (D16, D20, D24 greyed). RESULTS reads DERATED D12*, MTOW(perf) 501.6* t is the D12 limit (the same take-off at FLEX: 44 °C, MTOW(perf) 570 t).

items: Three exclusive choices. TOGA, FLEX and DERATED are three buttons of the TAKEOFF RUN panel: a derate and FLEX cannot be combined (FCOM: on the aircraft too, the MFD takes either a level or a FLEX temperature). The Thrust input of the AIRCRAFT section follows the same choice, both ways.

The level picker D04 to D24 replaces the FLEX slider. The levels the TOW does not permit are greyed. DERATED starts at the deepest permitted level; the deepest one is written at the right ("D12 max").

RESULTS shows `DERATED D12*` in its header; with a shallower level than the deepest one it adds the maximum, e.g. `DERATED D04* (max D12)`. The speeds, MTOW(perf), the margin and the run are those of the chosen level.
If DERATED is chosen and no level is possible at this weight, the run goes back to TOGA with the message Derate Not Possible.

blocks.text: D04 picked by hand: header DERATED D04* (max D12), MTOW(perf) 547.2* t, the run needs 2197 m of the 2947 m available.
All derate values are estimates of the FBW model (amber, with a star):

items: Weight limit = the TOGA weight limit at the actual OAT x (1 - level %). In the pictures: TOGA limit 570 t, so D04 = 570 x 0.96 = 547.2 t and D12 = 570 x 0.88 = 501.6 t. In DERATED mode MTOW(perf) shows this derated limit.
Default level = the deepest level whose limit is still at or above the TOW (D12 for 480 t above: D16 would allow only 478.8 t).

Speeds: as for TOGA, with VMCG and VMCA lowered by the square root of the thrust ratio. The FCOM says that a lower thrust lowers them but gives no values: this factor is our estimate. When the speeds are set by the stall margin (V2 at least 1.13 VS1G), they do not change.
Takeoff run: the V1, VR and 35 ft distances are computed for the thrust of the level.

blocks.text: FLEX is not permitted on a contaminated runway (FCOM PER-TOF-CTA); a derate is permitted on dry, wet and contaminated runways. So on a contaminated runway the flyPad offers TOGA and DERATED only. The A380 calculator still computes dry runways only: wet and contaminated runways still show the "runway condition not supported" message (see Limitations).

children.title: On the MFD: DERATED company T.O data

items: Send to FMS with DERATED sends the thrust DERATED and its level with the speeds of that level.
The RECEIVED COMPANY T.O DATA page shows the thrust as `DRT D12` (TEMP: dashes).
INSERT sets PERF T.O to DERATED with the level. The engines then use the derated limit: the E/WD shows the level (e.g. D12) and the takeoff N1 is lower than the TOGA one.
A CPNY T.O REQUEST for DERATED carries no level (the request page has none): the flyPad then picks the deepest permitted level.
A320: no derate. The A320 calculator never offers it, and the MCDU refuses a DERATED uplink with INVALID TAKEOFF UPLINK.

children.title: On the PFD and the ECAM during the takeoff

items: FMA: with a derated takeoff and the thrust levers at FLX/MCT, the first column of the PFD FMA shows `MAN` over `DTO` in a white box (not `MAN FLX +XX`, which is for a FLEX takeoff). This needs the fix e54ede63e (FMA shows MAN DTO for a derated takeoff).

No TOGA: TOGA is not allowed for a derated takeoff (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70). With a derate selected, thrust levers at TOGA, even for a moment (e.g. pushed through TOGA on the way to FLX/MCT), trigger the master caution ENG THR LEVERS NOT SET, as on the real A380. The ECAM action is `THR LEVERS ... MCT/FLEX`. So set the levers straight to FLX/MCT.

The derate is computed for dry runways only. Why: The Airbus charts behind the calculator are dry only, and the FCOM has no wet or contaminated A380 takeoff numbers (only the rules and the crosswind table). What to do: Wet and contaminated runways show "runway condition not supported": no result.

Derate speeds, weight limits and distances are estimates (amber *). Why: The FCOM gives the levels and the rules, not the performance per level; the VMC decrease factor is our own. What to do: Use them for simulation and training only.

No "optimum derate" for a VMCG-limited takeoff. Why: The FCOM caution not to use a derate deeper than the one giving the highest MTOW(perf) applies to VMCG-limited takeoffs. The chart model has no VMCG-limited weight, so it cannot find that optimum: the deepest level is simply the deepest one the TOW permits.
Calculate the takeoff as usual (see the A380 takeoff calculator above).
In TAKEOFF RUN press DERATED (or choose DERATED in the AIRCRAFT Thrust input): the deepest permitted level is selected.
Pick another level if you want a smaller reduction; check MTOW(perf), the speeds and the margin.
Press Send to FMS, then on the MFD PERF T.O: RECEIVED CPNY T.O, check `DRT Dnn`, INSERT.
For the takeoff, set the thrust levers straight to FLX/MCT: TOGA is not allowed with a derate, and even passing through TOGA triggers ENG THR LEVERS NOT SET. The PFD FMA shows MAN DTO.

blocks.text: On the A380 the flight plan, the winds and the takeoff data come from the airline by datalink (FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-40-90). A request takes time: the button shows REQUEST PENDING... until the answer, and NO COMPANY REPLY appears when nothing comes within 4 minutes. FBW answered instantly; now the answer arrives after a reply time you choose.
flyPad > Settings > Realism: Company Datalink Reply Time, Real by default.

head: Setting
Answer to a request
Message sent without a request (e.g. SEND TO FMS)
