blocks.text: Airbus gives no figure: these are typical airline values, below the 4 minute limit of the FCOM.

items: INIT > CPNY F-PLN REQUEST opens COMPANY F-PLN REQUEST (flight number, company route, free text).
Press SEND F-PLN REQUEST. The button becomes REQUEST PENDING..., here and on INIT; one request at a time.
After the reply time the SimBrief flight plan is delivered to the FMS, as before.
If SimBrief does not answer (no network, no flight plan), NO COMPANY REPLY appears after 4 minutes.

blocks.text: Request sent: REQUEST PENDING... (greyed until the answer).
INIT shows the pending request too.
Without a Navigraph account or a SimBrief ID in the flyPad settings: NO NAVIGRAPH USER, no request.

items: CPNY WIND REQUEST (INIT or WIND page, or SEND WIND REQUEST on the COMPANY WIND DATA REQUEST page): the winds are delivered after the reply time (see "Company winds" below).

Takeoff data (PERF T.O > CPNY T.O REQUEST, see the A380 takeoff calculator above): the answer of the flyPad Send to FMS reaches the FMS not before the reply time of the request; without a request, after the transit time only.
Real, request sent: REQUEST PENDING... for one to two minutes, then the data.
Instant: The data at once, as before this change.

A second request while one is pending: Not possible: the button stays REQUEST PENDING.... (F-PLN request). For winds, the CPNY WIND REQUEST button of the plan that asked still opens the COMPANY WIND DATA REQUEST page, whose SEND WIND REQUEST button reads REQUEST PENDING.... and does nothing.
No answer: NO COMPANY REPLY after 4 minutes.
No Navigraph user / SimBrief ID: NO NAVIGRAPH USER; nothing is sent.
The reply times are typical values. Why: Airbus publishes no figure for the airline answer. What to do: Choose Fast or Instant if you prefer.
The A32NX MCDU uplink stays instant. Why: This change is for the A380 FMS; the A320 uplink has its own messages.

blocks.text: The A380X WIND page and its company wind request come from FlyByWire master (merged into `core/a380x-mfd-fms`). FlyByWire's wind request goes through the ATSU and delivers the answer of SimBrief at once; two rules were put back on top of it, and a third closes a gap:

items: The reply time applies to the winds again. The request time is recorded per flight plan and the answer is held until the reply time of the flyPad setting (Instant, Fast, Real) has passed; REQUEST PENDING... stays up meanwhile. Without this, only the company flight plan was delayed.

One wind request per flight plan, NO COMPANY REPLY after 4 minutes (A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-40-90). The FMC remembers which flight plan asked: REQUEST PENDING... shows on the CPNY WIND REQUEST button and on the COMPANY WIND DATA REQUEST page of that plan only; on another plan the button is disabled (one company request at a time). If no answer comes within 4 minutes, NO COMPANY REPLY appears and a late answer is refused. Without this, a reload of the systems left REQUEST PENDING... up until a flight reload.
SEND F-PLN REQUEST is blocked while a wind request is pending (the FMC dropped such a request silently).
flyPad > Settings > Realism > Company Datalink Reply Time (F-PLN, Winds, T.O Data): Instant, Fast or Real (default).
Send the company requests as usual (CPNY F-PLN REQUEST, CPNY WIND REQUEST, CPNY T.O REQUEST) and wait for the answer while the button shows REQUEST PENDING....

blocks.text: Before the descent, the crew checks that the aircraft can land on the planned runway: the landing distance for the runway condition and braking, the margin left, the approach speed VAPP and the go-around performance. On the real A380 this is the LDG PERF application of the OIS (FCOM PER-LND); on the A320 it is the QRH (in flight) and the FCOM tables (dispatch). This page does both, with the data of each aircraft.

items: IN-FLIGHT (default): the actual landing distance for the braking mode you will use, as in the QRH / OIS, with the stop margin.
DISPATCH: the regulatory (factored) required landing distance, to check a runway before departure.

blocks.text: The A380 landing screen before any input. Amber labels are the inputs still missing for a calculation.

head: Part
Contents
rows: The ICAO code; Fill data from imports the data from the FMS (A380 FMC / A320 MCDU), the OFP (SimBrief) or the METAR.
Runway from the list (or Manual), heading, landing distance available (LDA), elevation, slope, and on the A380 the go-around altitude.
Runway condition, wind (direction/speed), OAT, QNH; on the A380 the anti-ice and air conditioning (they change the go-around gradient).
Landing weight (MLW button = the maximum landing weight), landing configuration, and on the A380 the approach type, the required go-around gradient and the VLS increment.
Manual landing or autoland, braking mode, reverse thrust, and on the A320 the overweight procedure.
The results in the OIS layout (below).
A picture of the runway with the touchdown, the stop point of each braking mode, the stop margin, and on the A380 the BTV lines and the runway exits.

blocks.text: Fill data from: FMS (destination, runway, predicted landing weight and the PERF APPR QNH, temperature, wind and landing configuration), OFP or METAR.

items: In flight, with the destination and the arrival runway in the flight plan and PERF APPR filled: choose FMS and press Fill data from. Otherwise type the airport, choose the runway and fill the conditions.
Check the landing weight (the FMS prediction) and the configuration.
Choose the braking mode you plan to use (manual, autobrake LO / 2 / 3 / HI, or BTV).
Press Calculate.

blocks.text: Dry runway, 3000 m, 380 t, CONF FULL, manual braking: landing distance 1130 m, stop margin 1870 m, VAPP 141 kt (VLS 136 + 5). The landing roll shows where each braking mode would stop.
Reading the results

head: Line
Meaning
rows: The highest landing weight the runway and the go-around allow: the lower of the weight whose landing distance just fits the LDA and the weight that still gives the required go-around gradient. It is a performance limit, not the structural maximum landing weight (395 t on the A380): it can be above it. Above the structural MLW the page shows OVERWEIGHT LANDING.
WGT: your weight is below MLW(perf), nothing limits you. LDA (red): the landing distance limits the weight. ACG: the go-around gradient limits it.
The landing configuration used (with AUTO CONF: the one the page chose).
In flight: the actual landing distance for the braking mode. Dispatch: the required (regulatory) distance.
LDA minus the landing distance. Negative (red): the aircraft does not stop on the runway.
The go-around speed and the climb gradient of the go-around configuration.
VLS of the landing configuration + the VLS increment (the wind increment, or what you enter).
The actual landing distance (ALD), the wind taken into account, the go-around configuration, and whether reverse thrust was credited.

blocks.text: Colours follow the flyPad takeoff calculator: green values come from Airbus data; values in amber with a star (*) are estimates of a model fitted on that data (see Limitations).
A380 braking modes: Manual, autobrake LO, 2, 3, HI (picture taken before the BTV mode was added: the list now ends with BTV, see "A380 landing calculator: BTV braking mode" below).
Landing configuration: CONF FULL, CONF 3 or AUTO CONF (the page chooses, as the OIS does).
Same landing with autobrake 3: 1507 m. The stop point of the chosen mode is highlighted; the others stay visible for comparison.

AUTO CONF (A380, FCOM PER-LND): CONF FULL when its go-around in CONF 3 gives the required gradient, otherwise CONF 3 with a go-around in CONF 2; for an overweight landing, CONF 3 with a go-around in CONF 1+F.

The runway condition follows the runway condition codes (RWYCC): dry, wet, water and slush 1/4" or 1/2", compacted snow, ice. The crosswind limit of the condition is shown at the top of the landing roll.

items: Reverse thrust is credited only on a contaminated runway (FCOM: no credit on dry and wet runways); the result line says REVERSE THRUST CREDIT or NO REVERSE THRUST CREDIT.
On the A380, BTV is prohibited on a contaminated runway (FCOM LIM-32-30): the BTV line says so and advises autobrake 3.
With 1/2" of water or slush, a message reminds you that Airbus does not recommend these distances: a deeper contaminant gives a shorter distance in the data.

blocks.text: Wet runway, autobrake 3.
Water 1/4" with reverse thrust: credited, BTV prohibited, crosswind limit 15 kt.

On the A380, the page shows the BTV DRY and WET lines: where the aircraft stops with the BTV decelerations (FCOM DSC-32-10-30-20), from 400 m after the threshold plus 5 s of roll. When the runway comes from the list and a Navigraph account is linked, the runway exits of the airport map are drawn and rated:

head: Exit
Meaning
rows: The first exit beyond the WET line (the FCOM SOP choice, even on a dry runway).
Between the DRY and WET lines: only on a dry runway.

blocks.text: Without the runway list or the Navigraph data, the line says "Select the runway in the list for its exits". This is information for your briefing: the BTV selection itself is made on the OANS, as on the real aircraft.

DISPATCH gives the required landing distance used to check a runway before departure: the actual distance divided by 0.6 on a dry runway, ×1.15 on a wet one, and on a contaminated runway the higher of the wet value and ALD ×1.15 (A380 FCOM PER-LND). Braking is manual (the braking mode is greyed out). The orange bar is the required distance.
Dispatch on the same runway: required landing distance 1883 m (REG LDG DIST).

children.title: When the runway is too short or the aircraft too heavy

blocks.text: 1600 m wet runway at 420 t: OVERWEIGHT LANDING (above the 395 t MLW), limitation code LDA in red, negative stop margin (-172 m): the aircraft does not stop on this runway with autobrake 3.

The A320 uses the same screen with its own data: the QRH in-flight landing distances (shown ×1.15, the QRH margin) and the FCOM dispatch tables (PER-LDG-DIS-RLD) with the autoland correction and the wet minimum. Braking modes are Manual, LO and MED; the Overweight Procedure switch applies the QRH overweight landing corrections. There is no go-around section.
A320 in flight: 62 t, 2400 m dry, autobrake MED: 1382 m (1590 m with the 15 % margin).
A320 dispatch on a wet runway: required 1741 m from the FCOM tables (green: Airbus data).

items: Inputs missing: Amber labels; the Calculate button stays dim until they are filled.
Fill data from FMS without a flight plan: Only what the FMS has is filled; complete the rest by hand.
Dry or wet runway, reverse thrust on: NO REVERSE THRUST CREDIT: the FCOM gives none there.
Contaminated runway: Longer distances, lower crosswind limit; A380: BTV prohibited.
Landing weight above the MLW: OVERWEIGHT LANDING in the RESULTS; A380 AUTO CONF lands in CONF 3.
LW above MLW(perf): Limitation code LDA or ACG in red; the stop margin may be negative.
Change of an input after Calculate: Press Calculate again.

Most A380 values are estimates (amber *). Why: The only public A380 landing data is the landing field length chart of the Airbus A380 Aircraft Characteristics (dry, manual, CONF FULL). The other cases use a model fitted on it (0.8 % error on the chart) and the FCOM rules. What to do: Use the results for training and planning, not as certified data.
Autobrake and BTV distances are estimates. Why: They come from the autobrake decelerations of the FCOM, not from Airbus tables.
BTV exits need the runway from the list and a Navigraph account. Why: The exits come from the Navigraph airport map (the OANS data). What to do: Choose the runway in the list; link Navigraph.
No BTV on the A320. Why: The A320 has no BTV.
The go-around gradient is calibrated on one FCOM example. Why: No A380 go-around tables are public.

In flight, with the destination, the arrival runway and PERF APPR (QNH, temperature, wind) in the FMS: flyPad > Performance > Landing, Fill data from FMS. Otherwise type the airport, choose the runway and enter the conditions.
Keep IN-FLIGHT (DISPATCH before departure), check the landing weight and the configuration, choose the braking mode and reverse thrust.
Press Calculate; read LDG DIST, STOP MARGIN, VAPP and the landing roll; on the A380 note the recommended BTV exit.

children.title: A380 landing calculator: BTV braking mode

blocks.text: The A380 can land with the Brake To Vacate (BTV) autobrake. The calculator gave the BTV DRY and WET lines and the exit advice, but BTV was not a braking mode. A380 FCOM DSC-32-20-220: the BTV landing distance is the BTV DRY line on a dry runway and the BTV WET line on a wet one (autoland plus autobrake distances until an exit is selected). BTV is now the last entry of the Brk mode list.

items: IN-FLIGHT, dry runway, Brk mode BTV: LDG DIST = the BTV DRY line of the landing roll; the BTV stop point is drawn with the other modes.
IN-FLIGHT, wet runway, BTV: LDG DIST = the BTV WET line.
Contaminated runway, BTV: Error "BTV: dry or wet runway only", no result (BTV is prohibited there, FCOM LIM-32-30). With another mode, the landing roll shows no BTV stop point.
DISPATCH: Braking is manual (the mode is greyed), as before.
The BTV distance is an estimate (amber). Why: The BTV lines come from the BTV decelerations of the FCOM (DSC-32-10-30-20), not from Airbus tables. What to do: Use it for planning only.
Selecting BTV here does not arm BTV in the cockpit. Why: On the aircraft the BTV runway and exit are selected on the OANS. What to do: Select the exit on the OANS.
On the Landing page, in IN-FLIGHT, set Brk mode to BTV on a dry or wet runway.
Press Calculate and compare LDG DIST with the exits shown under the landing roll.

children.title: A380 landing calculator: 40 kt crosswind on dry and wet runways

blocks.text: The landing calculator limited the crosswind to 35 kt on dry and wet runways (A380 FCOM PER-LND-CTA-CWD). The A380 FCOM revision for the EA engines (the GP7200 of the FBW A380X) increases the maximum certified crosswind at landing from 35 kt to 40 kt, gust included. The contaminated runway values are unchanged: 20 kt with slush or dry snow, 15 kt with standing water or compacted snow, 5 kt on ice. The 30 kt takeoff limit is unchanged too.

items: Dry or wet runway, crosswind up to 40 kt: The calculation runs without a question; the crosswind limit shown at the top of the landing roll is 40 kt.
Crosswind above 40 kt: A question "Crosswind above 40 kt": "The crosswind of N kt is above the maximum of 40 kt for this runway condition. Calculate anyway?"
Contaminated runway: The lower limit of the condition (20, 15 or 5 kt), as before.
Enter the wind as usual (or Fill data from FMS / METAR); the page computes the crosswind component.
If the question appears, answer it: the result is computed anyway when you accept.

blocks.text: The FMS computes the top of descent (T/D) for the managed descent. The crew still needs other answers: how long an emergency descent takes, where to start a descent at a given V/S, whether the aircraft is late on the profile after a shortcut, and a cross-check of the FMS T/D. The A380 OIS has an in-flight descent module for this (FCOM PER-IFT-DES); this page does the same on both aircraft, and replaces the old Top of Descent calculator.
It uses the same flight and engine models as the FBW FMS predictions, so its T/D agrees with the one drawn on the ND for the same inputs.
The descent calculator. Amber labels: inputs still needed.

head: Part
Contents
rows: Cruise level (or the current altitude when lower), destination elevation + 1500 ft, gross weight, the FMS speed limit, the ECON speeds and the distance to the destination.

ECON: the managed descent speeds of the FMS. Standard: the FCOM speed schedule (A380 M.85 / 300 kt / 250 kt below FL100; A320 M.78 / 300 / 250). Given V/S: a constant vertical speed. Emergency: MMO / VMO with the speed brakes.
Initial altitude (A/C: the current one) and target altitude; speed brakes.
Mach, speed, speed limit and its altitude. Empty = the standard values shown in grey.
Gross weight, ISA deviation (A/C: from the current temperature), wind component (positive = headwind, negative = tailwind), anti-ice (off / engine / total), fuel factor.
Time, distance, fuel, mean V/S and flight path angle, and the "3 × altitude" rule of thumb for comparison; the crossover altitude and where the aircraft slows to the speed limit.
With the distance to the target: when to start down, or how late you are.
Profile chart or table every 5000 ft.

items: Press Fill data from FMS in cruise with a flight plan, or type the initial altitude, the target altitude and the weight.
Choose the descent type and, if needed, the wind component and anti-ice.
Press Calculate.

blocks.text: FL380 to 1500 ft, 420 t, 20 kt tailwind, standard speeds: 22 min, 140 NM, 1022 kg, -1660 ft/min on average (-2.5°). The chart shows the T/D, the crossover altitude (Mach to CAS), the deceleration (DECEL) and the speed limit (SPD LIM).

Table view: time, distance, fuel, CAS, Mach, TAS, RATE (rate of descent, ft/min) and GRDT (descent gradient, degrees) every 5000 ft, named and signed like the FCOM table results (PER-IFT-DES-DSR: both positive in descent); the crossover, DECEL and SPD LIM lines in blue. The RESULTS line gives V/S and FPA negative, as set on the FCU.
The deceleration to the speed limit is flown on the -1° idle path of the FMS descent strategy, which is why the profile flattens between DECEL and SPD LIM.

Enter the distance to the target (Fill data from FMS enters the distance to the destination). The page reads the aircraft altitude and ground speed (shown top right of the box) and compares the aircraft with the profile. The aircraft is the triangle on the chart.
160 NM to go, T/D at 140 NM: "Start the descent in 20 NM (3 min)".
95 NM to go at FL380: "45 NM late for the profile: V/S -3000 ft/min (FPA -3.6°) to the target".
After a shortcut, the late message gives the V/S (or FPA) that still makes the target, to set in V/S or FPA mode, or tells you to use the speed brakes.

Given V/S adds a V/S field. The page flies that V/S with the thrust it needs. Where the V/S is steeper than an idle descent can give, the page flies idle there and says so in amber (the aircraft cannot descend faster at idle without speed brakes).
2000 ft/min: shallower than idle at high level (149 NM, more fuel: 2605 kg), and steeper than idle below FL150, where the page flies idle.
Emergency uses MMO / VMO with the speed brakes extended (the schedule fields turn grey).
Emergency descent from FL380: 8 min, 62 NM, -4550 ft/min on average.
ECON needs the FMS: it asks the FMS for its managed descent speeds. Without a flight plan in the FMS, a message says so and the page stays on the previous type.
ECON without FMS data.

Anti-ice (engine or total) raises the idle thrust and flattens the descent. Its effect uses the corrections of the A320 FCOM descent table (no A380 table is public): the values it changes turn amber with a star. The fuel factor (a percentage) scales the fuel burn, like the FMS PERF FACTOR.
Total anti-ice: 138 NM, 23 min, 1475 kg, in amber (estimate).

items: Inputs missing: Amber labels; no results.
Any input changed: The results are cleared: press Calculate again.
Target above the initial altitude: Message "The target altitude must be below the initial altitude".
Initial altitude above the aircraft ceiling, or weight out of range: A message gives the limit (maximum altitude, or the weight range from the empty weight to the MTOW).
Given V/S steeper than idle: Amber line: idle descent below the altitude it names.
ECON without FMS flight plan: "No FMS data: enter a flight plan in the FMS".
Distance to target larger than the descent: Green "Start the descent in X NM (Y min)".
Distance shorter than the descent: Amber "N NM late for the profile" with the V/S and FPA needed.

The descent is a still-air profile plus a mean wind. Why: The wind is one component for the whole descent, as in the FCOM and OIS; the FMS uses the wind of each altitude. What to do: Use the mean wind of the descent.
About 8 % longer than the A320 FCOM table. Why: The FCOM table is for the CFM56 A320; the FBW A320neo engine model idles differently. What to do: Compare with the FMS T/D, which uses the same model.
Anti-ice values are estimates. Why: Only the A320 FCOM has anti-ice descent corrections.
No descent path constraints or approach. Why: The page computes a clean descent to one target altitude, not the FMS path with its constraints. What to do: Use it as a cross-check of the FMS.
In cruise with a flight plan: flyPad > Performance > Top of Descent, Fill data from FMS (or type the initial and target altitudes and the weight).
Choose the descent type (ECON, Standard, Given V/S, Emergency), the wind component and anti-ice.
Press Calculate; read TIME, DIST, FUEL, V/S and FPA, and the DESCENT CHECK line (start in X NM, or late with the V/S needed).

blocks.text: After a calculation, a quick answer to "what if I start down earlier (vectors) or later (a shortcut)?" without a new calculation: the V/S and path angle the moved descent needs, against the calculated ones.

children.title: What if the descent starts earlier or later?

blocks.text: After a calculation, the T/D distance slider under the profile moves the start of the descent: to the left farther from the target (earlier, e.g. vectors), to the right closer (later, e.g. a shortcut), up to 60 NM each way. The chart draws the moved top of descent dashed, straight to the target, and the line under the slider gives the V/S and the path angle it needs, to compare with the calculated ones.

items: Later: steeper than the idle descent: the figures turn amber, "speed brakes or a higher speed needed" (red when the calculation already used the speed brakes: start earlier).
Earlier: shallower than the idle descent: "thrust needed, more fuel".
The figures keep the mean ground speed of the calculated descent: an estimate for the decision, not a new calculation.

blocks.text: Slider 25 NM later: 115 NM, -2020 ft/min, -3.0°: steeper than idle.
Slider 25 NM earlier: 165 NM, -1410 ft/min, -2.1°: shallower.
The Calculate and Clear buttons are at the bottom of the page, where they are on the takeoff and landing pages.

items: Calculate a descent.
Move the T/D distance slider under the profile: left = earlier (farther from the target), right = later.
Read the line under the slider: the V/S and FPA needed, and whether speed brakes or thrust are needed.

children.title: Descent calculator: target waypoint from the flight plan

blocks.text: The target of a descent is often a waypoint with an altitude constraint (the first constraint of the STAR, a crossing restriction from ATC), not the destination. The FMS (A380 FMC, A32NX MCDU) now sends the waypoints ahead of the aircraft, up to the missed approach, with their altitude constraints and their distance along the route. The Target wpt list of the flyPad picks one as the target.

items: The list shows each waypoint with its constraint written as on the F-PLN: `9000` (at), `+9000` (at or above), `-9000` (at or below), `11000/9000` (window). A dash = no target waypoint (the destination).

Picking a waypoint sets the target altitude from its constraint (the upper altitude of a window, to the nearest 100 ft; a waypoint without a constraint keeps the target altitude you entered) and the distance to target along the flight plan.
The distance follows the aircraft: it is refreshed every 5 s. When the waypoint is sequenced, the target waypoint is cleared.
Typing a distance yourself clears the target waypoint (the distance is no longer the waypoint's).
The waypoints need the FMS. Why: They come from the active flight plan. What to do: Without a flight plan the list holds only the dash.
Climb constraints of the SID are not used as targets. Why: An "at or above altitude 2" constraint is a climb constraint.
In cruise, with a STAR in the flight plan: Top of Descent page, Fill data from FMS.
Open Target wpt and pick the waypoint with the constraint you must meet.
Press Calculate and watch the DESCENT CHECK line as you fly.

children.title: Shared landing calculators above the tailwind limit

blocks.text: The shared A380 and A320 landing calculators no longer stop with an error when the tailwind is above the limit of the aircraft data (A380 10 kt, A320 15 kt, compared in whole knots). The distances, the stop margin and the MLW(PERF) continue the tailwind correction of the data, and the result is flagged as extrapolated. This is so that the A380X OIT LDG PERF of `core/a380x-ois` calculates like develop. The flyPad landing page of this branch reads the flag and keeps stopping at the limit with its message, as before.

items: The flyPad page shows no figures above the tailwind limit. Why: The extrapolated display, the red wind banner and the Wind check tab need the redesigned flyPad page kit and are on `core/efb-redesign`. What to do: Use core/efb-redesign, or the OIT LDG PERF of core/a380x-ois.
A tailwind less than half a knot above the limit is no longer refused. Why: The limit is now compared in whole knots (10.4 kt counts as 10 kt).
flyPad > Performance > Landing: as before; above the tailwind limit the page gives its message and no result.

children.title: A380X pedestal printer: FMS pages and the ATIS on paper

blocks.text: The A380 has a printer on the pedestal. The FMS prints its data (initialization, takeoff, winds, flight reports) and the ATC COM prints the ATIS, so the crew has them on paper. The printer now works as on the FBW A320: the sheet comes out of the printer, you tear it off and read it.

head: From
What prints
rows: F-PLN INIT, T.O DATA, WIND DATA; the active flight plan PRE-FLIGHT, IN-FLIGHT and POST-FLIGHT reports; the SEC 1 to 3 reports; the AUTO PRINT options (company data on reception, reports at engine start, takeoff and shutdown)
PRINT of a secondary flight plan
PRINT of one ATIS, PRINT ALL (all the ATIS on one printout), and the auto print (printer icon) when an ATIS is received

blocks.text: FMS DATA / PRINTER: the PRINT buttons and the AUTO PRINT options.
ATC COM ATIS: the printer icon (auto print) and PRINT ALL.

items: Each printout starts with its title, the date and the time (UTC); an ATIS printout shows the time of the ATIS message.
A sheet holds 45 lines: a longer page (e.g. a flight report) comes out on several sheets, one after the other.
Click the sheet in the printer to tear it off: it goes on the pedestal (or the captain's pull-out table), where you can page through the torn sheets and discard them, as on the A320.

blocks.text: FM ACTIVE PREFLIGHT REPORT.
FM ACTIVE TAKE-OFF DATA.
ATC COM ATIS printout.

head: Limitation
Why
rows: The paper needs the aircraft-large-files companion

the FBW A380 cockpit model has no paper nodes: they are in the aircraft-large-files companion pedestal printer paper (36b4bd9 on the fork TCdr/aircraft-large-files). Without it the printouts still reach the flyPad Printouts page
The paper looks like the A320 one
the paper, its animation and its buttons come from the A320 printer

items: Printer powered (AC 1) and ON (green window on the printer control panel).
MFD FMS > DATA > PRINTER: press the PRINT of the page or report; or SEC INDEX > PRINT; or ATC COM > ATIS: PRINT (OPTIONS menu), PRINT ALL, or the printer icon for the auto print.
Watch the sheet come out of the printer, click it to tear it off.
Read the torn sheets on the pedestal (or the CPT pull-out table when it is out): page through them, discard them.

children.title: A380X ATC COM print: SD mailbox and MSG RECORD

blocks.text: The FCOM lets the crew print an ATC message from the mailbox (DSC-46-10-20-60) and the message record from the MFD (DSC-46-10-20-30 P 29, DSC-46-10-40 P 30). These buttons said PRINTER NOT AVAIL; they now print on the pedestal printer, through the same queue as the FMS prints.

head: From
What prints
Printout title
rows: The message displayed in the mailbox; PRINTING in the information area while it prints
MFD ATC COM > MSG RECORD (list): PRINT ALL
All the recorded messages: for each one its time, direction, station and status, then its text, in 64 columns
MFD ATC COM > MSG RECORD (zoom): PRINT
The message shown in the zoom

blocks.text: A stray closing brace at the end of the printed CPDLC text is gone. With the printer off or unpowered, the buttons show PRINTER NOT AVAIL (see the printer buttons below).

items: SD mailbox: with the message displayed, press PRINT.
MFD ATC COM > MSG RECORD: PRINT ALL for the whole record, or ZOOM a message and PRINT it.
Tear the sheet off the pedestal printer as for any printout.

blocks.text: Neither cockpit model had an animated printer door. A click on the paper door (or its latch on the A380X, its handle on the A32NX) now opens or closes it: the door swings up about its forward edge and shows the paper roll and the roller unit under the slit. The A320 FCOM has a PRINTER DOOR LATCH (DSC-45-30); the A380 FCOM does not describe the door: its look and travel are design choices. Opening the door has no effect on printing.

items: Click on the closed door (or latch / handle): The door swings up (about 80 degrees on the A380X): paper roll, roller unit and the paper going up into the slit.
Click again: The door closes.
Printing with the door open (A380X): The sheet still comes out of the slit; its lower part shows in the open compartment.

Needs the aircraft-large-files companion models. Why: The door parts, the compartment and the mechanism are in the cockpit models: A380X 27d6123 (on the pedestal paper 36b4bd9), A32NX 99237fb. What to do: Install them with this branch; a full MSFS restart is needed after a model change.
Click the printer paper door (or its latch / handle) to open it; click again to close it.

children.title: No torn paper edge left in the printer slit

blocks.text: The torn paper edge of the FBW printer (the PRINT_TORN part) stood in the slit whenever the printer was not printing: it looked like a sheet stuck in the printer. It is no longer shown on either aircraft: paper only comes out of the slit while printing.

items: Printer idle: Empty slit, no paper strip.
Printing: The sheet comes out of the slit as before; once torn off, the slit is empty again.
Nothing to set: print and tear off sheets as usual.

children.title: A380X printer control panel: ON/OFF, SLEW, TEST, ABORT

blocks.text: The A380 cockpit model has the printer control panel (ON/OFF with a green window, SLEW, TEST, ABORT), but nothing was clickable. The printer is supplied by AC 1 (FCOM DSC-46-20-70). The A380 FCOM does not describe the buttons: SLEW, TEST and ABORT follow the usual printer functions (design choices).

head: Button
What it does
rows: Switches the printer on or off. The green window shows while the printer is on and AC 1 is powered. Off or unpowered: an FMS print shows PRINTER NOT AVAIL (type II, FCOM DSC-22-FMS-20-110) and nothing prints; the ATC COM prints show their PRINTER NOT AVAIL.
Prints the test page: PRINTER TEST, date and time, lines of the character set, END OF TEST.
Drops the sheets waiting to be printed.

items: The green window needs the aircraft-large-files companion. Why: Its emissive material is in the companion change 8c14d21 (on the door 27d6123). What to do: Install it; restart MSFS.
No buttons on the A32NX printer. Why: The A32NX model has no printer button parts (the FCOM SLEW switch, DSC-45-30): it needs model work.
Keep the printer ON (green window) to print.
SLEW to feed a blank sheet, TEST to check the printer, ABORT to cancel a long printout.

children.title: flyPad ground: taxi route, ATC frequencies and GSX

blocks.text: Before taxiing, the crew gets a taxi clearance from ATC such as "taxi to holding point runway 09 via M, K, A". On an unknown airport, following it on the chart is where mistakes happen: a wrong turn, a runway crossed without clearance. This page draws the route of the clearance on the airport map, lists the runways it crosses and stops it at the runway holding point.

The real A380 has no taxi routing: its OANS (the airport map on the ND) only lets the crew place green flags and white crosses (FCOM DSC-34-10-70-20), and MSFS has no datalink taxi clearance (D-TAXI). So the route is built on the flyPad, and the cockpit displays stay as the FCOM describes them. On the A380, the accepted route is marked on the OANS with those green flags (see "A380X: the accepted taxi route on the OANS" below).

items: Departure (default): from a gate, a ramp or cargo stand, or the aircraft position, to a runway entry.
Arrival: from the runway exit you plan to take (or the aircraft position) to your gate.
The page suggests the shortest route; you type the taxiways of the ATC clearance and accept it.

Navigraph account linked in the flyPad settings (third party options). The airport map comes from the Navigraph airport database, the same data as the A380 OANS. Without it the page says "No airport database".
Airport: type the ICAO code, or press ORIG / DEST to take the airports of the SimBrief flight plan loaded in the flyPad. The line below shows how many gates, ramp and cargo stands the map has.
An airport that is not in the Navigraph airport database shows "Not in the Navigraph airport database".

blocks.text: The Taxi page after entering the airport: the airport map on the right, the route inputs on the left. Amber labels show what is still missing.

head: Part of the page
What it does
rows: Departure or Arrival, the ICAO code, ORIG / DEST buttons, the number of stands on the map.
Where the taxi starts: a gate / ramp / cargo stand (departure), a runway exit (arrival), or the aircraft.
Where it ends: the runway and its entry (departure), or the gate (arrival).
The taxiways of the clearance, in order. SUGGEST fills it with the shortest route, ACCEPT confirms it, the red bin clears the page.
The route as a clearance reads, its length, the taxiways and the runway crossings in red.
The airport with the route, the runway entries (cyan), the holding point (amber bar), the aircraft (yellow). Drag to move, buttons to zoom and to fit the route.

children.title: Departure: from the gate to the runway

items: Keep Departure selected and enter the airport.
In FROM, keep Gate/ramp/cargo and type your gate. While you type, the gates that match appear as buttons under the field: tap one. You can also tap the gate on the map (zoom in to see the names).
In TO, choose the runway. The entry is set to the full length entry; choose another one for an intersection departure.
The shortest route appears on the map as a dashed magenta line ending at the HOLD bar of the runway holding point.

blocks.text: Typing "4" lists the gates 40 to 47: tap one.
A name that is not on the map: the amber line says so.

Gate names are found even when they are written differently on the map: "16" finds "016", spaces and dashes do not matter. If nothing matches, the airport map uses another name (for example a letter prefix): tap the gate on the map instead.

Gate 42 to runway 09, full length: the suggested route (dashed) along M, K and A to entry S1, stopped at the holding point (HOLD 09). The route box reads it as a clearance: Gate 42 → M → K → A → S1 → Holding point RWY 09, 2.6 km.
Runway entries

The Entry list shows every taxiway that enters the runway, in order from the threshold. The first one is the full length entry; the others show the runway length remaining from them, to check an intersection departure against your takeoff performance. On the map, the entries of the selected runway are the cyan dots with their names.
The entries of runway 09: S1 full length, then C (2500 m left), B1 (1700 m), D (1500 m) and so on.
Intersection departure from D: the route stops at the holding point of D, with 1500 m of runway ahead.
Type the taxiways of your clearance in the order ATC gives them, separated by spaces (commas and dashes work too). The route then follows them strictly, in that order:

items: Short unnamed connecting lines between two cleared taxiways are allowed.
The runway entry can be left out: "via M, K, A" to a holding point still ends on the entry you chose.
While the typed route is not accepted, the box reads "Route along the clearance (not accepted)" and the line stays dashed.

blocks.text: SUGGEST copies the taxiways of the suggested route into the clearance field: a quick start when ATC clears you along the obvious way. ACCEPT confirms the route: the line turns solid. Any change (gate, runway, entry, clearance) takes the acceptance away.
After SUGGEST: the clearance field holds M K A S1, the route is a preview.
After ACCEPT: solid line, "Accepted route". On the A380 the route is also flagged on the OANS.
A different clearance, "M L A": the route goes the long way round via L (4.0 km instead of 2.6 km), as ATC asked.
A clearance with a taxiway that does not exist here, or taxiways that do not connect in that order: "No route along these taxiways, in this order". Check the spelling and the order.

Every runway the route crosses is circled in red on the map with its name, and listed in red under the route ("Crossing runway 01/19"). A runway crossing always needs its own ATC clearance: stop at the holding point before it and ask if you do not have it.
From cargo stand R2 to runway 09: taxiway A crosses runway 01/19 (red circle, red line in the route box).

children.title: Arrival: from the runway exit to the gate

items: Select Arrival and enter the airport (DEST fills it from the flight plan).
In FROM, keep Runway exit, choose the landing runway and the exit you plan to take. The exits are those of the landing calculator, with their distance from the threshold.
In TO, type or tap the gate.
Check the route, type the clearance if ATC gives another one, and ACCEPT.

blocks.text: The exits of runway 09 with their distance from the threshold.
Exit B1 to gate 44: Exit B1 → A → K → M → Gate 44. The green dot is the start.

Prepare the arrival route during the descent briefing with the exit from the landing calculator: after landing, the page is ready. If you vacate by another exit, choose it (or use the aircraft position) and the route updates.

Choose Aircraft in FROM to start the route where the aircraft is, for example after a pushback, or when ATC changes the route while you taxi. The page takes the position when you select it; press Update to take it again. The route starts on the taxi line nearest to the aircraft and prefers its heading: it does not start by turning back if there is a way ahead.
The aircraft (yellow) on M facing west, for runway 27: the route goes ahead via K and A (2.9 km) rather than turning back on M.
"The aircraft is not at this airport" means the aircraft is more than 8 km from the airport of the page.

children.title: Locate the aircraft, taxiway names of several words, proposed entry

items: Locate button (pin, under the zoom buttons): centres the map on the aircraft and zooms in until the stand names show. It is greyed when the aircraft is not at this airport.
Taxiways named with several words (e.g. SOUTH RAMP, NORTH RAMP at Montreal CYUL) are read as one taxiway in the clearance: type them as the map shows them, or press SUGGEST.

The runway entry proposed first is the first one from the threshold you can reach without crossing a runway. At CYUL, runway 24L full length (R) is across 06R/24L from the terminal: the entry proposed is the first one on the terminal side; choose R in the Entry list if ATC clears you across.

blocks.text: The whole airport, the aircraft on M.
After the locate button: centred on the aircraft, stand names shown.

items: Drag the map to move it; + / - zoom; the frame button fits the route (or the whole airport).
The map is north up. Aprons are lighter grey, taxiways dark grey, runways black with a white edge. The thin yellow lines are the taxi guidance lines the route follows.
Taxiway names are shown in yellow; the taxiways of the route in magenta. Gate names appear when you zoom in.
Tap a gate on the map to choose it (when the page asks for a gate).

blocks.text: Zoomed on the apron: the gate names, the route to gate 46 along M.

items: Airport entered, nothing else: The airport map, amber labels on the inputs still missing, the help text in the route box.
Start and end chosen: The suggested route, dashed, with its clearance text, length and crossings.
SUGGEST: The clearance field holds the taxiways of the suggested route; the route is a preview (dashed).
Clearance typed: The route follows the typed taxiways in order (dashed until accepted), or the red message "No route along these taxiways, in this order".
ACCEPT: Solid line, "Accepted route" in green (A380: green flags on the OANS).
Any input changed after ACCEPT: Back to a preview: accept again.
Departure to a runway with holding position lines: The route stops at the HOLD bar before the runway.
Two entries behind the same HOLD bar (e.g. RJTT 34R C2 and C3): The same route to the holding point: the entries only differ after it.
Gate whose lead-in is another stand's line (e.g. RJTT gate 5 behind 5R): The route leaves along that line: "Gate 5 → Gate 5R → W ...".
Runway without holding position lines on the map: The route ends on the runway entry itself and the box says "Runway 09" instead of "Holding point RWY 09".
The route crosses a runway: Red circle with the runway name on the map, red "Crossing runway" line.
Aircraft start, aircraft far from the airport: "The aircraft is not at this airport"; no route.
Leaving the page and coming back: Everything is kept, except an Aircraft start: press Aircraft or Update again.

Needs a Navigraph account. Why: The airport map (taxi lines, stands, holding points) exists only in the Navigraph airport database; MSFS does not give it to the aircraft. What to do: Link your account in the flyPad settings.

Closed taxiways, one-way taxiways and NOTAMs are unknown. Why: The airport database has the lines painted on the ground, not their status of the day. What to do: Type the taxiways of the ATC clearance: the route follows them.

The suggestion is the shortest route, not the usual one. Why: Airports have preferred flows (ATC habits, one-way loops) that are not in the data. What to do: Always check against the clearance and the airport chart.

Some real airports have gaps in their taxi lines. Why: A lead-in line may stop a few metres short of the taxi line. Gaps up to 15 m between parts that are otherwise not connected are joined; larger ones are not. What to do: If "No taxi line of the airport map connects the start to the end" appears, choose another start (the nearest taxiway, or the aircraft) or end.
Gate names follow the airport database. Why: The database may use names that differ from the gate signs. What to do: Tap the gate on the map.
No route on the A380 OANS, only flags. Why: The A380 FCOM has no taxi route display; the flags are the FCOM way to mark points on the airport map.
The aircraft position is taken once. Why: The route is a plan to check, not a moving map that follows you. What to do: Press Update after a change.

head: What you see
Why
What to do
rows: There is no route yet: the gate is not found (amber label, no terminal next to the name), or the runway / entry / exit is missing.
Pick the gate from the suggestion buttons or tap it on the map; check the amber labels.
"No such name on the airport map"
No stand of the map has this name.
Tap the gate on the map.
"No taxi line of the airport map connects the start to the end"
The start and the end are on parts of the map that are not connected.
Start from the nearest taxiway (Aircraft), or choose another gate or entry.
"No route along these taxiways, in this order"
A taxiway of the clearance is misspelt, missing, or they do not connect in that order.
Check the clearance; press SUGGEST to see the names the map uses.
Navigraph has no airport map for this airport.

items: Link your Navigraph account (flyPad > Settings > 3rd Party Options).
flyPad > Ground > Taxi: Departure or Arrival, the airport (or ORIG / DEST).
FROM: your gate (departure), the runway exit (arrival) or the aircraft; TO: the runway and its entry, or the gate.
Type the taxiways of the ATC clearance in order (or SUGGEST), check the route and the runway crossings, press ACCEPT.

children.title: A380X: the accepted taxi route on the OANS

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM has no taxi route display: the OANS lets the crew mark points of the airport with green flags (DSC-34-10-70-20). When the crew accepts a route on the flyPad, the A380X marks it with those flags, so the route can be followed on the ND.

children.title: On the A380: the route on the OANS

blocks.text: When you accept the route on the A380 flyPad, green flags appear on the OANS (the airport map on the ND) at the start of each taxiway of the route and at the gate or holding point. They are the crew flags of the FCOM ("to locate or mark a given point on the airport"), so you can remove them like any flag: click one and DELETE, or ERASE ALL SYMBOLS in the ND menu. Flags you placed yourself are never touched.

items: The flags appear when the OANS displays that airport (they come back if the OANS reloads it).
A new accepted route replaces the flags of the previous one; a route that is no longer accepted removes them.
The A320 has no OANS: nothing else changes on it.

blocks.text: The A380 ND (OANS, ARC, zoom range) at gate 42 facing south, after ACCEPT of the departure route above (gate 42 to runway 09): green flags where M, K and A start (S1 and the holding point are further west, off the picture). Harness picture: the test airport has no buildings.
Tested in the sim by the user: OK: the flags are set on ACCEPT and removed when the route changes.

items: Flags only, no route line. Why: The A380 FCOM has no route display on the OANS; flags are its way to mark points.
An Aircraft start is lost when leaving the Taxi page, so its flags go away when you come back. Why: The aircraft start is local to the page. What to do: Select Aircraft again and ACCEPT.
Accept a route on the flyPad Taxi page (A380X).
On the ND, select the OANS (ARC or ROSE, a zoom range) at that airport: the flags show the start of each taxiway and the end of the route.

children.title: Airport ATC frequencies on the taxi page

blocks.text: Before taxi the crew needs the ground, tower and delivery frequencies of the airport. The taxi page shows them in a box laid out like the frequency box of an airport chart, for the origin, the destination or the airport of the page. The Navigraph airport map has no frequencies: they come from the sim's own airport data.

items: A green Frequencies button at the bottom left of the map; it opens the FREQUENCIES box (X closes it).
Airport buttons at the top: ORIG and DEST of the SimBrief flight plan loaded in the flyPad, and Airport when the page airport is another one.

One row per chart label, in the chart order: ATIS, AWOS, ASOS, CTL, APP, DEP, TWR, GND, DLV, CTAF, UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS; the frequencies in MHz, two columns, without duplicates, in the order of the sim data. Other types (ILS...) are left out.
Messages: "Enter an airport", "Loading the frequencies...", "Not in the sim's airport data", "No frequency for this airport in the sim's airport data".
The list is the sim's, not the chart's. Why: The chart's selection of frequencies is in no data the aircraft can read; MSFS lists all its frequencies. What to do: Check the chart for the one to use.
No station names, no tuning. Why: The box is a reference, like the chart box. What to do: Tune the RMP as usual.
On the Taxi page, press Frequencies (bottom left of the map).
Choose ORIG, DEST or the page airport; read the frequency you need.

blocks.text: With GSX installed, the ground services are GSX's, but the flyPad Services buttons called the sim's own vehicles. A GSX services switch now links the page to GSX through the GSX Remote API (version 2, local server on port 8744): the service buttons request the GSX services and show what GSX is doing. With the switch off the page works as before.

items: The GSX panel under the right-hand group of buttons (GPU, cargo door): the switch and a status line: "GSX not found: start GSX, with its Remote control server on (GSX settings)" (switch greyed), "GSX is starting...", "GSX found" (switch off) or "Service buttons linked to GSX, GSX menus and messages shown here".
Linked: Jet Bridge, Stairs, Fuel Truck, GPU and Catering Truck request the GSX services. The Baggage Truck button is hidden: GSX loads the bags during boarding.
The panel adds the services without an aircraft button: Deboarding, Boarding, Pushback (Departure), De-ice, Water, Lavatory, Cleaning, named as GSX names them.

Under each linked button a status line: On its way, Waiting, GSX's own phase (or In progress), Leaving, Done, with its count; a progress bar for the fuel truck from the "x / y kg" refuelling status. Button colours follow the service: amber when called or waiting, green while performed, amber and locked while leaving, dim when GSX cannot serve it.
Linking switches on the flyPad GSX Fueling and GSX Payload Synchronization (Settings > 3rd Party Options), so GSX boards the passengers and loads the fuel set on the Payload and Fuel pages.

While linked, GSX is under remote control: no GSX pop-up menu or notification in the sim. GSX's questions (menus that stay open, e.g. the choice of operator) and its messages appear on the panel; tap an answer, or "Close the GSX menu".
A request GSX refuses (e.g. boarding before the doors are open) gives the message "GSX did not accept ‹service>" with GSX's reason.
Needs GSX with its Remote control server on. Why: The link uses the GSX Remote API (GSX 4). What to do: Turn on the Remote control server in the GSX settings.

The four bugs of the first sim test (panel over the fuselage drawing, Board counter stuck at 0, passenger count not moving, switch not greyed without GSX) are fixed here but not checked in the sim on this page. Why: The fixes came after the test. `core/efb-redesign` reworks the counter (the flyPad counts the GSX passengers itself and gives GSX its passenger number) and the greyed switch again; that version is the one tested in the sim. What to do: Merge `core/efb-redesign`; report any of them if seen again.
Turning the link off leaves the GSX fuel and payload syncs on. Why: Only linking changes them. What to do: Turn them off in Settings > 3rd Party Options if wanted.
The page keeps the classic FBW look on this branch. Why: The Material 3 redesign of the Services page is in `core/efb-redesign`.
Start GSX with its Remote control server on.
flyPad > Ground > Services: when the panel says "GSX found", turn on GSX services.
Request the services with the buttons and the GSX panel; answer GSX's questions on the panel.
Turn the switch off to go back to the FBW services.

children.title: GSX external power sync when it is enabled

blocks.text: The FBW option GSX External Power Synchronization makes the external power available (`L:A32NX_EXT_PWR_AVAIL`) when the GSX GPU is connected or the jetway is requested or connected, until pushback. It only looked at GSX when a GSX state changed: enabling the option with the GPU or the jetway already connected did nothing until the next GSX change. It now checks GSX at once when it is enabled.

items: Option enabled with the GSX GPU or jetway already connected: External power available at once: EXT AVAIL on the overhead ELEC panel.
Option enabled before GSX connects: As before: available when the GPU connects.

With GSX 4, EXT AVAIL may already show before the option is enabled. Why: GSX 4 also sets the sim's own external power variable. What to do: Watch `L:A32NX_EXT_PWR_AVAIL:1` with a SimVar tool to see the sync itself.
flyPad > Settings > 3rd Party Options: turn on GSX External Power Synchronization, before or after GSX connects its GPU or jetway.
Press the EXT PWR pushbutton when AVAIL shows.

children.title: Taxi route along real ATC clearances

blocks.text: At RJTT the clearance `W A E C1 C1` typed from the aircraft after pushback gave "No route along these taxiways", and a full BeyondATC instruction ("via L4 cross runway 34L, taxi to holding point C1, runway 34R, via L4, A4B, W4, W, A, E, C1") could not be used. Real clearances leave out the apron taxiways, repeat the holding point, name runway exits and come as sentences. The route finder now accepts them:

items: Typed list or pasted instruction: the clearance field reads a list of taxiways or a pasted ATC instruction. Phraseology words (VIA, TAXI, TO, HOLDING POINT...), runway designators, the stand after STAND or GATE and frequencies are left out. The runways after CROSS (RUNWAY) are the cleared crossings. The clearance limit (after TO or HOLDING POINT) is the last taxiway. HOLD SHORT (OF) a taxiway is left out. "A-4B" is read as the airport name A4B. A name said twice in a row is one taxiway.

Apron taxiways before the clearance: before the first cleared taxiway, taxiways that are not in the clearance may lead to it, within 2000 m of the start. They cost more (x1.5), so the route joins the clearance as soon as it can. A cleared taxiway is never used out of order.

Uncleared runway crossings: in that first part, a runway crossing that the clearance does not mention costs a large penalty: the route goes round when it can; the crossing still shows on the map. "cross runway 34L" in the clearance removes the penalty.

Runway exit lines named in the clearance are cleared taxiways; a clearance that starts with the landing exit ("B1 A K M") works. Exit lines are listed in the route taxiways (SUGGEST), except the start exit.

Unknown names: the page lists the cleared names that are not a taxiway of the airport map, under the clearance field in amber ("Not a taxiway of the airport map: X9"). The field placeholder now says "e.g. A K M, or paste the ATC instruction".
From the aircraft after pushback, clearance `W A E C1 C1`: A route: the apron taxiways from the aircraft to W are added, then W A E C1.
A full ATC instruction pasted in the field: The taxiways in order (for the RJTT example L4 A4B W4 W A E C1); "Crossing runway 34L" shown if the route crosses it.
A name in the clearance that the airport map does not have: "Not a taxiway of the airport map: ‹name>" under the field.
A clearance taxiway used out of order would be shorter: Not used: the clearance order is kept.

The RJTT taxiway names A4B, W4 and L4 are not checked against the real Navigraph map. Why: No real airport map data offline: the tests use a synthetic map. What to do: Report any name listed as "Not a taxiway of the airport map".

The apron taxiways before the clearance are searched within 2000 m of the start only. Why: Keeps the route from wandering on other taxiways. What to do: Add the first taxiway to the clearance if it is further.
flyPad > Ground > Taxi: set FROM (gate, exit or Aircraft) and TO as before.
Type the cleared taxiways in order, or paste the whole ATC instruction (for example from BeyondATC) in the clearance field.
Check the route, any "Crossing runway" line and any "Not a taxiway of the airport map" line, then ACCEPT.
At RJTT (Departure, From Aircraft after pushback near gate 67, runway 34R entry C1): "W A E C1 C1" gives a route with the first taxiways added from the aircraft.
The pasted BeyondATC instruction gives L4 A4B W4 W A E C1, with "Crossing runway 34L" if L4 crosses it.
Note any name listed as "Not a taxiway of the airport map".
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: GSX power sync: the setting is re-read, so enabling it takes effect

blocks.text: Follow-up of the feature above. The flyPad switch stores the setting and signals the change through a listener that the extras host (the code that runs the GSX sync) never registers, so the change did not always reach it: turning the sync on with the GSX GPU or jetway already connected could still leave EXT PWR unavailable. The extras host now re-reads the stored setting (at most once a second) and checks the GSX power source again when the setting goes from off to on.

items: Up to one second between the switch and EXT AVAIL. Why: The setting is polled once a second.
As above: turn on GSX External Power Synchronization, before or after GSX connects its GPU or jetway.
Turn the flyPad GSX power sync on with the GSX GPU connected: EXT PWR AVAIL at once.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: External power follows the sim's ground power (GSX GPU, sim GPU, jetway)

blocks.text: The aircraft read the sim's external power only on the first frame and when the flyPad GPU button was used. A GPU or a jetway connected after the flight loaded (GSX 4, the sim GPU) did nothing until the GPU door moved. Now the external power follows the sim's ground power, whoever connects it.

items: Sim ground power appears (GSX GPU, sim GPU or jetway power), aircraft at or below 0.3 kt: EXT PWR AVAIL on the overhead (if the external power was not already available).
That sim ground power goes: EXT PWR no longer available, but only if it was connected from the sim power.
Crew connection from the flyPad GPU button, or EXT PWR set by the GSX sync: Kept: the sim power going does not remove it.
Not above 0.3 kt. Why: A moving aircraft cannot be on ground power.
Connect the ground power any way (GSX GPU or jetway, the sim GPU, or the flyPad GPU button) and press EXT PWR when AVAIL shows.
GSX GPU and jetway connect / disconnect after the flight is loaded.
The flyPad GPU button.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: flyPad Material 3 redesign and independent flyPads
Material 3 look of the Ground pages

blocks.text: The flyPad pages get a Material 3 dark look on the flyPad cyan: tonal cards, dense list rows with switches and chips, a segmented control for the tabs. A shared Material kit (page, cards, section headers, list rows, status and action chips, switch, segmented control, buttons, progress bar, banner) on new theme tokens for the blue, dark and light themes is used by every redesigned page. The Ground pages came first. The functions of the pages do not change.

head: Page
New look
rows: Three columns: the doors and the ground equipment as scrolling lists (switch or Request / Release chip, GSX status and fuel progress on the rows); the aircraft from above, nose up and zoomed on the fuselage, its doors coloured with their state, the holds and service tags (A380X two decks, A32NX one); the GSX card (switch, turnaround timeline of the departure or arrival with its Baggage step, other GSX services as chips, GSX questions and messages; a long GSX menu scrolls inside the card; see "GSX services link" and "GSX turnaround" below). Status chips: GPU, tug, doors open, chocks and cones (A32NX).

The map fills the left card. A control rail: system switch, Call / Release tug button, parking brake row, Backward / Paused / Forward, a steering dial over the direction slider, the speed slider, Left / Straight / Right and the controller switch. When the aircraft is at the SimBrief origin or destination, the Navigraph airport map (aprons, taxiways, runways, guidance lines, stands) is drawn under the pushback map, heading up.

The aircraft with its tanks on a wide card and a refuel rail (target, slider, start and stop, duration, plan summary). A380X: the whole aircraft outline with the tank quantities in tables (each feed tank now shows its own quantity; before, the four feed tanks of the drawing read feed tank 3). A32NX: the over-wing outline with its tanks filled, the quantities as tiles.
The cabin and seat map on a full-width card with the holds under it (load over capacity, click to plan), then the load table, the boarding controls and the balance chart.
The route form as cards, the runway crossings as banners, the map buttons and the frequency box in the kit.

blocks.text: Pushback map fix: the airport under the pushback map redrew only after the map centre had moved about 100 m, so the aircraft slid over a frozen airport while the map was dragged. It now follows every move.
Pushback map: only the visible airport, at most 10 times a second

The airport layer drew the whole Navigraph airport (thousands of points) on every position update, 20 times a second: the A380X ran at 21 FPS on the Pushback page against 42 FPS on another page (capture). It now draws only the shapes and lines that reach the map window, and redraws only when the picture moves by about a pixel, at most 10 times a second.
The pushback goes on when another flyPad page is opened

Leaving the Pushback page stopped the tug (with a short "Pausing Pushback" message), because the rudder pedal and sidestick steering lived in the page. The steering now runs in the captain flyPad itself, whatever page is shown (when the controller switch of the Pushback rail is on). The page resets the tug commands only when it opens with no tug attached (captain flyPad), so a pushback in progress goes on when the page is left and opened again.
A380X Services door buttons: Main 5 R and a new Main 4 R

The aft right door button said "Main 4 R" but opened MAIN 5R, the door the SD DOOR page and the FWS name. It is now labelled Main 5 R and its marker on the planform sits on door 5 R. A new Main 4 R button opens and closes MAIN 4R. The catering truck still docks at MAIN 5R: a button only moves its door; the door a ground vehicle (or GSX) docks at comes from the aircraft configuration.
A380X Services door switches: Main 4 L and Main 5 L

The A380X GSX profile boards at MAIN 1L, 2L, 4L and 5L, but the Doors card had switches only for MAIN 1L and 2L on the left side: a door GSX opened at 4L or 5L for boarding had no row and no planform marker, so it could not be closed from the flyPad. The Doors card now has the rows Main 4 L and Main 5 L, and the planform the markers 4 L and 5 L on the left side. The card lists Main 1 L, Main 2 L, Upper 1 L, Main 4 L, Main 5 L, Main 4 R, Main 5 R and the cargo row; its header counts 8 ("n open · 8"), and the list scrolls (it keeps at most half the column, so that the ground equipment keeps the other half).
A long GSX menu scrolls inside the GSX card

With a long GSX menu (e.g. "Activate Services" with 10 entries) the GSX card ran past its bottom border and the "Close the GSX menu" link lay on top of the last menu buttons. The menu ("GSX asks", its title and one chip per entry) now scrolls inside the card, a long entry is cut with "...", and "Close the GSX menu" has its own line under the entries.

Tug speed slider fix: the handle of the vertical tug speed slider of the Pushback rail sat 5 px right of its rail (the slider library offset suits its own 14 px handle, the flyPad handle is 24 px). It is now centred on the rail.

items: The airport under the pushback map needs the Navigraph airport map. Why: It is drawn from the Navigraph airport database, only at the SimBrief origin or destination. What to do: Link a Navigraph account and import a SimBrief flight plan.
A380X: no switch for MAIN 2R and UPPER 1R, the doors GSX catering uses. Why: Only the doors GSX boards at (MAIN 1L, 2L, 4L, 5L) got switches.
Spacing is made with margins, not the CSS gap. Why: The sim browser (Coherent GT) ignores the CSS gap property.
Open flyPad > Ground and pick the tab (Services, Fuel, Payload, Pushback, Taxi) at the top right.
Use the switches, chips and buttons as before: open or close a door, request a service, refuel, board, push back.

children.title: Material 3 look of the frame and of the other pages

blocks.text: The rest of the flyPad in the same Material look, so that every page matches. The shared switch, segmented selects, text fields, drop-downs and tooltips take the new look, so every page follows.

head: Part
New look
rows: A tab bar (see "Tab bar" below; first built as a navigation rail with the icon names), the status bar, the quick controls as a card (brightness sliders with their Auto switch, state tiles, sim rate tile at the bottom right), the section tabs as a segmented control.

First the flight card (airports, progress, figure tiles, route, SimBrief import) and the Important Information column; replaced by the context-aware Dashboard (see "Dashboard: the context-aware landing page" below).
Overview: the nose drawing on a wide card and the aircraft figures in three lists; OFP and Printouts in kit cards and buttons.

A shared calculator kit (form cards, labelled rows, result tiles, the fill-from button): takeoff, landing and descent results as tiles; temperature correction with one row per published altitude and its corrected value beside it. A32NX: a new Buffet tab (see "Performance > Buffet" below).
Chart list, viewer controls and pinned charts in the kit.
Type filter chips, controller cards with their buttons always shown, the COM 1 card.

One layout: the ATA chapters on the left (failure count, red count of active ones), the open chapter failures on the right as rows with a switch (red when failed). A search lists the matching failures of every chapter; Active failures lists everything failed, with Restore all. The "not yet guaranteed" note is the info icon beside the title.
The list with done / next marks and counts, the open checklist with its progress.
One page (see "Presets on one page" below): the aircraft states as a stepper and the lighting presets as a grid of slots.
Two panes: the categories beside the open page. Settings > flyPad has the theme choice, with a custom theme (see "Custom flyPad theme" below).

items: Pick a section on the navigation rail on the left, then a tab in the segmented control at the top right.
Open the quick controls from the status bar (brightness, Auto, state tiles, sim rate).

children.title: flyPad UI fixes after the redesign

blocks.text: A check of every flyPad page on both aircraft and both tablets after the redesign found 23 problems: three layout bugs and parts still in the old look or with poor texts. They are fixed:

head: Area
Fix
rows: Opened inside the two-pane Settings it was taller and wider than the pane: the button bar was cut and, with 4 axes on the A380X, Axis 4 and Save and Apply were off screen. It is now one card that fits, the axes in one row, the button bar always visible, a new detent gauge. The in-detent highlight also works at exactly 0 (its colour is now the light primary, not green).

About: the content covered the title, now in the page flow with build info rows. The open Settings category gets its icon colour and bold label (the active class was lost). Navigraph sign-in, SimBrief trash, Aircraft Options Select, Automatic Call Outs Reset and the Sim Options Calibrate button and SimBridge status in the kit look; language and keyboard selects sized like the others.
Confirmation and alert dialogs, scroll buttons, progress bar, card, divider, the critical error page and the toasts (each toast type its own colour, errors red) no longer use the old colours.

Services legend at its small size; Taxi frequencies button and panel, empty-state text, one-line database chip, Entry chevron; Payload balance chart in the new colours and font; Fuel: no "NaN %" or full bars while the tank capacities are still 0.

Presets help texts with the A380X wording (MFD with KCCU, AFS CP; the help tab has since gone, see "Presets on one page"); Performance tab "Descent"; "1 active failure", "1 failure"; descent notes without a trailing separator; the A380X descent legend names the A320 FCOM anti-ice source; chart list and pinned charts empty texts; ATC network name in capitals and an empty controller list message.

items: A tooltip (for example the one on a preset name) can stay on screen after leaving the Presets page under the mouse. Why: An older flyPad bug, not part of these fixes. What to do: Move the mouse over the flyPad again.
Nothing to set. Calibrate the throttle from flyPad > Settings > Sim Options > Calibrate as before.

children.title: Payload page: LOAD title row and balance chart

blocks.text: On the redesigned Payload page the LOAD title sat on its own line above the load table and the balance chart left an empty band in its card. Now:

items: The LOAD title sits on the PLANNED / CURRENT header row of the load table.

The SimBrief fill action is a full-width button under the table, as on the Fuel page. It shows with the same rule as before (an OFP loaded that differs from the planned load, no boarding or GSX payload sync running).
The balance chart fills the height of its card (never smaller than the former 280 px).

The weight grid ends at the lowest labelled weight (A32NX 40 t, A380X 270 t) instead of leaving an empty band under the envelope; the weight labels are centred on their grid lines, the unit sits under the lowest label, and the MTOW / MLDW / MZFW names are re-placed for the new scale.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The chart scale lives in the aircraft config files (flypad-payload.json5). What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Ground > Payload; plan the load in the table or with the SimBrief button under it.
Read the centre of gravity on the balance chart.

children.title: Independent captain and first officer flyPads

blocks.text: Both tablets showed the same flyPad: their screens share one material in the cockpit model and one gauge drew on it, so one pilot changing a page changed it for the other. Now the first officer tablet has its own flyPad gauge (`efb.html?Index=2`), with a new material on its screen in the cockpit model.

children.title: What is per tablet and what is shared

head: Per tablet
Shared
rows: The page shown and the navigation
The aircraft state (doors, services, fuel, payload)
The brightness and its Auto setting (first officer: `L:A32NX_EFB_2_BRIGHTNESS`, settings `EFB_2_*`)
A32NX: the power button (first officer: `H:A32NX_EFB_2_POWER`; before, both buttons sent the same event, so one press toggled both tablets)

blocks.text: The actions that change the shared aircraft state by themselves run on the captain flyPad only: the tug release after a pushback, the automatic loading of lighting presets, GSX remote control, the rudder pedal and sidestick steering of the pushback, and the reset of the tug commands when the Pushback page opens with no tug attached. A flyPad clears only the OANS taxi flags it has set itself.

items: Without the aircraft-large-files companion, the first officer tablet keeps showing the captain flyPad. Why: The new screen material is in the high-detail cockpit model, which lives in aircraft-large-files (A380X 24f7b02, A32NX d3060ea); the large-files pointer of this branch is not bumped yet. What to do: Merge the two large-files commits, then bump the `large-files` pointer.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: panel.cfg, the cockpit behaviour and the model change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Lighting presets load automatically from the captain flyPad only. Why: Two flyPads would load them twice. What to do: Keep the captain flyPad on.
Use each tablet on its own: open any page, import the OFP, run the checklists.
Set each tablet brightness from its own quick controls.
A32NX: each tablet has its own power button.

children.title: Quick controls clicks no longer open the troubleshooting page

blocks.text: The quick controls pane is drawn inside the status bar. When the status bar shows an issue (red), a click on it opens the troubleshooting page, so every click in the quick controls, and the click that closes them, also opened that page. The pane and its backdrop now keep their clicks, and the backdrop closes the pane on the click itself (closing on mouse down let the click land on the status bar under it).

items: Open the quick controls from the status bar, use them, close them with a click outside.
To open the troubleshooting page, click the red status bar itself.

children.title: Checklists: always loaded, green check when marked complete

items: Checklists sometimes missing. The checklist file was read without waiting for its text, so an empty list was returned; the flyPad stored (and froze) it and the checklists parsed later could not be added. The file is now read and parsed before the list is returned; a second call waits for the same read, and a failed read is tried again by the next call.

Green check. The list showed the done mark only for the checklists of the current or previous flight phases, so with the aircraft unpowered (flight phase 0) a completed checklist kept an empty circle. A checklist marked with Mark checklist as complete now shows a filled green check, whatever the flight phase. One with all items done but not marked keeps the empty circle.
Open flyPad > Checklists, pick a checklist, check its items.
Press Mark checklist as complete at the end.

children.title: Automatic lighting preset loading lists all eight presets

blocks.text: The Day, Dawn/Dusk and Night drop-downs of the automatic preset loading offered only the presets that had a name: with unnamed presets they offered only "None". They now list the eight presets as "‹number> - ‹name>" ("‹number> - Preset ‹number>" when unnamed).

items: Open flyPad > Presets and save the cockpit lighting into a preset.
Turn on Auto-load and pick a preset for Day, Dawn/Dusk and Night in the strip at the bottom.

children.title: Error details on the flyPad error screen

blocks.text: The flyPad error screen only said that something went wrong. It now shows the error (name and message), the first lines of its stack and the React components it was thrown in, so a crash can be reported and found.

items: If the flyPad shows the error screen, take a screenshot of the error box and report it.
Press Reset Display on the error screen to recover.

children.title: Landing calculator above the wind limits, with a wind check

blocks.text: A crosswind above the maximum asked "Calculate anyway?" and a tailwind above the limit gave an error and no result. Now the calculation always runs: the pilot sees the figures with a warning and can compare the other runways and the alternate. This is on this branch because it changes the redesigned performance widgets.

items: Crosswind above the maximum: Results shown, with a red banner "Crosswind n kt, maximum m kt": above the maximum for this runway condition, figures for information.

Tailwind above the limit: Red banner "Tailwind n kt, limit m kt". The distances, stop margin and MLW(PERF) continue the tailwind correction of the data and are marked extrapolated (~ and a dagger, amber), with a note under the results.

Wind check tab (beside Landing roll, red dot when the wind is above a limit): The destination runways ranked by wind: within limits first, most headwind on top; LDA, HEAD/TAIL, CROSS and LIMITS columns; each with a Use button that loads it.
Alternate card in the wind check: The OFP alternate (ICAO editable), its METAR from the weather source of the settings and its best runway, with Calculate for ‹ICAO> ‹runway>.
Wind entered without a direction: The ranking asks for the wind with its direction (e.g. 330/45).

head: A32NX
A380X
rows: Dry, good or wet 38 kt; 29, 25, 20 or 15 kt on contaminated runways (A320 FCOM PER-LDG-DIS-MAT)
Dry / wet 40 kt; 20 kt slush or dry snow; 15 kt standing water or compacted snow; 5 kt icy

blocks.text: Gusts are included in the components as in FCOM LIM; a variable wind is taken from the worst direction.

items: The wind check is not an Airbus function. Why: It is a design choice of the flyPad: advice only, the flight crew decides.
Figures beyond the tailwind limit are extrapolated. Why: The Airbus data stop at the limit; the tailwind correction is continued. What to do: Use them as an indication only.

The alternate check needs an internet connection and the OFP. Why: The METAR comes from the weather source set in the flyPad settings; the alternate from the SimBrief OFP. What to do: Enter the alternate ICAO by hand if the OFP has none.
Fill the landing calculator as usual and press Calculate.
If a red wind banner shows, open the Wind check tab beside the landing roll picture.
Load a better runway with Use, or the alternate with Calculate for, and calculate again.

children.title: RAT stow (maintenance) row on the Services page

blocks.text: The flyPad side of the RAT ground stow: a maintenance row that asks the systems to stow the RAT after the landing (A320 FCOM DSC-29-10-20: the RAT "can be stowed only when the aircraft is on the ground"). The systems side (`L:A32NX_RAT_STOW_REQUEST`, the shared Rust RAT model) is on `core/rat-ground-stow`; see that manual for the rules, the limitations and the full test.
Merge both branches: without `core/rat-ground-stow` the row shows while the RAT is out but pressing Stow has no effect.

items: RAT stowed: No RAT row.
RAT out, aircraft stopped on the ground: "RAT stow (maintenance)", status "RAT extended", button Stow.
RAT out, in flight or moving: Row greyed, status "RAT extended · stow when stopped on the ground".
Stow pressed: Status "Stowing" for about 3 s; the row disappears when the systems have stowed the RAT, or stays if they refused (an extension still commanded).
Stop on the ground with the RAT out and normal electrical power back.
flyPad > Ground > Services: press Stow on the row "RAT stow (maintenance)".

children.title: A380X cargo door row shows the real doors

blocks.text: The cargo door row of the Services page read the open request of the ground crew, not the doors. With an engine running the request could be on while the doors did not move, and the row said "open". The row now shows the real forward and aft doors (position and lock, from the systems) and says when the request waits for hydraulic power.

Merge both branches: the row reads `L:A32NX_HYD_CARGO_DOOR_OPERATION_INHIBITED`, which only `core/a380x-cargo-doors` writes (without it the row reads 0 = not inhibited and shows the real doors only). That manual describes the systems rules (A380 FCOM DSC-29-10, DSC-52-30-40-10) and the full test.

items: Both doors closed and locked, hydraulic power available: Row "Cargo fwd + aft", status "Closed", switch off.
Engine running, doors closed: Status "Closed · no hydraulic power, engine running"; the switch is greyed out.
Engine running, an open request is on and the doors are closed: Status "Closed · opens once the engines are stopped". The switch can still cancel the request.
Doors moving: Status "Moving" with a progress bar; the FWD and AFT holds on the planform follow the position of each door.
Doors open (from 98 %, where the systems lock them open): Status "Open". Below 98 % the status is "Moving" (before: "Open" from 90 %).

A door stopped open or unlocked by an engine start: Amber row, status "Not locked · no hydraulic power, engine running"; the switch can still ask the door to close (it follows once the engines are stopped).

blocks.text: The row stays one row for both doors (the request moves both); it is closed only when both doors are locked and open only when both are open. The planform now shows the FWD and the AFT cargo door as two holds, each with its own position.

items: Stop the engines.
flyPad > Ground > Services > Doors: switch "Cargo fwd + aft" on to open, off to close; read the status line.

blocks.text: Use the same sim test as `core/a380x-cargo-doors`, with both branches installed.

children.title: Custom flyPad theme, and a readable Light theme

blocks.text: The flyPad had three fixed themes: Blue, Dark and Light. A fourth choice, Custom, lets the pilot pick the colours: a base (the surfaces and text of the Gray, Black or Light theme) plus a primary and a secondary colour. The Blue, Dark and Light themes keep their exact colours.

items: Primary colour: buttons, switches, progress bars, chart lines.
Secondary colour: selected tabs, segmented buttons, chips and the navigation rail. "Same" uses the primary colour.
