The flyPad adjusts only the lightness of the picked colours until every text and control pair reaches the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for controls). A contrast list beside a preview card shows each pair with "AA" (or "FAIL").

Amber and red are the alert colours: the preset discs offer none, and a colour close to their hues (picked on the wheel or typed) is accepted with a note that buttons and switches in it may look like warnings.

The pencil button at the end of the colour discs opens the colour wheel: the 12 pure colours of the painter’s wheel (yellow at the top, then clockwise yellow-green, green, sky blue, blue, violet, magenta, crimson, red, red-orange, orange, amber) on 5 rings, from the pure colour at the rim to pale tints next to the centre. Every wedge can be picked, red and yellow included; a theme stored in red or yellow is kept. Beside the wheel: the picked colour, a hex field (type a code, then Enter), a preview, the contrast checks of that colour, and, when the flyPad must adjust the colour for the chosen base, the shade it will really use. Nothing changes before Apply; Cancel keeps the theme as it was. The secondary wheel also offers "Same"; only the hue and colourfulness of a secondary colour count (the base sets its lightness).
The theme applies to both tablets and to the Payload balance chart. An existing user keeps their theme after the update (the old setting is carried over once).

blocks.text: Light theme fix: several titles and labels were hard-coded white and disappeared on the Light theme (and on a Light base): the Settings page title, the ATC frequency cards and callsign, the checklist and failure (ATA) titles, the preset names, the aircraft symbol of the pushback map, the battery level and the slider labels. They now use the theme text colour; a selected ATC frequency card uses its own text colour.

items: Orange, amber or red theme colours look like alerts. Why: These hues mean caution and warning on the flyPad; the warn and error colours are never themed. The flyPad allows them with a note. What to do: Prefer another hue.
A picked colour can look lighter or darker than its disc or hex code. Why: Its lightness is moved until the contrast reaches AA on the chosen base.
Open flyPad > Settings > flyPad and scroll to Theme.
Press Blue, Dark or Light for a standard theme, or Custom.
Custom: pick the Base (Gray, Black, Light), then a Primary color and a Secondary color disc, or press the pencil button to pick it on the colour wheel (or type a hex code, then Enter), then Apply.
Check the contrast list beside the preview card; press Reset to Blue to go back to the usual cyan flyPad.

children.title: GSX services link: passenger counts, request chips, greyed switch

blocks.text: Fixes of the GSX link of the Services page (the GSX services card, from `core/efb-ground`), found in the sim (A380X at RJTT, GSX Remote API). The link needs the third-party add-on GSX Pro (FSDreamTeam) with its Remote control server on.

items: Passenger number. GSX boarded its own number of passengers and the Board counter stayed at 0. The flyPad now gives GSX its passenger number (`L:FSDT_GSX_NUMPASSENGERS`, which GSX uses in place of its own figure when set before the boarding or deboarding, GSX manual DEVELOPERS): the passengers planned on the Payload page, or the passengers on board once a deboarding is requested or after landing. The Services page and the Payload pages of both aircraft use the same rule; before, a GSX deboarding started from the Payload page was given 0 passengers.

Passenger counter. The flyPad counts the GSX boarding and deboarding passengers itself: the Board line shows boarded over planned (e.g. 45/120) and its bar fills; before, it showed GSX's own figure twice.

Request chips. A turnaround step offers Request only while GSX lets the service be triggered, and Stop while it runs. A completed service no longer offers Request (also the Ground equipment rows, e.g. the Catering Truck).

Greyed switch. Without GSX the GSX services switch is faded and does not move. The disabled look of the Material controls is now set by the flyPad itself (the sim browser does not reliably support the CSS :disabled state).
Needs GSX Pro. Why: A third-party add-on (FSDreamTeam); the flyPad only drives it. What to do: Install GSX Pro and turn on its Remote control server (GSX settings).

GSX resets its passenger number to 0 when it restarts. Why: GSX behaviour (GSX manual). What to do: The flyPad gives the number again while the Services page is linked, and just before a Board / Deboard request.
Start GSX Pro with its Remote control server on.
Plan the passengers on flyPad > Ground > Payload (do not press Board).
On Ground > Services, turn the GSX services switch on when the card says "GSX found".
Request the jet bridge or stairs, then Board > Request in the Turnaround card; after landing, Deboard > Request.

children.title: GSX turnaround: completed services remembered, Baggage steps

blocks.text: Needs the third-party add-on GSX Pro. GSX gives one completion signal, the service state 6 "completed", and does not keep it: in the sim (A32NX) GSX set the boarding state back to 1 (available) 14 s after the end of the boarding, so the turnaround offered the boarding again as if it had not been done.

items: Completed services remembered. The flyPad itself remembers the completed boarding, deboarding, catering and refuelling of the current turnaround (also across flyPad page changes). A service requested or running again is forgotten; the boarding is forgotten when a deboarding starts, and the reverse; everything is forgotten at the end of the turnaround (an engine running or the pushback requested). The jet bridge, stairs and GPU follow the sim.

Baggage steps. A Baggage row after Board in the departure turnaround (catering, boarding, baggage, pushback) and after Deboard in the arrival turnaround (deboarding, baggage, catering). GSX has no baggage service to request: it loads the baggage during the boarding and unloads it during the deboarding, so the row has no Request button ("Loaded with the boarding" / "Unloaded with the deboarding" while idle) and shows the GSX baggage progress (`L:FSDT_GSX_BOARDING_CARGO_PERCENT` / `L:FSDT_GSX_DEBOARDING_CARGO_PERCENT`). It is Done when 100 % is reached after the loading was seen running in this turnaround (a 100 % left from an earlier loading does not count), remembered and forgotten with its boarding or deboarding.
List fixes. The Turnaround list scrolls vertically only (no horizontal scrollbar), and the progress bar of a step sits in its own full-width box under the texts (it was pushed out of the card).
Needs GSX Pro. Why: A third-party add-on; the states come from its variables and Remote API. What to do: Install GSX Pro with its Remote control server on.
The Done marks last for the current turnaround only. Why: GSX does not keep its completion; the flyPad clears them when an engine runs or the pushback is requested.
No Request on the Baggage rows. Why: GSX has no separate baggage service. What to do: Request Board or Deboard.
On Ground > Services, link GSX with the GSX services switch.
Run the turnaround steps in order with their Request chips; a Done step keeps its check mark.
Follow the baggage on the Baggage row during the boarding or deboarding.

children.title: GSX refuel progress and jet bridge state

blocks.text: Needs the third-party add-on GSX Pro with its Remote control server on, the GSX services switch on. Two rows of the Ground equipment list showed the wrong GSX state:

items: Fuel Truck. With the flyPad fuel sync on (flyPad > Settings > 3rd Party Options > GSX Fueling Synchronization) the flyPad pumps the fuel and GSX does not know the target: GSX keeps its own target just above what was pumped, so the row read 99-100 % right after the refuel started. While the flyPad refuel runs, the row now shows the progress towards the flyPad fuel target (fuel received since GSX started / fuel to load) and the whole minutes left, measured from the fuel flow of the last minute, e.g. "Refueling 25% · 12 min". The minutes appear once a few seconds of flow are measured. Without the flyPad refuel, GSX's own progress stays.

Jet Bridge. GSX 4 reports the jetway (and the stairs) as completed after a dock and after an undock alike; only its phase tells which. The sim does not see a GSX jetway, so the row showed "Done": after an undock with no Request (the jetway could not be called again), and while docked with Request. Now a docked jetway or stairs reads "Connected" with a Release chip, "Leaving" while it undocks, and an undocked one offers Request again (GSX accepts the call).
Needs GSX Pro. Why: A third-party add-on; the states come from its Remote API. What to do: Install GSX Pro with its Remote control server on.
No minutes left during the first seconds of the refuel or while no fuel flows. Why: The time left comes from the measured fuel flow. What to do: Wait a few seconds after the hose connection.
The fuel progress needs GSX to report its fuel in kg or lb. Why: The fuel figures come from GSX (its unit setting). What to do: Without them the row shows GSX's own progress.
On Ground > Services, link GSX with the GSX services switch.
Request the jet bridge; Release it before the pushback, Request it again if needed.
Refuel with the flyPad (fuel target and start on Ground > Fuel, GSX fuel sync on) and follow the progress and the minutes left on the Fuel Truck row.

children.title: Taxi page: A380 taxiway width check

blocks.text: The taxi route page did not know whether a taxiway suits the A380 (wingspan 79.75 m, aerodrome reference code letter F). ICAO Annex 14 Volume I, 3.9.3 (taxiway width of the straight portion) gives 25 m for code letter F. On the A380 flyPad, each taxi line of the Navigraph airport map is now rated:

items: Wingspan limit of the line in the airport map, when the map has one, against 79.75 m (not seen in the Navigraph data so far; read only when present).

Else the pavement width under the line: measured across the line (60 m each side) through the taxiway, apron and runway areas of the map (adjacent areas joined, holes left out), the narrowest of samples every 30 m away from the junction fillets, against 25 m with 1 m tolerance.
Else "not verified" (no data), which is not treated as unsafe.
SUGGEST, or the proposed runway entry: The route keeps off the lines too narrow when it can.

A typed clearance that needs a line too narrow: The route still follows the clearance and is drawn, but flagged: the route text marks the line, and a chip and a banner list the narrow taxiways (ATC may know better: the crew decides).
The map: Lines too narrow in orange, lines not verified dashed grey, with a legend.
A32NX: No width check (the A320 is code C).
Pavement width is not wingtip clearance. Why: Buildings and parked aircraft are not in the check. What to do: Follow the airport charts.
Lines on aprons measure wide. Why: The apron area around them counts as pavement.
An airport may clear the A380 on narrower taxiways with restrictions. Why: The flag means "check the airport A380 notes", not "forbidden". What to do: Check the airport A380 notes.
Airport loading may take longer. Why: The runway intersection layer is now loaded for the pavement, and every line is measured.
A380X flyPad > Ground > Taxi: plan the route as usual.
Look at the map legend: orange lines are too narrow, dashed grey ones not verified.
If the route chip or banner lists narrow taxiways, check the airport A380 notes or ask ATC for another route.
At RJTT (A380): which taxiways turn orange or dashed, and whether known A380 routes show as too narrow.
The airport load time.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X smart FIVE HUNDRED pin option back in the flyPad

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM automatic callouts (DSC-34-10-50) have a "smart FIVE HUNDRED" pin programming: the FIVE HUNDRED callout is given only when the aircraft is more than half a dot off the glide slope, or without a valid glide slope. The flyPad option was commented out. The Automatic Call Outs page shows it again, as a sub-option Inhibited When Glideslope Captured under Five Hundred (greyed while Five Hundred is off).

items: The option does nothing without `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`. Why: The FWS callout that reads the pin is on that branch. What to do: Merge both.
flyPad > Settings > Aircraft Options / Pin Programs > Automatic Call Outs: Five Hundred on, then Inhibited When Glideslope Captured on.
The option is saved and greyed correctly; the callout follows it with the FWS branch merged.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: Ops-panel look and the Dashboard header colours

blocks.text: The flyPad pages are laid out like an operations panel: square panels with a header bar, dense label and value fields, flat status boxes and uppercase buttons. The look is the same on the ground and in the air, on every page, in the Blue, Dark and Light themes and in a custom theme. On the Dashboard the title bar of each panel has its own section colour; a setting chooses strong (Vivid) or toned-down (Soft) colours.

The pictures of this manual are captures of the A380X flyPad in a browser test harness at 1430 x 1000 with a made-up SimBrief OFP (RJAA to RJOA, alternate RJBB) and made-up weather reports. Values that come from the aircraft (fuel on board, turnaround services, checklist states) are harness values, not a real flight. The A32NX flyPad uses the same code; it was not captured.
Dispatch > Overview: panels with a header bar and dense label / value rows.
Performance > Takeoff: dense fields, flat result boxes, uppercase buttons.

head: Part
Look
rows: Square corners, a header bar with the title in capitals, no rounded tonal cards.
Small label above or beside the value; the inputs of the calculators are dense rows.
Flat boxes with a short word (Complete, Not started, OK, FMS, OFP) instead of switches or big chips.
Uppercase text (IMPORT SIMBRIEF OFP, OPEN COCKPIT PREPARATION, GROUND SERVICES).
One colour per panel: flight blue, advisories red, turnaround green, fuel orange, payload purple, ground services magenta, weather yellow, checklists grey.

blocks.text: Dashboard Header Colours: Vivid (the default).
Dashboard Header Colours: Soft (the same hues, dimmed).
Blue theme.
Light theme.
Settings > flyPad: Tab Bar Position, Dashboard Header Colours (Soft selected) and the Theme row.

items: The header colours apply to the Dashboard only. Why: The other pages use one neutral header bar. What to do: None.
Pictures show the A380X only. Why: The harness build with the redesign was installed for the A380X. What to do: The A32NX pages use the same components.
flyPad > Settings > flyPad > Theme: Blue, Dark, Light or Custom.
Same page, Dashboard Header Colours: Vivid or Soft. Open the Dashboard to see it.

blocks.text: A full-width bar of icon tabs replaces the navigation rail on the left. The pages use the full width of the flyPad. The bar sits at the bottom of the flyPad (default) or at the top.

items: Ten icon-only tabs in this order: Dashboard, Dispatch, Ground, Performance, Navigation, ATC, Failures, Checklists, Presets, Settings.
The open tab shows its name under the icon, in the accent colour, with a line on the edge of the bar facing the page. The other tabs show the icon only.
At the bottom the status bar (date, clock, flight progress, battery) stays on top of the page. At the top the status bar content shares the row of the tab bar, on the right.

blocks.text: Tab Bar Position: Bottom (Dark theme).
Tab Bar Position: Top (Dark theme): the status bar is in the bar row.
Settings > flyPad with Tab Bar Position set to Top.

items: The tabs have no label except the open one. Why: Ten labelled tabs do not fit the width of the flyPad next to the status bar when the bar is at the top. What to do: The icons are the same as on the old rail; open the tab to read its name.
Only two positions: Top and Bottom. Why: The bar is full width by design. What to do: None.

Whether the bar moves at once when the setting is changed in the sim was not checked. Why: In the browser harness the stored setting is read when the flyPad starts; the harness does not pass setting changes on to the open page. What to do: If the bar does not move, reopen the flyPad (power cycle it).
Touch a tab icon to open its section; the section tabs are in the segmented control at the top right of the page as before.
flyPad > Settings > flyPad > Tab Bar Position: Top or Bottom.

blocks.text: The SimBrief OFP is one long text. A Sections menu on the left of the OFP page lists the parts of the OFP (flight summary, fuel, navigation log, weather, ...) and jumps to the one you touch. The menu is built from the PDF bookmark comments that SimBrief writes at the start of every OFP section, in every OFP layout. A section has sub-sections (for example Fuel under Route and Fuel); they are indented.
Dispatch > OFP: the Sections menu on the left, the first section highlighted. (The OFP text of the harness is a made-up filler text with SimBrief-style bookmarks.)
After touching Weights: the OFP scrolled to it; the menu highlights the section being read and its parent.

items: The highlighted entry follows the scrolling: it is the last section whose start is at or above the top of the view.
While a sub-section is highlighted, its parent section is shown in the accent colour.

An OFP without bookmarks has no menu; the OFP is shown as before. Why: The menu is built from the bookmark comments SimBrief puts in the OFP text. There is nothing to build it from without them. What to do: Use another OFP layout, or scroll.
Only two levels (section and sub-section). Why: SimBrief bookmarks have level 0 and 1 in the OFP. What to do: None.
Import a SimBrief OFP (Dashboard > IMPORT SIMBRIEF OFP).
Open Dispatch > OFP. Touch a title in the Sections menu to jump to it; scroll the OFP and watch the highlight follow.

blocks.text: The Dashboard shows what matters now. It chooses its layout from the flight phase and from whether a SimBrief OFP is loaded, so the pilot sees the turnaround at the gate, the flight and the destination weather in the air, and a summary on arrival. It replaces the single layout of the old Dashboard.

head: Layout
When
Panels
rows: On the ground, stationary, no OFP loaded.

Flight strip with IMPORT SIMBRIEF OFP (and LOAD PRESET), advisories, aircraft state (power, doors, park brake, ADIRS), checklists, ground services, fuel and payload (No plan), weather with an ICAO field, cabin controls.
On the ground, stationary, an OFP loaded, not flown yet.
Flight strip with the off-blocks countdown, advisories, turnaround rows, checklists, ground services, fuel and payload status, trip weather (departure, destination, alternate).
Taxi out to approach, with an OFP.
Flight strip with the progress line, checklist card with the next checklist, fuel, payload, flight plan, destination weather, cabin controls.
On the ground, stationary, after the OFP has been flown.
Flight summary (block time, flight time, fuel used, landing weight, each against the plan), advisories, checklists with the missed ones, fuel, payload, destination weather and IMPORT NEXT OFP.
Any phase except at the gate, no OFP.
The live values only (altitude, speed, local time), with the advisory to import an OFP.

blocks.text: Gate, no OFP: only live values; IMPORT SIMBRIEF OFP is on the strip and in the advisories.
Gate with an OFP: flight strip with the T/C and T/D marks and the off-blocks countdown, the FMS advisory, turnaround rows, fuel and payload chips, trip weather.
Flight strip

items: Flight number, the airports, the alternate, scheduled off-blocks (STD) and arrival (STA), planned taxi time, flight level, cost index and flight time, and the route.
The progress line with the aircraft and the T/C and T/D marks from the OFP navlog, with the planned time over each. After takeoff the times are counted from the real takeoff.
The phase: AT GATE, TAXI OUT, TAKEOFF, CLIMB, CRUISE, DESCENT, APPROACH, TAXI IN or ARRIVED.

A countdown that changes with the phase: OFF-BLOCKS IN at the gate (until 60 minutes after the scheduled time), RUNWAY IN when taxiing out, T/D IN from takeoff to descent, ARRIVAL IN (planned) when no T/D is known, GATE IN when taxiing in. "planned" under it means the value comes from the OFP, not from the aircraft.

blocks.text: In flight (cruise): the strip shows T/D IN; checklist card with the next checklist; destination weather with runway, headwind and crosswind.
Approach: the countdown is ARRIVAL IN (planned).
Advisories
A list of short messages, the most urgent first (red, amber, then information), each with a tag and a link to where to act. The rules in the code:

head: Advisory
When
rows: Destination or alternate, from the TAF and METAR at the planned arrival time; in every phase from the gate to approach. Needs a report with a TAF or METAR.

From 80 % of the aircraft limit: at the departure airport at the gate, taxiing out and on takeoff; at the destination in flight. Uses the planned runway and the METAR wind (gusts included). Links to Performance.
In flight, within 15 minutes before the planned T/D (or in the descent phase when no T/D is known), when the destination QNH or the minimums are not entered. Names the MFD / MCDU PERF APPR page.
The FMS has no flight plan yet

At the gate with an OFP loaded. The flyPad asks the FMS itself every 5 seconds, so the message goes away as soon as the plan is entered. Names the MFD FMS ACTIVE INIT page (A380X) or the MCDU INIT page (A32NX).
At the gate, when the projected end of the turnaround is within 5 minutes of the scheduled departure or later. Links to Ground.
Cruise and descent, route average of 50 kt or more.
Without an OFP. Links to the import.
One or more failures activated in the flyPad Failures page.
Fuel used differs from the plan
When arrived, with a difference of 500 kg or more. Links to Ground > Fuel.

blocks.text: Turnaround, fuel, payload

items: At the gate with an OFP: one row each for Refuel, Cargo, Boarding, Doors closed and Pushback with its status box (Not started, in progress, Complete) and the time, read from the GSX services and the aircraft doors. The ground services panel shows GPU and pushback.

Fuel and payload have a status chip (for example Complete, Not started) and the figures planned in the OFP against the loaded ones. In flight the fuel panel gives the fuel on board against the plan at this point of the route, as a chip with the difference.

blocks.text: Checklists

A card with every checklist of the aircraft and a mark each: done, missed (a later phase is already reached), optional (the names written between ‹‹ >>), next and later. The first checklist not done is marked next, and its first items are previewed beside the list. A button opens the next checklist (OPEN COCKPIT PREPARATION, ... OPEN PARKING).
Weather card and cabin controls

items: At the gate: one tile per airport of the trip (departure, destination, alternate) with the wind and a status box (OK, or the problem). In flight and when arrived: the destination with the runway, headwind, crosswind and gust crosswind, the colour-coded METAR and the TAF.
CHARTS opens the charts; METAR / TAF opens the weather page (see the next section) on that airport. Without an OFP an ICAO field takes any airport.
The cabin card has the lighting / cabin preset selector with Auto and PRESETS.

blocks.text: Arrived: the flight summary against the plan, the checklists with the missed ones, IMPORT NEXT OFP. (Block and flight time read 0:00 in the harness: no flight was recorded.)
A flown OFP loaded again

The flyPad marks the OFP as flown at touchdown. If that same OFP is loaded again with the aircraft on the ground at its departure airport (the flight was reloaded in the sim), it is a new flight: the Dashboard goes back to the gate layout and forgets what was recorded for the old flight. At the destination the same OFP stays Arrived. The airport is told by position only.
The flown OFP imported again at RJAA: a new flight, back at the gate.

items: The phase comes from the FMGC flight phase, the on-ground flag, the engines, the pushback and the stationary flag. Why: There is no single sim "flight phase" for the ground. A transient FMGC phase in the air (0 or 7) is shown as the nearest sensible phase. What to do: None.
Turnaround status needs GSX or the aircraft doors. Why: Refuel, cargo, boarding and doors are read from them. What to do: Without GSX the rows follow the aircraft state only.

Thunderstorm and crosswind advisories need a report. Why: They are computed from the METAR and TAF of the airports; the FlyByWire server returns no TAF at the moment (see the weather page). What to do: Open the weather page and load the OFP report.

The trip weather tiles only show the reports the weather source returned. Why: An airport without a report shows "No report" even if the OFP carries one (the alternate in the picture). What to do: The weather page offers the OFP report (next section).
The new-flight rule works by position. Why: The OFP has no way to tell a flown flight from a reload. What to do: A reload at the destination stays Arrived; import the next OFP.

Not captured in the harness: the turnaround late, approach data, thunderstorm and crosswind advisories, and live GSX statuses. Why: They need the sim (GSX, FMS, real METAR at the real position). What to do: Test them in the sim with the steps below.
At the gate, touch IMPORT SIMBRIEF OFP (the SimBrief user is set in Settings > 3rd Party Options).
Read the advisories and follow the link of each one.
Work through the turnaround rows and the checklists; the next checklist is marked and previewed.
In flight watch the countdown and the destination weather; METAR / TAF opens the full weather.
On arrival read the summary; IMPORT NEXT OFP prepares the next leg.

blocks.text: The METAR and TAF of the airports of the flight (departure, destination, alternate) or of any ICAO code, decoded and drawn: what the weather is, which runway end suits the wind, and how the weather will change.

Along the top: a button per airport of the flight (DEP, DEST, ALTN), the airports of the OFP that have a report but are not part of the trip (OFP), an ICAO field for any other airport, and the METAR / TAF switch.
METAR view

items: A header with the airport name, the observation time and the age of the report.

The flight category box (VFR, MVFR, IFR, LIFR) and the main weather in words. The category is the worse of the ceiling and the visibility: LIFR below 500 ft or 1 sm, IFR below 1,000 ft or 3 sm, MVFR up to 3,000 ft or 5 sm.
Fields: wind (with gusts), visibility, ceiling, temperature and dew point (humidity), QNH in hPa and inHg, sunset (UTC, or local time when the aircraft is at that airport).

Runway wind: a compass with the wind arrow and the runway drawn, and bars for headwind or tailwind, crosswind (left or right) and gust crosswind. Buttons for each runway end choose the runway used for the bars; a tailwind is red.
Sky: the cloud layers drawn on a height scale up to the field elevation, the ceiling layer marked.
Report: the raw METAR coloured, then the report read out in plain sentences.

blocks.text: METAR, VFR: runway end button 16L chosen; the 8 kt wind is a tailwind for that end.
METAR, IFR (RJOA): ceiling 1,200 ft, visibility 4,000 m, gusts.
TAF view

items: A timeline over the validity period. A forecast band coloured by flight category for the main forecast and its BECMG changes; below it the TEMPO / PROB rows.
The visibility and ceiling curves over time, each with the worst value of the period.
Wind with direction, speed and gusts of each part, and the BECMG changes drawn as a ramp.
The raw TAF below.

blocks.text: TAF timeline of RJOA, loaded from the OFP (From OFP chip): forecast band, TEMPO and PROB40 rows, visibility and ceiling curves, wind with BECMG ramps, raw TAF.
Reports from the OFP

SimBrief puts the METAR and TAF of the plan's airports in the OFP. The flyPad keeps them when the OFP is imported. When the weather server has no report for the airport you are looking at, the page says so and offers LOAD METAR FROM OFP or LOAD TAF FROM OFP. After you load it, the report is shown with a From OFP chip: it is as old as the OFP. Airports of the OFP outside the trip (takeoff and en-route alternates) get an OFP button of their own.
No METAR for the alternate RJBB: LOAD METAR FROM OFP.
The OFP METAR loaded: LIFR with the From OFP chip.
TAF view without a TAF from the server: LOAD TAF FROM OFP.

items: The FlyByWire weather server currently returns no TAF for any airport. Why: The server answers without a TAF. This is why the OFP fallback exists. What to do: Use LOAD TAF FROM OFP; the TAF is as old as the OFP.

The METAR of the sim comes from MSFS (the METAR source setting). Why: It is the weather the sim uses; other sources (BeyondATC, SayIntentions, the FlyByWire servers) are chosen in the settings. What to do: Choose the source in Settings.
An OFP report is as old as the OFP, not live. Why: It was copied from SimBrief when the OFP was made. What to do: The From OFP chip and the age in the header show it.
Only airports of the OFP can be loaded from it. Why: Other airports have no OFP report. What to do: Type the ICAO; it needs the weather source.

The runway compass needs the airport from the sim. Why: The runways come from the sim facility data; the page says "Runways not available for this airport" otherwise. What to do: The report is still shown.
The pictures use made-up airports and reports. Why: The harness has no sim weather or facility data. What to do: None.
Open Navigation > Weather (or touch METAR / TAF on the Dashboard: it opens on that airport).
Touch DEP, DEST or ALTN, or type an ICAO code in the ICAO field.
METAR: touch a runway end to see the wind components. TAF: read the bands and curves.
No report from the server: touch LOAD METAR FROM OFP or LOAD TAF FROM OFP.

blocks.text: The Presets section had three tabs (Interior Lighting, Aircraft States and a help tab), so loading an aircraft state and loading a lighting preset were two separate trips. Both are now on one page with no tabs, and the help tab is gone: its text is now a one-line hint on each panel. The page is flyPad > Presets; the cabin card and the flight strip of the Dashboard open it. The preset functions on the sim side do not change.

items: At the top the title Presets and two status chips: On ground / In flight and AC BUS 1 powered / AC BUS 1 not powered.

Aircraft state panel: the five states (Cold & Dark, Powered, Ready for Pushback, Ready for Taxi, Ready for Takeoff) as buttons joined by arrows, in the order the cockpit procedure goes. The Fast loading (unrealistic) switch is in the panel header. A hint line says that the procedure runs step by step from the current state, asks before it starts and can be cancelled at any time. Pressing a state asks for confirmation first. The aircraft must be on the ground, as before.
While a state loads: its button is highlighted and marked LOADING, the other buttons are dimmed, and a line shows the current STEP text, the percentage, a progress bar and Cancel.

Interior lighting panel: the Auto-load switch in the header, then a grid of eight slots, two columns by four rows. Each slot has its number, its name (or "Preset n" while it has none) with a pencil icon, a line of tags, an icon Save button and a Load button. The tags say for which time of day the slot is loaded automatically (Day, Dawn/Dusk, Night), or "No auto-load" for a named slot that is not assigned, or "Not named yet". Save asks for confirmation first.
Rename in place: press the name, type, then Enter or press elsewhere to keep it; Esc cancels. No popup opens. Clearing the name returns the slot to "Preset n" and "Not named yet".
When AC BUS 1 is not powered, a red banner says that Load and Save need AC BUS 1 powered, and the Save and Load buttons are dimmed. Names and auto-load can still be edited.

At the bottom the strip Auto-load at power-up with three drop-downs, Day, Dawn/Dusk and Night. The one for the current time of day is marked NOW. The drop-downs list None and the eight presets as "n - name"; a preset with no name is listed as "n - Preset n".

blocks.text: A380X on the ground, powered, at night: three named slots with their Day, Night and Dawn/Dusk tags, Auto-load on, the Night drop-down marked NOW.
Ready for Taxi loading: the button highlighted, step text, 42 %, progress bar and Cancel (progress text made up in the harness).
A32NX with AC BUS 1 off: red banner, Load and Save dimmed; the names and the auto-load strip still work.
Renaming slot 2 in place: the field and the hint "Enter keeps the name, Esc cancels".

head: Situation
What the page shows
rows: The chip says In flight; the aircraft states cannot be loaded (the ground is needed). Lighting presets follow the AC BUS 1 power only.
Red chip and banner; Save and Load dimmed. A state such as Powered can still be loaded on the ground.
LOADING on its button, the step text, percentage, progress bar and Cancel. Cancel stops the procedure.
Every slot reads "Preset n" and "Not named yet"; the drop-downs list "n - Preset n".

items: The pictures are made in the browser harness. Why: The harness has no sim: the progress text and percentage were injected by hand and the lighting does not change. What to do: The real progress and light loading need the sim.
A state loads only on the ground. Why: The cockpit procedure on the sim side needs the aircraft stopped. What to do: Land or load on the ground first.
Open flyPad > Presets.
To set up the cockpit: press a state, confirm, and watch the step and the progress bar. Press Cancel to stop. Turn on Fast loading only if you accept the unrealistic speed.
To keep a lighting setup: set the cockpit lights, press the Save icon of a slot and confirm. Press the name to rename it. Press Load later to get the same lighting back.
For automatic loading: turn on Auto-load and pick a slot for Day, Dawn/Dusk and Night in the strip at the bottom.

children.title: A380X cockpit buttons, lights and probes
A/THR disconnect, EVAC HORN, DFDR EVENT and ACMS TRIGGER pushbuttons work

blocks.text: The cockpit behaviour XML named model nodes or animations that are not in the A380X cockpit model, so these pushbuttons could not be clicked or did not move. Checked against the cockpit model:

head: Pushbutton
Before
Now
rows: A/THR instinctive disconnect pbs (thrust levers 1 and 4)
Clickable (ATHR_DISCONNECT_ENG1/2): they disconnect the A/THR through the existing FBW interface

items: DFDR EVENT and ACMS TRIGGER only move. Why: There is no flight data recorder or ACMS function behind them; their tooltips still say (Inop.). What to do: None.
Press an A/THR instinctive disconnect pushbutton on thrust lever 1 or 4 to disconnect the A/THR.
Press EVAC HORN SHUT OFF on the overhead EVAC panel, DFDR EVENT or ACMS TRIGGER on the right pedestal as on the aircraft.

children.title: Clickable RESET panel buttons and side slip probe vanes

blocks.text: All 52 circuit breakers of the overhead RESET panels can now be pulled and pushed, with their FCOM label as tooltip. Each one writes `L:A32NX_RESET_PANEL_‹name>` (true = pulled, computer reset).

items: Read by the avionics: ARPT NAV, FMC A, FMC B, FMC C, FWS 1, FWS 2, AESU 1, AESU 2, NSS AVNCS, NSS FLT OPS.

The other 42 (AICU, ATC, AVS, BSCS, CIDS, CPCS, DSMS, DTLNK ROUTER, EIPMs, ESS TR, TR 1, TR 2A, FLAPS, FQMS, GCU, LGCIS, PACK CTL, PAX BBAND, SCS, SDF, SLATS, TCS, VCS) are clickable but no system reads them yet.

blocks.text: The three side slip probe vanes on the nose now follow the side slip angle (sim `INCIDENCE BETA`, up to 60 degrees each side): they line up with the airflow.

items: 42 RESET buttons do nothing in the systems. Why: The systems they reset are not wired to the RESET panel yet. What to do: Use the 10 wired ones to test a reset.
Hover a RESET panel button to read its label; click to pull it (reset), click again to push it back.
Look at the nose from the outside view to see the side slip vanes.

children.title: FMC-C reset button checked in the all-FMCs-reset test

blocks.text: The FMS stops and resets when all the FMC reset buttons are pulled. The check read FMC-B twice and never FMC-C, so pulling FMC-A and FMC-B alone reset the FMS and lost the flight plan while FMC-C was still in. Per A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-30 FMC-C is the standby FMC, and FMS 1 and FMS 2 are only lost when FMC-A, FMC-B and FMC-C all fail (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-22-FMS AUTO FLT FMS 1+2 FAULT). The check now covers A, B and C.

items: FMC-A and FMC-B pulled, FMC-C in: The FMS keeps running; the flight plan stays.
FMC-A, FMC-B and FMC-C pulled: The FMS stops and resets (the flight plan is lost), as before.
Pull FMC A, FMC B and / or FMC C on the overhead RESET panels to reset those FMCs; push them back in to restore.

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-22-FG-80-100: the AUTOLAND light flashes in autoland below 200 ft RA when the autoland conditions are lost, and "as long as the AUTOLAND light is pressed, the AUTOLAND light flashes" (light test). The cockpit lamp code cannot read the sim time, so the old flashing expression never lit the light. The flashing (1 Hz: half on, half off) is now computed in the systems host, for the light test and for the autoland warning.

items: AUTOLAND light held pressed: It flashes red at 1 Hz until released.
Autoland below 200 ft RA, autoland conditions lost: Both AUTOLAND lights flash (the warning itself is the existing FBW logic).
Press and hold the AUTOLAND light on the glareshield to test it (cockpit preparation).

children.title: MFP vanes follow the angle of attack

blocks.text: The angle of attack vanes of the three multifunction probes on the nose (one on the left, two on the right, A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-30-10) now follow the angle of attack (sim `INCIDENCE ALPHA`, up to 60 degrees each way, smoothed so that the jumps at very low speed on the ground do not show).

items: The vanes do not move without the companion model change. Why: The MFP_ANGLE1..3 animations are in the A380_FUSELAGE model of the aircraft-large-files repository (fork branch feat/a380x-mfp-vane-animations, b8fb739). What to do: Install that model change with this branch.
Look at the nose probes from the outside view in flight.

children.title: ACD keys beside the OITs work; F/O laptop keyboard keys

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-46-20-20-60: each pilot has an Additional Control Device (ACD), a pad with OIS XFR, OIS MENU, ESC, ENTER and four arrow keys, for the OIT when the keyboard is stowed. Its keys were in the model but could not be clicked. They now send the same event as the laptop key of the same name, so the OIT takes ESC, ENTER and the arrows like keyboard keys, and OIS XFR / OIS MENU like the laptop OIS keys. Their legends were painted into the side console texture at about 3.5 texels per mm (a smear): each key now has a sharp, lit legend. The F/O laptop keyboard had no clickable keys and no legends: it now has the same keys, legends and press animation as the captain keyboard.

items: Mouse over an ACD key: The key highlights and shows its name (ESC, ENTER, Up, Down, Left, Right, OIS MENU, OIS XFR).
ACD key clicked: The key moves in and out; the OIT gets the key.
F/O laptop keyboard pulled out: The same legends as the captain keyboard; the keys move when clicked.
OIS XFR and OIS MENU do nothing on this branch. Why: The OIT handling of those two keys (X-OIS, FLT OPS menu) is on core/fcom-gap-fixes. What to do: Merge core/fcom-gap-fixes too.

The legends, click areas, F/O keyboard keys and tiller fix need the companion model change. Why: They are in the A380_COCKPIT_LOD00 model and two new textures of the aircraft-large-files repository (fork branch feat/a380x-acd-keys-fo-keyboard, 7f56bcb). What to do: Install that model change with this branch.

Some keys can be hard to reach with the mouse from some head positions. Why: The flyPad (when mounted) and the sidestick stand between the seat and the pad. The tiller handle was split into small pieces so that it no longer hides the OIS and ENTER keys. What to do: Move the view slightly.
Click the ACD keys below your OIT as on the aircraft: ENTER validates, ESC cancels, the arrows move, OIS MENU shows the FLT OPS menu, OIS XFR shows the other OIT (FLT OPS side, laptop on, logged in).
Pull out the F/O meal table, then the F/O keyboard, to use the F/O laptop keyboard.

children.title: A380X electrical alerts and AC ESS loads
ELEC alerts from the electrical network

blocks.text: The A380X ECAM had the ELEC alert texts but nothing raised them. The flight warning system now computes them from the electrical network (busbars, engine and APU generators, TRs, pushbuttons), with the procedures, the flight phase inhibitions and the master lights of A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-24:

items: ELEC AC BUS 1(2)(3)(4) FAULT, AC ESS BUS FAULT, AC ESS BUS ALTN (AC ESS supplied through AC 4: AC ESS FEED in ALTN), DC BUS 1(2) FAULT, DC ESS BUS FAULT, EMER CONFIG (all four AC busbars lost, master warning).

ELEC GEN 1(2)(3)(4) FAULT (stays, with its GEN OFF line ticked, after the generator is switched off, until it works again), GEN 1(2)(3)(4) OFF (GEN pb-sw OFF with its engine running, after 5 s), DRIVE 1(2)(3)(4) DISCONNECTED, APU GEN A(B) FAULT, TR 1(2)(ESS) FAULT (no master light, no chime), APU TR FAULT, BUS TIE OFF.

Procedure lines are sensed where the FCOM says so (switches set, OFF THEN ON resets, AIR DATA SWTG, WXR & TAWS / XPDR & TCAS SYS 2...). Lines that the FBW texts had from another FCOM standard and that the FCOM procedure does not contain are hidden.
ELEC AC BUS 2 FAULT shows LDG DIST: AFFECTED (FCOM: LDG DIST IMPACT ON WET/CONTAM RWY ONLY).

ELEC AC ESS BUS FAULT has its FCOM STATUS: LIMITATIONS (APPR & LDG) SLATS SLOW; INOP SYS all phases ADR 1, GPS 1, WXR 1, XPDR 1, TCAS 1, HF 1, FEED TK 2 MAIN PMP, STBY PITOT HEATG, L WINDSHIELD HEATG, DFDR; INOP SYS APPR & LDG SLAT SYS 1, CAT 2, GLS AUTOLAND, LS 1, TAWS 1; REDUND LOSS (STATUS MORE) RA SYS C, FEED TK 3 STBY PMP, TRIM TK L PMP, ENG 1+2+3+4 IGN A, PACK 1 CTL 1, PACK 2 CTL 1. GPWS 1, TERR SYS 1 and ADS-B RPTG 1 are not shown as separate alerts while it is active.

blocks.text: The XPDR 1 INOP SYS text is defined once for the ELEC and the SURV XPDR alerts, and the L WINDSHIELD HEATG INOP SYS text of this STATUS is added here (the same text and code as on `core/ecam-fws`).

items: A bus fault alert needs at least one AC busbar powered. Why: Design choice: with all four AC busbars off the aircraft is unpowered on the ground or in ELEC EMER CONFIG, whose procedure covers the lost busbars. What to do: None.
"Failed" means "no normal output although it should give one". Why: The sim gives no health word for the generators and TRs, only their output. What to do: None.

Not done here: combined busbar faults, DRIVE OIL, units that are not simulated, T.O CONFIG. Why: First part of the ELEC alerts. The battery, EXT PWR, RAT, TR monitoring and drive disconnect alerts and the STATUS of the GEN, DRIVE, APU GEN and TR alerts came later (next feature); the combined busbar alerts and the T.O CONFIG check of the GEN / DRIVE alerts are on `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`. What to do: Use that branch for them.
VENT AVNCS EXTRACT lines are never ticked. Why: There is no avionics ventilation pushbutton in the sim. What to do: None.
REDUND LOSS needs the ECP MORE key fix. Why: The MORE key and light fix is on `core/ecam-fws`. What to do: Merge that branch to page to STATUS MORE.
When an ELEC alert shows, follow the E/WD procedure (the sensed lines tick by themselves as you act).
Check the ELEC AC / DC SD page (called with the alert) and the STATUS page afterwards.

children.title: AC ESS and AC EMER loads

blocks.text: The A380X electrical model uses the A320 bus names: the real A380 AC ESS busbar (400XP) is the A320 "AC ESS SHED" bus in the code, and the AC EMER busbar (491XP) is the A320 "AC ESS" bus. About twenty consumers read the wrong one, so they were on AC EMER where the FCOM puts them on AC ESS. They now use the AC ESS busbar (TypeScript, cockpit XML and Rust):

items: SURV SYS 1 (XPDR 1, TCAS 1, TAWS 1, WXR 1), RA SYS C, the slat motor, the 427XP EHAs, the feed tank 2 main, feed tank 3 standby and trim tank left pumps, channel 1 of both pack controllers, the F/O OIT and the FLT OPS ANSU (A380 FCOM DSC-24, DSC-34-20-100, DSC-46-20-70, DSC-21).
The AC ESS FEED FAULT light shows a loss of the AC ESS busbar (FCOM DSC-24-20: "The AC ESS busbar is not supplied"). An AC EMER failure leaves AC ESS supplied: no FAULT light.

The manual crossbleed control is powered by DC ESS (FCOM DSC-36-30) and the outflow valve manual control by its controller supplies DC 1 / 2 or DC ESS (FCOM DSC-21-30-10). Before, both were on A320 buses that the A380 does not have, so they had no power.
With only the batteries (static inverter on AC EMER), the AC ESS loads (427XP EHAs, TAWS 1, XPDR 1...) are unpowered and the AC EMER loads (VOR 1, LS 1, GPS 1...) remain.
The flyPad labels are AC ESS (the real AC ESS busbar) and AC EMER; the code names stay the A320 ones. Why: Renaming the buses in the code would touch every system. What to do: Use the flyPad labels.
Nothing new to set. In an AC ESS loss, follow ELEC AC ESS BUS FAULT (AC ESS FEED ALTN).

children.title: XPDR 1 / XPDR 2, per-system TCAS faults and SURV XPDR alerts

blocks.text: The A380 has two surveillance systems, each with its transponder and TCAS: SURV SYS 1 on AC ESS and SURV SYS 2 on AC 4 (FCOM DSC-34-20-100). MSFS has one transponder: it now acts as the transponder of the selected system (XPDR & TCAS SYS 1 / SYS 2 on the SURV panel or the MFD SURV page). The XPDR 2 failure did nothing before.

items: XPDR 1 failed or unpowered: TCAS 1 is inoperative too; same for 2. The sim TCAS computer fault counts for the selected system only.
SURV TCAS 1(2) FAULT is per system: no false TCAS 2 FAULT when AC ESS is lost (TCAS 2 is on AC 4). They need the busbar of that system powered (ELEC AC ESS BUS FAULT lists XPDR 1 / TCAS 1 itself).

New SURV XPDR 1 FAULT, XPDR 2 FAULT and XPDR 1+2 FAULT (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-34-20): caution, line XPDR & TCAS ..... SYS 2 (1) when the failed system is selected and the other one works; STATUS INOP SYS XPDR 1(2) and TCAS 1(2), plus AP/FD TCAS MODE when the failed system is selected; XPDR 1+2 FAULT: XPDR 1+2, TCAS 1+2. The TCAS FAULT alert of the same system is not shown with it.
MFD SURV STATUS & SWITCHING: XPDR 1(2) and TCAS 1(2) shown failed when that XPDR is failed or unpowered.
Select the XPDR & TCAS system on the pedestal SURV panel or MFD SURV > STATUS & SWITCHING.
On SURV XPDR 1(2) FAULT, select the other system as the E/WD line asks.

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-46-20-30: the avionics side of the network server system (NSS AVNCS) has two servers; ANSU 2 provides the functions when ANSU 1 fails. Only ANSU 1 existed (the ANSU 2 failure did nothing). ANSU 2 is now built and takes over; with both failed the NSS AVNCS applications (AOC, eLogbook, maintenance) are lost. Supplies (FCOM DSC-46-20-70): ANSU 1 AC 2 or BAT 2, ANSU 2 AC 1 or AC EMER or BAT 1, FLT OPS ANSU AC ESS or BAT 1.

items: Nothing to set: the OIT avionics applications use whichever NSS AVNCS ANSU works.

children.title: Battery, EXT PWR, RAT generator, TR monitoring and drive disconnect failures

blocks.text: Sixteen new flyPad failures, simulated in the Rust electrical system, with the ELEC alerts of A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-24:

head: flyPad failure (ATA 24)
What it does
ECAM
rows: BAT 1, BAT 2, BAT ESS, APU BAT

children.title: Trim air duct overheat and jammed valve alerts

blocks.text: The trim air failures above now give the alerts of the A380 FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-21-10). The temperature controller monitors each trim air duct and valve: a duct above 70 deg C for 1.2 s is an overheat, latched until its HOT AIR pushbutton is set OFF; a valve that does not follow its demand is jammed. The FWS reads both from the controller and raises:

items: COND DUCT OVHT (master caution, single chime, FAULT light in the HOT AIR pushbutton, SD COND page) with the CKPT DUCT OVHT, CABIN DUCT OVHT and FWD CARGO DUCT OVHT cases, the deferred procedure WHEN DUCT OVHT OUT, and its STATUS lines (INOP SYS, CABIN TEMP REGUL DEGRADED, FWD CRG TEMP REGUL DEGRADED).

COND FWD CARGO TEMP REGUL FAULT for a jammed forward cargo trim air valve: CARGO TRIM AIR VLV FAULT, CARGO TEMP ... MONITOR, STATUS INFO FWD CRG TEMP REGUL DEGRADED (SD COND page only: no chime, no master light).
SD COND page: the amber OVHT mark of an overheated cockpit or cabin zone duct and the trim air valve mark of a jammed valve (before: never shown).
Cockpit duct overheat: COND DUCT OVHT, CKPT DUCT OVHT: HOT AIR 2 ... OFF; if the hot air valve stays open (HOT AIR JAMMED OPEN): PACK 2 ... OFF. HOT AIR 2 FAULT light, OVHT on the SD COND page.
Main deck zone duct overheat: CABIN DUCT OVHT: HOT AIR 1 ... OFF (HOT AIR 2 for an upper deck zone); if jammed open, PACK 1 (2) ... OFF; CARGO TEMP ... MONITOR.
Forward cargo duct overheat: FWD CARGO DUCT OVHT: HOT AIR 1 ... OFF; if jammed open, PACK 1 ... OFF.
Overheat gone (duct cooled, HOT AIR OFF): Deferred procedure WHEN DUCT OVHT OUT: HOT AIR 1 (2) ... ON, and PACK 1 (2) ... ON if it was switched off.
Forward cargo trim air valve jammed: COND FWD CARGO TEMP REGUL FAULT; STATUS INFO FWD CRG TEMP REGUL DEGRADED; the valve mark on the SD COND page.
Which HOT AIR valve supplies which zone is a design choice. Why: The FCOM does not say it: the main deck zones and the forward cargo are on HOT AIR 1, the cockpit and the upper deck on HOT AIR 2.

A jammed forward cargo valve counts as a degraded regulation (no INOP SYS). Why: Design choice: the aircraft has two forward cargo trim air valves and the FCOM says a jammed valve loses the "optimized" regulation.

The alerts are inhibited during the takeoff and the landing (FWS phases 3 to 7, 9, 10). Why: The FCOM gives the inhibition as a figure: that of COND HOT AIR FAULT / FWD CARGO ISOL FAULT is used. What to do: Test on the ground before takeoff or in cruise.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 21 Air Conditioning and activate a "... duct overheat (hot trim air)" or a "... trim air valve jammed" failure.
Follow the ECAM with the HOT AIR and PACK pushbuttons of the overhead AIR panel; check the SD COND page.
Deactivate the failure; when the duct has cooled, follow WHEN DUCT OVHT OUT.

The FAULT lights, the SD FUEL page and the FCOM alerts compare the selection with the real state (A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28, DSC-28-20).

blocks.text: The A380X port of the A32NX engine failures. Eight new failures in the flyPad chapter ATA 72 Engine. A flameout cuts the engine fuel once: the crew relights the engine with ENG MASTER OFF then ON inside the in-flight relight envelope of the A380 FCOM. A seizure also stops the core: no relight while the failure is active. The FWS gives the FCOM ENG FAIL, ENG SHUT DOWN, TWO ENGS OUT and ALL ENG FLAME OUT alerts for the four engines.

head: Id
flyPad failure (ATA 72 Engine)
What the code does
rows: Cuts the engine fuel (latched, MSFS fuel valve 60-63). The engine runs down and windmills. ENG MASTER OFF then ON inside the envelope relights it; it then runs normally while the failure stays listed. Deactivate and activate it again for a new flameout.
Cuts the fuel and stops the core (N3). No relight while the failure is active; once it is cleared the engine relights by the normal procedure.

children.title: What changed after the first sim tests

items: No N3 overshoot at the end of an in-flight start. The three in-flight relights of took N3 from 61 % to 97.5 % for 5 to 7 s with the levers in CL: while the engine was out the FADEC thrust loop wound the MSFS throttle up to 100 %. Now the MSFS throttle stays at idle while the engine is out or starting and until it runs at idle, then the engine accelerates to the lever or A/THR demand (A380 FCOM DSC-70-30 "FADEC stabilizes the engine at idle speed"; ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT: THR LEVER IDLE, then WHEN IDLE REACHED).

A compressor stall no longer ends that idle hold early. The hold ends when the commanded N1 reaches idle; with the "Engine n compressor stall" failure active at the end of a relight, the stall N1 loss (up to 15 %) was counted in the commanded N1 and the hold ended about 0.8 s early. The stall N1 loss is now taken out of that check (native : FL200, 300 kt relight, levers in CL, with a stall).

TWO ENGS OUT STATUS lists the FCOM lines PART SPLRs, PART L/G RETRACTION, G (Y) HYD SYS, PACK 1 (2) and one GEN line for the two generators lost (GEN 1+2, 3+4 on the same side; GEN 1+3, 1+4, 2+3, 2+4 on opposite sides).

ALL ENG FLAME OUT: its RAT MAN ON line is sensed (it turns green when the RAT is deployed), it has the missing L/G GRVTY (EXTN 2 MIN) DOWN line before a forced landing, and it inhibits ELEC EMER CONFIG as in the FCOM. The ELEC EMER CONFIG alert itself is on `core/a380x-elec`: this branch only computes the inhibited signal, so the inhibition shows once both branches are merged.
ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT shows the single engine limits MAX GUARANTEED ALTITUDE : 30000 FT and MIN SPEED FOR WINDML RELIGHT : 260 KT (FCOM).

No starter air without a source. A starter assisted relight was granted with no APU or crossbleed air: the air trapped in a stopped engine bleed duct and the slowly venting starter duct (about 45 s) kept the starter pressurised. The duct of an engine with no air source now empties within about 3 s, and the starter duct is empty (below 5 PSIG) about 3 s after the start valve closes (design values: the FCOM gives none).

X BLEED selector OPEN opens the crossbleed valves. Their manual control used the A320 DC ESS SHED busbar, which the A380 does not have; it now uses DC ESS (A380 FCOM DSC-36-30). The crossbleed starter air of a starter assisted relight depends on it.
The FADECs read the ENG START selector. They read a non-existent variable (always 0) and never saw the selector at IGN START; a static check now guards the variable names.

Each FADEC reads the LGCIU of its side: engines 1 and 2 LGCIU 1, engines 3 and 4 LGCIU 2 (design choice, the FCOM does not say). Before, the on-ground input of engines 3 and 4 was read past the end of the two-LGCIU list.
ENG MASTER OFF closes the HP fuel valve and the engine stops burning at once: see "HP fuel valve" below.

The thrust pulse at the end of a relight is softened. At the end of an in-flight start MSFS jumps its core to its top speed for a few seconds (recorded: 57.7 to 96.2 % in 0.5 s, thrust from -2 100 to +11 800 lb on the relit engine, a yaw kick). The core spike guard only hid it from the indications. A new FADEC limiter now holds the MSFS core near idle until it has settled, so the real thrust pulse is gone.

blocks.text: The relight envelope, read off the chart (IAS, flight level):

head: Zone
Where
Needs
rows: 260-340 kt up to FL300 (multiple engines out: from 250 kt, up to FL280)
ENG START IGN START, ENG MASTER OFF then ON; the start valve stays closed
150-260 kt up to FL200; 185-260 kt from FL200 to FL250
