items: Flameout in flight: N3, EGT and FF run down, FF 0, N1 / N3 settle at the windmill values. Amber ENG n FAIL with its FCOM procedure lines (THR LEVER n IDLE reads its own lever; ENG n RELIGHT PROC CONSIDER).

ENG MASTER OFF in flight: ENG n FAIL goes, ENG n SHUT DOWN comes with its STATUS: INOP SYS BTV for engine 2 or 3, CAT 3 DUAL and CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY with the APU off; the engine 4 bleed INOP comes from engine 4 (it came from another engine before).

Windmilling relight (zone 3, no APU): At the MASTER ON the fuel comes back; engine at idle in about 35 s; the start valve stays closed; both engine pumps of that engine are off-loaded during the start.
Crossbleed relight (zone 1, X BLEED OPEN): The start valve opens and the starter is pressurised in about 0.5 s; engine at idle in about 35 s; the start valve closes at N3 about 58 %.
Quick relight (ENG START at NORM): MASTER OFF then ON at once: the engine relights from about 75 % N3, at idle in about 25 s.

Any in-flight relight with the levers in CL (A/THR ON): N3 reaches idle (about 62 %) and holds there until the engine runs, then rises in about 5 s to the N3 of the other engines; it does not go more than 1-2 % above them.
ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT procedure: Single engine: MAX GUARANTEED ALTITUDE : 30000 FT, MIN SPEED FOR WINDML RELIGHT : 260 KT; multiple engines: 28000 FT and 250 KT.

Two engines failed: ENG TWO ENGS OUT ON SAME SIDE or ON OPPOSITE SIDE caution with LAND ANSA; the multiple-engine envelope applies. STATUS: PART SPLRs, PART L/G RETRACTION, G (Y) HYD SYS, PACK 1 (2), the GEN line of the two generators lost, CAT 2 / CAT 3 INOP, CAT 2 ONLY.
Three engines failed: ENG FAIL shows RELIGHT PROC APPLY instead of CONSIDER.

All four engines failed: Red ENG ALL ENG FLAME OUT (the FCOM title; it was ALL ENGINES FAILURE). RAT MAN ON turns green once the RAT is out; L/G GRVTY (EXTN 2 MIN) DOWN before a forced landing. With `core/a380x-elec` merged: no ELEC EMER CONFIG while it is shown.
Starter assisted relight below 260 kt without APU BLEED and with X BLEED at AUTO: No starter air: the engine does not relight (the starter duct is empty). Set X BLEED OPEN.
On the ground: A failed engine starts again as a normal start, with APU air (ENG START IGN START, MASTER OFF then ON). Two engines shut down for taxi give no TWO ENGS OUT caution.
The envelope governs every in-flight relight, also after a crew shutdown without any failure: MSFS would otherwise relight anywhere.
The quick relight also works in zone 3, where the windmill alone lights the engine.
A windmilling engine keeps N3 = 11 % x IAS / 260 kt and N1 = 1.5 x N3 (the FCOM gives no values).
FBW models the Trent 972 (three spools): the FCOM N2 (GP7200 core) is read on the Trent N3. ENG FAIL keeps the N3 ‹ 50 % threshold of FBW (the FCOM says N2 below 61 %).
TWO ENGS OUT is shown only with exactly two engines out (with three, ENG FAIL RELIGHT PROC APPLY; with four, ALL ENG FLAME OUT).
During a windmilling start the two engine pumps are off-loaded (depressurised), not disconnected: the ENG PUMPS DISC clutch cannot be reconnected in flight.

Once a relight is granted in flight the FADEC holds the MSFS core at 25 % N2: MSFS only burns above 20 % N2, and its starter only turns with the APU bleed, so without it a windmilling or crossbleed relight would never burn.
The throttle hold of an in-flight start (idle until the engine runs) works in flight only; a fallback ends it for a start that settles just below the FBW idle N3.
With the ENG MASTER OFF in flight the MSFS core runs down to the windmill speed: also so, not a fault.
ENG TWO ENGS OUT ON OPPOSITE SIDE has no PACK line in its procedure. Why: Not added yet (FCOM); its STATUS has the PACK 1 (2) INOP SYS line.

The MSFS core jump at the end of a relight is held, not removed. Why: At the end of a start the MSFS engine model jumps its core from its low idle (60 % corrected) to the top of its fuel flow table (about 97 %) for 2 to 6 s. The FADEC filters this jump for the indications (core spike guard): the E/WD N1/N3, fuel flow, EGT and the FADEC logic stay at idle (sim-tested: MSFS 96.8 %, E/WD 61.6 %); the guard also holds the N1 (so the fuel flow and EGT) while the MSFS fan follows the core jump a few frames late. Since the MSFS core limiter also holds the MSFS core near idle, so the thrust pulse of about 10 s recorded (yaw rate at most 0.2 deg/s) is gone (sim : passed). A ground start shows no jump (recorded). What to do: None.
Multiple engines out: the windmilling relight needs at least 250 kt. Why: FCOM envelope (sim-confirmed). What to do: Descend to keep the speed.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems, FADEC and fbw WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 72 Engine and activate a flameout or a seizure.

Follow the ECAM. To relight: get inside the envelope (table above), ENG START selector (pedestal, engine panel) IGN START, ENG MASTER OFF for 30 s, then ON. Below 260 kt without the APU, set the X BLEED selector (overhead AIR panel) to OPEN for starter air.
For a quick relight, set the ENG MASTER OFF then ON at once (within 30 s, N3 above 45 %), at any ENG START position.
When the engine is at idle: ENG START NORM, X BLEED AUTO; clear the failure in the flyPad (a seizure must be cleared before a relight).

blocks.text: Needs one MSFS restart after installing the branch.
Windmilling relight: engine 1 relights by the airflow alone, no APU
Setup: in flight at FL200, 300 kt, AP and A/THR ON, APU OFF, X BLEED selector AUTO (overhead AIR panel), ENG START selector NORM (pedestal, engine panel with the four ENG MASTER levers).
Quick relight: engine 4 relights at NORM
Setup: FL150, 240 kt, ENG START selector NORM.
Starter assisted relight with crossbleed air: engine 3
Setup: FL150, 210 kt, APU OFF.
On the ground: relight with APU air, and two engines out for taxi
Setup: on the ground, four engines at idle, parking brake ON, APU AVAIL, APU BLEED pb ON (overhead AIR panel), ENG START NORM.
Two engines out at 255 kt: engine 1 relights by windmilling
Setup: FL100, 255 kt (FCU speed), flaps 0, AP and A/THR ON, APU OFF, APU BLEED OFF, X BLEED AUTO. Keep at least 250 kt: descend if needed.
All engines out at FL200
Setup: FL200, 300 kt, APU OFF, ENG START selector NORM, four engines running.

Recording used for the tests: per engine FUEL_CUT, RELIGHT_ATTEMPT, RELIGHT_IGNITION, ENGINE_STATE, ENGINE_N3, PNEU starter valve / pressurized, MSFS TURB ENG N2, GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION and fuel flow, with the airspeed, altitude, ENG START selector, X BLEED and APU BLEED.

children.title: Automatic relight with both igniters, and the engine feed tank fuel draw

blocks.text: In a flight of MSFS dropped the combustion of all four engines by itself at 7 900 ft. With the ENG START selector at NORM nothing relit them: the engines windmilled for 150 s until the crew selected IGN START. Two changes:

items: AUTO RELIGHT (A380 FCOM DSC-70-80-30-20 QUICK AND AUTO RELIGHT: "If the FADEC detects an engine flame out, on ground or in flight, continuous ignition with both igniters is automatically selected. The ignition is maintained for 60 s after engine relight."). When a running engine (ENG MASTER ON, FADEC supplied, fuel not cut) loses its combustion for 0.5 s, its FADEC turns on both igniters whatever the ENG START selector position, until 60 s of continuous combustion after the relight.

Feed tank draw. Each engine is fed by MSFS through a 1 gallon buffer tank that the FADEC drains by the fuel burned. The FADEC took the whole burn of an update at once and compared kilograms with pounds, so one long sim frame could empty the four buffer tanks together and leave no fuel at any engine (the suspected cause of the four-engine flameout). Now, while the feed tank holds fuel, the FADEC leaves a small quantity in the buffer and carries the rest of the burn over to the next updates, so the fuel burned is still taken in full. A dry feed tank still empties the buffer and the engine flames out (fuel exhaustion).

MSFS loses the combustion of a running engine, ENG START at NORM: Within about 1 s the FADEC turns on the ignition; the engine burns again as soon as it has fuel, back at the thrust of the others within about 30 s. SD ENGINE page: "A B" on that engine. 60 s after the relight the ignition goes off.
ENG MASTER OFF, ENG FIRE pb released, or a flyPad flameout / seizure failure: No auto relight: a manual abort, an unpowered FADEC or a failure the crew must relight (section above).
Long sim frame (stutter) in a climb: The four engines keep burning; the fuel used rises steadily.

There is no flyPad failure for an MSFS flameout. Why: The flyPad flameout cuts the fuel on purpose and asks for a crew relight; the auto relight is for a flameout the FADEC did not cause. What to do: The test closed the MSFS fuel valve of engine 4 for 5 s with a SimConnect tool. Since the HP fuel valve hold (below) the systems reopen an MSFS valve that disagrees with them, so that way of testing probably no longer cuts the fuel.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The FADEC WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to set: keep the ENG MASTER levers ON and the ENG START selector at NORM in flight.
If an engine flames out by itself, watch it relight on the E/WD; follow ENG FAIL if it does not.

blocks.text: The flameout needs MSFS to lose the combustion by itself, or a SimConnect tool that interrupts the engine fuel (see the limitation above).

The SD ENGINE page drew an "A" from the N2 during a start, whatever the FADEC did. It now shows the igniters the FADEC really energizes (A380 FCOM DSC-70-90: "The igniter A(B) is energized." / "Both igniters A and B are energized."), in this priority order:

items: None with the ENG MASTER OFF or the FADEC unpowered (ENG FIRE pb released).
"A B" when the FADEC selects both igniters itself: auto relight, an in-flight relight that lights up.
"A B" for the quick relight (ENG MASTER OFF then ON within 30 s above 45 % N3), for 60 s.

Start: in flight "A B"; on the ground the igniters of the start sequence (next section): one igniter from 20 % to 58 % N3, A or B alternated at each start, "A B" for a new automatic attempt, none during the automatic dry crank.

Continuous ignition (ENG START at IGN START, engine running): "A B" at once in flight; on the ground only after the selector was set to NORM then back to IGN START after the start, and not at low power (N1 below 53 % for more than 30 s), as in FCOM DSC-70-80-20.

A failed igniter is still shown when it is energized ("A" during the first attempt with igniter A failed). Why: The FCOM shows the igniter energized and has no line for a failed one; kept by decision.
The continuous ignition inhibition at high combustion chamber pressure is not modelled. Why: MSFS has no combustion chamber pressure.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The FADEC WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open the SD ENGINE page (ECP ENG key); the start parameters show the igniter letters above the start valve of each engine during a start, a relight or the continuous ignition.

children.title: Engine ignition and start failures, reference ground start

blocks.text: The FBW FADEC ran the engine model but not what a real FADEC does during a start. The ground start now follows the A380 FCOM (DSC-70-80-20 IGNITION, DSC-70-80-30 STARTING, DSC-70-80-40 CRANKING): ENG START selector to IGN START, then ENG MASTER ON; one igniter (alternated between starts) and fuel at 20 % N3; start valve closed and ignition off at about 58 % N3. A start that does not light up within 20 s, stalls, hangs or goes above 745 °C EGT is aborted, dry cranked for 30 s and tried again with both igniters, up to three attempts. A start valve stuck closed, no starter air or a failed starter leaves the core at rest. The ENG MAN START pbs work: dry crank (ENG START at CRANK, MAN START ON, ENG MASTER OFF), wet crank and manual start.

head: flyPad failure (ATA)
What it does
rows: That igniter does not light the engine. The first automatic attempt with only that igniter does not light up: START FAULT NO LIGHT UP, then a new attempt with both. ENG n IGN A (B) FAULT; both failed: ENG n IGN A+B FAULT.
No starter air: the core stays at rest. ENG n START VLV FAULT (NOT OPEN) with VLV STUCK CLOSED.
The valve does not close after the start: ENG n START VLV FAULT (NOT CLOSED).
Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) hot start (start EGT over limit) (80)
The start EGT overshoots: START FAULT EGT OVERLIMIT, the start is aborted.
Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) hung start (N3 stops below idle) (80)
The core stops accelerating below idle: START FAULT HUNG START.
The starter does not turn the core although it gets air: START FAULT LOW N2, no further attempt.

head: Alert
Lines (A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70)
rows: The sub-case (NO STARTER AIR PRESSURE, LOW N2, HUNG START, EGT OVERLIMIT, NO LIGHT UP, ENG STALL, STARTER TIME EXCEEDED, THR LEVERS NOT AT IDLE), then: no starter air: XBLEED OPEN, APU BLEED ON (in flight MIN SPEED FOR WINDML RELIGHT : 260 KT); automatic start on the ground: NEW START IN PROGRESS, then ENG n MASTER OFF once aborted; manual start: ENG n MASTER OFF, ENG START SEL CRANK, AFTER 30S: ENG START SEL NORM, ENG n MAN START OFF; levers not at idle: ALL THR LEVERS IDLE.
ENG n START VLV FAULT (NOT CLOSED)
ENG n BLEED OFF (in flight), APU BLEED OFF (engine 1), X BLEED CLOSE, ENG n MAN START OFF (manual start), ENG n MASTER OFF (on the ground), WING A-ICE OFF and AVOID ICING CONDs (engines 1 and 4).
ENG n START VLV FAULT (NOT OPEN)
VLV STUCK CLOSED; on the ground ENG n MAN START OFF, ENG n MASTER OFF; in flight MIN SPEED FOR WINDML RELIGHT : 260 KT, WINDMILL START INITIATED, ENG PARAMETERS MONITOR WITH CARE.
STATUS MORE: REDUND LOSS ENG n IGN A (B).
STATUS INOP SYS ENG n IGNITION.

blocks.text: The start alerts are inhibited in the flight phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10 (IGN A (B) FAULT also in phase 8), per the FCOM figures. START FAULT and IGN A (B) FAULT come without chime and MASTER CAUT; IGN A+B FAULT keeps them (see "Engine alerts as in the FCOM" below for the in-flight START FAULT cases).

items: Hung start, stall and starter detection times are design values. Why: The FCOM gives the symptoms, not the times; the FBW engine model has no compressor pressure.
START FAULT LOW N1 is not modelled. Why: No N1 rotor failure.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and FADEC WASM modules and the pedestal behaviour XML change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Normal start: APU BLEED ON, ENG START selector IGN START, ENG MASTER ON; the FADEC does the rest (ENG START NORM when the engines are running).
Failures: flyPad > Failures > ATA 74 Ignition or ATA 80 Starting; activate one, start the engine and follow the ECAM.
Dry crank: ENG START selector CRANK, ENG MAN START n pb ON (ENG MASTER OFF), then OFF.

blocks.text: Setup: A380X cold and dark, batteries ON, APU AVAIL, APU BLEED ON, all ENG MASTER levers OFF, thrust levers at IDLE, SD ENGINE page.

children.title: HP fuel valve: no engine burning without a FADEC start

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-70-30 ENGINE SHUTDOWN: with the ENG MASTER OFF "The FADEC closes the LP and HP fuel valves. The engine decelerates and stops." The ENG MASTER only closed an MSFS valve upstream of the engine buffer tank, so MSFS kept burning a shut down engine for 20 to 60 s, and a restart in that time skipped the start sequence. And with the ENG START selector at NORM, ENG MASTER ON on the ground let the MSFS starter turn the core and MSFS lit it at 22 % N2 without any FADEC start (the FCOM: IGN START first, fuel at 20 %; at NORM the MASTER ON starts nothing).

items: The HP fuel valve of each engine (the MSFS fuel valves 60-63 after the buffer tanks) is now closed with the ENG MASTER OFF or the fuel cut, and on the ground until the FADEC start sequence reaches its fuel-on point (IGN START then MASTER ON) or the quick relight opens it (MASTER OFF then ON within 30 s above 45 % N3). It is open for the aircraft presets and a flight loaded with the master ON. In flight the relight logic keeps the fuel cut until the engine may light up. Once open it stays open until the MASTER OFF or a fuel cut, so a running engine keeps its fuel at NORM and its auto relight has fuel.

MSFS could reopen a closed valve by itself a few seconds later (flight load, power-up of the valve circuit). The systems now watch the MSFS valve switch and command it again whenever it disagrees, and once on the first update of a flight.
An engine is shown running (ON) only when MSFS really burns in it: a core turned past 20 % by the MSFS starter at NORM no longer shows ON unlit (and no longer triggers the auto relight).
ENG MASTER OFF: The engine stops burning at once (FF 0, EGT falls) and runs down.
ENG MASTER ON again soon after a shutdown, ENG START at IGN START: A full start sequence: start valve, one igniter, fuel at 20 % N3.
ENG MASTER ON on the ground with the ENG START selector at NORM: Nothing lights up: no fuel flow, no EGT.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Start an engine the FCOM way: ENG START selector IGN START first, then ENG MASTER ON.
Shut it down with ENG MASTER OFF.

children.title: Engine oil failures (leak, filter clog, overheat)

blocks.text: Twelve new failures, three per engine, computed by the FADEC on the oil quantity, pressure and temperature, with the SD ENGINE page indications and the ECAM alerts of the A380 FCOM (DSC-70-90, PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70).

head: flyPad failure (ATA 79 Oil)
What it does
rows: The oil system empties at 2 qt/min (the tank reading falls about 1.6 qt/min); the pump pressure stays full down to 1.3 qt in the system and is gone at 0.3 qt, so OIL PRESS LO follows the low oil quantity indication.
CLOGGED on the SD ENGINE page and ENG n OIL FILTER CLOGGED; no other effect.

The oil temperature rises towards a target that grows with the core speed (170 °C at idle, 230 °C at 100 % N3, 60 s time constant): OIL TEMP HI about 2 min after the failure at cruise; reducing thrust brings it below 196 °C, at IDLE within about 1 min. Once cleared, the oil cools down gradually.

items: SD ENGINE page, oil quantity: Pulses below the 1.2 qt advisory (first white dash).
SD ENGINE page, oil temperature: Pulses above 163 °C.
SD ENGINE page, oil pressure: FCOM scale 0-100 / 100-440 PSI, red at or below 25 PSI; CLOGGED below it for a clogged filter.
Oil pressure below 25 PSI: Red ENG n OIL PRESS LO (MASTER WARN, continuous chime): THR LEVER n IDLE, ENG n MASTER OFF; then ENG n SHUT DOWN.
Oil temperature above 196 °C: Amber ENG n OIL TEMP HI: THR LEVER n REDUCE BELOW OIL TEMP LIM, IF HI TEMP PERSISTS: ENG n MASTER OFF.
Clogged filter: Amber ENG n OIL FILTER CLOGGED on the ground (phases 1, 2, 11 and 12), without chime or MASTER CAUT; in flight only the SD CLOGGED.
The leak and overheat rates are design values. Why: The FCOM gives no rates.
The alerts are monitored only with the engine running and its ENG MASTER ON. Why: Design choice: a stopped engine has no oil pressure, and the procedures end with the MASTER OFF.
Flight phase inhibitions. Why: OIL PRESS LO: phases 1, 5, 6, 12; OIL TEMP HI: 1, 4-7, 9, 10, 12; OIL FILTER CLOGGED: 3 to 10 (FCOM figures). What to do: Test in cruise.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and FADEC WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 79 Oil and activate a leak, a filter clog or an overheat.
Watch the SD ENGINE page; follow the ECAM (reduce thrust, or IDLE and ENG MASTER OFF).
Deactivate the failure.

blocks.text: Setup: level at FL200, 300 kt, A/THR ON, four engines running, SD ENGINE page.

children.title: Engine fuel filter clog, ENG MASTER FAULT light, SD start valve and N3 red cross

items: Fuel filter clog: new failures Engine 1-4 fuel filter clog (ATA 73). Amber CLOGGED below the fuel flow on the SD ENGINE page while the engine runs, and the ENG n FUEL FILTER CLOGGED caution (FCOM: pressure drop above 35 PSI, crew awareness, inhibited in flight phases 3 to 10). No effect on the engine: the filter is bypassed.

ENG MASTER FAULT light: it comes on when the FADEC aborts an automatic start (FCOM DSC-70-90), and goes off with the ENG MASTER OFF. It followed the MSFS engine failure before, which a start abort does not set.
SD start valve: amber when the start valve is abnormally open or closed (START VLV FAULT); with a valve fault the start parameters show even at NORM, so a valve stuck open after the start is seen.
N3 red cross: above the 118.7 % red limit a red "+" shows next to N3 until the next start of that engine on the ground (FCOM: N2 of the GP7200 core, read on the Trent N3).

Starter failure fix: with a sheared starter the MSFS starter could still turn the core to about 6 %, past the 5 % starter fault detection, so the start never aborted. The FADEC now keeps the core at rest and aborts the start without a new attempt (FCOM DSC-70-80-30-20).
The FAULT light has no HP fuel valve and no overthrust cause. Why: FBW has no HP fuel valve failure (the valve always follows its command) and no overthrust protection.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and FADEC WASM modules and the cockpit behaviour change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Call the SD ENGINE page (ECP ENG key).
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 73 (fuel filter clog) or ATA 80 (starter shaft shear, start valve stuck) and activate the failure, then start or run the engine as below.
Deactivate the failures after the test.

blocks.text: Setup: at the gate, APU running, APU BLEED ON, all ENG MASTER levers OFF, ENG START selector IGN START.

children.title: Engine stall, EGT overtemperature and vibration failures

blocks.text: Twelve new failures where the engine keeps running. What each one does is a design choice: the FCOM gives the symptoms, not values.

head: flyPad failure (ATA)
What it does
rows: Above 60 % N1 command the engine stalls: it loses thrust (the thrust loop aims lower), the EGT rises quickly, N1 / N3 fluctuate. It recovers with the lever at idle and stalls again above the threshold.
The EGT is higher, more so at high thrust: ENG EGT OVER LIMIT at climb thrust.

N1, N2 and N3 vibrations growing with the square of the rotor speed: above the SD advisory (5 units) at climb and cruise thrust, below it at reduced thrust and at idle. At a low cruise power the advisory can show on N3 only (fan 60 %: N1 4.7; core 81 %: N3 5.3), as the FCOM advisory is per rotor; reducing thrust clears it. No ECAM alert (ABN PROC).

items: Stall: Amber ENG n STALL (SD ENGINE page): THR LEVER n IDLE, ENG n PARAMETERS CHECK, IF ABNORMAL: ENG n MASTER OFF, ENG n RELIGHT PROC CONSIDER. Inhibited from V1 to 400 ft unless two or more engines stall.
EGT above its limit: Amber ENG n EGT OVER LIMIT: THR LEVER n REDUCE BELOW EGT LIMIT, IF OVER LIMIT PERSISTS: ENG n MASTER OFF; the amber attention box on the engine.
N1 or N2 above the red limit: Red ENG n N1/N2 OVER LIMIT: THR LEVER n REDUCE BELOW N1 LIMIT, IF OVER LIMIT PERSISTS: ENG n MASTER OFF.

E/WD EGT gauge: A red mark at the highest EGT reached above the red line. The amber limit comes from the active thrust limit (none at FLEX / TOGA or in reverse, the CLB / MCT limit otherwise), not from the lever angle.
SD ENGINE page: Separate N1, N2 and N3 vibrations that pulse above 5 units; N3 red above its limit.

The A380X has no overspeed failure (the A32NX has one). Why: Not part of this stage. The shared overspeed ceiling fields added for the A32NX LEAP-1A red lines are set to none on the A380X: no change here.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems, FADEC and fbw WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 72 Engine (stall, EGT) or ATA 77 Engine Indicating (vibration) and activate the failure at climb or cruise thrust.
Follow the ECAM: reduce the thrust of that engine; deactivate the failure.

blocks.text: Setup: four engines running, A/THR ON, CLB, climbing at 280 kt.

children.title: FADEC, thrust lever and reverser failures

blocks.text: Twenty-six new failures with the alerts, procedures and STATUS of the A380 FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70). Reversers exist on engines 2 and 3 only.

head: flyPad failure (ATA)
What it does
ECAM
rows: The FADEC still controls the engine, but the A/THR and the SD ENGINE page lose it (XX on the SD; the E/WD keeps N1, THR, EGT). The engine follows its thrust lever.
ENG n FADEC FAULT: THR LEVER n MAN ADJUST, ENG n PARAMETERS MONITOR, IF ABNORMAL: THR LEVER n IDLE, ENG n MASTER OFF; STATUS INOP SYS ENG n A/THR (A/THR engaged).
The FADEC has lost the lever: the engine is at idle on the ground and limited to CLB in flight (the A/THR still manages it between idle and CLB).
ENG n THR LEVER FAULT: on the ground ENG n IDLE ONLY, THR LEVER n IDLE; in flight ENG n CLB ONLY, THR LEVER n CLB; STATUS INOP SYS ENG n THR LEVER, INFO ENG n IDLE (CLB) ONLY.
The reverser does not deploy; the engine stays at reverse idle.
ENG 2 (3) REVERSER FAULT: T.O PERF CHECK (on the ground), LDG DIST IMPACT ON WET/CONTAM RWY ONLY.
The cowls stay stowed (no reverse thrust, no buffet); the FADEC sets the engine at idle.
ENG 2 (3) REVERSER UNLOCKED: ENG n IDLE ONLY, THR LEVER n IDLE, ENG n MASTER OFF on the ground; in flight IF BUFFET: ENG n MASTER OFF; STATUS INFO ENG n IDLE ONLY.
The tertiary lock stays released; the primary locks hold the cowls stowed.
ENG 2 (3) REVERSER ENERGIZED: THR LEVER n IDLE.
The locks are not released: no deployment.
ENG 2 (3) REV LOCKED: T.O PERF CHECK, LDG DIST IMPACT ON WET/CONTAM RWY ONLY.
ENG 2 (3) REVERSER CTL FAULT: T.O PERF CHECK, LDG DIST IMPACT ON WET/CONTAM RWY ONLY.

items: Reverse thrust stays at reverse idle until the reverser is fully deployed (FCOM DSC-70-70): a reverser that does not deploy no longer gives forward thrust with the lever in reverse.
Reverse thrust reaches MSFS. The in-flight start throttle hold (engine failures section) clamped the MSFS throttle at 0 and so blocked all reverse thrust; the reverse throttle now goes through.

An engine with a FADEC FAULT follows its thrust lever. In the test the engine stayed at its N1 with the levers in CL: the FADEC THRUST LOCK latched when the lost link took the A/THR away. The A380 ENG FADEC FAULT does not disconnect the A/THR (only that engine is lost, INOP SYS ENG n A/THR), and the procedure says THR LEVER ... MAN ADJUST, so the lock no longer latches for it.
ENG REVERSER SELECTED comes up when the lever of engine 2 or 3 is in reverse in flight: THR LEVER 2 (3)(2+3) FWD THR.
ENG 2 (3) REVERSER INHIBITED and REVERSER MINOR FAULT are not wired. Why: No flyPad failure for them (maintenance action / no effect).
"Before takeoff" lines (T.O PERF CHECK) show on the ground. Why: Design choice: before takeoff = on the ground.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and fbw WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 73 Engine - Fuel And Control (FADEC, thrust lever) or ATA 78 Exhaust (reversers 2 and 3) and activate a failure.
Follow the ECAM; for a FADEC FAULT adjust that thrust lever by hand.
Deactivate the failure.

blocks.text: Setup: FL100, 250 kt, flaps 0, AP and A/THR ON, four levers in CL.

children.title: ENG THR LEVERS NOT SET and ENG OIL TEMP LO

blocks.text: Two take-off alerts of the A380 FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70) that the A380X did not trigger. Both are amber cautions (MASTER CAUT, single chime), shown in flight phases 2 and 3 only.

items: ENG THR LEVERS NOT SET : a thrust lever of a running engine is at or between CL and FLX/MCT, or at FLX/MCT without a FLEX TEMP, for 3 s. Line: ALL THR LEVERS ... TOGA (no FLEX TEMP: TOGA take-off) or THR LEVERS ... MCT/FLEX (FLEX TEMP entered, levers below FLX/MCT).

ENG 1(2)(3)(4) OIL TEMP LO : on the ground the engine oil is below 50 °C 30 s after the engine is running, or after the T.O CONFIG pb, or at take-off power. Lines: THR LEVER n ... IDLE, DELAY T.O FOR WARM UP.
No derated take-off case. Why: FBW has no derated take-off.
A T.O CONFIG press keeps the oil monitor armed until the engine stops. Why: Design choice: the FCOM says "after the flight crew presses".
Nothing to set. Set all thrust levers to FLX/MCT (FLEX TEMP entered) or TOGA for take-off.
After an engine start in the cold, wait until the oil is warm before take-off.

children.title: FADEC thrust failures: ENG THRUST LOSS and ENG T.O THRUST DISAGREE

blocks.text: Two FCOM cautions that need a FADEC fault the sim cannot produce, with the failures that make them possible (they act on the FADEC models of the fbw WASM):

items: New flyPad failures, ATA 73: Engine 1 (2, 3, 4) max thrust miscalculated (thrust loss) (73050-73053): that FADEC computes a maximum THR 15 % lower, so the engine gives less thrust above idle (N1 command = IDLE + 0.85 x (limit - IDLE)).
ENG 1(2)(3)(4) THRUST LOSS (amber, phase 3 only): the maximum THR of an engine is 10 % lower than that of at least two other engines. Lines: THR LEVER n ... IDLE, ENG n MASTER ... OFF.
New flyPad failures, ATA 73: FADEC 1 (2, 3, 4) FLEX TEMP not received (T.O mode TOGA) (73060-73063): that FADEC takes off in TOGA mode (MCT thrust in the FLX/MCT detent).
ENG T.O THRUST DISAGREE (amber, phases 2 and 11): the FADECs do not all have the same take-off mode. No line (crew awareness).
THRUST LOSS shows in phase 3 only. Why: FCOM inhibition; the A380X FWS needs two levers at take-off power for phase 3. What to do: Set two levers (for example 3 and 4) to FLX/MCT.
Use FADEC 2, 3 or 4 for the FLEX TEMP failure. Why: The E/WD thrust rating is the one of FADEC 1.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The fbw WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
flyPad > Failures > ATA 73 Engine - Fuel And Control: activate one of the failures before take-off.
Follow the caution; clear the failure to end it.

children.title: E/WD N1 red above 111 % with a red cross

blocks.text: FCOM DSC-70-90 N1 INDICATIONS: the N1 value turns red above the 111 % red limit, and a red cross stays next to it after an exceedance until the next engine start on the ground. The A380X E/WD N1 stayed green.

items: Hard to see in the sim. Why: The A380X has no N1 overspeed failure; the N1 rarely passes 111 %.
Nothing to set. After an N1 exceedance the red cross stays until the next engine start on the ground.

children.title: Crossbleed engine start with X BLEED at AUTO

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-36-10-50 : the crossbleed valves "are normally closed. They open automatically, and at the same time: On ground, at engine start; When the APU bleed valve is selected open; In case any engine bleed system fails." The first case was missing: with the X BLEED selector at AUTO the valves stayed closed during an engine start, so the crossbleed engine start of PRO-SUP-70-10 (ALL ENG BLEEDS ON, X BLEED AUTO, SECOND ENG START) had no starter air without the APU. Now the three crossbleed valves open together on the ground while the FADEC commands the start valve of any engine open, and the running engines supply the starter air.

items: "At engine start" is from the ENG MASTER ON (or MAN START ON, crank) to the start valve closing at 58.4 % N3 or the end of the start. Why: The FCOM gives no opening or closing point (design choice).
On the ground only. Why: FCOM rule. In flight a starter assisted relight without the APU still needs X BLEED OPEN (engine failures section). What to do: Set X BLEED OPEN in flight.
An engine bleed failure is modelled as an ENG BLEED pb OFF. Why: There is no engine bleed failure with the pb ON yet.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Start the first engine with APU air as usual.
Set the APU BLEED pb OFF, keep all ENG BLEED pbs ON and the X BLEED selector at AUTO.
ENG START selector IGN START, then ENG MASTER ON for the next engine: the crossbleed valves open by themselves and close again after the start.

blocks.text: Setup: on the ground, PARKING BRK ON, APU running with the APU BLEED pb ON, engine 1 started and at idle, ENG MASTER 2, 3 and 4 OFF, ENG START selector IGN START, all four ENG BLEED pbs ON, X BLEED selector AUTO.

children.title: Engine alerts as in the reference

blocks.text: The engine alerts of this branch are aligned with A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70 and its figures (levels, inhibitions, SD pages, lines):

items: ENG n FAIL is no longer inhibited from V1 to 1500 ft (the FCOM figure has no inhibition). Its line AUTO RELIGHT IN PROGRESS shows only while the FADEC auto relight runs.
The IGNITION memo also shows for the continuous ignition the FADEC selects by itself (auto relight, quick relight).
ENG n START FAULT, IGN A (B) FAULT, OIL FILTER CLOGGED and FUEL FILTER CLOGGED come without chime and without MASTER CAUT (crew awareness). IGN A+B FAULT keeps the single chime and MASTER CAUT.
ENG n EGT OVER LIMIT and N1/N2 OVER LIMIT call no SD page. EGT OVER LIMIT does not come up with an ENG n FADEC FAULT (FCOM ENG FADEC FAULT: the EGT OVER LIMIT alert will not trigger in that case).

In flight, START FAULT NO STARTER AIR PRESSURE comes up with its windmill start lines (WINDMILL START INITIATED, ENG PARAMETERS MONITOR, IF ABNORMAL: ENG n MAN START OFF, ENG n MASTER OFF), and NO LIGHT UP comes after the 30 s of the relight (ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT), not after the 20 s of the ground start. The shared engine start schedule got two fields for this; the A32NX keeps its values.

New deferred procedures: ENG TWO ENGS OUT (ALL PHASES: IF GW DECREASE RQRD, JETTISON ARM ON, JETTISON ACTIVE ON), TWO ENGS OUT ON SAME SIDE (FOR APPROACH) and ON OPPOSITE SIDE (APPR & LDG), shown under their heading on the STATUS page. ENG n START VLV FAULT (NOT CLOSED) gets its LIMITATIONS, INOP SYS and, for engine 1 or 4, the FOR APPROACH deferred procedure IF SEVERE ICE ACCRETION: FOR LDG : FLAP LVR 3.

blocks.text: On this branch the JETTISON ARM / ACTIVE lines of the TWO ENGS OUT deferred procedures read the FUEL JETTISON pbs directly; with `core/fuel` merged they read its jettison FWS states.

items: A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes (engine start schedule). What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to set: follow the E/WD as usual. An alert without chime or MASTER CAUT is a crew awareness alert.
With two engines out, check the deferred procedures on the STATUS page before the approach.

blocks.text: Eight new failures of the braking control system (BCS), the emergency brake control unit (EBCU) and the steering control system (SCS), with the BRAKES and STEER alerts of A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-32. The Rust hydraulics choose the braking mode the faults leave (DSC-32-10-30) and the nose wheel steering supply (DSC-32-10-40).

head: flyPad failure (ATA 32)
What it does
ECAM
rows: The pedals brake in alternate braking (ALTN circuit, A-SKID available).
Alone: no effect while normal braking works. With the normal braking failed: emergency braking through the EBCU (no A-SKID, pressure limited).
BRAKES ALTN BRK FAULT; with the EBCU failed too: ALTN + EMER BRK FAULT
The EBCU is lost; with normal and alternate braking failed too, no pedal braking: the parking brake is the only braking.
BRAKES EMER BRK FAULT; all three: BRAKES PEDAL BRAKING FAULT (replaces the single alerts)
Steering normal nose wheel steering (NORM N/W STEER)
The nose wheel steers on the alternate system (steering LEHGS), at most 10 deg/s instead of 15 deg/s.
Steering alternate nose wheel steering (steering LEHGS)
No alternate NWS: with the normal NWS also lost, the nose wheel casters.
The body wheel steering stays centred and locked.
One SCS is enough (the backup takes over); with both lost neither NWS nor BWS works.
STEER CTL 1 (2) FAULT; both: STEER N/W + B/W STEER FAULT

items: BRAKES ACCU PRESS LO (accumulator below 3 000 psi for 10 s, design value) and PARK BRK PRESS LO (park brake on and pressure below 1 700 psi for 5 s, design value).
The second B/W STEER FAULT text is renamed B/W STEER NOT LOCKED, as in the FCOM.
With only engines 3 and 4 running (no GREEN), the nose wheel now steers on the alternate system instead of not at all, as the FCOM asks.
A brake fault acts on all wheel groups at once. Why: The model has one NORM circuit (GREEN) and one ALTN circuit (YELLOW, one accumulator) for all wheel groups; the real A380 splits them per gear.
The nose wheel steering request keeps the A-SKID condition of this base. Why: The change that drops it is on `core/fcom-audit-fixes`. What to do: Merge that branch for it.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 32 Landing Gear and activate a brake or steering failure on the ground.
Follow the E/WD; brake with the pedals (watch the triple brake pressure indicator) and steer with the tiller.
Deactivate the failure.

blocks.text: Setup: on the ground, four engines running, park brake OFF, below 10 kt.

children.title: Erroneous ADR airspeed and AOA failures, PRIM air data monitoring

blocks.text: Six new failures: ADR 1 (2)(3) airspeed erroneous (pitot) and ADR 1 (2)(3) angle of attack erroneous. The ADR then sends a wrong value with a valid status (airspeed 40 kt low, AOA 10 deg high; design values above the FCOM monitoring thresholds), which the PRIM model could never reject, as it only votes on the status.

A new systems module compares the three ADRs with the standby air data as the PRIMs do (A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-30-10 / -40) and rejects a diverging source until the end of the flight, or all of them when it cannot tell which one is wrong. A rejected ADR goes to the PRIM and SEC models as failed: alternate law with two ADRs out, direct law with all of them.

head: Alert (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-34-10)
When
Lines
rows: One or more sources rejected (not all).
ADR n (or STBY INSTRUMENTS) REJECTED BY PRIMs, RISK OF UNDUE OVERSPEED WARNING (two sources), AIR DATA XCHECK, AIR DATA SWTG AS RQRD.
ALL AIR DATA REJECTED BY PRIMs, the thrust and pitch target lines of the FCOM tables for the altitude, FLAPS & L/G MAINTAIN CURRENT CONF, ... FLY THE GREEN, FLY PITCH AND THRUST.
Two or more AOAs rejected (one alone gives no NAV alert).

blocks.text: Also: F/CTL DIRECT LAW MAX SPEED 310/.86 and MANEUVER WITH CARE are now APPR & LDG limitations, as in the FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-27-10); a limitation shown in ALL PHASES by another alert is not repeated in APPR & LDG.

items: A rejected ADR stays rejected until the end of the flight, also after the failure is cleared. Why: As the PRIMs do (FCOM). What to do: A new flight.
The cabin altitude table, the MFP heating lines and the level-off thrust table above FL 250 of ALL AIR DATA DISAGREE are not shown. Why: Not modelled.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems and fbw WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 34 Navigation and activate an ADR airspeed or AOA failure in flight.
Follow the E/WD (cross-check the air data, switch the AIR DATA source as required).
Deactivate the failure; the PRIMs keep the ADR rejected for the rest of the flight.

blocks.text: Setup: cruise above FL250, AP ON.

children.title: reference : RCL / RCL LAST, T.O CONFIG NORMAL, automatic SD pages, BTV INOP

items: RCL LAST brings back the alert of the last CLR action (both pbs wrote the same variable before). RCL brings back every cleared alert at once, or NORMAL for 3 s when there is none; only a press of more than 3 s shows the alerts inhibited by the flight phase, so a short press no longer removes the T.O INHIBIT memo for the flight (A380 FCOM DSC-31-40-20).

T.O CONFIG NORMAL follows the A380 checks of DSC-31-40-10 (the FCOM list of T.O CONFIG alerts: surfaces and trims, doors, BRAKES HOT, the generators and drives of the four engines, engine oil temperature, PITCH TRIM/FMS/CG and T.O FLAPS/FMS DISAGREE, T.O speeds) instead of the A320 GEN 1+2 / two doors condition.
Automatic SD pages (DSC-31-40-30): CRUISE from 1500 ft after take-off (it came 60 s after the flaps were up), WHEEL at the landing gear extension at any altitude (only below 16000 ft before).

BTV INOP: while an ECAM alert lists BTV in STATUS INOP SYS (ENG 2 (3) SHUT DOWN, TWO ENGS OUT, ENG 2 (3) REVERSER faults), BTV does not arm, and an armed BTV reverts to BRK HI (DSC-32-20-220, LIM-32).
T.O CONFIG NORMAL does not check the ELEC GEN / DRIVE alerts on this branch. Why: Those alerts are on `core/a380x-elec`. What to do: Use `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts` (both branches merged).
CONFIG L (R) SIDESTICK FAULT (BY TAKE-OVER) is not checked. Why: The sim has no sidestick take-over fault.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module (autobrakes) and the ECAM control panel XML change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
RCL LAST: bring back the last cleared alert. RCL: bring back all cleared alerts; hold it more than 3 s to see the alerts inhibited by the flight phase.
Before take-off press T.O CONFIG: T.O CONFIG NORMAL shows when no alert of the FCOM list is active.
The SD changes page by itself; with an alert that lists BTV INOP, select another auto brake mode.

blocks.text: Adapted from tests N3, N4 and N6 : the card used the generator failures, whose ELEC alerts are not on this branch; the feed pump failures of this branch give two cautions instead.

children.title: Relight EGT limit 865 °C: START FAULT EGT OVERLIMIT in flight

blocks.text: In flight the FADEC now watches the EGT of a relight against the A380 relight EGT limit, 865 °C (A380 FCOM DSC-70-90, ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT). The relight lasts from the ENG MASTER ON of an engine waiting for its relight until the engine runs at idle. Above the limit the start sequence reports EGT OVERLIMIT: amber ENG n START FAULT with EGT OVERLIMIT, whose in-flight action is ENG n MASTER LEVER OFF (FCOM ENG START FAULT). The fault stays until the ENG MASTER is set OFF, also when the EGT comes back down and the engine reaches idle. A running engine and the ground starts (745 °C) are not concerned. The shared start sequence change is also on `core/failures-a32nx`, where the A32NX schedule sets no relight limit.

items: Hard to see in the sim. Why: A normal relight stays well below 865 °C; the start failures of the flyPad (hot start, start stall) are made for the ground start and are not checked to push a relight above the limit.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The systems WASM module changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
On ENG n START FAULT EGT OVERLIMIT in flight: ENG n MASTER OFF, wait 30 s to clear the fuel vapours before a new relight (FCOM ENG START FAULT).

children.title: Engine and APU fire visual effects

blocks.text: A fire you can see from outside: flames at the exhaust of an engine on fire, smoke at the APU exhaust for an APU fire, until the fire is out. Also smoke for an engine failed from the MSFS failures menu and for an engine oil leak. A flyPad switch turns all these effects off.

items: A32NX: flames and smoke at the exhaust of the engine on fire (flyPad Engine 1 fire / Engine 2 fire, or a fire of the MSFS failures menu); smoke at the APU exhaust for an APU fire. The APU exhaust point of the model moved to the tail cone tip, where the real APU exhaust is.

The effects follow the fire itself, not the detection: nothing during a FIRE TEST, and the effect stays after the engine shutdown until the fire is out (deactivated failure, or put out by an AGENT discharge).
Smoke at the exhaust of an engine failed from the MSFS failures menu (engine damage), and of an engine with the flyPad Engine 1(2) oil leak (ATA 79) while the oil flows out.

A380X: the same for engines 1 to 4 and the APU; the stock MSFS engine fire, engine damage and oil leak effects are turned off so they do not show twice; the engine 2 effects (heat haze, contrails, fire) no longer vanish at the medium model detail (LOD01).

Fire model (both aircraft): an AGENT discharge, or the automatic APU discharge, can also put out a fire set from the MSFS failures menu, which then ends the ENG / APU FIRE warning (see "Fire detection model and fire failures").
flyPad > Settings > Sim Options > "Situation Visual Effects (Engine and APU Fire, Engine Damage, Oil Leak)": on by default; OFF hides all these effects (L:A32NX_CONFIG_SITUATION_FX, both flyPads).
Each AGENT discharge puts the fire out one time in two. Why: The FBW fire model (user decision). What to do: Use AGENT 2 if the FIRE pb stays red.
After the ENG FIRE pb the engine runs on for up to 2 min 30 s. Why: The FIRE pb closes the LP fuel valve; the engine stops once the fuel downstream is burnt (FCOM).

On this branch the A380X oil leak smoke has nothing to start it. Why: The A380X flyPad engine oil failures (ATA 79) are on `core/failures-a380x`; this branch has only the model part. What to do: Use a build with core/failures-a380x merged.

The A380X engine 2 effects at LOD01 / LOD02 need the exhaust nodes of the wing LOD models. Why: The model files are in the large-files repository, not in the code repository. What to do: Install the matching A380X wing models.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The exterior models, aircraft.cfg, the model behaviour XML and the systems WASM modules change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Keep flyPad > Settings > Sim Options > Situation Visual Effects ON (default).
Set a fire (flyPad > Failures > ATA 26, or the MSFS failures menu) and look at the aircraft from outside; fight the fire with the ECAM procedure.
Set the switch OFF to hide the effects (the fire itself and its warnings are not changed).

blocks.text: Setup: A32NX on a stand, both engines at idle, PARKING BRK ON, APU running; outside (drone) view of the left engine from behind.

The A380X Smoke Detection Function of the CIDS for the cargo compartments (FWD, AFT, bulk), the avionics bays and the IFE bay, each with two smoke detectors (A380 FCOM DSC-26-50, DSC-26-60). On the CARGO SMOKE panel the AGENT TO FWD / AFT pbs show SMOKE and DISCH, and the BTL 1 and BTL 2 lights come on when a bottle has discharged: bottle 1 first (about one minute), then bottle 2 slowly. It lives on this branch because it extends the shared fire model of both aircraft, which is only here.

The A380X SMOKE, SMOKE DET FAULT and CARGO BTL FAULT alerts, the A380X flyPad failure list and the simvar docs are on `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`. Merge both branches for the A380X smoke alerts; this branch alone only has the systems side and the panel lights.

items: The crew rests, lavatories, CWS / RCC and showers have no smoke detection; the SDF cannot fail as a computer. Why: Not modelled. The NSS has its own zone since 2026-10-18 (see the next feature).
Detector 1 is on the DC ESS bus and detector 2 on the DC 2 bus. Why: Design choice: the FCOM gives no supply.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The A380X systems WASM module and the cockpit XML change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
With `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts` merged: open the A380X flyPad > Failures > ATA 26 and activate a smoke or detector failure.
Follow the ECAM; push AGENT TO FWD or AFT on the CARGO SMOKE panel for a cargo smoke.
The A380X smoke failures from the flyPad and the CARGO SMOKE panel lights.

children.title: A380X NSS smoke zone and the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw

blocks.text: The A380X smoke detection function gets a tenth zone, the Network Server System (NSS), with two smoke detectors and the SMOKE logic of the avionics bays (both detectors, or one failed and the other one detecting). NSS smoke has no ECAM alert: it lights the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw, which stays on as long as smoke is detected, also with the NSS power cut off (A380 FCOM DSC-26-50-10, DSC-46-20-20-87). The failure mapping (26049 to 26051) is in the A380X systems module of this branch.

The flyPad failures that trigger it (Network server system (NSS) smoke, ... smoke detector 1, ... smoke detector 2) are on `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`. Merge both branches: this branch alone has the zone and the light but no way to fail it from the flyPad.

items: A failed NSS smoke detector shows nothing. Why: The FCOM has no NSS SMOKE DET FAULT alert; the fault is only kept in L:A32NX_SMOKE_NSS_DET_FAULT.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The A380X systems WASM module and the cockpit XML change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
With `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts` merged: flyPad > Failures > ATA 26, activate Network server system (NSS) smoke.
Watch the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw.

blocks.text: The eight display units of the A380 CDS (A380 FCOM DSC-31-15-10: CAPT PFD, CAPT ND, CAPT MFD, E/WD, SD, F/O MFD, F/O ND, F/O PFD) can be failed from the flyPad. The failed DU goes blank (on an ND, the weather radar and terrain picture too, the VD included) and the FWS raises the CDS ... DU FAULT alert with its FCOM procedure and its INOP SYS line (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-31).

children.title: The flyPad failures (ATA 31 Indicating / Recording System)

head: flyPad failure name
ECAM alert (amber)
STATUS INOP SYS
rows: (none: the FCOM lists no SD line)

items: Failure activated: The DU goes blank. Single chime, MASTER CAUT, and the amber alert on the E/WD.
ECAM procedure (each DU): xx DU ..... OFF 5 S THEN ON; IF NOT SUCCESSFUL: xx DU ..... OFF; DU RECONF P/B AVAIL (green). The SD DU FAULT adds: IF SD DU OFF : F/O DU RECONF P/B FOR ATC MAILBOX.
SD STATUS page: INOP SYS (all phases): the DU line of the table above.
Takeoff and landing: The alert is inhibited in the FWS flight phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10; the DU is blank anyway.
DU without power: No DU FAULT alert (design choice): the lost busbar has its own ELEC alert.
Failure cleared: The DU runs its self-test and shows its picture again; the alert and the INOP SYS line go.

The reconfiguration has limits. Why: See "A380X display unit reconfiguration" below: the PFD and the EWD move to another DU by themselves, the MFD never does, and the SD only on an ND DU with the DU RECONF pb, without the ATC mailbox. What to do: With the SD DU failed, press the F/O DU RECONF pb (it acts on the F/O ND DU) until the SD pages (STATUS included) show there.
The OFF 5 S THEN ON item does not bring the DU back. Why: The flyPad failure stays until it is cleared, which is the procedure's NOT SUCCESSFUL branch. What to do: Clear the failure in the flyPad.
The second FCOM trigger (a DU that declared two other DUs faulty in turn) is not modelled. Why: It needs the DU monitoring loops, which are not simulated.
Open flyPad > Failures, chapter ATA 31 Indicating / Recording System.
Activate one of the eight ... display unit failures.
Follow the ECAM procedure, then check the SD STATUS page.
Deactivate the failure to get the DU back.

blocks.text: The A380 CDS moves a lost display to another display unit (A380 FCOM DSC-31-15-20 CDS abnormal operations, DSC-31-20-50 PFD/ND pb). Before, a failed or switched-off DU simply lost its picture. Now:

items: Automatic: when a PFD DU fails, loses its power or is switched off, the PFD is shown on the ND DU of the same side (the ND is lost). When the EWD DU is lost, the E/WD is shown on the SD DU.
PFD/ND pushbutton: exchanges the on-side PFD and ND. With the exchange selected, the PFD is on the ND DU and comes back to the PFD DU if the ND DU fails (the PFD keeps the priority).

DU RECONF pushbutton: active only with a failed on-side DU; it acts on the DU the FCOM gives (CAPT: the MFD DU, then the ND DU if the MFD DU is failed, then the PFD DU if the ND and MFD DUs are failed; F/O: the ND DU, the MFD DU if the PFD or ND DU is failed, then the PFD DU) and steps through the displays of the FCOM order that this DU can draw, then back to its normal display.

EWD and SD on the ND DU: with the CAPT (F/O) PFD and MFD DUs failed, the pb acts on the ND DU, which shows the PFD automatically; it now cycles PFD > EWD > SD > PFD (the MFD of the FCOM sequence cannot be drawn there). With only the MFD DU (CAPT) or the SD DU (F/O) failed, the ND DU cycles ND > EWD > SD > ND the same way. The EWD (SD) is never shown on both sides at once (A380 FCOM DSC-31-15-20), and a PFD that moves to the ND DU later (its PFD DU fails afterwards) wins over a selection there.
The weather radar and terrain picture (ndwxr) is hidden while its ND DU shows another display (the PFD, the EWD or the SD).
CAPT PFD display unit failed (or switched off): The CAPT PFD DU is blank and the PFD appears on the CAPT ND DU, without weather or terrain on it.
EWD display unit failed: The E/WD appears on the SD DU.
PFD/ND pb pressed (CAPT or F/O): The PFD and the ND of that side swap DUs; press again to swap back.
CAPT ND and MFD DUs failed, DU RECONF pressed: The CAPT PFD DU steps from the PFD to the ND (with no weather or terrain image), then back to the PFD.
CAPT PFD and MFD DUs failed, DU RECONF pressed: The CAPT ND DU, which shows the PFD, steps to the E/WD, then to the SD, then back to the PFD. While the E/WD (SD) is shown there, the F/O pb skips it.
SD DU failed, F/O DU RECONF pressed: The F/O ND DU steps from the ND to the E/WD, then to the SD pages (without the ATC mailbox), then back to the ND.
Failure cleared: Each DU goes back to its normal display.

children.title: The mouse on a DU with hidden displays

blocks.text: With the reconfiguration, every DU also holds the gauges of the displays it can show (the ND DUs hold a PFD, an E/WD and an SD as well). A hidden gauge stayed on top and took the mouse, so the OANS clicks on the F/O ND did not work (and the ATC mailbox on an ND DU of `core/a380x-mailbox-du-reconf`). Now the hosted E/WD and PFD never take the mouse, the hosted SD takes it only while it is shown, and the ND keeps it (OANS). The build adds one CSS rule per hosted gauge, and the display gate of each DU marks the hidden ones, found by their panel.cfg URL.

items: The MFD is never drawn on another DU, and nothing is drawn on the MFD DUs; the DU RECONF pb skips them, so it does nothing when it acts on an MFD DU. Why: Every display is a gauge of its own on its DU texture: the MFD is one gauge over both MFD screens (one texture) that also runs the FMS. Design choice: the PFD and the ND on both DUs of a side, the E/WD and the SD also on the ND DUs, and the E/WD on the SD DU. What to do: Use the other side's MFD.

The SD on an ND DU has no ATC mailbox. Why: The mailbox stays with the SD DU's own SD (design choice of the hosted SD). `core/a380x-mailbox-du-reconf` brings it to the ND DU. What to do: With the SD DU failed, the ATC mailbox is lost on this branch alone.

A selected E/WD or SD replaces the PFD on that side. Why: With the PFD and MFD DUs of a side failed, the ND DU is the only DU left for the PFD (FCOM: the pb acts on the ND DU). What to do: Press DU RECONF again to get the PFD back.
The ND on the PFD DU has no weather radar or terrain image. Why: The native ndwxr gauges stay on the ND DUs. What to do: Use the other side's ND.
The KCCU keys do not reconfigure the DUs. Why: Not modelled. What to do: Use the DU RECONF pb.

A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: panel.cfg (new hosted gauges, the E/WD and the SD on the ND DUs included) and the cockpit behaviour XML change. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to do for the automatic reconfiguration: a lost PFD or EWD DU moves its display by itself.
Press the PFD/ND pushbutton of your side to exchange your PFD and ND.
With a failed on-side DU, press DU RECONF to step the display of the DU it acts on.
With your PFD and MFD DUs failed, press DU RECONF to bring the E/WD, then the SD, onto your ND DU; once more for the PFD.

children.title: A380X hosted EWD and PFD: hidden when not shown

blocks.text: The EWD and the PFD also run as hidden copies on the display units that can take them over (EWD: SD DU and both ND DUs; PFD: both ND DUs). Each copy has a gate that hides it and stops it while its DU shows its own display. The gate was never made: the instruments looked up their display unit before the sim had connected the gauge, found the wrong one and made no gate. The hidden copies then ran and rendered all the time and were never hidden. The gate is now made once the gauge is connected.

items: Normal configuration: The hidden EWD and PFD copies are hidden and stopped on the SD and ND DUs.
EWD DU failed (or DU RECONF), EWD on the SD DU or an ND DU: The EWD copy shows there, as before.
PFD shown on the ND DU: The PFD copy shows there, as before.
No visible change in the normal configuration. Why: The fix stops hidden copies; the effect is less work for the sim and no hidden copy in front of the DU.
Nothing to set: use the DU RECONF and PFD/ND pushbuttons as in the reconfiguration feature above.
SD mailbox and ND / OANS clicks.
The EWD on the SD DU after an EWD DU failure; the PFD on the ND DU; the DU RECONF cycle.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X CAPT PFD reads the CAPT side FMS data

blocks.text: The captain PFD picked its FMS side before the sim had connected the gauge, and the side number it used was never 1: the CAPT PFD read the F/O side FMS data (the FM message flags, the TO waypoint, the MRP and the RNP). The side is now set when the gauge is connected, from the PFD's own display index (1 = CAPT, 2 = F/O, also when the PFD is drawn on an ND DU). The same bug is in FlyByWire upstream. The A32NX PFD is not affected.

items: No visible change while both FMS sides agree. Why: The two sides normally show the same data. What to do: Make them differ to see it (test below).
Nothing to set.
The CAPT PFD FMA messages, RNP and TO waypoint match the CAPT FMS side.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X weather radar GAIN, ELEVN and TILT
ND messages of the manual GAIN, ELEVN and TILT

blocks.text: The GAIN button and the ELEVN/TILT option list of the MFD SURV CONTROLS page kept their state but showed nothing. The ND now shows the manual radar settings as the A380 FCOM WXR MESSAGES (DSC-34-20-30-20 P 17).

head: SURV CONTROLS setting
ND message
rows: GAIN 53% in cyan, above the mode line; with ELEVN/TILT at AUTO the mode line is empty and GAIN takes its place
TILT -12.0° in cyan instead of WX
ELEVN/TILT at ELEVN, value 12500, QNH reference
ELEVN 12500FT in cyan instead of WX
ELEVN/TILT at ELEVN, STD baro reference on that side
MAP in green (GAIN nn% above it with GAIN MAN); no ELEVN / TILT message
WXR OFF in white, no GAIN line

items: GAIN, ELEVN and TILT act on the radar picture only in part. Why: The MSFS radar has no gain, no cell heights and no tilt; tilting its beam crashed the gauge. What to do: GAIN moves the colour levels; ELEVN / TILT only hide the weather where they reach the ground (see the last feature).
Cyan is a choice. Why: The A380 FCOM gives no colour; cyan is the colour of the manual modes of the same radar family in the A320 FCOM (DSC-34-SURV-30-30 P 10).
The grey background the FCOM figure prints behind GAIN is not drawn. Why: Not reproduced.
MFD SURV > CONTROLS, WXR block (WXR AUTO, MODE WX).
GAIN: press the button to MAN, enter a value in the field below it (0 to 100 %).
ELEVN/TILT: select ELEVN (enter an altitude or FL) or TILT (enter -15.0 to +15.0 degrees) in the field below the list.
Read the message on the ND (WX overlay selected). Back to AUTO for WX.

children.title: GAIN, TILT and ELEVN take the reference defaults at the first selection

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-30-20-10 (GAIN and ELEVN knobs): "The default GAIN value is 50 %", "The default ELEVN value is the current aircraft altitude", the default TILT value is +3.00° on ground and 0° in flight. The page applies a default only when nothing is entered, but a value nobody had written read 0, a valid entry: after a power-up the first GAIN MAN, TILT or ELEVN selection kept 0. The MFD now starts with the three settings at no entry.

items: First GAIN MAN after the MFD starts: GAIN field 50 %; ND GAIN 50%.
First TILT selection on the ground: TILT +3.0°; ND TILT +3.0°.
First TILT selection in flight: TILT +0.0°.
First ELEVN selection: The current altitude, rounded to 100 ft (FL with the STD reference).
Later selections: The value entered or set before is kept.
Select GAIN MAN, ELEVN or TILT on the SURV CONTROLS page: the default value is entered.
Overwrite it in the entry field if needed.

children.title: VD white line of the manual ELEVN and TILT

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-30-20: "The VD displays a white line indicating the elevation or tilt value". In manual ELEVN the VD shows a horizontal white line at the selected altitude; in manual TILT a straight white line from the aircraft symbol at the selected angle (zero tilt = the horizon as seen by the ADIRS), as in the FCOM VD figures.

items: ELEVN selected: Horizontal white line at the selected altitude, from the aircraft to the end of the VD range.
TILT selected: Straight white line from the nose of the aircraft symbol, up for a positive tilt, down for a negative one.
Selected altitude off the VD scale: No line.
ELEVN/TILT AUTO, MODE MAP, WXR OFF or no WX overlay: No line (it goes with the ELEVN / TILT message of the ND).
The line shows only while that side's ND shows the WX function. Why: Design choice: the line goes with the ND message.
The tilt line is straight. Why: Design choice, as in the FCOM figure: no earth curvature or beam refraction.
The weather on the VD does not follow ELEVN or TILT. Why: The MSFS radar has no height data; the ground cut of a manual ELEVN / TILT applies to the ND only. The VD weather colours follow the GAIN.
Select the WX overlay on the EFIS panel and ND ARC or ROSE NAV (the pages with the VD).
On MFD SURV > CONTROLS select ELEVN or TILT and enter the value.
Read the white line on the VD.

children.title: GAIN and ELEVN/TILT change the radar picture

blocks.text: The manual GAIN, TILT and ELEVN entries changed the ND messages and the VD line only. They now act on the radar picture, within what the MSFS radar allows: its views take a table of rain rate bands, but have no cell heights and no tilt.

items: GAIN moves the rain rate each colour starts at, as the receiver gain moves the reflectivity of each colour (A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-30-10/-20; Honeywell RDR-4000 Pilot manual: MIN about -16 dBZ, MAX about +10 dBZ, calibrated in AUTO). 50 %, the FCOM default, is the calibrated gain (the same picture as AUTO); 0 % is the MIN, 100 % the MAX. A lower gain turns red to yellow, yellow to green and removes green (Airbus Safety First #22); a higher gain the opposite. Turbulence (magenta) does not change.

A manual TILT down shows the weather only up to the range where the tilted beam reaches the ground (the radar removes the ground returns with the TAWS terrain, DSC-34-20-30-10). A level or up tilt changes nothing.
A manual ELEVN at or below the ground under the aircraft shows no weather; above it, the full picture.
GAIN AUTO, or MAN at 50 %: The calibrated picture (as before).
GAIN MAN 0 %: Red cells shrink or turn yellow, yellow turns green, light green disappears.
GAIN MAN 100 %: More and larger green, yellow and red areas.
TILT -10.0 at about 10 000 ft above the ground: Weather only inside about 9 NM.
TILT -3.0 at about 10 000 ft above the ground: Weather out to about 34 NM.
ELEVN at or below the ground elevation: No weather on the ND.
VD: Its weather colours follow the GAIN; the TILT / ELEVN cut is on the ND only.
ELEVN and TILT cannot show a slice above or below the cells. Why: MSFS gives no cell tops: only the part in the ground can be removed.

The ground ahead is taken level at the elevation under the aircraft. Why: The gauge cannot read the terrain ahead back (design choice). The beam uses the earth curvature with the 4/3 radius of the standard refraction.
The GAIN scale is a design choice. Why: The FCOM gives the percentage but not its scale: 50 % calibrated, 0 % and 100 % the RDR-4000 MIN and MAX, linear in dB on each side.
A GAIN change may repaint the picture over a few seconds. Why: Not measured yet: the engine may repaint it sector by sector with its sweep.
MFD SURV > CONTROLS, WXR block (WXR AUTO, MODE WX).
GAIN MAN and a value: below 50 % to look into heavy cells (less colour), above 50 % to see weak returns. Back to AUTO for the calibrated picture.
ELEVN/TILT: TILT with a down angle (or ELEVN) to keep the weather only where the beam is above the ground. Back to AUTO for the full picture.

children.title: SURV panel GAIN and ELEVN knobs

blocks.text: The GAIN and ELEVN knobs of the SURV panel now work, on the CAPT and F/O sides (A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-30-20). They set the same WXR settings as the MFD SURV CONTROLS page, which follows them (GAIN button, ELEVN/TILT option list and entry fields), so the ND messages, the VD line and the radar picture of the features above follow too.

head: Knob action
GAIN knob
ELEVN knob
rows: GAIN MAN (50 % when nothing was entered)
ELEVN (the current altitude when nothing was entered); pulled again: TILT (+3.0° on the ground, 0° in flight when nothing was entered)
1 % per step, 0 to 100 %, in GAIN MAN only
ELEVN: 100 ft per step (0 to 60 000 ft); TILT: 0.1° per step (-15.0 to +15.0°); nothing in AUTO

items: The knobs do not move or turn in the cockpit. Why: The cockpit model has no animation for them (the VD AZIM knob has one): the knob node itself takes the mouse.
The step sizes are a design choice. Why: The real knob resolution is not known: the steps are the resolutions of the ND messages (GAIN 53%, ELEVN 12500FT, TILT -12.0).
Pulling ELEVN in TILT selects ELEVN again; turning changes only a manual value. Why: Design choices: the FCOM describes pull for ELEVN, a second pull for TILT and push for AUTO only.
With WXR OFF the knobs do nothing; in MODE MAP the ELEVN knob does nothing. Why: As the SURV CONTROLS page: the GAIN button is not shown with WXR OFF and the ELEVN/TILT list is not available in MAP.
The CAPT and F/O knobs share one set of settings. Why: The SURV CONTROLS page keeps one WXR setting for both sides.
GAIN: pull the knob for manual gain, turn it to adjust, push it to go back to AUTO.
ELEVN: pull for a manual elevation, pull again for a manual tilt, turn to adjust, push for AUTO.
In the sim: the tooltips of the knob show "Pull for manual WXR ...", "Push for AUTO WXR ...", "Increase / Decrease WXR ...".

children.title: A380X VD airports as flat ground
VD airports drawn as flat ground

blocks.text: The MSFS terrain map draws the airport diagram in light grey over the terrain, and no setting hides it. The VD read that grey as terrain far above its plot: spikes wherever the vertical cut crossed an airport, the destination on approach included.

items: The systems host searches the sim airports within 25 NM that have a land runway, and publishes up to 24 airports, closest first, as one circle each: the smallest circle around the corners of all its runways, plus 0.3 NM for the taxiways and aprons beside them, at the elevation of its highest runway threshold.
Where the cut crosses such a circle, the VD draws flat ground at the airport elevation instead of the terrain map.

The first version used a rectangle around each runway (plus 0.15 NM): taxiways and aprons between and beside the runways still showed as spikes. One circle per airport covers them (the user chose it over a fixed radius).
VD cut across an airport: Flat brown ground at the airport elevation over the whole airport (runways, taxiways, aprons), no spike.
Past the edge of the airport circle: The real terrain again.
Approach to the destination: The airport ahead shows as flat ground at its elevation.
After take-off, climbing away: The departure airport stays in the list (and flat) while it is within 25 NM.

Flight path and MSA line over an airport: The green path, the pink MSA / MORA line and the symbols stay visible over the flat ground (they used to be hidden over the first NM at the departure airport).

Real terrain inside an airport circle is flattened (for example a hill beside the runways). Why: Design choice: an airport is drawn as flat ground; the circle is the smallest one around the runways plus 0.3 NM.
Airports beyond 25 NM, or more than 24 airports, are not flattened. Why: Design choice of the search radius (enough for the VD ranges of the approach) and of the gauge list size.

Airports without a land runway of 100 m or more are not flattened. Why: The runway search leaves out heliports and water-only bases (`core/oans-btv-raas`), so they no longer push the real airports out of the list.
Nothing to set: read the VD terrain profile as usual (TERR SYS of the SURV page not OFF).

children.title: ND and VD map views across flight reloads

blocks.text: The ND weather and terrain and the A380X VD are drawn by native gauges (ndwxr) on sim map views. Over flight reloads the gauges could leak their map views: the module keeps its state while the next flight's gauges start before the old ones are closed. Once the sim's view budget was used up, the VD went blank.

A slot table now hands each gauge over: a new gauge of the same display or role takes over or replaces the previous flight's gauge, deletes its views (never a view another gauge of the same display still uses, as view numbers are per display), and keeps the module within its view budget.

items: The original blank VD after a reload was not reproduced. Why: In the reload test the sim restarted the module each time, so no old view was left; the blank VD seen before may come from another reload path. What to do: Report the reload path (flight reload, return to the main menu, new flight) if the VD goes blank again.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: The native module (ndwxr.wasm) changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to set: reload the flight as usual; the ND weather / terrain and the VD come back.

children.title: VD profile starts at the aircraft on the ground

blocks.text: The FMS profile starts at the take-off point of the flight plan. An aircraft parked or taxiing past it has that point behind it, so the first part of the climb fell off the left edge of the VD: the green path seemed to start at about 1,500 ft.
On the ground the whole profile is now moved back so that the take-off point sits at the aircraft (0 NM): the path rises from the ground and keeps the distances the FMS predicts.

items: On the ground, aircraft past the take-off point of the plan: The green path rises from the ground at 0 NM and matches the F-PLN altitudes and distances.
In the air, or the take-off point ahead of the aircraft: No change.

On the ground the path is shifted by the distance to the take-off point; waypoint symbols and the grey area keep their real distances. Why: Design choice: only the profile is moved, so the climb is complete at the aircraft.
Nothing to set: enter the flight plan with departure, SID and transition and read the VD on the ground.

blocks.text: The FCOM audit of compared every A380X system with the A380 FCOM. These eleven findings were one or two wrong lines each (a variable nothing writes, a copy-paste index, an inverted condition). Each is now fixed as the FCOM describes.

Before
Now
FCOM

TAWS FLAP MODE OFF on the MFD SURV CONTROLS page inhibits TOO LOW FLAPS
The FMS landing runway was compared with the FMS origin twice
The landing runway is green (selected) at the destination airport
Engine 4 was not checked (engine 3 read twice)
Engine 4 alone at takeoff power also delays the CRZ page after takeoff
The wing anti-ice input read an A32NX variable that the A380X never writes
WING ANTI ICE ON (STRUCTURAL DEICE SWITCH) enters the thrust limit computation
Never triggered (L:A32NX_BRAKES_HOT is not written on the A380X)
From the 16 reported brake temperatures: one brake at or above 300 °C
ELEC panel COMMERCIAL 2 and ELMU pbs
All three pbs toggled COMMERCIAL (ELMU shed the commercial loads)
Each pb has its own state
From the active thrust limit: none at FLEX/TOGA or in reverse, amber above the limit at MCT/CLB
A320 delta P limits applied to feet
Red above 9 550 ft, like the value
MAX SPEED 310 KT shown only in ALT 1A (inverted)
HYD G RSVR LEVEL LO / G SYS OVHT

Green pumps; ENG 3 pump disconnection on DC 2, ENG 4 on DC 1
CREW SUPPLY OFF could not show; the CABIN line followed the crew oxygen pb
CKPT legend amber and REGUL PR LO on the ground with CREW SUPPLY OFF; the CABIN line amber on a low pressure only

items: Only the wrong lines found by the audit were changed. Why: Each fix is kept to its finding so it can go upstream on its own; the rest of each system is as before.

ELMU and COMMERCIAL 2 have a state but no consumer yet. Why: Nothing in the electrical model sheds loads by those pbs (a380-simvars: A380X_OVHD_ELEC_COMMERCIAL_2_PB_IS_OFF, A380X_OVHD_ELEC_ELMU_PB_IS_OFF).
The EDP disconnection bus change has no cockpit test. Why: It only matters with DC 1 or DC 2 lost while disconnecting an engine pump; a Rust test covers it.
Nothing to do: the systems behave as in the FCOM.
TAWS FLAP MODE: MFD > SURV > CONTROLS, FLAP MODE OFF to inhibit TOO LOW FLAPS (e.g. a landing in a non-standard flap configuration).

blocks.text: Further FCOM gap fixes on the A380X: each line below differed from the A380 FCOM and now follows it.

Before
Now
FCOM

Shown at once whenever the value was outside 0.7-1.4 g, also on the ground; never XX

PRO-ABN HYD G (Y) SYS OVHT, DSC-29-20

INOP SYS BTV and CAT 3 DUAL, INFO CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY; the Y STATUS shows TAXI WITH CARE and NO BRAKED PIVOT TURN; FUEL CONSUMPT INCRSD / FMS PRED UNRELIABLE when the PRIM also failed; Y SYS PRESS LO shows L/G GRVTY EXTN ONLY with the limitation MAX SPEED 220 KT (gravity extension)
PRO-ABN HYD G (Y) SYS PRESS LO
Could trigger in flight phase 8 only
Can trigger on the ground before take-off and below 800 ft before landing (flight phases 1, 8 and 9)
PRO-ABN CAB PRESS EXCESS DIFF PRESS

Above 200 kt gear up (4A) and 180 kt flaps not in landing configuration (4B); a flat 500 ft (4A) / 245 ft (4B) ceiling while the terrain function is available, rising to 1 000 ft only with TERR SYS OFF or a TERR failure

The nose wheel steering stays: "A-SKID sw OFF does not cut off NWS"

Only RTO disarms 10 s after lift-off; a landing mode armed on the ground stays armed

items: "Turning the pumps OFF was not successful" is read from the pump section pressure switch. Why: It is the only pump output the FWS has (design choice).

The GPWS "terrain function available" is the TERR SYS pb and the TERR failure of the selected system. Why: The FCOM names the aircraft position and the terrain database; the sim has no failure of either (design choice). The 1 000 ft ceiling is reached at 250 kt, as on the A320 (the FCOM figure is not precise enough to read the speed).
CAB PRESS EXCESS DIFF PRESS has no practical sim trigger. Why: It needs a differential pressure above the limit; the phase change is covered by the FwsAbnormalSensedItems spec.
Nothing to set: the pages, alerts and systems behave as in the FCOM.
A landing AUTO BRK mode can now be armed on the ground before take-off: it stays armed for the landing.

blocks.text: A fast (re)alignment, the IR mode selector set to OFF and back to NAV within 5 s, took 180 s. Both FCOMs give about 30 s (A320 FCOM DSC-22_20-20-40, IRS alignment page: "a fast alignment takes 30 s"; A380 FCOM DSC-34-10-30-30). The shared systems code now takes 30 s.

items: Only the fast alignment changed. Why: A normal alignment from an unaligned IR is unchanged.
With the IRs aligned on the ground, set an IR mode selector to OFF and back to NAV within 5 s.

children.title: A380X FWS flight phases: engine 4 take-off power from lever 4

blocks.text: The FWS flight phases need two engines at take-off power for phase 3. The take-off power of engine 4 was read from thrust lever 3 (`eng4TLAFullPwr = eng3TLA > 43.3`), so lever 3 alone at TOGA counted as two engines, and lever 4 was never read. Each engine now reads its own lever; the rule (TOGA, above FLX/MCT, or FLX/MCT with a FLEX TEMP) sits in `FwsTakeoffPower.ts`.

items: Nothing changes with all four levers moved together. Why: Only a lever 3 / lever 4 split shows the fix.
Nothing to set: set the thrust levers for take-off as usual.

children.title: A380X door alerts and outflow valves for every door

blocks.text: The FWS and the pressurization read only some of the 18 A380X doors (10 main deck, 6 upper deck and 2 cargo doors). An open upper deck door or cargo door gave no alert, did not stop T.O CONFIG NORMAL and did not hold the outflow valves open. Every door now counts, as in the A380 FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-52 DOOR alerts, PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-21 CAB PRESS INHIBITED BY DOORS, DSC-31-40-10 Takeoff Configuration Test, DSC-21-30-30).

head: What
Before
Now
rows: Also DOOR UPPER 1L to 3R NOT CLOSED and DOOR FWD (AFT) CARGO NOT CLOSED
IF ABNORM CAB V/S line of a DOOR alert
MAIN 5L/5R and UPPER 2L/2R showed the lines below it without the condition and never set the MAX FL 100/MEA limitation
A condition the crew confirms on every door; the MAX FL : 100/MEA-MORA limitation follows it
Not with MAIN 1R, the upper deck doors or the cargo doors
Any door not closed and locked at take-off power
Checked MAIN 1L, MAIN 2R and the cargo doors
Every main deck, upper deck and cargo door and the two cockpit sliding windows must be closed for T.O CONFIG NORMAL
Outflow valves with a door open at take-off power (AUTO)
The four outflow valves stay open (FCOM DSC-21-30-30: "maintaining the four outflow valves open")
Door inputs of the pressure controllers, cabin air and packs
All 16 passenger doors and both cargo doors

items: No DOOR BULK CARGO NOT CLOSED. Why: The model has no bulk cargo door (no interactive point, no door in the systems).
A passenger door counts as not closed as soon as it moves. Why: The sim doors have no separate latch or lock.
The door alerts need an engine running. Why: They are inhibited in flight phase 1 (FCOM inhibitions).

A take-off with a door open keeps the outflow valves open until the next touchdown. Why: Design choice: the inhibition keeps its value from the lift-off. The manual pressurization mode is not affected (FCOM DSC-21-30-40).
Close every door and both cockpit sliding windows before the T.O CONFIG test.
With a DOOR ... NOT CLOSED caution, close that door (flyPad > Ground > Services, or the sim door controls) and follow the ECAM lines.

children.title: A380X L/G, NAV disagree and F/CTL law STATUS alerts

blocks.text: FCOM gap audit: alerts of the A380 FCOM that the FWS did not have. The landing gear alerts come from the two landing gear control and indicating systems (LGCIS 1 and 2), the NAV alerts compare what the CAPT and F/O PFDs display.

A gear door not closed 30 s after the gear stopped moving (design choice: the FCOM gives no time)

NAV CAPT AND F/O ALT DISAGREE

items: The flight phase inhibitions are taken from the matching A320 alerts. Why: The FCOM gives them as figures only (design choice; the NAV alerts use the phases of the NAV ADR/IR FAULT alerts).
The NAV alerts wait 10 s. Why: The FCOM gives no confirm time; 10 s lets the two pilots set STD or a new QNH one after the other (design choice).
The model has three gears (nose, left, right). Why: The wing gears follow the body gears.
L/G GEAR NOT LOCKED UP needs a jammed gear. Why: The gear actuator failures (e.g. Nose gear jammed actuator) are on `core/failures-a380x`, not on this branch. What to do: Merge it to test.
Nothing to set: follow the ECAM procedure when an alert shows, then read the STATUS page.

children.title: A380X exhaust heat haze of each engine
