blocks.text: The exhaust heat haze effects of aircraft.cfg read the wrong engines: the haze of engine 2 followed engine 1, and engines 3 and 4 followed engine 2 (an upstream bug). Each exhaust now reads its own engine.

items: Nothing to set: look at the engines from the outside view.

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM splits the GPWS mode 4 by the gear and flaps (DSC-34-20-20-10): 4A with the gear up and the flaps not in landing configuration, 4B with the gear up and the flaps in landing configuration, or the gear down and the flaps not in landing configuration. Gear up with the landing flaps gave TOO LOW TERRAIN at high speed, and a mode 4 alert stayed on after the aircraft climbed back above its ceiling.

head: Gear / flaps
Now
rows: Gear up, flaps not in landing configuration (4A)
Unchanged: TOO LOW GEAR below 500 ft under 200 kt, TOO LOW TERRAIN above 200 kt
Gear up, flaps in landing configuration (4B)
TOO LOW GEAR below 245 ft at any speed, never TOO LOW TERRAIN (the FCOM figure gives a flat 245 ft ceiling)
Gear down, flaps not in landing configuration (4B)
Unchanged: TOO LOW FLAPS below 245 ft under 180 kt, TOO LOW TERRAIN above 180 kt

items: Landing configuration = FLAPS FULL, or CONF 3 when CONF 3 is the landing configuration selected in the FMS. Why: As the existing FBW code (the flaps lever position, not the flap angle).
FLAP MODE OFF does not inhibit the gear-up 4B alert. Why: Design choice: the FLAP MODE pb is for a landing with an abnormal flaps configuration (FCOM); only the flaps alert changes with it.
Nothing to set: the GPWS calls out as in the FCOM.

children.title: A380X contrails from each running engine

blocks.text: The fuselage part drew the contrails from the fuselage centre, whatever the engines did, and the wings part had a second copy on the exhaust nodes. Contrails come from the water vapour of the burnt fuel, so an engine that burns no fuel leaves none. The contrails are now declared once, on the exhaust of each of the four engines, and each shows only while the sim's contrail conditions are met and that engine burns fuel (MSFS engine combustion and a FADEC fuel flow above 0). A flamed out, shut down or seized engine leaves no contrail; the other engines keep theirs.

items: One contrail per engine (engines 1 to 4), plus the ribbon contrail on engines 2 and 4 as before.
Engine 2 now uses its own exhaust point (FX_EXHAUST_RIGH, the node of the left inner engine in the wing model despite its name); the old copy used the FX_EXHAUST_LEF point.
No contrail is declared in the fuselage part any more.
Whether contrails form is decided by MSFS. Why: The effect uses the sim's CONTRAILS CONDITIONS MET (altitude and temperature), as the stock contrail templates do.
No N3 threshold for "running". Why: No source gives an A380 core speed limit for it; the fuel flow and the MSFS combustion flag are used instead (design choice).
Nothing to set: fly in contrail conditions (cold air at cruise level) and look at the engines from the outside view.

children.title: A380X OANS: ARPT NOT IN ACTIVE F/PLN in PLAN mode only

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM OANS message ARPT NOT IN ACTIVE F/PLN means: "In PLAN mode, the flight crew has displayed an airport that is not the origin, destination, or alternate airport". Upstream showed it in every ND mode but ARC (ROSE NAV too). It now shows in PLAN mode only.

items: ND in PLAN, OANS showing an airport that is not ORIGIN, DEST or ALTN: ARPT NOT IN ACTIVE F/PLN.
ND in ROSE NAV or ARC with the same airport: No message.
ND in PLAN with the origin, destination or alternate: No message.
The other OANS messages are unchanged. Why: Only this message differed from the FCOM.
Nothing to set: the message follows the ND mode and the airport shown.
The message only in PLAN mode, with an airport outside the flight plan.
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X flap automatic retraction and extension: regression tests

blocks.text: User report: the flaps seemed not to retract after a CONF 1+F takeoff. Checked end to end, no bug: with the flaps lever at 1 the SFCC gives CONF 1 above 212 kt and CONF 1+F again below 205 kt (A380 FCOM flaps and slats, automatic retraction system ARS). CONF 1 keeps the slats at 20 degrees: only the 8 degrees of flap retract, a small visible change. Two full-aircraft tests now guard this on the A380 hydraulics test bed (real SFCC, flap and slat assembly, four engines): a lever-1 takeoff through 212 kt and back below 205 kt, and an in-flight spawn with the lever at 1. The takeoff test gives each flap movement 60 s (30 s failed about once in ten runs with the random frame times of the test bed).

items: Takeoff with CONF 1+F, lever left at 1, accelerating through 212 kt: CONF 1: the flaps go from 8 degrees to 0, the slats stay at 20 degrees; PFD and SD show 1.
Lever at 1, decelerating below 205 kt: CONF 1+F again: the flaps extend to 8 degrees.
The retraction is hard to see from the cabin or the outside view. Why: Only 8 degrees of flap move; the slats stay out. What to do: Watch the SD F/CTL page.
Take off with lever 1 (CONF 1+F); the flaps go to CONF 1 by themselves above 212 kt. Retract the lever to 0 as usual.
Nothing new to check in the sim: tests only. Report any CONF 1 / 1+F change at other speeds.

children.title: Hold IMMEDIATE EXIT during the hold entry

blocks.text: A380 FCOM DSC-22-FMS-10-40-50 (HM, IMMEDIATE EXIT): the aircraft returns immediately to the hold exit fix, keeps the hold speed until it gets there, and exits the hold when it sequences the hold fix.

Before: with IMMEDIATE EXIT selected while the hold entry (direct, teardrop or parallel) was still flown, the entry brought the aircraft back over the hold fix, but the hold leg then started its own pattern and flew one more full circle (about 3.5 min at 220 kt) before leaving. Now the hold is left at that fix pass. Exit pressed on the racetrack itself was already right: the aircraft returns at once to the fix and exits there. The FMGC code is shared, so the A32NX MCDU IMM EXIT behaves the same.

items: IMMEDIATE EXIT pressed during a direct, teardrop or parallel entry: The entry ends over the hold fix and the aircraft leaves the hold there.
IMMEDIATE EXIT pressed on the racetrack (outbound or inbound): Returns at once to the hold fix and leaves there (unchanged).
After the press: The button shows RESUME HOLD*. The hold stays in the F-PLN until the hold fix is sequenced (by design).
RESUME HOLD pressed before the fix: The hold is flown again, with the hold entry logic.
Entering straight in (inbound course aligned, no entry turn) keeps the old behaviour. Why: There is no entry turn that ends at the fix; the hold leg handles the exit as before.

Pressed in the turn right after the fix (after the entry), the aircraft makes a full turn back to the fix before leaving. Why: The FCOM says the aircraft "returns immediately" to the hold exit fix; from that turn the way back is round the turn.
A380X: on the MFD ACTIVE/F-PLN page, click the amber IMMEDIATE EXIT* button on the HOLD line. A32NX: on the MCDU F-PLN page, press the key next to IMM EXIT*.
The aircraft flies back to the hold fix and continues the flight plan from there; the button now reads RESUME HOLD*.
To fly the hold after all, select RESUME HOLD* before the hold fix.
IMMEDIATE EXIT in each turning entry: the aircraft leaves at the first fix pass, no extra circle.
Not sim-tested with the fix installed yet.

children.title: RAT ground stow and A32NX RAT performance

blocks.text: Once the RAT had extended (both AC buses lost, RAT MAN ON, A32NX EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON), nothing stowed it again: it stayed out for the rest of the session, and on the A32NX HYD RAT FAULT stayed on. On the real aircraft the ground crew stows it after the flight.

A320 FCOM DSC-29-10-20 : "The RAT deploys automatically if AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 are both lost. It can be deployed manually from the overhead panel. It can be stowed only when the aircraft is on the ground."
A380 FCOM DSC-29-10 : "The green hydraulic system powers RAT retraction, on ground."

The systems now accept a maintenance stow request (`L:A32NX_RAT_STOW_REQUEST`) on the ground, while no extension is commanded. One shared Rust model (`ram_air_turbine_deployment.rs`) moves the strut of both aircraft, so the A320 and the A380X behave the same.

items: RAT stowed: No RAT row in the Services list.
RAT out, aircraft on the ground and stopped: Row "RAT stow (maintenance)", status "RAT extended", button Stow.
Stow pressed and accepted: Status "Stowing" for about 3 s; the strut moves in 1 s; the row disappears. A380X: the RAT rig retracts. A32NX: the HYD page RAT indication goes back to stowed.
RAT out in flight, or on the ground but moving: Row greyed, status "RAT extended · stow when stopped on the ground".
Stow pressed while an extension is still commanded (emergency electrical configuration, RAT MAN ON or A32NX EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON held in): Refused: the RAT stays out.
RAT MAN ON (or the automatic extension) after a stow: The RAT extends again.
A32NX on the ground with the RAT out: HYD RAT FAULT, as the FCOM says (PRO-ABN-HYD: "The RAT is not fully stowed"); it clears after the stow.

The stow needs no hydraulic pressure. Why: Design choice: the FCOMs say only "on the ground" (A320) and that green hydraulics power the retraction on ground (A380); the stow is a ground crew action, so it is not tied to the aircraft hydraulics being pressurised.
The strut travels in 1 s. Why: Design choice: the same speed as the stock extension; no FCOM value.

No RAT on the A32NX model on this branch. Why: The visible A32NX RAT (doors, strut, propeller) is on `core/a32nx-exterior`; with this branch alone only the HYD page, HYD RAT FAULT and the RAT pump show the stow. What to do: Merge `core/a32nx-exterior` to see the RAT go in.
A request in flight is dropped. Why: Each request is evaluated once (written back to 0), so a request in flight does not stow the RAT after the landing. What to do: Request again on the ground.
The flyPad row needs the stationary aircraft. Why: Design choice of the flyPad (like the other ground services); the systems themselves only need "on the ground". What to do: Stop the aircraft.
After a flight with the RAT out, stop on the ground.
Restore normal electrical power (engines or APU generators, or external power) so that no extension is commanded; on the A32NX the RAT MAN ON and EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON pbs are not pressed.
flyPad > Ground > Services: press Stow on the row "RAT stow (maintenance)".

blocks.text: The flyPad row is on `core/efb-redesign`: test with both branches merged. With this branch alone, replace each "press Stow" step by setting `L:A32NX_RAT_STOW_REQUEST` to 1 with an L:var tool (SimConnect); the "row" lines then do not apply.

children.title: A380X cargo doors follow the hydraulics
Cargo doors locked while their pumps are inhibited

blocks.text: On the A380X the cargo doors are moved by the green electric pumps. When the ground crew was asked to open a cargo door while an engine ran, the door unlocked anyway (0.24 % open in a sim run) although the pumps that move it are inhibited then. The cargo doors now follow the hydraulics.

A380 FCOM DSC-29-10 P 3: the green electric pumps are the only power of the cargo door actuation, and they are inhibited as soon as an engine runs. DSC-52-30-40-10: an inhibited door is isolated from the hydraulics, there is no power to open it.

The systems now compute whether the cargo door operation is inhibited. It is inhibited as soon as any of the four engines runs; this is the same rule as the one that stops the green electric pumps in the A380X hydraulics (a placeholder based on the engine oil pressure, which covers the FCOM cases: engines 1 and 2 running, engines 3 and 4 running, taxi and flight). The state is published as `L:A32NX_HYD_CARGO_DOOR_OPERATION_INHIBITED` (1 = inhibited).

items: Engine running, a closed cargo door is asked to open: The door stays closed and locked. The request is kept.
Engines stopped, the request still pending (or asked again): The door unlocks and opens (about 50 s); both doors, forward and aft.

Door moving or open, an engine starts: The door holds its position where it is (no further motion). It is not closed, so the usual open cargo door alerts apply (DOOR FWD CARGO / AFT CARGO NOT CLOSED, see the test).
Door held open, the request is switched off, then the engines are stopped: The inhibition ends, and the door closes and locks about 35 s later.
Engines stopped, normal open and close: As before: the doors open, then close and lock.
flyPad, engine running, door closed: Row "Cargo fwd + aft": "Closed · no hydraulic power, engine running"; the switch is greyed out (needs `core/efb-redesign`, see the next feature).

The inhibition is "any engine running". Why: The A380X electric pump controllers use a placeholder (the oil pressure of the engines) for the same condition. The FCOM cases (engines 1 and 2 running, taxi, flight, engines 3 and 4 running) are all covered by that one rule, so the same rule is used here.
The A32NX has no cargo door inhibition. Why: Design choice: the inhibition is in the A380X hydraulics (the green electric pumps). The A32NX only gets the full-open fix (next feature).

A door that is not closed at engine start stays open until the engines are stopped. Why: Without the green electric pumps there is no power to move it (FCOM DSC-52-30-40-10). What to do: Stop the engines.
The flyPad row shows the new state only with `core/efb-redesign`. Why: The row is a row of the Material 3 Services page, which is on that branch. What to do: Merge both branches.
Stop on the ground and stop the engines (the green electric pumps are then allowed).
flyPad > Ground > Services > Doors: switch "Cargo fwd + aft" on to open both cargo doors, off to close them.
With an engine running, expect the doors to stay closed (the row says so); stop the engines first.

blocks.text: (it also lists the SimConnect recorder command). The flyPad lines need `core/efb-redesign` merged too; with this branch alone request the doors from the exterior door interactive point of the sim and read the E/WD, the SD DOOR page and the exterior model. After a change of the Rust code: one MSFS restart (WASM).

children.title: Cargo doors open fully and are held locked open

blocks.text: An opened cargo door stopped near 90 % and then sagged back to about 88 % for good (A380X 87.7 %, A32NX 88.8 %). GSX starts loading above 80 %, so on the A380X its ULD loader went through the door. The real door is mechanically locked at the end of its travel. The doors of both aircraft now open fully and are locked open there.
A380 FCOM DSC-52-30-40-10 P2: the cargo door has a "FULLY OPEN AND ARRESTED" indicator.

items: Engines stopped, a cargo door is asked to open: The door opens to 98 % and is locked open there. A380X: about 50 s after the request; A32NX: about 25 s.
Door open, the hydraulic pumps stop: The door stays at 98 %, locked open. Before: it stopped near 88 % and GSX loaders went through it.
Door locked open, the close request: The door unlocks, closes and locks down (within about a minute), as before.
Door locked open, the operation inhibited (A380X, engine running): The door stays locked open; a close request is carried out once the engines are stopped.
A380X flyPad, row "Cargo fwd + aft": "Moving" with a progress bar up to 98 %, "Open" from 98 % (was 90 %; needs `core/efb-redesign`).
Stop the engines (A380X: the green electric pumps are then allowed).
Open the cargo doors: A380X flyPad > Ground > Services > Doors, row "Cargo fwd + aft"; A32NX flyPad > Ground > Services, cargo door button (or the exterior door interactive point of the sim).
Wait until the door is fully open before GSX cargo loading starts.

children.title: A380X ATC mailbox with the SD on an ND display unit
ATC mailbox follows the SD to the ND display unit

blocks.text: The ATC mailbox is the bottom section of the SD. The CDS SD DU FAULT procedure says "If the SD DU is turned OFF, use the F/O DU RECONF P/B for ATC mailbox" (A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-31). On `core/display-unit-failures` the F/O DU RECONF pb brings the SD to the F/O ND DU, but without the mailbox, so the ATC messages could not be read or answered with the SD DU off. Now the mailbox comes with the SD.

items: Normal operation (SD DU on): The mailbox at the bottom of the SD DU, as before.

SD DU off or failed, F/O DU RECONF pressed until the SD shows on the F/O ND DU: The SD with the mailbox on the F/O ND DU: the same queue and the same message; its buttons and the page arrows work with the F/O cursor.
SD DU on again: The mailbox is active on the SD DU again, with the same queue.

The SD shown both on the SD DU and on an ND DU (DU RECONF used because of another failed DU): The SD DU's mailbox is the active one; the mailbox on the ND DU shows the same message and takes no input (design choice).
The SD shown nowhere: No mailbox marks a new message as displayed or read: the ATC MSG lights stay on until a DU shows the mailbox again (design choice).
PRINT in the mailbox: PRINT NOT AVAIL (no cockpit printer on this branch; printing is on `core/printer`).

The systems host decides which DU has the active mailbox (`L:A380X_CDS_MAILBOX_DU`): the SD DU while it is working and shows the SD, else the ND DU that shows the SD (the SD is never on both sides at once, FCOM DSC-31-15-20), else none.
Only the active mailbox answers the crew and sends to the ATC function; another mailbox on screen mirrors the displayed message.
The A380X README and the simvar documentation describe the variable and the rule.

Needs an ATC connection with a message to see anything in the mailbox. Why: The mailbox shows the messages of the FBW ATSU (`core/a380x-atccom-datalink`). What to do: Log on to an ATC center (Hoppie or BeyondATC) or prepare a request with XFR TO MAILBOX.
No printing. Why: The cockpit printer is `core/printer`, not merged here. What to do: Merge it for PRINT.
A full MSFS restart is needed after an update. Why: It comes with the panel.cfg and cockpit changes of `core/display-unit-failures`. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
With the SD DU off or failed (CDS SD DU FAULT), press the F/O DU RECONF pushbutton (glareshield, F/O side) until the F/O ND DU shows the SD: first the E/WD, then the SD with the mailbox.
Read and answer the ATC messages in the mailbox on the F/O ND with the F/O cursor, as on the SD.
Press F/O DU RECONF once more to get the ND back, or switch the SD DU back on.

children.title: ATC MSG lights flashing, RING delay and the KCCU MAILBOX key

blocks.text: Three items of the A380 FCOM ATC datalink description (DSC-46-10-20):

items: ATC MSG lights flash at 2 Hz (250 ms on, 250 ms off) while an ATC message waits in the mailbox, until either ATC MSG pushbutton is pressed; then both go off (FCOM: "The pushbutton flashes at a frequency of 2 Hz"). A new variable `L:A380X_GLARESHIELD_ATC_MSG_LIGHT` drives the two pushbuttons.
RING delay: the ATC RING sounds only if the message is not read within 15 s (5 s for an urgent message), then repeats. The A32NX DCDU is unchanged.

KCCU MAILBOX key: puts the KCCU cursor of that side on the SD mailbox (FCOM: "When pressed, the cursor moves to the mailbox section of the SD"); the MFD of that side hides its cursor. The key works with the KCCU keyboard ON. Design choice: the cursor goes to the middle of the mailbox (the FCOM gives no position).
An ATC uplink arrives: Both ATC MSG pushbuttons flash at 2 Hz.
Message read within 15 s (5 s if urgent): No RING.
Message not read after 15 s (5 s if urgent): RING, then repeated until the message is read.
Either ATC MSG pushbutton pressed: Both lights go off.
KCCU MAILBOX key pressed (keyboard ON): The cursor of that side jumps to the SD mailbox.
The light changes need a flight reload. Why: The glareshield behaviour XML changes. What to do: Reload the flight after installing.
The MAILBOX key does nothing with the KCCU keyboard OFF. Why: FCOM: the KCCU keys work with the keyboard switch ON. What to do: Set the KBD switch ON.
When the ATC MSG lights flash, press one of them (or read the message) to stop them.
Press the KCCU MAILBOX key to bring the cursor to the SD mailbox, then answer the message.
ATC MSG flashing and the RING delay with BeyondATC.
The MAILBOX key cursor (both sides, also with the SD on an ND DU).
Not sim-tested yet.

children.title: A380X ELEC, fuel and reference gap alerts
Combined ELEC busbar alerts and ELEC STATIC INV FAULT

blocks.text: A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-24 has combined alerts for the loss of several busbars together. The A380X showed the single busbar alerts side by side instead. Six combined alerts now trigger when all their busbars are lost and replace the single alerts they cover, with their procedure lines, flight phase inhibitions (phases 4, 5 and 10) and STATUS:

head: Alert
Busbars lost
rows: ELEC AC BUS 1+2 & DC BUS 1 FAULT
ELEC AC BUS 2+3 & DC BUS 1+2 FAULT
ELEC AC BUS 3+4 & DC BUS 2 FAULT

items: A combined alert whose busbars are all part of another active one is replaced by it (DC BUS 1+2 FAULT inside AC BUS 2+3 & DC BUS 1+2 FAULT); combined alerts that only overlap are both shown.

The fuel lines of these procedures depend on the flight time above FL 300 since departure (more or less than 30 min, counted from lift-off) and lead to gravity feeding (descent, CROSSFEED ... OFF, EXPECT NORM COLLECTOR CELL DEPLETION, AVOID NEG G LOAD), shown in flight only.

The STATUS lists the FCOM lines that have an ECAM text, for example AC BUS 2+4 FAULT: MAX SPEED 310 KT, FUEL PARTLY UNUSABLE; INOP SYS F/CTL PROT, AP 1+2, A/THR, FD 1+2, ADR 2+3, TCAS 1+2, SATCOM, JETTISON, FEED TK 1 and 4 PMPs; INFO ALTN LAW : PROT LOST, FEED TK 1 (4) BY GRVTY ONLY. The JETTISON INOP SYS text (also in AC BUS 2+4, DC BUS 1+2 and DC BUS 1+ESS FAULT) is added here, identical to the one of `core/fuel`.

ELEC STATIC INV FAULT (crew awareness, phases 3 to 10 inhibited): the static inverter runs only on batteries (no AC ESS power, both battery contactors closed); it counts as failed when it runs but gives no normal output.
Some FCOM STATUS lines are missing (for example ATC COM VOICE ONLY, VHF 3, MOST FUEL XFR PMPs). Why: They have no ECAM text in FBW yet.
REDUND LOSS lines are not shown for these alerts. Why: They never reach the STATUS page in the FBW FWS.
The combined alerts do not trigger in ELEC EMER CONFIG. Why: Design choice: the bus fault alerts need one AC busbar powered; ELEC EMER CONFIG covers that case.
VENT AVNCS EXTRACT OVRD and OUTR TK XFR MAN lines are never ticked. Why: No avionics ventilation pb-sw; the manual outer tank transfer pb-sw is inoperative in the sim.
When a combined ELEC alert shows, follow its E/WD procedure (the sensed lines tick as you act).
Read the STATUS page; in flight follow the gravity feeding lines if they show.

blocks.text: Setup: cruise above FL300, AP ON.

children.title: FUEL wing feed pumps, wings balance and inner tank alerts

blocks.text: Four FUEL alerts of A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28 with their crossfeed procedure lines:

items: FUEL L (R) WING FEED PMPs FAULT: all pumps of feed tanks 1 and 2 (left) or 3 and 4 (right) at low pressure, abnormally not running or switched off. It replaces the two FEED TK n MAIN + STBY PMPs FAULT alerts of its tanks. Inhibited in phases 4 to 7, 9 and 10. Pumps switched off on request of FUEL WINGS NOT BALANCED do not count.

FUEL WINGS NOT BALANCED: on the ground, an imbalance above 6 600 lb between the symmetric feed tanks or the inner tanks, 5 500 lb between the mid tanks or 2 600 lb between the outer tanks (not while refuelling); in flight, more than 6 600 lb between feed tanks 1 and 4 or 2 and 3. In flight it stays until that pair is balanced (the lighter tank is no longer lighter), then FUEL WINGS BALANCED shows until its pumps are back ON and its crossfeeds OFF. Inhibited in phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10.
FUEL INR TKs QTY LO: fuel on board above 110 200 lb with an inner tank below 11 200 lb (ZFW and ZFCG entered, both outer tanks full). Inhibited in phases 3 to 11.
The "balanced" point of WINGS NOT BALANCED is a design choice. Why: The FCOM gives no balanced threshold.
Landing ends the in-flight balance procedures. Why: Design choice.
When a FUEL alert shows, follow its E/WD lines with the CROSSFEED and feed pump pbs of the overhead FUEL panel.
Watch the feed tank quantities on the SD FUEL page until the alert clears.

blocks.text: Setup: cruise.

children.title: ELEC alerts with the A380X failures: T.O CONFIG and ELEC EMER CONFIG

blocks.text: What this branch adds by having both parents together:

items: T.O CONFIG NORMAL (the A380 rule of `core/failures-a380x`) also checks the ELEC GEN 1 (2)(3)(4) FAULT, GEN OFF and DRIVE DISCONNECTED alerts of `core/a380x-elec`, as in the FCOM list (DSC-31-40-10).
ELEC EMER CONFIG (of `core/a380x-elec`) is not shown while ENG ALL ENG FLAME OUT is (FCOM: "This alert inhibits the ELEC EMER CONFIG alert").
Before take-off press T.O CONFIG with all four generators ON.
In an all engines flame out, follow ALL ENG FLAME OUT; ELEC EMER CONFIG does not come on top of it.

children.title: ADR and IR failures, ADIRU power supplies

blocks.text: Air data and inertial data could not be lost on their own, and the ADIRUs ran without their busbars. Now:

items: Six new flyPad failures: ADR 1 (2)(3) (air data lost, FAULT light) and IR 1 (2)(3) (inertial data lost, FAULT light). The outputs of that ADIRU part go to failure warning and its FAULT light comes on (new L:A32NX_ADIRS_ADR_n_FAULT_WARN_DISCRETE, shared ADIRS model).

Each ADIRU is supplied by its busbars, from the FCOM ELEC INOP SYS lists: the ADR needs its AC and its DC busbar, the IR runs on either. Power cuts up to 200 ms, and the first 5 s after a flight load, are ignored, so a flight loaded on the runway or in the air keeps its alignment.
An ADR that lost its DC busbar no longer gives a NAV ADR FAULT on top of the ELEC busbar alert.
Shared code: the A32NX ADIRU supplies come with it (the ADIRS model now needs each aircraft's supplies). The A32NX ADR / IR failures, ON BAT light and alerts are on `core/failures-a32nx`.
ADR 1 failed: ADR 1 FAULT light on the ADIRS panel; E/WD NAV ADR 1 FAULT; the air data of ADR 1 are lost.
IR 1 failed: IR 1 FAULT light; E/WD NAV IR 1 FAULT; the inertial data of IR 1 are lost.
An ADR busbar lost (ELEC alert): That ADR is lost, but only the ELEC alert shows, no NAV ADR FAULT.
No high angle of attack / sideslip thresholds for the A380X ADRs. Why: The FCOM gives no boundary.
The A32NX IR 10 min alignment is not on this branch. Why: It is on core/failures-a32nx only (merge note: keep it when both are merged).
Open flyPad > Failures > ATA 34 Navigation > and activate an ADR or IR failure.
Follow the NAV procedure on the E/WD (ADIRS panel and source switching).
Flights loaded on the runway and in cruise keep the IR alignment.
The ADR and IR failures from the flyPad (lights, alerts, lost data).

children.title: CAB PRESS, RAM AIR, APU FAULT, HYD, A-ICE and SURV alerts

blocks.text: A380X FCOM alerts and memos that were missing or never triggered:

items: CAB PRESS (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-21-30): EXCESS NEGATIVE DIFF PRESS (red warning, phases 8 and 9) is held until the differential pressure is back above -0.32 PSI; DIFF PRESS HI (phase 8) only in automatic mode; DIFF PRESS LO in phases 8 and 9; new CAB PRESS LDG ELEVN FAULT (phase 8) when neither FMS sends a landing elevation (no destination), with the LDG ELEVN deferred procedure.
RAM AIR memo with the RAM AIR pb ON (DSC-21-10-20): green on the ground with no engine running, amber otherwise.
AUTO FLT APPROACH CAPABILITY DOWNGRADED (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-22) when RA SYS B alone is failed: STATUS CAT 3 DUAL inoperative, CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY.
APU FAULT (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-49) after an APU emergency or automatic shutdown by its ECB: EMER SHUTDOWN or AUTO SHUTDOWN, -APU MASTER SW ... OFF; STATUS INOP SYS APU. Not shown while APU FIRE is.

Fuel memos (DSC-28-20): FWD XFR IN PROGRESS (fuel leaving the trim tank), OUTR TK XFR IN PROG (fuel leaving the outer tanks), OUTR TKS XFRD and TRIM TK XFRD (tanks emptied). The fuel model tells no transfer state, so the FWS watches the tank weights: more than 5 kg out of a tank in 10 s is a transfer.

HYD: ENG PMP PRESS LO lists the pumps of its system under STATUS INOP SYS (two or more failed) or REDUND LOSS (one failed); G (Y) RSVR AIR PRESS LO and G (Y) SYS OVHT get their FOR APPROACH deferred procedures (engine pumps back ON); G+Y SYS PRESS LO shows LDG PERF AFFECTED and the FCOM INOP SYS list (BTV, CAT 2, GLS AUTOLAND), without STABILIZER.
A-ICE ICE DETECTED and A-ICE SEVERE ICE DETECTED (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-30), cruise only (phase 8): ENG 1-4 A-ICE ... ON, and WING A-ICE ... ON for severe icing.
Cabin oxygen masks drop by themselves above 13 800 ft cabin altitude (DSC-35-30-10, supplied by DC ESS).
SURV GPWS 1 (2)(1+2) FAULT phases and lines; SURV TAWS 1 (2)(1+2) FAULT now triggers when the GPWS and the TERR SYS of a system are both failed, instead of the two separate alerts.

AIR ABNORM BLEED CONFIG after ENG SHUT DOWN or ENG FIRE with an engine bleed lost: all the FCOM lines (XBLEED, AIR FLOW, PACK, WING A-ICE). The title is shown (the FWS has no procedure without a title).
The fuel transfer memos come from the tank weights (5 kg in 10 s). Why: The fuel model gives no transfer state; the FCOM gives no detection rule (design choice).
No COLDFUEL OUTR TK XFR or GND XFR IN PROGRESS memo. Why: No fuel temperature model, no ground transfer function.
APU FAULT: the "failure but APU still available" and "failed start above FL 150" lines stay hidden. Why: The ECB tells neither case apart.
APPROACH CAPABILITY DOWNGRADED triggers only on RA SYS B. Why: The other FCOM triggers are PRIM monitorings the sim does not have.
The fuel transfer memos read L:A380X_FUEL_JETTISON_IN_PROGRESS directly. Why: The jettison signals of core/fuel are not on this branch. What to do: With core/fuel merged they use its signals.
Nothing to set: the alerts and memos come by themselves; follow the E/WD lines and read the STATUS page.
For a FOR APPROACH deferred procedure, apply it in approach as the ECAM shows.
The fuel transfer detection (5 kg in 10 s): no false memo in normal burn, memos during real transfers.
The masks drop above 13 800 ft cabin altitude, not below.
GPWS / TERR SYS / TAWS combinations of the SURV alerts.

children.title: PFD FMA messages, AVAIL, EGT start limits and SD items

items: PFD FMA line 3: CHECK SPD MODE (its L:var was already set by the FMC) and CHECK EO SPD SETTING now show.
E/WD AVAIL: stays 10 s after an engine start on the ground, pulses 1 min after a relight in flight, goes when the thrust lever is set above idle.
E/WD EGT: the amber limit is 745 C during a ground start and 865 C during a relight in flight; no EEC trim during a start.
SD FUEL: the tank quantities of an unbalanced pair are underlined amber, with the trigger of FUEL WINGS NOT BALANCED.
SD WHEEL: L/G CTL and L/G GRVTY EXTN IN PROGRESS now show.
ENG 2 (3) SHUT DOWN: the landing distance line reads LDG DIST IMPACT ON WET/CONTAM RWY ONLY.
No EXTEND / RETRACT SPD BRK or CHECK APPR SEL on the A380X. Why: They need VNAV outputs the FMS does not give.
No WHEEL UP LOCK indication. Why: The gear model has no uplock state.
The ENG SHUT DOWN bleed lines are not added. Why: Not done yet.
Nothing to set: the indications follow the FCOM by themselves.
The width of the fuel underline on the SD FUEL page.
The EGT colour during a hot start.
The AVAIL and fuel pulse animations.

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM (DSC-34-10-50 AUTOMATIC CALLOUTS) has a pin programmed "smart" FIVE HUNDRED callout: it is called only when the aircraft is more than half a dot off the glide slope, or without a valid glide slope. The callout logic (AutoCallOuts isFiveHundredCalloutDue, read by LegacyGpws) is on this branch.

items: The flyPad option that sets the pin is not on this branch. Why: The flyPad settings pages are on core/efb-redesign. What to do: Merge both: core/efb-redesign has the "Inhibited When Glideslope Captured" option.
flyPad > Settings > Aircraft Options / Pin Programs > Automatic Call Outs: under FIVE HUNDRED, set "Inhibited When Glideslope Captured" (needs core/efb-redesign).
Fly the approach: FIVE HUNDRED is only called when off the glide slope.
The callout on and off the glide slope with the pin option set and not set.

ECAM advisories (FCOM DSC-31-40-10 ADVISORY): when an ENGINE value (oil quantity, oil temperature above 163 C, a rotor vibration above 5 units) or the CAB PRESS cabin V/S (above 1 800 ft/min) pulses on its SD page, the SD calls that page if it shows a flight phase page and its ECP pb comes on; if the crew had selected another page, the ECP pb flashes. The E/WD shows a pulsing ADV with the memos. ADV goes when the ECP pb is pressed or the value is back in range. New L:A380X_ECAM_SD_ADVISORY_PB.
STATUS MORE (ECP MORE pb, DSC-31-40-10): new ALERTS IMPACTING LDG PERF section (the active alerts with a landing performance line), and the MORE INFO line of MISC OIS FAULT.
No advisory for the nacelle temperature, delta P, cabin altitude or APU OIL LVL LO. Why: The SD pages do not pulse these values yet.
When ADV pulses on the E/WD, look at the called SD page; press its ECP pb to acknowledge.
When MORE shows at the bottom of the STATUS page, press the ECP MORE pb.
No ENG advisory at flight load while the oil quantity still reads 0.

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM lists an EVAC ACTIVE memo while the evacuation command is on. The E/WD now shows EVAC ACTIVE while the EVAC COMMAND pb-sw is ON.

items: The memo colour is green. Why: Assumed: the FCOM does not give it.
Set the EVAC COMMAND pb-sw ON (overhead EVAC panel): the memo shows until it is set OFF.
The EVAC ACTIVE memo with the EVAC COMMAND pb-sw.

children.title: cabin pressure, generator drive oil, ELEC SD failures, e-pump inhibition

items: Manual cabin pressure: in MAN, the cabin altitude target holds the current cabin altitude and the V/S target 0 ft/min until the CABIN ALT TRGT or V/S TRGT selector is turned (it jumped to the selector position). Without the FMS landing elevation the controllers regulate to 7000 ft in descent (7500 ft also without ADIRU pressure) instead of 0 ft, and tell the FWS (new CPCS word bit 19).

Generator drive oil (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-24): new flyPad failures DRIVE 1 (2)(3)(4) Oil Leak and DRIVE 1 (2)(3)(4) Oil Cooling Lost; ELEC DRIVE n OIL LEVEL LO, OIL OVHT (above 200 C) and OIL PRESS LO (below 35 PSI); the DRIVE pb FAULT light (OVHT and PRESS LO); after 5 min of low level the generator switches off, after 5 min of low pressure or above 250 C the drive disconnects (then ELEC DRIVE n DISCONNECTED). Normal drive oil temperatures no longer reach 200 C at high N2.
The APU GEN A (B) pb-sw FAULT light comes on when the GGPCU disconnects the APU generator.
SD ELEC AC and DC pages: GEN, TR, STAT INV and RAT turn amber when they are failed.
Electric hydraulic pumps: on the ground the green ones are inhibited only by engine 1 or 2 running, the yellow ones by engine 3 or 4; all are inhibited in flight (FCOM).

Shared code: the engine generator drive oil model of the A32NX IDG (drive trait and oil failure types) is on this branch as the base of the A380X drive model; the A32NX IDG failures are not offered here (they are on core/failures-a32nx). The A32NX cabin pressure part is on core/failures-a32nx.

DRIVE 1 Oil Leak, engine 1 running: About 25 s after the leak starts the oil level is low (ELEC DRIVE 1 OIL LEVEL LO, shown only on the ground before the first engine start and after the last shutdown); about 50 s after, the pressure is low: ELEC DRIVE 1 OIL PRESS LO with the DRIVE 1 FAULT light and the SD ELEC AC page; 5 min later the drive disconnects (ELEC DRIVE 1 DISCONNECTED).
DRIVE 1 Oil Cooling Lost, engine 1 running: About 4 min later ELEC DRIVE 1 OIL OVHT with the DRIVE 1 FAULT light; about 100 s later (250 C) the drive disconnects.
The leak and heating rates are design choices. Why: The FCOM gives no normal oil values.
A disconnected drive cannot be reconnected in flight. Why: FCOM DRIVE pb DISC. What to do: Reconnect on the ground.
Drive oil alerts: follow the E/WD (GEN ... OFF or DRIVE ... DISC).
Manual cabin pressure: set MAN and turn the CABIN ALT TRGT or V/S TRGT selector to take control.
In MAN ALT / MAN V/S, the first selector turn jumps to the selector position.
The drive oil failure timeline (level, pressure, disconnection).
The APU GEN FAULT light during an APU start.

children.title: APU automatic shutdowns, smoke detection and cargo extinguishing alerts

items: APU ECB automatic shutdowns (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-49): the APU shuts down by itself, with APU FAULT, on an ECB failure, an overspeed, a low oil pressure, a high oil temperature (A380X: on the ground only) and when its DC supply is lost above N 70 % (1 s confirmation). Four new flyPad failures: APU electronic control box (ECB), APU overspeed (automatic shutdown), APU low oil pressure (automatic shutdown), APU high oil temperature (automatic shutdown on ground).

Smoke detection (FCOM DSC-26): the A380X FWS raises the SMOKE warnings and SMOKE ... DET FAULT cautions of 9 zones: FWD, AFT and BULK CARGO, L / R MAIN AVNCS, L / R UPPER AVNCS, AFT AVNCS and IFE BAY (for example SMOKE FWD CARGO SMOKE, SMOKE FWD CARGO DET FAULT), with their procedure lines.
Cargo fire bottles: SMOKE FWD+AFT CARGO BTL 1 (2) FAULT when a bottle has a low pressure; STATUS INOP SYS FWD+AFT CRGs BTL 1 (2).

New flyPad failures (ATA 26): Forward / Aft / Bulk cargo smoke, Left / Right main avionics bay smoke, Left / Right upper avionics bay smoke, Aft avionics bay smoke, IFE bay smoke, the smoke detectors 1 and 2 of each zone (for example Forward cargo smoke detector 1), Cargo fire bottle 1 (2) low pressure.

The SMOKE alerts need `core/failures-a32nx`. Why: The A380X smoke detection model (shared fire model) and the CARGO SMOKE panel lights (SMOKE, DISCH, BTL, AGENT pbs) are on that branch; the alerts here read its L:vars. What to do: Merge both; without it the smoke failures give nothing.
No smoke detection in the crew rests, lavatories, CWS, showers and facilities. Why: Those zones are not modelled.
No bottle diverter / control alerts (FWD (AFT) CARGO BOTTLES FAULT). Why: Not modelled.
Some APU shutdown causes are missing. Why: No model for them.
APU FAULT: set the APU MASTER SW OFF as the E/WD asks.
SMOKE warnings: follow the E/WD (ISOL VALVES, AGENT, CAB FANS ...), with core/failures-a32nx merged.
No APU shutdown during the normal power transfers (EXT PWR, APU GEN, engine generators).
The DISCH / AGENT / BTL light emissives (with core/failures-a32nx).
The smoke failures from the flyPad.

children.title: bleed monitoring, leak detection, BLEED FAULT and LEAK alerts

items: Bleed monitoring (FCOM DSC-36-10-20): the CPIOM-A closes an engine bleed valve on an overtemperature (260 C, or 245 C above 45 PSI, for 55 s; the HP valve too) or an overpressure (60 PSI, or 45 PSI above 245 C, for 15 s), held until the ENG BLEED pb is set OFF. A failed bleed opens the crossbleed valves at AUTO.
Leak detection (DSC-36-10-60): a leak of an engine pylon duct (above 180 C) or of a wing duct (above 124 C) closes that bleed valve and the crossbleed valves of its side.
The ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) BLEED FAULT light comes on for these cases and when a bleed valve is not in its commanded position (DSC-36-20).

New alerts (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-36): AIR ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) BLEED FAULT; AIR ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) BLEED LEAK and AIR L (R) OUTR (INR) WING LEAK with the AIR LEAK ISOLATED line. A BLEED FAULT also triggers AIR ABNORM BLEED CONFIG.
New flyPad failures (ATA 36): Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) bleed valve stuck closed, ... stuck open, Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) pylon bleed duct leak, Left / Right outer / inner wing bleed duct leak.
Shared code: the bleed air failure types of the A32NX pneumatic failures come with it (prerequisite commit, no behaviour of its own). The A32NX BLEED page part is on core/failures-a32nx.
No A380X pack alerts. Why: No pack valve or regulation failure model.
One leak loop per zone; no APU, pack bay or hot-air duct leak; no HP stage pressure low. Why: Not modelled.
A pylon leak is only detected at high power. Why: The duct must be pressurised enough to heat the loop. What to do: Test it with high thrust.
Follow the E/WD: ENG BLEED pb OFF for a leak or a bleed fault; AIR LEAK ISOLATED tells when it is done.
Use the AIR ABNORM BLEED CONFIG lines (crossbleed, air flow, packs, wing anti-ice) after a bleed is lost.
No false AIR ENG BLEED FAULT on a fast thrust increase at take-off.
The leak failures from the flyPad (the pylon leak needs high power to be detected).
The gear extension is inhibited above 280 kt (FCOM DSC-32-10-20; was 260 kt, the A320 value).

Hydraulic supply as in the FCOM: the nose gear on GREEN, each main gear assembly (body and wing) on GREEN and YELLOW: with GREEN or YELLOW lost the main gears no longer retract, and the gear is extended by gravity.
The gravity extension takes about 70 s from the L/G GRVTY switch to the last gear downlocked (was about 50 s).

Emergency braking (A-SKID off, or normal and alternate braking lost) follows the EBCU laws: 1 700 psi for taxi-out and take-off, 1 000 psi from lift-off until the PARK BRK handle is set ON (was 1 160 psi).
The RTO autobrake no longer activates below 40 kt, but an active one continues to the stop.
New alerts: BRAKES A-SKID FAULT ON ALL L/G (emergency braking with the A-SKID switch ON) and BRAKES AUTO BRK FAULT with the new flyPad failure Brakes autobrake (AUTO BRK).
The wing and body gears are still one gear per side. Why: The gear model has no separate wing gears.
With GREEN lost the body gear, with YELLOW lost the nose gear do not retract. Why: Known deviation of the shared LGCIU: the gears move only with all doors open.
No braking LEHGS, separate accumulators or BCS split; 16 BRAKES alerts still missing. Why: Not modelled.
Extend the gear below 280 kt (and below VLO).
For a gravity extension, set the L/G GRVTY switch DOWN and wait about 70 s.
The gravity extension timing in flight.
The L/G alerts and indications with GREEN or YELLOW lost.
The landing law after touchdown with A-SKID OFF.

children.title: HP fuel valve, FADEC faults, motoring and auto-idle

items: New flyPad failures Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) HP fuel valve stuck (ATA 73): the valve stays where it is; stuck closed, the engine gets no fuel and does not light up. When the valve position disagrees with the FADEC command for 2 s: ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) HP FUEL VLV FAULT (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-70; master caution, ENGINE page) and the ENG FAULT light.

New FADEC fault failures with their crew awareness alerts (no aural, no master light): Engine n fuel strainer clog - ENG n FUEL STRAINER CLOGGED; Engine n fuel filter monitoring - ENG n FUEL FILTER MONITORING FAULT; Engine n oil chip (metal particles) (ATA 79) - ENG n OIL CHIP DETECTED; Engine n FADEC minor fault (internal sensor) - ENG n MINOR FAULT; Engine n overthrust protection - ENG n OVTHR PROT LOST; Engine n pressure and temperature probes - ENG n SENSOR FAULT. 28 A380X failures in all.
Auto-idle: engines 1 and 4 are held at idle while a thrust reverser operates (FCOM).
Pre-start motoring of a hot engine (shared engine start code, as on core/failures-a32nx).
FUEL STRAINER CLOGGED: Shown in flight phases 1, 2, 11, 12 (inhibited 3 to 10).
FUEL FILTER MONITORING FAULT, OIL CHIP DETECTED: Shown only in phases 11 and 12 (after landing).
MINOR FAULT, OVTHR PROT LOST, SENSOR FAULT: Shown in phases 1, 11 and 12 (inhibited 2 to 10).
HP FUEL VLV FAULT: Inhibited in phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10.
Other ENG alerts are still missing. Why: They need engine models the sim does not have.
No approach idle; no A380X derates. Why: No FCOM value; no A/THR model for the derates.
HP FUEL VLV FAULT during a start: ENG MASTER OFF (and ENG MAN START OFF for a manual start), as the E/WD asks.
The crew awareness FADEC alerts need no action in flight; report them after the flight.
Hot restart motoring.
An A380X HP valve stuck open still stops the engine at ENG MASTER OFF.
The outboard auto-idle in reverse.

children.title: LP valve, emergency outer tank transfer and fuel leak detection

items: New flyPad failures ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) LP fuel valve jammed in place: FUEL ENG n LP VLV FAULT (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-28) when the valve stays closed while commanded open (engine start) or stays open while commanded closed (engine shutdown), on the ground; before take-off -ENG n MASTER ... OFF. Jammed closed, the engine cannot start. STATUS INOP SYS ENG n LP VLV.
The EMER OUTR TK XFR pb-sw opens the emergency outer tank transfer valves: the outer tank fuel flows by gravity into feed tanks 1 and 4 (flight_model.cfg gets the missing Feed 4 input line).

FQMS fuel leak detection (DSC-28-40): slow leak (block fuel minus (FOB + fuel used) above 15 450 lb) and fast leak (FOB decrease minus fuel used above 4 400 lb in 30 min); FUEL LEAK DETECTED (phases 2 and 8) with the full FUEL LEAK procedure; FUEL LEAK DET FAULT (phase 8) with STATUS INOP SYS FUEL LEAK DET. New flyPad failures Feed tank 1 (2)(3)(4) leak.
Shared code: the LP valve jam (engine_lp_valve.rs) is the same as on core/failures-a32nx, where the A32NX part is.
A full MSFS restart is needed. Why: flight_model.cfg changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Other fuel alerts are still missing. Why: They need temperature, overflow, inerting or FQMS transfer models.
FUEL LEAK DETECTED: follow the FUEL LEAK procedure on the E/WD.
EMER OUTR TK XFR pb ON to move the outer tank fuel into feed tanks 1 and 4.
EMER OUTR TK XFR into feed tanks 1 and 4.
No false FUEL LEAK DETECTED.

children.title: anti-ice valves, wing anti-ice, oxygen, anti-ice key events

items: A380X wing anti-ice system (FCOM DSC-30): the WING ANTI ICE pb commands two valves per wing on bleed air: 30 s ground test, then 10 min inhibition; inhibited during the take-off until the thrust reduction; FAULT light. The flight controls and the FADECs now get the real wing anti-ice state.
Engine anti-ice valves (both aircraft, shared model): open with the pb ON, or unpowered once the HP air is above 10 psig; 2 s travel; FAULT light. The MSFS engine anti-ice follows the valves.
New A380X alerts (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-30): A-ICE ENG 1 (2)(3)(4) VLV CLOSED / VLV OPEN, A-ICE L (R) WING VLV CLOSED / VLV OPEN / VLV PRESS HI / VLV PRESS LO.
A380X oxygen (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-35): cockpit and cabin bottle pressures on the DOOR/OXY page; OXY CKPT BOTTLE PRESS LO, OXY CABIN BOTTLE PRESS LO, OXY CABIN VLV CLOSED.

New flyPad failures: ATA 30 Left (Right) wing anti-ice valves stuck closed, Left (Right) wing outer anti-ice valve stuck open, Engine 1 (2)(3)(4) anti-ice valve stuck closed / stuck open; ATA 35 Cockpit oxygen bottle leak, Cabin oxygen bottles leak, Cabin oxygen regulator supply valve stuck closed.

Key events (both aircraft): MSFS anti-ice events (ANTI_ICE_TOGGLE_ENGn, ANTI_ICE_SET_ENGn, ANTI_ICE_ON / OFF / SET / TOGGLE, TOGGLE_STRUCTURAL_DEICE) now move the ENG and WING ANTI ICE pbs, so key bindings and hardware panels keep working.

The A32NX engine anti-ice valves (with their ENG ANTI ICE pb FAULT light) come with the shared key event code: without them the A32NX would not build. The A32NX probe and window heat, alerts and failures are on core/failures-a32nx.
No A380X probe / window heat model and its 15 alerts; no wing anti-ice on the SD BLEED page. Why: Not done yet.
No ADR probe heat bits. Why: Not done yet.

blocks.text: Fix-up commit de9a236e6 removes a native stub of the systems WASM that these changes left unused (the workspace clippy check failed on it). No effect for the user.

items: Use the ENG and WING ANTI ICE pbs (or your key bindings / hardware panel) as usual.
On an A-ICE or OXY alert, follow the E/WD.
Key binding / hardware panel toggles of ENG and WING anti-ice: no loop, no toggle storm at flight load.
A32NX ENG A.ICE FAULT light before about 25 % N2.
A380X wing pb ground test and take-off inhibition.
The oxygen leak failure on the DOOR/OXY page.

children.title: avionics network failures, SFCC channels, TAIL STRIKE

items: New ATA 42 failures (FCOM DSC-42-10/20) of the 16 AFDX switches (for example AFDX switch 1 (network A)), the 8 IOMs (IOM A1 to IOM A8) and the 22 CPIOMs (for example CPIOM C1 (FWS, FCDC), CPIOM F1 (fuel)). A failed switch is rerouted around; a failed module is no longer available, and the EWD, SD, PFD and FWS parts that already watch the CPIOM availability react to it.
New ATA 27 failures SFCC 1 (2) flap channel and SFCC 1 (2) slat channel: the failed channel stops its motor (flaps or slats at half speed); F/CTL FLAP (SLAT) SYS 1 (2)(1+2) FAULT now have a trigger.

TAIL STRIKE caution (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-27-10, LAND ANSA) after a detected contact, and TAIL STRIKE DET FAULT (STATUS INOP SYS TAIL STRIKE DET) with the new failure Tail strike detector (ATA 31). Contact = pitch 11.5 deg or more with a main gear compressed (the FCOM LIM-10 geometry limit, design choice); it is remembered until the next flight (phase 1).
Network losses have no effect on FMS, datalink, braking, steering, transponder or PFD yet. Why: Not modelled.
No actuator, sidestick, THS or WTB failures; no backup control (BCM / BPS); no ALT 1C reconfiguration. Why: They need the flight control model (Simulink).
The tail strike contact is a pitch / gear rule. Why: The sim has no fuselage contact sensor.
Activate the failures in the flyPad ATA 27, 31 and 42 lists.
After a TAIL STRIKE, land as soon as possible (LAND ANSA).
No false TAIL STRIKE on normal rotations and flares.
Half-speed flaps / slats with a channel failure.
CPIOM C1 / C2 or AFDX switch failures and their FWS / EWD / SD loss.

children.title: reactive windshear, GPWS mode 2, alpha floor Mach limit

items: Reactive windshear (FCOM DSC-22): the PRIMs detect a decreasing performance windshear at take-off and landing below 1 300 ft, CONF 1 or more: red WINDSHEAR on both PFDs (L:A32NX_REACTIVE_WINDSHEAR_WARNING). The FCOM gives no formula: F-factor above 0.13, filtered (design choice). The voice comes with the voices feature below.
Alpha floor is inhibited above M 0.5 (was M 0.6), in the generated PRIM code.

GPWS mode 2 (excessive terrain closure rate) works again with a filtered radio altitude rate: TERRAIN then PULL UP on the PFD with the PULL UP aural, TERRAIN only in landing configuration. The PFD now shows the PULL UP of mode 1 (excessive rate of descent): the mode 2 bit overwrote it.
Shared code: the windshear detector, the PFD warning and the egpws Rust are the same as on core/failures-a32nx, where the A32NX part (FAC windshear, GPWS test, TCAS failure) is.
No REAC W/S DET FAULT alert, SRS escape guidance, FLS modes, THR DES / DCLB, TAD / TCF or predictive windshear. Why: They need models, terrain or wind data.
The Simulink PRIM model still has M 0.6. Why: Only the generated code is changed. What to do: Change the model before a regeneration.
On WINDSHEAR or PULL UP, apply the FCOM escape manoeuvre.
No false WINDSHEAR in gusts or turns.
A380X mode 2 over rough terrain.

children.title: NAV FM / GPS POS DISAGREE and NAV LS TUNING DISAGREE

items: NAV FM / GPS POS DISAGREE (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-34-10) now triggers when the FMS finds its position too far from the GPS position (latitude-dependent FCOM thresholds; L:A32NX_FM_GPS_POS_DISAGREE of the FM position model of `core/gps`, merged here through core/a380x-elec): master caution, -ACFT POS ... CHECK, STATUS INFO FLS : RAW ONLY. Inhibited in phases 1, 3 to 6 and 12.
NAV LS TUNING DISAGREE when the two MMRs (sim NAV 3 and NAV 4) disagree on frequency or course: master caution, phases 8 and 9 only; STATUS INOP SYS CAT 2, GLS AUTOLAND.
The approach mode is not compared for LS TUNING DISAGREE. Why: The sim receivers have no approach mode.
On NAV FM / GPS POS DISAGREE, check the aircraft position (POSITION MONITOR page) as the E/WD asks.
No false NAV FM / GPS POS DISAGREE or LS TUNING DISAGREE in normal flights.

children.title: A380X FWS voices: sidestick priority, intermediate RA callouts, WINDSHEAR, TERRAIN, GLIDE SLOPE, PITCH PITCH, COMPANY MESSAGE

items: PRIORITY LEFT / PRIORITY RIGHT (FCOM DSC-27-10-20) when a pilot holds the sidestick pb with the priority for 1 s (a short press to disconnect the autopilot does not call it; it waits during a GPWS alert).

Intermediate RA callout: below 400 ft, the height rounded to 10 ft (for example TWO HUNDRED SEVENTY) 11 s after the previous callout; below 100 ft, the height to the foot (for example FORTY SEVEN) 4 s after it.
WINDSHEAR said three times with the reactive windshear warning; it also silences the GPWS alerts.
TERRAIN for GPWS mode 2 and GLIDE SLOPE (louder when hard) for mode 5.
PITCH PITCH (DSC-22-27-20) in a manual landing below 400 ft RA with the pitch above 12 deg, once per event (the FWS computes it: the PRIM output is always false).
COMPANY MESSAGE (DSC-46-40-20) when a company (AOC) message arrives, except in take-off and landing and below 10 000 ft in phase 8.
The clips are made with tools/fws-voice (Piper TTS, public-domain LJ Speech voice) and play from the Wave Data slots of the A380X sound.xml.
TERRAIN and GLIDE SLOPE may stay silent. Why: The A380X Wwise sound bank lacks 13 A32NX events (upstream large-files branch align-a380x-sounds). What to do: Wait for that upstream merge.
No DUAL INPUT voice. Why: The F/O sidestick sends no input in the sim.
No SPEED SPEED, SELCAL or time marker voices. Why: No FCOM threshold / PRIM output, no SELCAL source, the FCOM contradicts itself on the time marker.
No COMPANY ALERT or CALL COMPANY. Why: The AOC has no urgent or call-company messages.
A full MSFS restart is needed. Why: sound.xml changes. What to do: Restart the sim after installing.
Nothing to set: the voices come by themselves.
The volume of the WAV clips against the Wwise voices, and their retrigger.
The A380X Wave Data slots play at all (warning, misc and instrument slots).
The bank + Piper voice mix below 100 ft (gap, volume); the intermediate callouts are not too chatty.
PITCH PITCH once per manual flare; COMPANY MESSAGE per Hoppie telex.
The TERRAIN / GLIDE SLOPE events are present in the A380X bank.

children.title: No BRAKES BTV FAULT while an inner engine is not running

blocks.text: The FCDC sets BTV LOST when engine 2 or 3 is not running, and the FWS raised BRAKES BTV FAULT (single chime, MASTER CAUT) straight from it, for example during the engine start on the ground. The FCOM trigger is "The BTV auto-brake mode is failed" (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-32); an inner engine out makes BTV inoperative through the ENG SHUT DOWN STATUS. The caution now needs both inner engines running; STATUS INOP SYS BTV and LDG DIST AFFECTED still follow the FCDC BTV LOST.

items: Nothing to set.

children.title: Engine exceedance marks only on displayed values

blocks.text: The red N1 / EGT exceedance marks and the N3 red cross latched any value, also while the gauge showed XX (FADEC not sending) or on an infinite value, and a NaN after an exceedance put the mark at NaN. The FCOM shows XX for a value that is not available. The exceedance memories now take only displayed, finite values (E/WD gauge active flag, SD FADEC powered) and keep the highest value through a NaN. The A32NX part is on core/failures-a32nx.

items: Nothing to set.

children.title: XFR pushbuttons start in AUTO and drive the manual fuel transfers

blocks.text: The OUTR, MID and INR TK XFR and TRIM TK XFR pb L:vars were never set at load (read 0 = MAN) and MAN did nothing. Now (FCOM DSC-28-40, "fuel transfers are fully automatic"):

items: They start in AUTO at every flight load (released, no light), also with the hangar, taxi and climb flights.

MAN (FWD for the trim tank) suspends the automatic transfers and lines up the FCOM manual transfer: OUTR outer tanks into the feed tanks (with an outer tank pump OFF, the emergency valves feed tanks 1 and 4 by gravity); INR and MID with their aft pumps into the feed tanks; TRIM FWD trim tank into the inner tanks.
Back to AUTO restarts the automatic logic. Jettison and refuel suspend the manual transfers; no lineup takes fuel out of a feed tank.
No AUTO GND XFR. Why: The FCOM rule is incomplete and flight_model.cfg has no wing-to-trim line.
No outer gravity transfer to feed tanks 2 and 3, no XFR FAULT lights, no MAN XFR ECAM procedures. Why: Not done.
The jettison suspension reads L:A380X_FUEL_JETTISON_IN_PROGRESS. Why: core/fuel (its jettison signals) is not on this branch. What to do: With core/fuel merged it uses them.
Leave the XFR pbs in AUTO for normal operation.
Press one to MAN (FWD) for a manual transfer, as the FCOM asks; press it again for AUTO.

blocks.text: Test this first, before the other fuel tests.

items: First: at load (cold and dark, apron, in flight) all four XFR pbs released / no light and no tank level change on the ground.
The flow of each pb on the SD FUEL page, and back to AUTO.
INR MAN runs the right inner pump (pump index swap).

children.title: No CAB PRESS caution while a CPIOM B is not powered

blocks.text: The FWS counted a cabin pressure control (CPCS) application of a CPIOM B as failed whenever its discrete word was in failure warning, which an unpowered CPIOM B also sends. At a power-up (EXT PWR, APU) the four CPIOM B buses come back one after the other (B1 DC 1, B2 and B3 DC 108PH, B4 DC 2), so CAB PRESS CTL REDUNDANCY LOST (two applications lost, FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-21-30) or CAB PRESS AUTO CTL FAULT (all four) came up with the master caution. A CPCS application now counts as failed only while its CPIOM B is powered, as the FWS already did for the AGS, TCS and VCS applications.

items: Nothing to set.

children.title: No EXCESS RESIDUAL DIFF PRESS warning at a power-up on a high pressure day

blocks.text: The outflow valve controllers filter the ambient pressure they get from the ADIRS and use the standard sea level pressure (1013.25 hPa) until the ADIRS sends it. The A380 ADIRUs run on the AC buses, so in a cold and dark aircraft the first ambient pressure arrives only after EXT PWR or the APU is on and the ADRs have initialised. The cabin differential pressure was then sent as valid while the filter was still moving to the real ambient pressure: on a high pressure day (QNH 1031.8 hPa) about 0.23 PSI for about 2.5 s, above the 0.072 PSI of CAB PRESS EXCESS RESIDUAL DIFF PRESS (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-21-30: on ground with no engine running), so the red warning and the master warning came up. The filter now starts from the first ADIRS ambient pressure.

items: Nothing to set.

blocks.text: Three new flyPad failures for the smoke detection of the Network Server System (NSS): Network server system (NSS) smoke, Network server system (NSS) smoke detector 1 and Network server system (NSS) smoke detector 2 (ids 26049 to 26051). NSS smoke has no ECAM alert: it lights the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw, which stays on as long as smoke is detected, also with the NSS power cut off (A380 FCOM DSC-26-50-10, DSC-46-20-20-87). The detection logic is the one of the avionics bays: both detectors, or one failed and the other one detecting.

items: The SMOKE light needs `core/failures-a32nx`. Why: The NSS smoke zone of the smoke detection model and the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw are on that branch, with the rest of the A380X smoke detection model; this branch has the flyPad failures and their failure mapping. What to do: Merge both; without it the NSS failures give nothing.
A failed NSS smoke detector shows nothing. Why: The FCOM has no NSS SMOKE DET FAULT alert.
With `core/failures-a32nx` merged: flyPad > Failures > ATA 26 Fire Protection > Network server system (NSS) smoke.
Watch the SMOKE light of the NSS MASTER sw; deactivate the failure to clear it.

children.title: Stall warning over the GPWS, automatic TCAS TA ONLY

items: GPWS: the FWS STALL warning now removes the GPWS visual and aural alerts, as the reactive windshear warning already did ("Stall or windshear alerts override GPWS visual and aural alerts", A380 FCOM DSC-34-20-20-10). It is read from the FWS output word of either FWS.

TCAS: TA ONLY is selected automatically during a windshear or stall warning and in emergency electrical configuration (the four AC busbars lost), on top of the existing TAWS warnings and the below 1 000 ft rule (FCOM DSC-34-20-40-10). All RAs are inhibited and the ND shows TA ONLY. The TCAS returns to TA/RA when the warning ends.

The STALL warning comes only outside normal law, above 1 500 ft radio altitude. Why: The FWS rule of the stall warning; in normal law the protections prevent the stall. What to do: Test in alternate or direct law.
Without the TAWS system-in-use and gear-down mode 5 changes of develop. Why: Not part of this placement.
Nothing to set: on a STALL warning fly the stall recovery; the GPWS alerts stay silent until it ends.
With TA ONLY on the ND after a windshear, stall or emergency electrical configuration, follow the TAs only.

children.title: CAB COM, COM and PA IN USE alerts

blocks.text: The A380 FCOM (PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-23, DSC-23-20) has alerts for the cabin communication and the radio transmissions. The sim has no CIDS and no push-to-talk (PTT) switches, so new flyPad failures stand in for them:

items: CAB COM CIDS 1+2+3 FAULT: the three CIDS directors are failed. STATUS INOP SYS: CIDS 1+2+3. It replaces the two alerts below.

CAB COM CIDS CABIN COM FAULT: the cabin interphone, the upper deck PA or the main deck PA is failed (the LOWER DECK PA FAULT line shows with them but does not trigger the alert). STATUS INOP SYS names the failed functions.
COM DEGRADED: PA or cabin interphone failed in some areas of the cabin only (lines PA DEGRADED and CABIN INTERPHONE DEGRADED).

COM CAPT (F/O)(THIRD OCCUPANT) PTT STUCK: the PTT switch of that seat stays in transmit for more than 40 s while no transmission key is selected on the RMP of that seat (RMP 1 CAPT, RMP 2 F/O, RMP 3 third occupant).
COM VHF 1 (2)(3) EMITTING: that VHF transmits (a PTT in transmit with its VHF transmission key selected on the RMP) for more than 60 s, with the line RMP TX KEY ... DESELECT.

COM VHF 3 DATALINK FAULT on the VHF 3 failure (STATUS INOP SYS: VHF 3 DATALINK), and COM DATALINK FAULT (line VHF & HF & SATCOM DATA NOT AVAIL) when VHF 3 is failed or in voice mode, because VHF 3 is the only data medium of the sim.
PA IN USE memo while the PA transmission key of any RMP is on.

blocks.text: All the alerts except COM DEGRADED and PA IN USE are inhibited in flight phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10 (COM DEGRADED: phases 3 to 11; PA IN USE: never inhibited).

items: With the three CIDS failed only CIDS 1+2+3 FAULT shows. Why: Design choice: all the cabin communication is lost then, the other two alerts are not active while it is.
VHF EMITTING is raised after 60 s with the chime; the silent 35 s to 60 s stage is not shown. Why: The FWS gives the single chime and MASTER CAUT only when an alert first appears.
No HF 1(2) EMITTING, HF DATALINK FAULT or SATCOM alerts; COM DATALINK FAULT has only its VHF & HF & SATCOM DATA NOT AVAIL line. Why: The sim has no HF and no SATCOM radio and no ACR failure.
COM DATALINK FAULT also shows when VHF 3 is only in voice mode. Why: VHF 3 is the only data medium of the sim; failure only may be preferred later.
When one of these alerts shows, follow its E/WD lines and read the STATUS page.
For PTT STUCK or VHF EMITTING, deselect the transmission key on the RMP when the line asks for it.

blocks.text: Setup: A380X at the gate, powered (flight phase 1 or 2), flyPad open.

children.title: SMOKE DET FAULT, cargo smoke TEST, APU MACH LIMIT and OIL FILTER alerts

items: SMOKE DET FAULT (caution, single chime, MASTER CAUT; inhibited in phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10): the smoke detection function (SDF) is failed with the new flyPad failure. No smoke and no detector fault is then reported anywhere (avionics bays, IFE and NSS, cargo, cabin). STATUS INOP SYS: ALL SMOKE DET, FWD CRG VENT, FWD CGR TEMP REGUL, BULK CRG VENT, BULK CRG HEATER. Lines: IFEC OFF, IF NO LIVESTOCK, FWD ISOL VALVES OFF, BULK ISOL VALVES OFF, BULK CARGO HEAT OFF (the aircraft procedure has no CWS line: it is hidden).

Cargo smoke TEST pb: held for at least 3 s (until released) it shows the cargo and avionics bay SMOKE warnings (continuous repetitive chime, MASTER WARN flashing) and lights the VENT AVNCS SMOKE light. A failed SDF cannot run the test.
APU MACH LIMIT EXCEEDED (caution, SD APU page; flight phase 8 only): the APU runs above M 0.5. Lines: IF APU NOT ABSOLUTELY RQRD, APU MASTER SW OFF. STATUS INOP SYS: APU.
APU OIL FILTER CLOGGED (crew awareness, no chime, no master light; phases 1 and 12 only): the new flyPad failure sets an impending oil filter clogging while the APU runs.

The SMOKE DET FAULT alert has no source on this branch. Why: The smoke detection function (Rust, L:A32NX_SMOKE_DETECTION_FUNCTION_FAULT) is on `core/failures-a32nx`; here are the flyPad failure, its failure mapping and the FWS alert. What to do: Merge `core/failures-a32nx`; without it the failure gives no alert and the cargo smoke TEST has no detector to test.
No automatic shutdown on a fully clogged APU oil filter. Why: Not modelled; the alert shows while the APU runs, because the filter pressure drop exists only with oil flowing.
Crew rest, lavatory, CWS, shower smoke alerts and FWD (AFT) CARGO BOTTLES FAULT are not fed. Why: No such detector or diverter valve in the sim.
The BULK CARGO HEATER line is never ticked. Why: The pb is not read.
On SMOKE DET FAULT, follow the E/WD lines (IFEC, ISOL VALVES and bulk heat).
To test the cargo smoke detection, hold the TEST pb of the CARGO SMOKE panel for 3 s and release it.
On APU MACH LIMIT EXCEEDED, slow below M 0.5 or switch the APU MASTER SW off.

blocks.text: Needs `core/failures-a32nx` merged for the SMOKE DET FAULT and the TEST rows. A380X at the gate, EXT PWR on, APU running for the APU rows.

A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-42 has AVIONICS NETWORK alerts for the AFDX switches (network A: 1-7 and 9, network B: 11-17 and 19) and the IOMs. A single switch or IOM failure gives no ECAM alert (maintenance message only). The alerts come from the flyPad failures of the switches and of the IOMs A1 to A8:

head: Alert
Condition
rows: All 16 switches failed. Replaces the others. Phases 4 to 7, 9, 10 inhibited. LIMITATIONS: A/THR NOT USABLE, XPDR MODE A ONLY, ATC COM VOICE ONLY, MAN PRESS : DO NOT USE; approach and landing limitations (MAX SPEED 220 KT, JETTISON, L/G GRVTY EXTN ONLY, CAT 1 ONLY, A-SKID, N/W STEER).
Two switches failed, on one network only. Phases 2 to 11 inhibited.
AVIONICS NETWORK MULTIPLE SWITCH FAULT (NETWORK DEGRADED)
One or more switches failed on both networks (not all). Phases 3 to 7, 9, 10 inhibited.
AVIONICS NETWORK MULTIPLE SWITCH FAULT (REDUNDANCY DEGRADED)
Three or more switches failed on one network only.
Two IOMs failed, no pair completely lost. Phases 2 to 11 inhibited.
AVIONICS NETWORK MULTIPLE IOM FAULT (NETWORK DEGRADED)
Both IOMs of a pair failed (pairs A1+A2, A3+A4, A5+A6, A7+A8).
AVIONICS NETWORK MULTIPLE IOM FAULT (REDUNDANCY DEGRADED)
Three or more IOMs failed, no pair completely lost.

items: No MULTIPLE CABLE FAULT alert. Why: The sim has no cable model.
The procedure lines that depend on which switch or IOM failed are missing. Why: The sim does not map the aircraft systems to switch ports or IOM pairs.
The IOM pairs are a design choice. Why: The real pairing is not known; the two IOMs of a pair sit on different switches and power supplies in the Rust model.
Two failed switches or IOMs always give DOUBLE FAULT. Why: The FCOM combinations that count as double for MEL purposes are not listed.
When an AVIONICS NETWORK alert shows, follow its E/WD lines and read the LIMITATIONS and INOP SYS of the STATUS page.

blocks.text: Setup: A380X at the gate, powered, flyPad open.

children.title: ATA 46 information system COM alerts and ATC RESET

blocks.text: Four COM alerts of the information system (A380 FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM-10-46), inhibited in flight phases 3 to 7, 9 and 10:

items: COM ATC DATALINK FAULT: CPIOM D1 is lost, or the ATC RESET pb of the overhead RESET panel is pulled (the ATC datalink is powered down while it is pulled). STATUS INOP SYS: ATC DATALINK; LIMITATIONS: ATC COM VOICE ONLY.
COM ADS DATALINK FAULT: the ADS function is failed (new flyPad failure). STATUS INOP SYS: ADS DATALINK. With the whole ATC datalink lost only COM ATC DATALINK FAULT shows.
COM NSS DATA TO AVNCS XFR FAULT: the NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw is OFF. STATUS INOP SYS: NSS DATA TO AVNCS.
COM NSS/AVNCS DATA XFR FAULT: both SCIs are failed (SCI 1 and SCI 2). It replaces the previous alert. STATUS INOP SYS: NSS/AVNCS DATA XFR.

blocks.text: The new flyPad failures are SCI 1 and SCI 2 (NSS / avionics secure communication interface) and ADS function (ATC datalink).

items: Only the alerts: pulling ATC RESET does not power-cycle the ATC datalink here, and there is no SD mailbox or KCCU effect. Why: Those parts of the same change are not on this branch. What to do: Not placed on a core branch yet.
Losing VHF 3 or both SCIs does not stop the datalink or the AOC. Why: Those effects are on `core/a380x-ois-datalink`. What to do: Merge it for the effects; here only the alerts show.
The COM NSS DATA TO AVNCS XFR FAULT alert from a single faulty SCI is not simulated. Why: Only the pb-sw OFF case gives it; both SCIs lost give the next alert.
On COM ATC DATALINK FAULT, use voice for ATC; push the ATC RESET pb back in if it was pulled.
On the NSS alerts, set the NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw to ON; with both SCIs lost nothing can be done in the cockpit.

blocks.text: Setup: A380X at the gate, powered (phase 1 or 2).

children.title: A380X OIS and ATC datalink system model
ATC MSG lights and RING inhibited in takeoff and landing

blocks.text: During takeoff and landing the ATC MSG pb lights and the RING stay off. An uplink received then, or a sixth uplink that needs an answer while five already wait for one, is rejected: the ATC center gets an automatic ERROR downlink. A message that already waits flashes again after the phase.

items: An uplink waits, FWS phase 3 to 7 (takeoff power to 1500 ft) or 9 to 10 (800 ft to 80 kt): ATC MSG lights dark, no RING.
A new uplink arrives in those phases: It is not shown; the center receives ERROR.
After the phase, a message still waits: The ATC MSG lights flash again.

Taxi is not inhibited. Why: Design choice: the manual names taxiing in one sentence only; inhibiting the taxi would reject the taxi and departure clearances. Same phases as the COMPANY MSG memo inhibition. What to do: None.
A32NX unchanged. Why: The rules are behind the A380X mailbox flag of the shared ATC datalink. What to do: None.
Nothing to do: the inhibition follows the FWS flight phase.

children.title: ARU start: STANDALONE and SYNCHRONIZATION NOT AVAIL

blocks.text: The laptops connect to the FLT OPS network through the ARU, which operates 2 minutes after the FLT OPS ANSU is powered. A laptop started before that, or without the network, works as a stand-alone: STANDALONE on its Login page and SYNCHRONIZATION NOT AVAIL on the FLT OPS STS page.

items: The ARU follows the FLT OPS ANSU. Why: Design choice: the ARU supply and failures are not modelled. What to do: None.
A laptop started before the ARU stays a stand-alone. Why: As the manual: restart it once the ARU operates. What to do: Log off and start the laptop again.
After a power-up, wait 2 minutes before starting the laptops.

children.title: OIS MENU and OIS XFR keys (X-OIS)

blocks.text: OIS MENU shows the FLT OPS menu. OIS XFR starts X-OIS: the OIT shows the FLT OPS page of the other OIT with "X-OIS Activated", and follows it; OIS XFR again (or OIS MENU) ends it.

items: X-OIS shows the other OIT's page, with this OIT's own laptop data. Why: Design choice: the two OITs share only the page code (L:A380X_OIT_CAPT/FO_FLT_OPS_PAGE); the synced bus does not reach the other OIT of the same VCockpit. What to do: None.
The ACD keys need core/a380x-cockpit. Why: The ACD legends and click areas are there. What to do: Use the laptop keyboard keys.
Press OIS XFR to see the other side's FLT OPS page; press it again to come back.

children.title: COMPANY COM weather request and free text

blocks.text: COMPANY COM gets a METAR / TAF request page and a free text page, sent through the AOC (Hoppie network); the answers come into the Inbox.

items: No NOTAM request. Why: The datalink has no NOTAM source. What to do: None.
COMPANY COM > Requests > Weather: enter the airports, tick METAR / TAF, SEND.

blocks.text: EXIT SESSION returns to the Login page and clears the FLT OPS STS page for the next flight. It is not available while the FLT FOLDER is open.

items: None known.
Close the FLT FOLDER, then FLT OPS MENU > EXIT SESSION.

blocks.text: PRINT under a displayed Inbox message prints it (subject, sender, reception time, text) on the pedestal printer, through the FMS printer of the MFD. The AOC also gets a downlink inhibition (no messages sent, uplinks still received), which the NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw drives (see "AOC hosted by the NSS AVNCS ANSUs" below).

items: No print while the printer is off or unpowered. Why: The FMS printer answers PRINTER NOT AVAIL. What to do: Switch the printer on.
Inbox > select a message > PRINT.

children.title: VHF 3 failure stops the datalink; SCI 1 and SCI 2 failures

items: VHF 3 is the only data medium of the A380X datalink router (no HF or SATCOM datalink in the sim). A failed VHF 3 (flyPad failure VHF 3, id 23007) is now treated as not in DATA mode: CPDLC and AOC stop, as COM VHF 3 DATALINK FAULT tells the crew on the aircraft. Before, the datalink kept working with VHF 3 failed.

Two new flyPad failures: SCI 1 (NSS / avionics secure communication interface) and SCI 2 (NSS / avionics secure communication interface) (46008, 46009). With both lost the AOC is inoperative: it can no longer send or receive messages (A380 FCOM COM NSS/AVNCS DATA XFR FAULT). One SCI alone changes nothing.

No ECAM alert: no COM VHF 3 DATALINK FAULT, no COM NSS/AVNCS DATA XFR FAULT. Why: The FWS avionics network and ATA 46 COM alerts (and the ADS function failure 46010) extend develop alert code that is on no core branch; they stay on develop. What to do: Know which failure you set.
flyPad > Failures > ATA 23 Communication: VHF 3 to lose the datalink.
flyPad > Failures > ATA 46 Information Systems: SCI 1 and SCI 2 together to lose the AOC.

children.title: AOC hosted by the NSS AVNCS ANSUs; NSS DATA TO AVNCS OFF stops the AOC downlinks

items: The AOC ran while AC BUS 1 was powered. It now runs while one NSS AVNCS ANSU is healthy: "In the case of an ANSU 1 failure, ANSU 2 provides the AOC application" (A380 FCOM DSC-46-40-10-20). An ANSU is healthy when powered, not failed (flyPad NSS AVNCS ANSU 1 / NSS AVNCS ANSU 2), not reset (RESET panel NSS AVNCS) and with the NSS MASTER sw on; the OIT writes it (L:A32NX_NSS_ANSU_1(2)_IS_HEALTHY). With both SCIs lost the AOC stays off.

NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw OFF (pressed in, OFF light) stops the AOC downlinks (messages and requests); the uplinks still come in (FCOM DSC-46-20-20-80). The systems host reads the pb-sw itself: 1 = normal, 0 = OFF.

While the AOC is off it receives no company message (a free text the ground sends then never reaches the aircraft), and no COMPANY MSG stays after it powers down (92a4d3b28, the AOC part of develop 1e9ee7910; fbw-common, the A32NX AOC behaves the same).
The AOC follows the ANSU health written by the OIT. Why: The ANSUs are modelled in the OIT instrument; the systems host reads their L:vars twice a second.
No COM NSS/AVNCS DATA XFR FAULT or AVIONICS NETWORK alert. Why: Those FWS alerts are on `core/a380x-elec-fuel-alerts`; merge it to get them.
Keep the NSS MASTER sw on and the NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw in its normal position for the company datalink.
Press NSS DATA TO AVNCS (OFF) to stop sending to the ground while still receiving.

children.title: A380X OIS: NSS AVNCS and FLT OPS applications
NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw read the right way round

blocks.text: The pb-sw variable `L:A32NX_OVHD_NSS_DATA_TO_AVNCS_TOGGLE` is 1 in its normal (released) position and 0 when pressed in (OFF light). The OIT read it the other way round, so it treated the data link to the avionics as OFF in normal use: one-way, avionics to NSS only. On the aircraft only OFF does that: the AOC can no longer send and the logbook loses its ground link.

items: No visible change on master alone. Why: On master no OIT function is paused by this switch yet; the effect shows with the logbook ground link of the OIS applications. What to do: None.
Leave the NSS DATA TO AVNCS pb-sw in its normal position; press it (OFF) to cut the data link to the avionics.

children.title: Menu bars, message toolbar, switching bar and task bar

blocks.text: The two OIS domains now have the menu bars the FCOM describes:

items: FLT OPS: MENU, the active application name in cyan, FUNCTIONS (HOME, PREVIOUS, NEXT, PRINT, STORE, UPDATE, UNDO, REDO, HELP, HIDE / SHOW SWITCHING BAR, CLOSE APPLICATION with their shortcuts; an item is enabled only when the application has that function), the MSG counter, its list and CLEAR. At the bottom the switching bar shows the open applications in opening order, the active one highlighted, with scroll arrows; HIDE SWITCHING BAR (F11) gives the full screen.

NSS AVNCS: NSS AVNCS MENU, MAXIMIZE / MINIMIZE (full screen without the navigation tree), MSG and CLEAR; line 2 HOME, BACK, FORWARD, PRINT (pedestal printer, on the pages that can print), UPDATE, HELP (greyed) and CLOSE (closes the application). At the bottom the task bar shows the open applications (LOGBOOK, COMPANY COM, REFUEL, A380X SYSTEMS) in opening order; a key shows its application where it was left. All applications close at the log-off.
A company message received posts a notification on both domains; reading the message removes it; selecting it on the NSS AVNCS side opens the message.

blocks.text: NSS AVNCS menu page: LOGBOOK, COMPANY COM and REFUEL
FLT OPS FUNCTIONS list on LOADSHEET: PRINT enabled once a loadsheet is generated, the greyed items have no function there

items: UPDATE, UNDO, REDO and HELP of FUNCTIONS are greyed. Why: They are greyed in the FCOM figures too. What to do: None.
HOME goes to the application home page, not to the FLT OPS MENU. Why: As the FCOM function list. What to do: Use MENU > FLT OPS MENU or the OIS MENU key.
Open applications from the menu; switch between them with the switching bar (FLT OPS) or the task bar (NSS AVNCS).
Use FUNCTIONS (FLT OPS) or the line-2 buttons (NSS AVNCS) for PRINT, CLOSE and full screen.

children.title: COMPANY COM folders, report and request forms

blocks.text: COMPANY COM opens on its Inbox and counts the unread Inbox messages and the Outbox messages. The Outbox holds what was sent until the network confirms it, then it moves to Sent. The airline forms (INIT Data, Fuel Figures, Refuelling, Loadsheet Acceptance, Departure / Take Off / Gate Delay, Delay Code, ASR, Ramp Service, Diversion, ETA, Flight Summary) are plain forms pre-filled with the flight data the OIT has and sent as a free text to a station (COMPANY without one) over the Hoppie network.
DEPARTURE DELAY form: amber boxes are mandatory, cyan dashes optional; the entries stay while COMPANY COM is open

items: The forms are a design of ours. Why: The AOC is customised by each airline and the FCOM shows no form. What to do: None.
NOTAM request stays greyed. Why: The datalink has no NOTAM source. What to do: None.
COMPANY COM > Pre-flight / In-flight / Post-flight > Requests or Reports > the form.
Fill the amber boxes, check the pre-filled values, SEND. Follow it in Outbox, then Sent.

blocks.text: Shows the fuel on board, the preselected fuel quantity (PFQ) and the refuel state, and on the ground sets a new PFQ for the automatic refuel.
